author: chaliy
body:
## What changed
The lifecycle start events a phase emits are now stored in batches: `session.activated`, `turn.started`, `reason.started`, `capability.usage`, `output.message.started`, `act.started` and `tool.started`. These are the events the worker's write-behind queue already stores in the background.

- **Worker:** events that queue up behind an in-flight store go out together in one `EmitEventStream` call. Before, each one got its own RPC.
- **Control plane:** `emit_batch` inserts a run of consecutive durable events with one statement.
  - One `event_sequences` bump per session reserves the run's sequences.
  - Each row gets the same consecutive sequence, in batch order, that repeated `allocate_event_sequence` calls would have given it.
  - The events table's statement triggers (session event count, last turn status, turn count) fire once per batch.
- **Delivery:** publish and listener notification keep the after-commit rule from #4301.
- Events that a caller reads back still use the single-event path. That covers anything outside the write-behind set.

## Why
The llmsim load test showed event INSERTs as the largest share of Postgres time per turn. Each insert was its own round trip and its own trigger pass.

## Before / After
Local llmsim load test (release build, 10 then 25 sessions, 0.5 s think), from `pg_stat_statements`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| single-row `INSERT INTO events` per turn | ~11 | ~7 (plus ~2 batched inserts) |
| event insert DB time per turn | 15.8 ms | 14.4 ms |
| 25 sessions: turn overhead p50 / total p50 | 210 / 354 ms | 172 / 275 ms (first run); 117 / 190 ms (second run, 15 sessions after a session-create 429) |

The win is modest. The first queued event usually leaves before the rest of the phase's burst arrives, so a phase sends about two batches instead of one. Run-to-run noise on this 4-core box is large, so the statement counts are the reliable signal.

## Risk
- Low
- A failed batch fails all of its events together. These events were already logged-only on failure.
- Sequence allocation for a batch takes the per-session `event_sequences` row lock once, the same lock single inserts take.

## Security
- Threat categories reviewed: no security-relevant code changes (internal event write path; inputs are already-validated events from the worker).
- Findings and resolutions: none.

## Follow-ups
Per-org turn reservation lock (about 4 ms of lock wait per turn) is next, in its own PR.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added or updated (`emit_batch_keeps_each_sessions_sequence_in_batch_order`, `events_queued_behind_a_store_in_flight_go_out_as_one_batch`)
- [x] Backward compatibility considered (no wire or schema change; `EmitEventStream` already existed)
- [x] Security review performed against relevant threat model categories
- [x] Final CI ran checks affected by this PR
- [x] All review comments addressed (code change or written reasoning)

author: justinhwang
body:
## Summary

The per-resolution digest lines were SHA-256 over a whole resolution's stream text, which only one process walking every cell in order could produce. Resolution 7 is 98.8 million cells and takes about an hour that way, so the files stopped at 6.

This PR redefines each resolution's stream digest as the SHA-256 of the 122 base-cell hex digests concatenated in base-cell order. The base-cell lines are unchanged and remain the primary record; resolution lines are derived from them, so any number of processes can produce the base-cell lines and one cheap step combines them. Resolution 7 is now in the files.

## Changes

- **Format** (`README.md`): resolution digests derived from base-cell digests; files cover resolutions 0 through 7, 115,664,014 cells. Every resolution line changes under the new definition; no base-cell line does.
- **Generator** (`gen.c`): digest loop split into `digestBaseCell` and a `ResolutionDigest` accumulator that refuses out-of-order base cells. New modes `--digests <res> <first> <last>` (base-cell lines of a slice to stdout), `--resolution-row <res>` (derived resolution line from base-cell lines on stdin) and `--manifest` (rewrite the manifest from the files on disk, also used by the full run).
- **`digests.sh <res> [suite-dir]`**: one generator process per base cell with every online CPU busy, rows concatenated in order, that resolution's lines replaced in both digest files, manifest rewritten. `generate.sh` still writes resolutions 0 through 6 in one process and does not keep resolution 7, so `digests.sh 7` is run after a full regeneration.
- **Runner** (`digests_test.go`): `TestResolutionDigests` computes base cells in parallel and combines them the same way; stream failures are returned as errors rather than `t.Fatalf` from goroutines. Default resolution stays 3.

## Timings

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| `digests.sh 7` (C, 12 cores, 16 processes) | about 7 min |
| Go runner, `H3_CONFORMANCE_DIGESTS_MAXRES=7 go test -run Digests` (both digest tests, res 0 through 7) | 924 s |

The pure-Go port matches every base-cell and resolution digest at every resolution 0 through 7.

## Test plan

- [x] Strict compile of `gen.c` clean (`-Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -Wpedantic`)
- [x] Full regeneration: only `digests/resolutions.jsonl` and the manifest differ from master
- [x] `digests.sh 7 x/h3go/conformance/testdata` appends 122 base-cell lines and one resolution line
- [x] `go test -count=1 -race -cover ./x/h3go/conformance/` passes, 100% coverage
- [x] `H3_CONFORMANCE_DIGESTS_MAXRES=7 go test ./x/h3go/conformance/ -run Digests` passes
- [x] `golangci-lint run ./x/h3go/...` clean

author: picatz
body:
Closes #1425

## Why

A `switch:` or nested `parallel:` inside a parallel branch merged its step ids out for the validator but not for either driver. `flow validate` accepted a later step reading `steps.inner`, then both drivers failed the run with `no such key`. The collision check in `validateParallel` also used a narrower rule than the scope walk.

## What changed

`v1.MergedStepNodes` (and `MergedStepIDs`) is the one spelling of what a branch contributes to the scope after it. The validator's scope walk, the cross-branch id-collision check, and the local and durable parallel joins all read it. The separate `branchStepNodes` and `switchStepNodes` walks are gone.

## Design choices

Merge nested ids out rather than refuse the reference: the issue's own lean, and consistent with how a top-level `switch:` already merges its case-body ids. A loop still contributes only itself.

## Verification

- New `ControlFlowCases` entry with the issue's reproducer; it fails on the local driver without the fix, and the durable driver runs the same corpus.
- New validator test: a nested id repeated by a sibling branch is refused, and the reproducer file validates.
- `go test -short` over `pkg/flowstate/v1`, `pkg/flowstate/v1/flowfile/...` and `pkg/flowstate/v1/engine` passed.
- `go run ./tools/gate`: NOT VERIFIED locally (too slow in this container); CI is the check.

## Risk, compatibility, and rollout

A file that repeats a nested id across parallel branches is now refused at validate where it previously overwrote silently. Greenfield; no migration.

## Remaining uncertainty

None known.

author: napetrov
body:
## Summary

Structured traceability from each ADR to the use cases it serves, the public surfaces (CLI, typed API, Action, report) that reach it, and the scenarios that exercise those surfaces. Enforced by a ratcheted gate.

## Motivation

ADRs, `usecase-registry.yaml` and `tests/scenarios/*.yaml` had no links to each other. So an ADR could read "implemented" while no surface reached it, a cited flag could be renamed without any signal, and use cases had no link to the vision's user tasks (PR review, local check, release, audit). Concepts adapted from another project's tooling.

## Changes

- **ADR-076** (`docs/contribute/adr/076-adr-use-case-surface-traceability.md`) defines the contract; it is added to the index.
- **`docs/contribute/adr/adr-surface-registry.yaml`**: one entry per ADR (all 78, including the 020a/b and 021a/b pairs). Each entry has a disposition: `surfaced` 44, `partial` 13, `gap` 2, `internal` 19. `partial`/`gap` entries carry `missing`; `internal` entries carry `reason`. Each entry also lists its use cases and its surfaces (`cli` / `api` / `action` / `report`). I filled these in from each ADR's Status and index summary. Where I was unsure the entry says `partial`/`gap`, never `surfaced`.
- **`usecase-registry.yaml`**: every UC gets `user_task:` and `adrs:`. The `adrs:` list must mirror the registry exactly. Schema tests are added in `tests/test_usecase_registry.py`.
- **`scripts/check_adr_surfaces.py`** checks:
  - CLI commands and flags, by introspecting the click tree (aliases such as `-o` and `--output` count as the same option).
  - API symbols, by importing them.
  - Action inputs, from `action.yml` and `actions/*/action.yml`.
  - Report fields, from `abicheck/schemas/*.schema.json`. Formats come from `compare -o`'s declared export formats.
  - Disposition against the index Status: a retired ADR must be `internal`; a fully "implemented" ADR (no partial-type qualifier anywhere in its Status) must be `surfaced` or `internal`.
  - Each scenario's `surfaces:` claim against that scenario's own `flow` command.
  - The ratchet against `adr_surface_baseline.json`. It fails on a disposition downgrade, a lost surface or use case, a newly untraced ADR surface, or a new cli+api+action use case with no shared scenario `family`. To accept such a change on purpose, run `--write-baseline` in the same PR.
  - It also renders `docs/contribute/generated/adr-surface-coverage.md` and fails if the committed copy is stale.
- **Scenarios**: 8 scenarios declare `surfaces:` that their flows actually run. `family:` is documented in the README. I did not add a `family` to any CLI-only scenario just to pass the gate. So the 4 multi-channel use cases with no family (UC-CHANGE-taxonomy, UC-WF-appcompat, UC-WF-baseline, UC-WF-compare) stay listed in the baseline as open gaps, as do 113 untraced ADR surfaces.
- **Wiring**:
  - new `verify.py` step `adr-surfaces` (pr/full profiles)
  - added to CI's `ai-readiness` `--only` list and to `tests/test_verify_profiles.py`
  - the generated report is registered in `GENERATED_FILE_MARKERS`
  - new row in the `scripts/CLAUDE.md` inventory
  - new section in `agent-guide/quality-gates.md`, plus one routing row in `AGENTS.md`
- **Tests**: `tests/test_adr_surfaces.py`, 70 class-based tests on synthetic fixtures. They cover each rule's failing shape, surfaces that resolve and ones that don't, the full disposition ladder, flow verification and the ratchet. One more test runs the gate on the committed tree.

Validation: ruff check/format clean; `mypy abicheck/` untouched; `check_ai_readiness.py` 0 errors; `check_architecture.py` 0 errors; `verify.py --profile pr --only adr-surfaces,usecase-docs-sync,docs-contract` passed; the focused pytest run (adr_surfaces, usecase_registry, scenarios, verify_profiles, ai_readiness, docs_contract) gives 745 passed. `mkdocs build` was not run locally because mkdocs isn't installed here. The full `pr` profile was not run.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added / updated for new behaviour
- [x] Changelog fragment added — not applicable, no `abicheck/**/*.py` touched
- [x] Docs updated if user-visible behaviour changed
- [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes locally (focused gates run instead; see above)
- [x] No new `mypy` or `ruff` errors introduced

author: agoodkind
body:
Unprivileged LXC gateways reject host-only sysctl settings such as `kernel.printk*`. LXC guests also require `pct exec` for commands. The watchdog's filesystem freeze check applies only to QEMU guests.

`mwan install --guest-type qemu|lxc` replaces container detection. The command defaults to `qemu` and rejects other values with exit code 2. QEMU installs write every sysctl key. LXC installs write only `net.` keys and skip sysctl files without a remaining key.

The OpenTofu data source `mwan_role` accepts an optional `guest_type` with the same values and default. The installer and provider use `File.Content(guest)` to select file content. The watchdog skips filesystem freeze checks for LXC guests. `RealOps.GuestExec` executes LXC commands through `pct exec`.

Deployment configuration must use one OpenTofu value for `mwan_role.guest_type` and the gateway's `guest-type` leaf. The gateway leaf requires a separate change.

## Testing

`make -C gateway test-provider-drift` passes all six combinations of `wan`, `failover`, and `host` with `qemu` and `lxc`. The test compares provider output with installed files.

Installer tests check that LXC sysctl files contain only `net.` keys. Another test checks that `--guest-type docker` exits with code 2 and writes no files.

author: loganrenz
body: ## What B3 ambient, part 2: the ambient family's arrangement (part 1, the DSP, is #1594). Selected with `SongSettings.family = .ambient`. - `AmbientArrangement`: a drone that moves with the progression, pads on the drone/pad voices, no drums, risers, impacts or tape stops. The five existing sections are reused as Logan chose, with swell/settle meaning: stillness (intro), swell (build), bloom (drop), settle (breakdown), radiance (drop2). - Dynamics follow the signal level: pad velocity and density are functions of the level, so the music swells as the signal rises and settles as it falls. author: thinkclay
body:
Closes #1022. Part of #1036 (wave 2). Also fixes the two Teams entries of #1025.

## What was wrong
#814 put `ScreenHeader` on every top-level screen. The second-level office screens kept a hand-rolled `<Row justify="space-between"><Stack>{title}{subtitle}</Stack><Button/></Row>`. Its text column had no `flexShrink`, and on React Native Web a flex child defaults to `flexShrink: 0`, so at 390 the title and subtitle ran off the edge and the primary action **left the screen**. Project hiring's "New Project" wasn't visible at all.

| Before (390) | After (390) |
|---|---|
| ![](https://github.com/Scaffald/SaaS/blob/ca1936a453e34ed9db557d360f4b6f5aac63403d/office/mobile-light--employer--office--compliance--project-hiring.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/Scaffald/SaaS/blob/c0d2488b5a3963ac500ea5899e33f95a6c103df4/pr/1022/mobile-light--employer--office--compliance--project-hiring.png?raw=true) |
| ![](https://github.com/Scaffald/SaaS/blob/ca1936a453e34ed9db557d360f4b6f5aac63403d/office/mobile-light--employer--office--ats--scheduling.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/Scaffald/SaaS/blob/c0d2488b5a3963ac500ea5899e33f95a6c103df4/pr/1022/mobile-light--employer--office--ats--scheduling.png?raw=true) |

## Change
- **`ScreenHeader`** (kicker / title / tip / actions; the actions wrap under the title when narrow) now heads EEO reports, Project hiring, Interview scheduling, HRIS, Background check providers, Payment analytics, Transaction history, API keys, and the Jobs board view. EEO's header also moves **above** its coverage banner, where it had ended up second.
- **Teams (both pages):** `DashboardPage` already rendered the shared header, and the screen then printed its own "Teams" row beneath it. That's the title twice (#1025), in a row that couldn't wrap. The tip and **Manage invitations** move into the shared header through `DashboardLayout`'s `screenTip`/`screenActions`, and the inner row goes.
- **Gutters:** EEO, Project hiring and API keys rendered outside `OfficeLayout` (a bare `Stack`/`SafeAreaView`) at an **8 px** gutter where the office sits at **16 px**. They now use `OfficeLayout` like HRIS, and `DeveloperPortal` drops its own padding (only that route uses it).

## Evidence
Built from a static export and swept in light and dark at 1440 and 390:
- every action is on screen;
- the sweep's `CLIPPED` flags on these routes are gone (before: EEO 2, Project hiring 3, Scheduling 1, HRIS 2, Background checks 2, Teams 1; API keys also scrolled sideways). The one left on Project hiring is its chip strip, #1031;
- all ten titles sit at **x=16 at 390 and x=332 at 1440**, the same as the office screens that were already right.

All the 390 captures, light and dark: [contact sheet](https://github.com/Scaffald/SaaS/blob/c0d2488b5a3963ac500ea5899e33f95a6c103df4/pr/1022/headers-mobile.png). Desktop: [API keys and EEO](https://github.com/Scaffald/SaaS/blob/c0d2488b5a3963ac500ea5899e33f95a6c103df4/pr/1022/headers-desktop.png).

## Corrections to the issue
- #1022 said the standard gutter was 32 px. That was device pixels from a 2× capture; it's **16 CSS px**, as measured above.
- `OfficeProjectsList.tsx:227` in the issue's list is a list **row** whose text already flexes, not a page header, so it's unchanged.

## Not in this PR
- Project hiring renders `MOCK_PROJECTS`, and its "New Project" has no `onPress`. Like the integrations screens, that's invented data, so it's noted on #1024.
- The HRIS and background-check "N connected" badges also come from #1024's hardcoded lists; they keep their current behaviour here.

author: mmmries
body:
**Needs a maintainer decision: the release's fence-wait timeout is code `timeout`, which until now meant only a caller-supplied deadline (`await_converged`); `conflict` is the alternative. Also open: whether the release's second wait, on the transform's definition row (`for no key update`, behind a resume, drop or eviction), should be mapped the same way. It is still a raw `55P03` classified `internal`.**

## Summary

Two fixes to `trellis release` (#759 / #841's per-key release), both found in #841's review:

1. **`trellis status` prints held keys so they paste into `trellis release`.** The quarantined-rows listing printed each key with Rust's `{:?}`, so a key containing `"` or `\` showed Rust escapes, and pasting it into `trellis release <TRANSFORM> <SOURCE_TABLE> <KEY>` named a different key (`not_found`). Worse, the `"..."` it printed is a double-quoted shell word, so a `$` or backtick in a key was expanded by the operator's shell. The transform, table and key are now quoted for the shell where they need it. Control characters, which every composite key carries (U+001F between its columns), are written as `$'\ooo'` octal words instead of raw bytes. The `release` confirmation line uses the same quoting. A `--` now ends the CLI's options, so a key that is exactly `-h`, `--help`, `-d` or `--database-url` can be released too.
2. **A release that waits out the lock timeout is a typed, retryable error.** `Trellis::release_key`'s first lock is a bump of the key's table's version fence, which waits for every drain page in flight on that table. A page that holds it past the session's `lock_timeout` (`LOCK_TIMEOUT`, 30 s) used to surface as a raw `55P03` with code `internal`. It's now `ApplyError::ReleaseLockTimeout { transform, src_table, key }` (wrapped in `TrellisError::Apply`), code `timeout`, and its message says the release waited for the work in flight on the table (its drain pages, and any define, alter or column build on it, which also hold the fence to their commit), changed nothing, and can be retried.

## Root cause

1. `cli/src/commands/status.rs`'s `format_poisoned` formatted `entry.key` with `{:?}`.
2. `staging::quarantine::release_key` passed the fence bump's `tokio_postgres::Error` through `?` as `ApplyError::Db`, which `classify_pg_error` maps to `Internal` like any unrecognised SQLSTATE.

## Design

**Quoting scheme.** `release::shell_quote` leaves a word bare when every character is in `[A-Za-z0-9_.,:/@+-]`, so `key=42` and `table=public.orders` read as before. `=` and `%` aren't in the set: zsh expands a word that starts with `=` to a command's path. Otherwise the word goes inside single quotes, where only the quote itself is special, written `'\''`. A control character (C0, DEL or C1) is never written raw. A terminal would drop it from a copy, so a composite key's U+001F separator would never round-trip, or obey it, so an escape sequence in a source row's key would reach the operator's terminal. Instead it's written as a `$'\ooo'` word of its UTF-8 bytes in octal, joined onto the quoted text: `1\x1f2` prints as `'1'$'\037''2'`. bash, zsh, ksh and POSIX.1-2024 shells read that back. dash before 0.5.13 and fish don't, which only matters for keys with control characters. The text stays in plain single quotes, so `!` never triggers bash history expansion. Postgres text can't hold NUL, so a key never contains one. The error text stays `{:?}`: it's only read, and Debug keeps it on one line. The release hint under the listing still shows placeholders, `trellis release <transform> <table> <key>`, and now tells the operator to paste each value as shown. `trellis release --help` and `docs/transforms.md` describe the quoting and the `--`.

**`--` ends the options.** The CLI strips `-d`/`--database-url` from anywhere in argv, and `release` treats any `-h`/`--help` as a help request, so a key spelled exactly like one of those couldn't be released whatever its quoting. `connection::extract_database_url` no longer looks past a `--`, `release`'s help check doesn't either, and `release::parse` drops a leading `--`. A leading `-` in general (`-7`) already parsed as a positional.

**The lock timeout.** I looked for an existing convention first. No operator call (resume, pause, alter, drop, define) maps a lock timeout: they all return the raw `55P03`, classified `internal`. `ErrorCode::Timeout`'s doc said so explicitly ("a Postgres statement or lock timeout is classified by its SQLSTATE"), and `docs/embedding.md` describes a define/drop that "fails with a lock timeout". So there is a convention, and it's the raw error. Following it would mean not fixing #842. This PR therefore names **only the release's fence wait** and leaves every other call, and every other lock wait inside the release (the definition row, ring and projection rows), unchanged.

- **Code `timeout`, not `conflict` or `internal`.** `ErrorCode::Timeout` is "a wait ran out before the condition it waits for held … expected and retryable … kept apart from `Internal` so a host can tell it from a bug". That's exactly this case. `Conflict` reads as "existing state blocks this request", which a retry doesn't fix. The trade-off is that `Timeout` was documented as covering only waits bounded by a caller-supplied timeout, and that doc is amended to name the release. Every other lock timeout is still classified by SQLSTATE.
- **Surfaced, not retried.** No operator call retries lock timeouts internally. The internal retry loops (`DdlRetry`, the drain's transient retry) belong to background work. A retry inside the call would also stretch a 30 s wait to a multiple of it with no feedback. The caller gets the error and decides.
- **Rollback.** The bump is the transaction's first statement, and the error returns before anything else runs. Dropping the transaction rolls back the bump's statement, so the fence is unchanged, as with `KeyNotHeld`.

## Test changes

All of these fail on `main`:

- `trellis/tests/release_held_key.rs::a_release_that_waits_out_the_lock_timeout_is_a_retryable_timeout_and_changes_nothing`: holds `nums`' fence `for share` (a page's lock) from another connection while a facade connected with `options='-c lock_timeout=100'` releases the held key. The session keeps a setting shorter than the 30 s cap, so the test waits only for the release's own 100 ms timeout and doesn't sleep or poll. It asserts the variant, `ErrorCode::Timeout` and the message, then that the fence version, `poison` and `poison_held` are unchanged. Once the page ends, the same release succeeds and the target converges. On `main` it fails with `left: Internal, right: Timeout` (the error was `Apply(Db(… E55P03 … while locking tuple … in relation "source_table_versions"))`).
- `cli/src/commands/status.rs::a_held_key_pastes_from_status_into_release_unchanged`: formats held entries whose key is ``it's a "key" \ with $HOME `and` \`` (it contains `'`, `"`, `\`, spaces, `$` and backticks), `=ls`, and `-7` with a transform and table containing spaces. It pastes each line's `transform=`/`table=`/`key=` words into `sh -c "printf '%s\0' …"`, and checks that `release::parse` of the resulting argv equals the entry. With `main`'s `{:?}` it fails: the shell expanded `$HOME`, ran `` `and` ``, and the key came back as `it's a "key" \ with /home/mike  \`.
- `cli/src/commands/status.rs::a_composite_or_control_character_key_pastes_from_status_into_release_unchanged`: the same round trip through `bash` for keys containing U+001F, U+0001, a newline, ESC and a C1 control. It also checks that the status line contains no control character. This runs through `bash`, not `sh`, because CI's `sh` is dash, which may not read `$'...'`. It fails with the first commit's plain single quotes.
- `cli/src/commands/release.rs`: `a_plain_word_is_left_bare`, `anything_else_is_single_quoted_with_quotes_escaped` (now including `=ls`, `%1`, `~root` and `é`), `a_control_character_is_written_in_octal_never_raw`, `a_leading_double_dash_ends_the_options`.

author: donz-dev
body:
**Rupture 455.0 → 488.5, +33.5**, with the other twenty-two profiles identical to the decimal. Census: **14 ruled out → 12**, live gaps unchanged at 3.

Two halves, both from the ruleset owner: three talents that pointed at Ambush and did nothing, and Vanish.

---

## 1. Ambush had three talents pointing at it and all three were switched off

**One false premise, shared by three.** Improved Ambush (45% crit), Initiative (a second combo point) and **Opportunity's Ambush clause** (+10% damage) each carried an `unmodelled` entry reading:

> Ambush requires stealth and is absent.

That stopped being true the day the owner ruled that **Cutthroat's proc IS Ambush's stealth requirement** and the ability was declared. Ambush was in the book, in the Rupture list, and dealing 1.6% of that profile's damage while three talents aimed at it reported themselves out of scope. Six of the profile's fifty-one points.

### The `scope` tag is why nobody looked again

This is the part worth carrying forward, and it is a **good mechanism being misapplied** rather than a bad one. A `scope` tag means "the owner has ruled this out" — so the effect is deliberately kept off the live-gap list and shown apart in the Talent panel, the whole point being that a ruling is not a work queue item.

**Tagging a LIVE effect `stealth` therefore removed it from the only list anybody re-reads.** An ordinary `unmodelled` reason would have been counted as a gap and re-read when the blocker cleared. Recorded in CLAUDE.md beside the scope table, because the next widened ruling will do exactly this again.

### What each was worth, isolated

60 batches of 10 each, knocked out one at a time against the finished list.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Improved Ambush, 45% crit on Ambush | **+14.0** |
| Opportunity's Ambush clause, +10% damage | **+4.8** |
| Initiative, the second combo point | **+1.4**, inside the interval |

**Initiative is the odd one and the cause is the LIST, not the talent.** At 3/3 it is 100%, so every Ambush is worth two combo points rather than one — into a build whose only damage finishers are Rupture at exactly five points and an Eviscerate that fires **zero** times. The extra points arrive with nowhere to go. *A correct talent can be worth nothing because of where the points go*, and the figure would move if the Eviscerate floors were revisited.

Initiative is now **partly** modelled rather than ruled out: its Ambush clause is live and its Garrote and Cheap Shot clauses keep the `stealth` tag, which will not expire. Same for Opportunity's Garrote.

---

## 2. Vanish, and stealth as a gate rather than a system

**Ambush goes from 0.4 casts a fight to 2.8**, and from 1.6% of the profile's damage to **12.4%**.

The owner's ruling is what keeps this small:

> It's a stealth ability, but we don't need stealth to properly function — it just needs to enable Ambush.

So there is **still no stealth system**. `STEALTH` is an aura Ambush reads in `canCast`, exactly the shape Cutthroat already had, and the two are *alternatives* rather than a new requirement.

**Two routes, one aura.** The Rogue carries it from `openingAuras` at the pull — the owner's "you start from stealth" — and Vanish applies the same definition mid-fight. One code path, so the opening window and a Vanish window cannot drift apart. It is on the **class** rather than a profile, because opening stealthed is a fact about a Rogue; the Venom and Combat lists have no Ambush entry, so both are unchanged to the decimal and the containment run says so.

**Cutthroat is spent first when both are up.** A real decision rather than an arbitrary order: Cutthroat comes off a Backstab proc several times a fight and a stealth window comes off a five-minute cooldown, so spending the renewable one first keeps the scarce one.

### Vanish's numbers, and the one that is not stated

From `forever-rogue-spellbook.json` at rank 2, which is max: `Instant`, `5 min cooldown`, `Reagents: Flash Powder` — so **no energy cost**, a consumable not being a resource this engine tracks.

**Five minutes is longer than every fight here**, which is what makes PREPARATION the second half of the cycle rather than a tidy-up at the end: it finishes the cooldown on every other Rogue ability and therefore on this one. The measurement shows **1.7 Vanishes a fight** — one, a Preparation, and a second — which is the owner's design arriving as specified.

**The duration of plain Stealth is in no source.** Only Vanish states one ("improved stealth mode for 10 sec"), and the opener reuses it rather than taking an invented number or an unbounded one. **The choice is not load-bearing**: the list spends the opening window inside the first two global cooldowns, so ten seconds and forever behave identically. `STEALTH_DURATION_MS` is the single place to change it.

**It takes a global cooldown, which is the engine's DEFAULT and not a stated fact.** Nothing in the source says otherwise, so `triggersGcd` is left derived rather than a guess being written down as data.

---

## 3. The owner's four sequences are three entries

```
Opener:                                    Stealth, Premeditation, Ambush
When <= 3 combo points:                    Vanish, Ambush
When Vanish + Premed on CD and CP <= 1:    Preparation
When Prep is on CD and the others are not: Vanish, Premeditation, Ambush
```

**A priority list cannot hold a sequence and does not need to.** It is re-read from the top every global cooldown and the first castable entry wins, so a sequence is what *emerges* when each step is in turn the highest castable entry. Premeditation, Ambush and Vanish at the top produce all four — **including the last, which needs no entry at all**: once Preparation has reset their cooldowns, the same three are castable again and the list walks them. Said out loud at the call site, because an absent entry for a clause the owner named reads exactly like an omission — and a second entry per ability would be the duplicate-id shape this project only wants deliberately. The opener's "Stealth" is not an entry either; it is the aura the fight starts with.

**Ambush's entry is unconditional now**, because its own `canCast` is the gate. It used to restate half that rule as `selfActive('cutthroat')` — harmless with one route to the gate and wrong with two. It is **not a floor** under the list despite being ungated, because `checkCast` refuses it whenever neither aura is up.

### Three refinements measured, one shipped

60 batches of 10 each, against 482.8 for the list as first written.

| | DPS | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Vanish also gated on 60 energy** | **488.5 ± 2.9** | **+5.7 — shipped** |
| Ambush above Premeditation | 484.9 ± 2.9 | +2.1, inside |
| Premeditation gated at ≤3 points | 482.8 ± 3.4 | **+0.0 exactly** |
| Preparation ungated and last, as it was | 481.6 ± 3.3 | −1.2, inside |

**The energy gate is the only one that measured.** Ambush costs 60 of a 100 pool, and the failure it prevents is not usually a lost window — it is a stealth Ambush arriving several global cooldowns *late*, behind the builders that refilled the pool it was waiting on. On Vanish rather than on Ambush, deliberately: a free Cutthroat proc should be spent whatever the pool looks like and a five-minute cooldown should not.

**The Premeditation point gate measures exactly nothing and is not shipped.** Worth recording because its arithmetic looks compelling — it grants two points, so a pool at four throws one away. The reason it buys nothing is the **cooldown**: at two minutes it fires at the pull and once more after Preparation, and the pool is low at both. *A guard against a case that cannot arise is still a decision somebody has to read*, so the owner's simpler entry stands.

**Preparation's new place and condition are the owner's and measure flat**, and both halves of that are the note: it fires 1.0 times a fight either way, and what the gate changes is WHEN, which a sixty-second fight is too short to reward. The old comme

author: kentin0-fiz0l
body:
## What this changes

BasicSynth and PanUtil were the last two editors wiring their controls by parameter index. Unlike the three fixed in #48, they did keep up with the host, but by re-reading every parameter 30 times a second. They now use the shared `AudioForge::ParameterAttachments` like the rest. This is a cleanup; nothing in either window behaved wrongly before.

- **Mode:** PanUtil wrote `index / (choices - 1)` into a choice parameter, which takes an index. With two modes those are the same number, so it worked, but a third mode would have broken it. The attachment writes the index.
- **The 30 Hz polling is gone.** Only BasicSynth's patch menu is still read on the timer, because the current patch is a program, not a parameter.
- **Width text:** PanUtil's Width parameter now has percent text, so Live shows "140 %" instead of "1.40". The window still shows "140%", and typing text with no number in it still changes nothing rather than going to 0 (mono).
- **Size:** the two editors are 239 lines shorter.

## How it was checked

Freeze source gameplay during handoff. Authenticated control requests use operation IDs for retries; refused switches restore source state only after durable cancellation of an unused destination arrival. Uncertain outcomes retain destination ownership. Modern forwarding preserves account UUIDs. Direct `/server` switches are blocked so they cannot bypass MTMC snapshots. Existing transfer configurations retain their default behavior. MTMC is versioned 0.2.0+26.3.

Production deployment:

- The home website's `MC_PORT` is `26101`; its Cloudflare Worker continues forwarding live APIs to the home service. DNS, Cloudflare routing and Worker code are unchanged. The retired Playit tunnel's saved port was restored to 9002 and remains disabled.

One separate fixture timed out on its initial session claim before any transfer; its log is retained. Full clustered and focused reconnect runs passed.
- Production Minecraft status pings pass on all 14 endpoints. Both home and public website APIs return HTTP 200 with all 15 dimensions up. Controlled zero-player checks correctly show RPG Nether maintenance and lobby unavailable while Velocity remains available; tested servers were restarted.

author: marcelxpfeifer
body: Three follow-ups to the composer's inline images (#1287). Each started as its own commit; review round 1 added two. ## #1293: "Save as reply" stored pasted images as empty `` tags A pasted image lives in the composer body as `` with no `src`. Its bytes are a part on the draft row. The server sanitizes a saved reply with the Postbox allowlist, which drops the marker, so the row kept a bare ``. Every later draft that inserted the reply then sent an empty image. A saved reply has no storage for image bytes. Copying the parts into reply-owned storage and re-attaching them on insert would be a new feature with schema and storage work. Inlining them as `data:` URIs would run into the 64 KB body cap, and many mail clients block `data:` images. So the simple fix is to leave pasted images out and tell the user: - `SavedReplySaveDialog.vue` strips every marked image from what it saves (`stripInlineImages` in `@owlat/shared/inlineImages`). When it removed any, a line under the text preview says so: "A saved reply cannot keep pasted images, so this one is left out. Paste it again after you insert the reply." It is pluralized, with a German version using "du". - `savedReplyRules.ts` also cleans images on the server. It removes a `cid:` `src` (a part of another message), then drops an `` only when neither a `src` nor a sanitized `srcset` is left to show it. `` keeps its srcset. Ordinary `https:`/`data:` images stay. `stripInlineImages` on the client keys on the `data-inline-cid` marker only, which only the editor writes on pasted images, so it does not have this rule. This applies to create and update in both `savedReplies.ts` and the previous release's `snippets.ts`, so a web client from before this change can't store one either. ## #1294: part URLs were cached against the device clock `loadMessagePart.ts` kept a minted `/sealed-blob` URL until shortly before the `exp` in its query string (server time) and checked that against `Date.now()` on the device. A device clock running behind reused expired URLs, so the open fell back to downloading the whole raw `.eml`. A clock more than an hour ahead never reused any URL. The loader now reuses a URL for 50 minutes, counted on the device from when the mint returned. It never reads `exp`. The proxy's tokens live an hour from minting (`lib/sealedBlob.ts`), so 50 minutes leaves ten for the round trip. If the proxy still refuses a reused URL (the clock jumped, or a shorter token lifetime later), the loader mints once more before returning `null` and sending the caller to the raw `.eml`. A fresh URL that fails still returns `null` right away, as before. I used a client-side cap rather than having `getMessagePartUrl` return a lifetime. Changing that action's return type from `string | null` would break web clients one release behind, and a second action would add API for no gain over the cap and the retry. ## #1301: "Preview as sent" showed pasted images as broken The preview rendered the stored body. The send path rewrites marked images to `cid:` first, but the preview skipped that step, and the renderer drops `data-inline-cid`. So each pasted image reached the preview frame with no source. `buildSentPreview` now takes a resolver and runs `resolveInlineImageSrcs` (new, next to `rewriteInlineImageCids`, same tag parser) on `bodyHtml` before rendering. It points each marked image at the URL the editor already shows the draft's part from. `PostboxComposer` passes its `inlineImageSources` (from `usePostboxDraftInlineImages`) through the footer to `PostboxPreviewAsSent`. An image whose URL hasn't arrived yet keeps no `src`, like in the editor. The plain-text part is identical either way, since the text derivation drops images. The preview frame's CSP is unchanged (`img-src https: data:`). The proxy URLs are `https:` in production, so they load. I checked this in a real browser with an https image host: the image loads inside the `sandbox=""` srcdoc frame under the meta CSP. On a plain-`http:` development backend the preview still shows them broken, which the CSP comment now notes. `PostboxComposer.vue` sits at the 500-line cap, so I shortened one three-line comment to two to make room for the new prop line. Closes #1293 Closes #1294 Closes #1301 ## Compatibility - No schema change, no migration, no new env vars. - The server-side image filter only affects what new saves write. Existing saved-reply rows are not rewritten. - No API signatures changed. `getMessagePartUrl` returns the same string. - Deploy order doesn't matter. An old web client saving a reply with a pasted image now gets the image dropped by the server instead of stored empty. ## Testing Each regression test was confirmed failing with its fix reverted: - #1293: `SavedReplySaveDialog.test.ts` (new) checks the saved body has no ``, the note and its plural, and that a body without pasted images saves unchanged. `savedReplies.test.ts` saves a body with a marked image, a `blob:` image, a `cid:` image and an https image, then checks the stored row keeps only the https one. A second case checks, on create and on update, that a `cid:` src with a usable srcset keeps the image (srcset only), and that one whose srcset sanitizes away is dropped. `inlineImages.test.ts` covers `stripInlineImages`. - #1294: `loadMessagePart.test.ts` adds a device clock 10 minutes behind (the 50-minute reuse cap mints anew at 52 minutes, where the token's `exp` would still have allowed reuse), a token that has really expired by the server clock while the device still holds it inside the cap (the device clock was set back, so the proxy refuses and exactly one fresh mint answers it), a clock two hours ahead (must keep reusing), a refused reused URL after a server clock jump (one more mint, success), and a failure after that retry (gives up and forgets the URL). - #1301: `postboxSentPreview.test.ts` checks the resolved URL in the light and dark renderings, no `src` without a URL, an https URL under the frame CSP, and unchanged plain text. `PostboxPreviewAsSent.test.ts` (new) checks the iframe `srcdoc`. `PostboxComposerAnswerFrame.test.ts` checks the composer hands the preview its `inlineImageSources`. `inlineImages.test.ts` covers `resolveInlineImageSrcs`, including attribute escaping. Gates on the round-1 head, all exit 0: - apps/web full suite: 10260 tests passed - packages/shared full suite: 1804 tests passed - apps/api full suite (`--maxWorkers=4`): 1139 files passed, 6 skipped (14830 tests) - `turbo typecheck --filter=@owlat/web --filter=@owlat/shared` - `turbo typecheck --filter=@owlat/api` - `bun run --cwd apps/api lint` - `bun run ci:lint` - After merging main (#1307, api test helpers only): `bytes.test.ts`, `sealedBlobStream.test.ts` and `savedReplies.test.ts` pass. ## Screenshots Same mocked draft (a reopened draft with one pasted logo), same viewport and theme in both shots of each pair. **Preview as sent (#1301)** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wolvesdotink/owlat/55c90abc15363885304e71b68bf29516ab9c1e77/1293-preview-as-sent-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wolvesdotink/owlat/55c90abc15363885304e71b68bf29516ab9c1e77/1293-preview-as-sent-after.png) | **Save as reply (#1293)** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wolvesdotink/owlat/55c90abc15363885304e71b68bf29516ab9c1e77/1293-save-as-reply-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wolvesdotink/owlat/55c90abc15363885304e71b68bf29516ab9c1e77/1293-save-as-reply-after.png) | #1294 has no visual change.

author: avranu
body:
Closes five of the six rows the N30 third pass left under "Unhandled". The sixth, the smart-list resync, is #254, stacked on this one, so merge this first.

## Changes

**`resolve_deferred_pin_locations` has `max_retries=None`: fixed.**
- `max_retries` is now `_DEFERRED_MAX_RETRIES`: the two-day deadline divided by the shortest gap between retries, which is Google's fixed 65 s wait (now `_GOOGLE_RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_SECONDS`). Rounded up, that is 2,659.
- A batch that keeps resolving a cid or two resets to that shortest gap, so the bound never ends a batch the deadline would keep alive.
- The bound only ends a batch whose `started_at` the deadline cannot read. `_deferred_deadline_passed` treats an unparseable stamp as "not expired", and the task re-sends whatever stamp it was given, so such a batch used to retry for ever.
- At the bound the task takes the deadline's give-up path: `PinImportFailure` rows plus a notification. It does not call `retry()`, which Celery would refuse with `MaxRetriesExceededError`, losing the pins.
- The signature and positional argument order are unchanged.
- The review also found a pre-existing bug in that give-up path: it recorded every cid as failed, including ones the same final round had resolved. Those are now placed first, and only the still-pending ones fail (0cd954fde).

**Wikipedia-cache hook seeds one article per pin: fixed already.** 40d418c1d (P181, 2026-10-01) removed the per-pin loop two days after the third pass.
- The hook makes no outbound request; it reads the cached row.
- The wiki cover step is a no-op until a wiki cover has an owner (the TODO in `_store_cover_from_url`).
- A bulk import never runs the per-pin prefetch.
- `test_wikipedia_cache_hook_cost.py` pins this down:
  - the same query count with 1 or 25 pins on the location;
  - no pin is seeded or linked;
  - any HTTP request fails the test, with egress opened. I checked this by locally giving a wiki cover an owner, which made all four tests fail.

**Calendar export makes one Google request per activity: not batched; filed as P334.**
- Why not batch:
  - Google counts every request inside a batch against quota.
  - The limiter reserves one slot per HTTP request, so a batch would either under-count or need multi-slot reservations the limiter does not have.
  - The gateway is plain `requests`, so batching means hand-built `multipart/mixed` requests and parsing.
  - A batch whose response is lost leaves every event in it without a link row, so the retry duplicates them all.
- Measuring it against the real limiter found a real defect, filed as P334. A trip with 30 or more scheduled activities can never finish an export under the site-wide `google_calendar` budget of 30 a minute. Each attempt sends 30 calls, re-patching the same first 29 activities. With 40 activities, four attempts sent 120 requests and the last 11 activities were never written.
- The options in P334 involve policy values, so they are Jess's call.

**Retention: `ReputationEvent`/`WikiEdit` (Batch 30) and trivia questions (Batch 31).** Recorded under "Kept" as "Jess, 2026-10-06: kept indefinitely; no prune task". No code. No `docs/PROBLEMS.md` or N31 entry listed either row as awaiting her.

## Tests
`UL_TEST_DB_NAME=test_ul_grok bash bin/host_pytest.sh --reuse-db` on:
- `test_deferred_lookup_retry_window.py` (new `DeferredLookupRetryBoundTests`, which drive Celery's real `retry()` through `.apply(retries=...)`)
- the six other `resolve_deferred_pin_locations` test files
- `test_wikipedia_cache_hook_cost.py` (new)
- `test_cross_user_pin_isolation.py`

All pass: 85 and 19. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy src/urbanlens` are clean. `bin/check_docs_index.py` reports only the existing N43 drift.

## Review
One adversarial review found two real problems, both fixed here: the Wikipedia hook's cover claim, and the pre-existing give-up ordering. It confirmed:
- the off-by-one against Celery's `retries > max_retries` check;
- the 65 s shortest gap;
- the deadline-before-bound ordering for honest stamps;
- every number in P334.

It could not verify the retention rulings from the repo. They came from Jess through the coordinating session.

author: lethabarb
body:
S00.02.03, Deploy to test from main.

## What this adds
`deploy.yml` runs when CI completes successfully on a push to `main`. It has one job in the `test` environment, runs one deploy at a time, does no checkout and no build, and uses only the `grow2notes` artifact from the triggering CI run. It runs design.md §10.4 steps 1 to 8:

1. `azure/login` with OIDC from the environment's secrets (D65).
2. `az deployment group what-if`, then `create`, with CI's `main.json` and `test.parameters.json`. The SQL admin group and alert email come from secrets as overrides, and `create` prints only errors. The app identity's IDs are masked first.
3. The UTC time, written to the job summary as the point-in-time restore target, with the restore command.
4. Sign in again, then the runner's IPv4 address as a firewall rule named `deploy-<run id>-<attempt>`. Signing in again avoids AADSTS700024, because the GitHub OIDC token expires after 5 minutes.
5. `efbundle` with `Active Directory Default`, signed in as the deployment identity (`db_owner`).
6. Rule removal in an `always()` step whenever step 4 started.

author: zmaril
body:
run-make was not run before because rustdoc failed to build, and the docs gave the wrong reason. They blamed Cargo's per-crate build directories. The real cause is in the runtime:

- Instrumenting `tempfile` makes 61 compiler crates depend on `mirth_runtime`.
- rustdoc is compiled by bootstrap without the wrapper, so it couldn't find the runtime: `can't find crate for mirth_runtime which rustc_abi depends on`.
- Copying the runtime into the stage 0 sysroot doesn't help, because bootstrap re-syncs that directory.

**Fix:**
- `build.sh` and `suites.sh` pass `-L dependency=<runtime dir>` in both `RUSTFLAGS_BOOTSTRAP` and `RUSTFLAGS_NOT_BOOTSTRAP`. At this commit the compiler and rustdoc get the second.
- The flags must be identical in every `x.py` run. Otherwise Cargo recompiles the compiler, this time without the wrapper. `HACKING.md` records this.
- `suites.sh` runs 46 run-make tests: the ones on metadata, crate loading, incremental and emitted files. It uses `--force-rerun`, and a watchdog kills and names test compiles that hang for more than 5 minutes.

**Results** (`docs/edits/*.txt` regenerated):

| | incremental | ui | run-make |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | 180 pass | 532 pass | 46 pass |
| 1 write in place | pass | pass | pass |
| 2 drop deprecation | pass | 5 fail | pass |
| 3 env var | pass | pass | pass |
| 4 HashMap | pass | pass | pass |
| 5 eager decode | 6 hang | 4 hang | 2 hang |
| 6 untracked extern | 9 fail | pass | pass |
| 7 keep tempdir | pass | pass | pass |

run-make catches nothing the other suites missed. The score is still mirth 7/7 and rustc's tests 3/7. Edits 1 and 7 change how the `.rmeta` is published. run-make checks the files that come out, not how they were written.

`report.md`, `results.md` and `plan.md` are corrected. Edit 5's hung-test list had two blank entries, because run-make compiles use relative paths. I filled those two names in by hand. The watchdog now reads them from the process's working directory.

author: jacksonfergusondev
body:
## Summary and motivation

`yaml_ast._load` read every YAML document twice: `codec.compose(content)` to check the bounds and tags, then `codec.load(content)` to build the document, which parses the same text again. The check and the build now share one parse: the document is built from the tree that was already composed and checked.

A no-op `sync` on a library scaffold reads 20 YAML documents, so this halves the YAML work:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ruamel` time in `sync` (compose + load) | 0.109s (0.045 + 0.050) | 0.058s (0.045 + 0) |
| `sync` total | 0.665s | 0.607s |

Warm cache, macOS arm64, medians of nine runs per side, alternating old and new code on the same project.

## Planning and key decisions

This follows from profiling `sync`, `status` and `diff` on a project that has nothing to do. A first `cProfile` pass overstated the parser cost, so the numbers above come from wall-clock timers on every `ruamel` entry point. Those showed `compose` and `load` taking almost the same time, which is what exposed the double parse.

**Rejected: sharing parses between callers with a copy.** The plan also called for deduping the repeat parses, since the same text reaches `_load` from both `decode_yaml_baseline` and `reconcile_yaml`. Copying a parsed document is about six times cheaper than parsing it again (1.3ms against 8ms), so a cache of copies looked attractive. It breaks the merge-key cases. ruamel's `CommentedMap.copy_attributes` calls `copy.deepcopy(getattr(self, a, memo))`, so the `memo` goes to `getattr` and not to `deepcopy`. A copied document therefore gets its own copy of every merge target, and the shared-structure detection stops seeing that the merged mapping and the anchored mapping are one object. Two existing tests caught it.

Working around that would mean skipping the cache for documents with merge keys and trusting ruamel's copy fidelity in an engine whose promise is non-destructive edits, all for roughly 25ms (each repeat parse is already half its old cost). I left it out. The decode path already memoizes its plain values.

## Notes for review

- The bounds, node count, depth, tag and key checks still run on the composed tree before any document is built, so nothing changes about what is rejected or when.
- `_load` now uses one codec for compose and construct. The old code used two, which also ran the `%YAML` version check on a different codec than the one that built the document.
- Two new tests: one composes once and never calls `load`, the other builds a document with anchors, a merge key, quotes and comments, checks that the merge target and the alias are the same object as the anchored mapping, and compares its round-trip dump with a plain `load`'s.
- Spiked beforehand on 20 real documents (workflows, pre-commit, readthedocs, plus anchor and `%YAML` cases): identical dumps, and parse time of the largest drops from 16.3ms to 8.2ms.

## Not in this PR

`tomlkit` is still about 0.077s of a no-op `sync` (36 parses over 17 distinct documents, plus `dumps`). I did not touch it. The TOML documents are mutable too, so the same copy question applies, and I want its own measurement first.

## Test plan

- [x] Full suite (pre-push `pytest`), docs build and snapshot drift
- [x] `tests/test_yaml_ast.py`, including the merge-key and shared-anchor cases
- [x] Before/after timings, as above

author: excavador
body:
The AWS CLI switches \`aws s3 cp\` to a multipart upload above 8MB. Into an SSE-KMS bucket a multipart upload also needs \`kms:Decrypt\` on the key (a single PUT needs only \`kms:GenerateDataKey\`), so a write-only backup role started failing with \`AccessDenied\` on \`UploadPart\` once a snapshot crossed 8MB. Both halves:

- **Chart**: new \`snapshot.upload.s3.multipartThreshold\` (default \`1GB\`; empty keeps the CLI's default), written into the CLI config file the S3 preset already supports (\`AWS_CONFIG_FILE\`), alongside \`addressing_style\` when \`pathStyle\` is on. Only the upload sets it.
- **awsserver.SnapshotPolicy**: \`kms:Decrypt\` on the backup key, so a snapshot above the threshold does not fail either. Still no \`s3:GetObject\`; the backup key policy already admits the writer for Decrypt.

author: homeopsrenovate[bot]
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [ghcr.io/lexfrei/charts/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller) | major | `4.0.0` → `5.0.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller (ghcr.io/lexfrei/charts/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller)</summary>

### [`v5.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/releases/tag/v5.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/compare/v4.0.0...v5.0.0)

#### Highlights

- Listener isolation: a request is answered only by routes on the most specific listener that matches its host ([#​947](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/947)).
- HTTPRoute `retry` is implemented, on the Experimental channel ([#​952](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/952)).
- Route matches are ranked one match at a time, in the order the Gateway API lists ([#​973](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/973)).
- Route status no longer depends on the Cloudflare tunnel document. The document holds one rule per hostname, has no size cap, and is cached between syncs ([#​966](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/966), [#​967](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/967)).
- Backend TLS fails closed when the controller cannot read what decides it ([#​981](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/981)), and invalid backends answer the statuses the spec requires, gRPC `UNAVAILABLE` included ([#​974](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/974), [#​977](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/977)).
- Most status and routing fixes in this release come from a spec audit against Gateway API v1.6.2 ([#​986](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/986)).

#### Security

##### Backend TLS could be skipped while BackendTLSPolicies could not be read ([#​981](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/981))

If the controller could not list the BackendTLSPolicies in a namespace, it treated every backend there as having no policy and pushed plaintext config for them. A backend whose policy required authenticated TLS was then dialed without TLS until a later sync could list the policies again. This could happen on any read error other than not-found. The same applied to a `sectionName`-scoped policy when the Service it targets could not be read.

The `appProtocol` lookup had the same flaw. If the controller could not read a backend Service, for any reason other than not-found, it treated the Service as declaring no `appProtocol`. A backend marked `appProtocol: https` or `kubernetes.io/wss` with no BackendTLSPolicy, which should fail closed, was sent the request in plaintext, headers and body included, to its TLS port.

`RequestMirror` destinations had the same plaintext window. When a `sectionName`-scoped policy targeted a Service the controller cache had not seen yet, typically one just created, the policy was skipped and the mirrored request went out in plaintext.

Affected: v3.0.0 through v4.0.0.

Fixed: while any of these reads fails, the controller holds back that data plane's config push. Replicas keep their last accepted config, and the sync is retried every 15 seconds. Other planes are unaffected. A held push logs `proxy config not pushed` and counts in `cftunnel_sync_errors_total{error_type="proxy_push"}`. A `sectionName`-scoped policy on a Service the controller has not seen yet applies to every port of that Service until the Service shows up.

##### Client certificate validation was accepted but never enforced ([#​968](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/968))

A Gateway that set `spec.tls.frontend` was reported `Accepted=True` and `Programmed=True`, and its routes were served, but no client certificate was ever validated: TLS terminates at the Cloudflare edge, and the proxy never sees a client certificate. Clients without a certificate could reach backends the operator believed were protected by mTLS.

Affected: v3.0.0 through v4.0.0.

Fixed: such a Gateway is refused with `Accepted=False` and reason `Invalid`, and serves no routes. To require client certificates, enforce them at the Cloudflare edge with Cloudflare's mTLS or Access policies.

#### Breaking changes

v5 changes what is served in several places where v4 did not follow the spec. The chart values, CRDs, RBAC, the Kubernetes floor and the Gateway API bundle are the same as in v4.0.0. The [upgrade guide](https://cf.k8s.lex.la/latest/upgrading/v4-to-v5/) says who each change reaches, how to check, and what to do. Read it before `helm upgrade`.

- [Listener isolation](https://cf.k8s.lex.la/latest/upgrading/v4-to-v5/#breaking-listener-isolation): a route on a wildcard or hostname-less listener stops answering hostnames a more specific listener of the same Gateway owns ([#​947](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/947)).
- [A Gateway that sets `spec.tls.frontend` is refused](https://cf.k8s.lex.la/latest/upgrading/v4-to-v5/#breaking-a-gateway-that-sets-spectlsfrontend-is-refused) and its dedicated data plane is removed ([#​968](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/968), [#​979](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/979)).
- [`spec.addresses`](https://cf.k8s.lex.la/latest/upgrading/v4-to-v5/#breaking-specaddresses-other-than-the-tunnel-hostname): an `IPAddress`, `NamedAddress` or untyped entry refuses the Gateway with `UnsupportedAddress`; a Hostname other than the tunnel CNAME gives `Programmed=False` with `AddressNotUsable` ([#​979](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/979)).
- [`group: ""` in `allowedRoutes.kinds`](https://cf.k8s.lex.la/latest/upgrading/v4-to-v5/#breaking-group-in-allowedrouteskinds-names-the-core-group) names the core group and admits no route kind ([#​979](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/979)).
- [Route matches are ranked one match at a time](https://cf.k8s.lex.la/latest/upgrading/v4-to-v5/#breaking-route-matches-are-ranked-one-match-at-a-time): a request can be served by a different rule, and `RouteShadowed` can move to the other route of a pair ([#​973](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/973)).
- [An empty GRPCRoute match](https://cf.k8s.lex.la/latest/upgrading/v4-to-v5/#breaking-an-empty-grpcroute-match-matches-everything) next to specific matches now matches everything on the rule's hostnames ([#​980](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/980)).
- [Redirect ports](https://cf.k8s.lex.la/latest/upgrading/v4-to-v5/#breaking-redirect-ports): a redirect without `scheme` and `port` carries the listener port when the edge serves it (8080, for example), and `Location` leaves out `:80` for `http` and `:443` for `https` ([#​948](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/948), [#​975](https://redirect.github.com/lexfrei/cloudflare-tunnel-gateway-controller/issues/975)).
- [`RequestRedirect` and `URLRewrite` in different filter lists](https://cf.k8s.lex.la/latest/upgrading/v4-to-v5/#breaking-requestredirect-and-urlrewrite-in-different-filter-lists) of one rule are refused with `IncompatibleFilters` ([#​975](https://redirect.github.com/

author: rodchristiansen
body:
Every release now publishes a complete, unsigned `Crypt-<version>.pkg` beside `checkin` and the Managed Encryption Escrow package, so a deployment pipeline can sign and ship the whole client as a drop-in for the upstream package.

## What the package installs

Same paths as the upstream 5.0.2 package:

- `/Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins/Crypt.bundle`, the authorisation plugin (universal)
- `/Library/Crypt/checkin`, the Swift client (universal), which the Managed Encryption Escrow helper runs
- `/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.grahamgilbert.crypt.plist`
- `/private/etc/newsyslog.d/crypt.conf`
- preinstall and postinstall. The postinstall creates the log folder and runs `checkin auth-mechs install`.

The package identifier is `com.grahamgilbert.Crypt`, and `postinstall-action` is restart, as upstream.

## Versioning

- The plugin's `CFBundleVersion` is the tag's digits (`v2026.10.06.1800` becomes `202610061800`), so it always sorts above upstream's commit-count build numbers (279 for 5.0.2).
- The project's build phase only stamps the source `Info.plist`, which the build has already copied, so the script also stamps the built bundle directly.
- The component plist turns off `BundleIsVersionChecked` and `BundleIsRelocatable`.
- The release fails if the build number doesn't reach the package's `PackageInfo`.
- The Managed Encryption Escrow package now takes its version from the tag too.

## Signing

Everything in the package is ad hoc signed or unsigned. The deploying pipeline signs innermost first: the plugin bundle, then `checkin`, then the package.

## Verified

- `swift test`: 32 tests pass.
- Built locally with `Package/build-unsigned-pkg.sh 2026.10.06.1800 202610061800`. The payload matches upstream 5.0.2's paths. It drops the embedded Swift runtime dylibs, since the deployment target is 13.5.
- Installed on a clean macOS 26.6 VM: the `Crypt:Check,privileged` mechanism was registered in `system.login.console`, `checkin verify` exited 0 and reported the mechanisms as installed, and the bundle carried build 202610061800.
- Installed over upstream 5.0.2 (bundle 279): the bundle was replaced with 202610061800, and the upstream Frameworks folder was gone.
- Uninstalled afterwards: the mechanisms were removed, the files deleted and the receipt forgotten.

## Not covered

- A real tag run on GitHub Actions.
- A local build leaves AppleDouble entries in the payload when files carry a provenance attribute; a CI build shouldn't.

author: tin-berri
body:
A healthy session could stop on its fourth mid-turn correction, even when tools completed successfully between corrections. Hermes counted cancelled requests across the entire turn, and its finalizer could hide the real cause behind “a tool result was still pending.”

Backport the runtime hunks of [NousResearch/hermes-agent@40aa839](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/40aa83919e999082badd1df6fafad8e85691b171) by FroRaut into the existing Hermes pin. A completed model response resets the restart counter; consecutive cancellations and fallback rebuilds remain bounded. Preserve explicit stop reasons and save an accepted but unapplied correction for an explicit resume, without automatically restarting failed/incomplete turns.

The patches install during image creation and before Hermes starts in restored snapshots. Both runners refresh the installer and patch files. Installation is idempotent and rejects incompatible sources before any patch is applied or agent tool runs. Active turns receive the change on their next sandbox launch after deployment.

Validation:

- **104 focused checks passed**, covering native steering, model cancellation, durable receipts, checkpointing, goal continuation, and both runners.
- **40 final demo checks passed** after adding resume-history verification. The real pinned runtime reproduces the old failure at correction four; the patched runtime incorporates six corrections, writes seven files exactly once, and produces one final answer without `continue`.
- Verified provider retry limits, explicit Stop, consecutive cancellation/fallback limits, specific stop reasons, idempotent patch installation, rejection of incompatible snapshots, and preservation of the final correction through resume.
- Model replies/cancellations are scripted; Hermes, Moyai steering, file tools, and conversation processing are real. No production deployment or live provider/Slack requests.

Local demo: set `HERMES_TEST_SOURCE` and `HERMES_TEST_PYTHON`, then run `uv run python scripts/steering_runtime_demo.py` and open `http://127.0.0.1:8830`. The page runs the actual regression suite on click. A 38-second recording and screenshot were captured in the Codex task. Setup and patch maintenance notes are in `sandbox/HERMES_PATCHES.md`.

author: aceguru-mjh
body:
## 事故复盘（2026-10-06，用户报告「软件的更新有问题」）

**现象**：v1.4.7.25 已发布到 Release 仓库（25 个资产齐全），但 App 检查更新永远提示已是最新 —— 全体客户端断更。

**根因链**（run [37547956763](https://github.com/AceGuru-mjh/Android-Guru-Agent/actions/runs/37547956763) 日志定位）：

1. `Mirror Release to dev repository` 步骤的 `files:` 同时携带 `dist/*.apk` 通配与显式 `dist/SHA256SUMS.apk` —— **SHA256SUMS.apk 被并行上传两次**，第二次撞 `404 Not Found`（update-a-release-asset），Mirror 步骤失败；
2. `Commit version.json to release repo main branch` 排在 Mirror **之后**且无容错 —— Mirror 一倒，清单提交被跳过 → main 分支 `version.json` 卡在 v1.4.7.24 → **客户端全体收不到新版本**；
3. 次生事故：清单不落位 → 下一次发布（v1.4.7.26）的 resolve 读到旧 versionCode 71 → **.25/.26 撞同一 versionCode 72** → .25 用户对 .26 永远判「已是最新」。

## 四项修复

| # | 修复 | 内容 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mirror files 去重 | `dist/*.apk` + `dist/version.json`（SHA256SUMS.apk 由通配命中，不再重复携带） |
| 2 | 步骤重排 | 清单提交前置于主仓库镜像 —— 客户端更新入口是关键路径，展示位殿后 |
| 3 | Mirror 容错 | `continue-on-error: true`（镜像失败仅告警，绝不再连累发布） |
| 4 | resolve 防撞号 | `LAST_VCODE` 对账 `releases/latest` 的 version.json 资产，取 max —— 清单滞后时不再撞号 |

## 清单提交步骤强化

- **索引幂等合并**替代盲覆盖：远端被 backfill/hotfix/人工恢复推进时不丢边（只重放指向本版 tag 的边，幂等键 `variant|fromTag|toTag`）；
- **push 三次重试**：被拒时重拉远端重放（防 backfill/hotfix 竞态）；
- **无变更感知**：幂等重跑不产生空提交。

## 跨版本直更（用户需求确认已达成）

- CI 每版发布生成 **10 基底 × 2 变体 = 20 个补丁**（语义序窗口，公开仓库 Actions 免费额度支撑）；
- 客户端 `PatchIndex.resolveChain` BFS 最短路径：跨度 ≤10 版本必有**单跳直达边**（1 个补丁直接到最新），更老版本自动链式，断链回退全量；
- 本次修复保证的是这条链路的**可靠性** —— 之前坏在清单不落位，直更边生成了客户端也看不到。

## 发布仓库侧恢复（已手工完成，随本 PR 说明）

- main `version.json` → v1.4.7.26（versionCode 72）✓（.26 run 自身成功提交）
- main `patches.json` → 357 条（补入 .25 的 20 条多基底边，避免老版本用户走 10+ 跳链）✓
- 本 PR 合并将触发 v1.4.7.**27**（versionCode **73**）—— 解救被撞号卡住的 v1.4.7.25 用户（72 → 73 判定为有更新）

## 验证

- `scripts/check_workflow_yaml.py` 8 个工作流全过（EXIT=0）
- YAML 解析 / 两个改动 run 块 `bash -n` 语法检查通过
- 步骤顺序断言：Commit version.json(17) < Mirror(18)，Mirror 带 continue-on-error
- 合并脚本端到端测试：远端 357（含 .25 边）+ 本版 20 = 377 条，**不丢边 / 无重复 / latestTag 正确**

author: bbthorson
body:
> ⚠️ **Stacked on #613. Merge #613 first.** This branch merges #613's branch, so the diff shows #613's changes until it lands. Once it does, the `WHY.planDate` ledger lines are gone and `bp-plan-created-no-period` expects the TypeScript to miss.

## Why

A Stage-8 criterion lives in four places, and `check:measures` only ties the FSH names to the TypeScript. Nothing compared what the CQL and `evaluateMeasure()` actually **compute**. A planted 7→8-day change to the follow-up window in `measures.ts` passed every gate and every test.

## What

- **`tests/cql/cqlMeasureEngine.ts`** translates the CQL in-process with `@cqframework/cql` 5.4.0, the translator the IG Publisher bundles, using the same default options. It then executes the result with `cql-execution` + `cql-exec-fhir`.
  - FHIRHelpers 4.0.1 and the FHIR model info come from `~/.fhir/packages/fhir.cqf.common#4.0.1`, which SUSHI downloads. If the package is missing, the test fails with instructions rather than skipping.
  - The System model info is vendored from the translator's v5.4.0 tag, because the JS build registers no default providers.
- **`tests/cql/boundaryPatients.ts`** adds 36 synthetic patients that sit on window edges: day 7/8, 24h/25h, 48h/49h, and each reassessment interval ±1 day. It also adds one patient per record shape the two engines might read differently. Each patient states what the TypeScript is designed to answer, so a fixture that misses its edge fails as a fixture.
- **`tests/measuresCqlParity.test.ts`** compares every population of every Measure group, patient by patient. It also fails if:
  - a CQL definition the Measures reference is missing,
  - a CQL result is not true/false/null,
  - any population is never true on either engine.

## Findings

Every window edge agrees. Eight root causes did not. The two that were the CQL's fault are fixed in this PR; the other six are recorded in `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES`. The ledger is exact both ways: a new divergence fails, and so does a line that has stopped diverging.

| Cause | Affected | Likely wrong side |
|---|---|---|
| Safety plan with no `period`: TypeScript falls back to `created` | **demo 001, 011** | undecided |
| Risk-level Observation with no profile claim: TypeScript accepts it by content | **demo 008, 009, 010** | CQL lags the TypeScript rule |
| Reassessment at 7d + 1h: CQL `days between` counts whole days and calls it on time | synthetic | undecided |
| Positive screen via interpretation `A` or tier only | synthetic | undecided |
| Pathway stage carried in `category` or derived from the form response | synthetic | undecided |
| Packet content item as the second coding: CQL read `coding[0]` only | synthetic | **CQL — fixed here**: it now reads every coding in the SPiER system |
| `psy` disposition under a local code system | synthetic | **CQL — fixed here**: it now requires HL7's discharge-disposition system |
| Counseling `performedPeriod` that runs past the episode end | synthetic | undecided |

Related, and tracked separately: the production CarePlan mapper writes neither `period` nor `created`. App-written safety plans therefore fail Measure 3 on both engines.

## Proved it can fail

Each of these was planted, watched go red, then reverted:

- TypeScript: 7→8 days, and 24→25 hours.
- CQL: 48→47 hours, `<=` → `<` on the reassessment comparison, and a renamed define.
- A CQL compile error fails the run (exit 1).
- A missing `fhir.cqf.common` package fails with an error naming the fix.
- A ledger line that no longer diverges fails.

## Also

- Docs updated: `docs/internals/measures.md`, the Measures section of CLAUDE.md, and the CQL and `measures.ts` headers.
- Fixed a stale `web/src/lib/measures.ts` path in the CQL header.
- New devDependencies, test-only and exact-pinned: `@cqframework/cql` 5.4.0, `cql-execution` 3.3.2, `cql-exec-fhir` 2.2.0.

`npm run verify` passes locally.

author: princeberenger
body:
Follow-up to #31999. `useActionRunner` closed the top detail after the Trakt request. If the user left that detail and opened another one while the request was in flight, the new detail closed.

The detail is now captured when the action starts and closed only if it is still the top view.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small UX fix in detail-stack closing logic with no auth or data-handling changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes detail navigation closing the wrong screen after list actions complete.
> 
> **`useActionRunner`** now calls **`captureTopDetail()`** when an action starts (when `onSuccess` is set) and runs that captured closer after the Trakt request succeeds, instead of always calling **`closeTopDetail()`** on whatever detail is topmost at finish time. If you opened a different detail while the request was in flight, that newer detail stays open; only the stale detail you started from closes when it is still the innermost view.
>

**Soul Army** (`scripts/army.gd`)

body:
Documents changes from microsoft/aspire#20571

``@sebastienros``

**Target branch**: Targeting `release/17.0` based on the source PR milestone `17.0`.

## Why

PR microsoft/aspire#20571 fixes Mongo Express failing to connect to a MongoDB server configured with `WithReplicaSet()` (single-member replica set). The single-member replica set advertises a `localhost:<port>` member address that assumes `directConnection=true`; Mongo Express previously connected via the individual `ME_CONFIG_MONGODB_SERVER`/`_PORT`/credential variables, which don't set `directConnection=true`, causing it to loop back to its own container and exit. The fix configures Mongo Express via the full connection string (`ME_CONFIG_MONGODB_URL`) in that case, and also makes Mongo Express wait for the MongoDB server to be healthy (not just for the TCP port) before starting, to avoid a startup race against replica-set primary election.

This is a behavior change to an already-documented experimental feature (`WithReplicaSet()` / `WithMongoExpress()`), so the docs needed an update to describe it.

## What changed

- `src/frontend/src/content/docs/integrations/databases/mongodb/mongodb-host.mdx`:
  - Noted that the Mongo Express resource now waits for the MongoDB server to report healthy before starting.
  - Added a note under "Add MongoDB Express resource" explaining that, for servers using the simple single-member replica set (`WithReplicaSet()`), Mongo Express is configured via `ME_CONFIG_MONGODB_URL` (the full connection string) instead of the individual `ME_CONFIG_MONGODB_SERVER`/`_PORT`/`_ADMINUSERNAME`/`_ADMINPASSWORD` variables, and why. Clarified that advanced `AddMongoDBReplicaSet(...).WithMember(...)` members are unaffected.

No new pages were created; this is a targeted update to the existing MongoDB hosting integration page.
