## Summary

Post-release production verification and a small asset fix for the GitHub Pages
invitation. This is **not a new product phase**: `docs/PHASES.md` is unchanged, no
`INV-011` is created, and `.ai/state` is untouched.

**GitHub Pages is the sole production hosting target.** No Vercel deployment is added
and no runtime dependency on Vercel exists.

## Root cause

The original defect — `https://ngowda759.github.io/Invitation/` serving the repository
`README.md` through Jekyll instead of the built invitation — had two causes:

1. **Pages published the repository tree, not an application build.** Pages was in the
   legacy "deploy from a branch" mode (`source: main:/`), so Jekyll rendered the repo
   root and, with no `index.md`, `README.md` became the site index.
2. **No application deployment existed.** `next.config.ts` was not a static export and
   no workflow built or published the app.

Both were already fixed in **PR #13**. GitHub Pages is now `build_type: "workflow"` and
the `Deploy to GitHub Pages` workflow publishes the Next.js static export from `out/`.

This PR **verifies** that deployment against the live URL and closes the one remaining
production asset gap the verification surfaced: the deployed document had **no app
icon**, so `/Invitation/favicon.ico` returned 404 and browser tabs showed a blank icon.

## Application correction

- **`src/app/icon.svg` (new)** — a branded diya app icon in the approved palette, using
  the Next.js `app/icon.svg` file convention. Next.js emits the `<link rel="icon">` tag
  and exports the asset, so it resolves under `/Invitation/` with no hard-coded path.
- **`tests/unit/deployment.test.mjs`** — guards that the app icon ships, so a blank tab
  icon cannot silently return.
- **`README.md`** — corrects the stale "Phase 1 — Foundation" status (the app is a
  released static export published to Pages).

## GitHub Pages correction

No change to the deployment architecture was needed — it is already correct and was
verified working:

- `next.config.ts` sets `output: "export"` with `basePath` read from `PAGES_BASE_PATH`
  (empty locally, `/Invitation` on Pages, supplied by `actions/configure-pages`). There
  is no `"/Invitation"` literal anywhere in `src/`.
- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` builds the export, uploads **only** `out/` as the
  Pages artifact, and deploys with `pages: write` / `id-token: write` / `contents: read`.
  It never publishes the repository root or documentation.

## Static export

The app is compatible with static hosting: a single `/` route, no API routes, no route
handlers, no server actions, no cookies and no runtime image optimization
(`images.unoptimized: true`). `next build` exports `/`, `/_not-found` and `/icon.svg`
as static output. No functionality was removed to make the export pass.

## Validation

Local run (Node 24.21.0, npm 11.19.1):

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run lint` | clean |
| `npm run typecheck` | clean |
| `npm test` | **164 unit tests passed** (14 files) |
| `npm run test:e2e` | **45 passed, 1 skipped** (mobile-only LCP/CLS budget) |
| `npm run build` | static export, `/` prerendered |
| `PAGES_BASE_PATH=/Invitation npm run build` | static export with `/Invitation`-prefixed assets |
| `node .ai/scripts/antislop.mjs` | **PASS** (0 error, 0 warning) |
| `node .ai/scripts/validate-loop-config.mjs` | consistent |
| Security | no `secrets.*` in CI/deploy; read-only permissions; CSP/noopener e2e pass |

The generated `out/` was served at `/Invitation/` and exercised with Playwright Chromium
on mobile (Pixel 7) and desktop: HTTP 200, one `h1`, 11 regions, no horizontal overflow,
programme anchor scrolled into view, **0 failed requests, 0 console errors**, and the app
icon served as `image/svg+xml`.

## Visual verification

The live URL was compared against the intended invitation experience:

- **Reference** (`weinviteu-for-athmiyageleyarabalaga.vercel.app`) is a WebGL 3D
  invitation for a *different* event (Athmiya Geleyara Balaga / Ganesha festival). It was
  used **only** as a visual benchmark: an immersive full-screen opening, a temple hero
  with event identity and CTAs, and a continuous scroll of programme/temple/location/
  share sections. No proprietary code or content was copied, and the app has no runtime

- **This app** matches that experience shape within the repository's honest-content
  scope: opening veil → full-screen hero with the event identity and both CTAs →
  Darshan / Festival / Programme / Guru Rayaru / Temple map / Seva / Gallery / Location /

- Live checks: invitation UI shows, no README/document page, CSS + JS + fonts load, hero
  and `#programme` work, temple experience sections present, mobile and desktop layouts

## Hosting

GitHub Pages is the sole production hosting target. Vercel is not used for deployment and
is not required at runtime.

## Autonomous loop

Unchanged and intact. The loop sits at its terminal `NEXT_PHASE` state for `INV-010` with

author: latand
body:
## Problem

A successor pipeline created on an existing pull request branch (`baseBranch` = the PR branch, delivery `{ branch: refs/heads/<that branch>, pr: N }`, delivery epoch 2) ran its stage, the agent pushed to that branch and reported pass, and settlement then failed with `adopting the stage branch: another pipeline owns the stage branch`. The lane parked in `needs_decision` until the seat skipped the stage by hand. This was seen on three lanes on 2026-10-07.

## Cause

`ownedByOther` in `src/lib/pipelines/stageBranch.ts` returned true for any other pipeline whose own `branch` had the stage branch's name. A PR branch opened by an earlier lane is that lane's `pipeline/<slug>-<id>` branch, so the completed previous lane kept "owning" it after its delivery claim was released.

## Fix

- A terminal lane (completed or closed) with no active delivery claim owns no branch for adoption.
- An active delivery claim still owns both the lane's branch and its delivery target, whatever the lane's state.
- A running or parked lane still refuses its branch, so the existing protection stays.
- `stageBranchOwnershipFence` also records the terminal flag, so a lane entering or leaving a terminal state during adoption is caught by the fence.

## Tests (`src/lib/pipelines/engine.test.ts`)

These were written failing-first. Before the fix, both settle cases failed with the production error.

- A successor after a **completed** lane settles end to end through `tickPipelines`: its state is running, the cursor is on `review`, `lastPassedCommit` is the stage head, and the PR branch is published at that head.
- A successor after a **closed** lane settles in the same way.
- A successor while the previous lane is **running** or **needs_decision** is still refused with `another pipeline owns the stage branch`.
- A terminal lane whose delivery claim is still active keeps owning its branch.
- The existing linked-worktree test `another pipeline owns the stage branch` is unchanged and still passes.

## Verification

- `src/lib/pipelines/engine.test.ts`: 757 pass, 0 fail. It ran in isolated state with private HOME, TMPDIR and `LLV_STATE_DIR`, and with `LLV_VIEWER_CONTROL_URL` on a closed port.
- `tsc --noEmit` passes, run through `scripts/gate-slot.sh`.
- eslint reports no errors on the changed files.
- The privacy-publication gate passes from the merge base with `--require-known-values --check-commits`.
- The pre-push hook passed.

author: shunnag
body:
## 概要

ライセンス上問題なく書き込める圧縮形式・方式・レベルを増やす。C ライブラリは同梱せず、encoder は純 Swift で実装した。足りない部分は Apple の Compression・libbz2 で補う。

### 追加した書き込み

**ZIP**
- 方式: method 12 (BZip2)、14 (LZMA)、95 (XZ)、98 (PPMd var.I rev.1)、93 (Zstandard)
- レベル: 方式ごとに選べる

**7z**
- coder: Copy、Deflate、BZip2、LZMA、PPMd (var.H)
- 7z の LZMA2 / LZMA にレベル 0〜9 と extreme
- ソリッド圧縮
- フィルタ: BCJ x86、ARM64、Delta

**LHA**
- -lh6- / -lh7-、レベル 1〜9、無圧縮 (-lh0-)

**tar 系**
- tar.lzma、tar.lz、tar.lz4、tar.br、tar.Z、tar.zst
- tar.xz にレベル 0〜9 と extreme

**単一ファイルの圧縮(作成のみ)**
- .gz、.bz2、.xz、.lzma、.lz、.lz4、.br、.Z、.zst

### 新しい encoder

| encoder | 実装 |
|---|---|
| LZMA1 / LZMA2 | 自前 |
| PPMd var.H / var.I | 自前 |
| Zstandard frame (RFC 8878) | 自前 |
| LZ4 frame | Apple の LZ4_RAW に、自前のフレームと XXH32 を組み合わせる |
| Brotli | Apple Compression(品質固定) |
| UNIX compress (LZW) | 自前 |

**出所**
- LZMA と PPMd は、パブリックドメインの LZMA SDK と 7-Zip C ソース(Ppmd7*、Ppmd8*)を参考にした。各ファイルにパブリックドメインの表記がある。
- 7-Zip の C++ 部分(LGPL)と lzip(GPL)のソースは読んでいない。lzip は互換性確認の検証用ツールとしてだけ使った。

### 高速化(f273d34 以降の 25 コミット)

- **encoder**: LZMA(level 1 で約 2 倍、level 3 で 3〜4 倍、既定 level は xz と同程度)、PPMd(約 2 倍)、zstd(L1 で 2〜3 倍、出力 +0.12% 以内)。
- **writer の複数 core 化**: ZIP / 7z / LHA で項目・folder・member を並列に圧縮する。出力順と byte は 1 thread と同じ。入力の保持量は上限を設け、大きい出力は disk spool に逃がす。
- **試験**: 大入力の `…FullSize` 14 件を debug suite では opt-in にし、CI では release build で実行する。CI の時間上限は 240 分。
- Mac mini M4 の交互比較(release、best-of-5、`Documentation/verification/2026-10-08-integrated-mini-ab.md`)で、256 MiB の混在入力を t=12 で圧縮したときの元の版比は次のとおり。

| 方式 | 元の版 → この PR | 倍率 |
|---|---|---:|
| ZIP Zstd | 1.65 → 0.15 秒 | 11.2 |
| ZIP PPMd | 29.2 → 6.0 秒 | 4.8 |
| 7z PPMd solid | 26.1 → 6.6 秒 | 4.0 |
| ZIP XZ | 19.3 → 4.9 秒 | 3.9 |
| LHA LH7 | 3.76 → 1.00 秒 | 3.7 |
| ZIP LZMA | 27.9 → 8.0 秒 | 3.5 |
| 7z LZMA solid | 26.3 → 8.8 秒 | 3.0 |
| ZIP BZip2 / 7z LZMA2 solid | 20.4 / 16.8 → 8.1 / 6.7 秒 | 2.5 |

元の版の複製との揺れは ±2%。ZIP Zstd 以外の出力 byte は元の版と同じ。残る退行は LHA の 10 MiB + 小 file 128 個を t ≥ 10 で圧縮したときの 3〜5%(約 1.5 ms)。

### 実行環境と CI

- ビルドは Xcode 27 / Swift 6.4 以上だけをサポートする。Swift 6.3.3 の `-O` は `TaskLocal<関数型?>` の `withValue` を誤コンパイルし、release で EXC_BAD_ACCESS になるため(2026-10-08 に確認)。
- 動作環境は macOS 26 以上のまま。CI は `xcode-27` で debug 全体スイートと release `…FullSize` を実行し、さらに Xcode 27 でビルドしたテストを `macos-26` に運んでコンパイルせずに同じ試験を行う(Xcode 26 の system xctest は Xcode 27 のテストを読み込めないため、Xcode 27 の xctest を同梱する)。

### 制限

- Brotli と LZ4 のレベルは固定。
- zstd の書き込み速度は 1 thread で CLI 比 L1 約 40〜62%(M4 Max で 315〜355 MB/s)。サイズは目標内。
- ZIP の method 12/14/93/95/98 は macOS のアーカイブユーティリティで開けないため、既定は Deflate のまま。

## 検証

- Mac mini M4(macOS 27.2 / Xcode 27.0)で b93420f の debug 全体スイートを実行し、785 テスト・42 スキップ・失敗 0 件(41.6 分)。release の `…FullSize` 14 件も成功(127 秒)。
- GitHub Actions(run 37707708543)の macOS 26.6.2 で、Xcode 27 でビルドしたテストを実行し、debug 785 テスト・42 スキップ・失敗 0 件、release `…FullSize` 14 件も成功。
- 同じ GyoshukuKit で KaitoFinder PR #12(3480cb3)の全体スイートが 1742 テスト・33 スキップ・失敗 0 件。
- 7zz、xz、bzip2、lha-unix、lz4、brotli、compress、zstd、lzip を検証用ツールに使い、相互に展開できることを確かめた。
- LZMA L6 の書き込み速度は xz -6 -T1 比 82〜84%、サイズは -0.03〜-0.17%。

KaitoFinder 側の対応は PR #12。この PR のマージ後にマージする。

author: matiusjbg
body:
## Qué cambia

Exige comprobación de **pertenencia** (no solo de rol) en los endpoints que el inventario E3-01 marcó sin ella: `PATCH /hour-logs/:id/review` pasa a rechazar con **403** a cualquier tutor que no sea el asignado al placement, y se aplica el mismo criterio a `GET /offers/:offerId/applications`, `PATCH /applications/:id/decide`, `POST /offers`, `PATCH /offers/:id/publish`, `PATCH /offers/:id/close` y `GET /offers/:id` (borradores).

## Por qué

`PATCH /hour-logs/:id/review` solo exigía rol `TUTOR`, así que **cualquier tutor podía aprobar o rechazar horas de una práctica que no supervisa**: el `curl` del hallazgo 1 de `docs/inventario-acceso.md` (E3-01) devolvía `HTTP 200` y dejaba la hora `APPROVED` con el `reviewedById` del tutor equivocado. Eso vacía de sentido el acta de acreditación.

El mismo patrón (guard de rol sin chequeo de pertenencia) estaba en otros cuatro hallazgos del inventario, así que el arreglo se aplica de forma consistente:

| Hallazgo | Endpoint(s) | Antes | Ahora |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `PATCH /hour-logs/:id/review` | 200 a cualquier tutor | 403 si no es el tutor asignado |
| 2 | `GET /offers/:offerId/applications` | 200 a cualquier empresa | 403 si la oferta no es de su empresa |
| 3 | `PATCH /applications/:id/decide` | 200 a cualquier empresa | 403 si la oferta no es de su empresa |
| 4 | `POST /offers`, `PATCH /offers/:id/publish`, `PATCH /offers/:id/close` | 200/201 suplantando a otra empresa | 403 |
| 5 | `GET /offers/:id` | 200 viendo borradores ajenos | 403 si el borrador no es de su empresa |

Closes los hallazgos 1–5 de `docs/inventario-acceso.md` (E3-01). *(Si esta tarea tiene un issue propio, reemplazar por `Closes #NN`.)*

La coordinación **conserva sus permisos**: es el único rol global del dominio, así que el helper `assertOwnership` la deja pasar siempre, y los `@Roles(...)` de cada endpoint no se modifican.

## Deuda técnica

- [ ] Este PR **paga** deuda de `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` (indica cuál, ver KNOWN_ISSUES.md)
- [x] Este PR **no toca** deuda existente
- [ ] Este PR **introduce** deuda a propósito (justifícala)

No paga ni introduce deuda de `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`. Aclaraciones de transparencia:

- **D-02** (`HourLogService` god service) se mantiene: el chequeo nuevo vive donde ya vivía `assertPlacementAccess`. No se aprovechó para separar el servicio.
- **D-04** (`listByOffer` con N+1) sigue igual: el PR solo añade la comprobación de dueño antes de listar, no optimiza la consulta.

## Cómo probarlo

```bash
git fetch origin
git checkout fix/E3-01-aprobar-horas-practica-ajena

pnpm install
docker compose up -d
pnpm db:deploy
pnpm db:seed
pnpm test        # specs nuevos: hour-log.service.spec, offer.service.spec, application.service.spec, common/ownership.spec

# con el backend arriba (pnpm dev):
T1=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"tutor1@miyura.com","password":"yura1234"}' | jq -r .accessToken)
T0=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"tutor0@miyura.com","password":"yura1234"}' | jq -r .accessToken)

# 1) DENEGADO — antes 200, ahora debe ser 403 (hour-log 16 = placement 1, tutorizado por tutor0)
curl -i -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/api/hour-logs/16/review \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $T1" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"status":"APPROVED"}'

# 2) PERMITIDO — el tutor asignado sigue pudiendo (200)
curl -i -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/api/hour-logs/16/review \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $T0" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"status":"APPROVED"}'

# 3) Mismo criterio en los otros hallazgos (antes 200, ahora 403)
E1=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"empresa1@miyura.com","password":"yura1234"}' | jq -r .accessToken)
curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/offers/1/applications -H "Authorization: Bearer $E1"   # oferta de empresa0
```

Los ids (`hour-log 16`, `offer 1`) son los del seed usados en el inventario; si tu base ya se movió, elige cualquier hora `SUBMITTED` de un placement cuyo `tutorId` sea otro.

## Checklist

- [ ] Los tests pasan en local (`pnpm test`)
- [x] Agregué tests para el comportamiento nuevo
- [x] El PR apunta a `develop`, no a `main`
- [x] El PR tiene menos de 400 líneas de diff *(10 archivos, +323/−46 = 369)*

author: mobeenabdullah
huntharo
body:
During OS power-off, Chromium helpers can be terminated while the browser process remains alive, causing fatal GPU restart attempts. Port the shutdown notification fix from [PwrGit #421](https://github.com/pwrdrvr/PwrGit/pull/421) into PwrAgent's existing quit and resource cleanup path.

Register the Linux/macOS `powerMonitor.shutdown` listener immediately after app-ready, before asynchronous startup. Retain Electron's OS shutdown delay with `preventDefault()`, bypass the interactive running-thread confirmation, and enter normal `app.quit()` cleanup. A three-second `exit(0)` fallback bounds stalled resource or diagnostics cleanup; completed quit cancels it. Repeated notifications retain the delay without restarting cleanup or resetting the deadline.

Electron's generated callback type omits the documented event, so the listener accepts an optional event. See the [Electron shutdown API](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/power-monitor#event-shutdown-linux-macos).

Validation on current main, run sequentially:

- 144 targeted tests passed across system shutdown, main-process lifecycle, quit manager, quit reentry, and shutdown barriers. New coverage includes Linux/macOS shutdown during pending CPU-profiler startup, cleanup without confirmation, repeated notifications, normal-quit fallback cancellation, and the three-second deadline.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 pnpm lint` passed, including ESLint, typechecking, storage/SQL/color checks, dependency licenses, and boundaries. The larger heap accommodates this machine's default Node heap limit.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 pnpm build` passed, including the main bundle boundary check.
- Hidden-window native quit reentry probe passed all 12 cases on Electron 44.4.5.
- Temporary built-app probes passed simulated shutdown and native SIGTERM with and without startup CPU profiling. Shutdown retained the delay and reached normal quit in 28–53 ms; SIGTERM completed in 26–78 ms. No normal case used the fallback.
- A deliberately blocked built-app quit exited successfully via the fallback at 3012 ms.

Built-app probes used hidden windows and isolated PwrAgent data directories. No host reboot or power-off was performed. The unrelated packaging-test adjustment from PwrGit #421 is excluded.

body:
## Summary

When a Gateway failed at start, Quasar showed only `gateway_start_failed: process_exited`. The actual reason, for example a `dlopen` failure for `steamclient.so`, was visible only in the Host's own output.

- **Host:** reads the Gateway's stdout and stderr through pipes and passes each line on to its own output, prefixed with `[gateway CLUSTER]`. It keeps the last 20 lines (300 characters each) in the new `ProcessOutputTail`.
- **On exit:** the Host reports `process_exited:exit_code=N` and the lines in the new optional `GatewayStatus.Output` field. The lines are also saved in the launch record, so the status still has them while the respawn waits.
- **Quasar:** copies them into `ClusterReconcileStatus.GatewayOutput`. The cluster detail panel shows them under **Last Cluster Registry process output**.
- Documented in `Docs/Configuration.md`. The terminology count in `Docs/ClusterTerminology.md` is updated.

## Trade-off

The Host runs with `KillMode=process`, so a Gateway outlives a Host restart. A Gateway that was already running when the Host restarted keeps running, but from then on its output is lost (before this change it went to the Host's journal), and its exit is reported as plain `process_exited`. .NET 10's `Process` can't hand a child a file as stdout, which would have avoided this. Node processes are unchanged.

## Testing

- `Quasar.Host --self-test`: new case where a fake Gateway prints 26 lines and exits with code 3. It checks the exit code, the 20-line tail, the cut long line and the tail during the respawn wait. Passes.
- New `ClusterReconcilerTests.FailedGatewayStartCarriesTheGatewayOutput` passes.
- Full `Quasar.Tests`: 484 passed, 36 failed. All 36 are in `ClusterApiRouteTests` and fail the same way on `main` (the route test doesn't register `ClusterUpdatePreparationService`). They are unrelated to this change.
- Not tested live on a Host with a failing Gateway.

body:
## Problem
Since the MUI X Charts move (#31), hovering a chart highlights the bar or point but shows no information.

## Cause
MUI X renders the tooltip inside the chart's own layer, positioned with `position: fixed`. The chart sits in a card whose blurred glass background (`backdrop-filter`) makes the card the reference for fixed descendants, so the tooltip was placed hundreds of pixels outside the screen (found in a real browser: `x` 2032 on a 1440 px wide window).

## Fix
`ChartView` passes `slotProps.tooltip.container = document.body` to the bar/line/area charts and the donut, so the tooltip is placed against the page.

## Testing
Checked in a browser: the line chart tooltip shows "May 2026 – Fuel 3.15 L/100 km" next to the pointer, the bar chart tooltip lists every series of the month ("Jul 2026: Expenses · HUF 18,000 …") with the vehicle's units and currencies. jsdom cannot lay out SVG or position popovers, so there is no unit test for the placement; `mise`-level frontend tests (474), lint and typecheck pass.

author: atinfinity
body:
Fixes the Windows CI failure on main after #71 ([run 37569375995](https://github.com/atinfinity/cc-calendar/actions/runs/37569375995)): `tests/test_notes.py::test_reloads_when_the_file_changes` failed with `assert '' == 'theirs'`.

## Cause

`Notes` decided whether `notes.json` had changed on disk by `st_mtime_ns` alone. On Windows, two saves in quick succession can get the same mtime, so `refresh()` did not notice the other instance's write.

## Fix

`Notes._stat()` now returns `(st_mtime_ns, st_size, st_ino)`. Each save writes a temporary file and renames it into place with `os.replace`, so the inode changes on every save even when the mtime does not (on Windows, Python reports the file index as `st_ino`).

## Testing

- macOS: `uv run pytest -q` — 87 passed.
- Windows: covered by this PR's CI.

author: tillkruss
body:
This PR adds movies and series as App Intents entities and adds Shortcuts actions for automations. On iOS 27, opening movies and series uses the new Siri `.system.open` schema.

## Entities
- **`Ruddarr/Services/Entities.swift`** (new): `MovieEntity` and `SeriesEntity` (`IndexedEntity`), each with an `EntityStringQuery`.
  - `entities(for:)` fetches each item from the Radarr/Sonarr API, so it works on a cold launch.
  - `entities(matching:)` and `suggestedEntities()` fetch the libraries of all configured instances in parallel. Instances that fail to respond are skipped.
- Identifiers use `MediaEntityID` (`<instanceId>:<mediaId>`), and a test locks the format because users' shortcuts store it.
- **Details for Shortcuts** (`@Property`). The display stays "Title" with the year as subtitle, so text output is unchanged.
  - **Movie:** Title, Year, Status, Monitored, Downloaded, Size on Disk, In Cinemas, Digital Release, Physical Release, IMDb ID, TMDB ID, Instance.
  - **Series:** Title, Year, Status, Monitored, Network, Seasons, Episodes, Downloaded Episodes, Size on Disk, Next Airing, Previous Airing, IMDb ID, TVDB ID, Instance.
- **Detail views**: `.appEntityIdentifier(...)` on the details content of `MovieView` and `SeriesDetailView` for on-screen awareness. This needs iOS 18.4+ and is compiled only for arm64 (see Build status).
- **Spotlight**: each indexed movie and series item is now linked to its entity (`CSSearchableItemAttributeSet.associateAppEntity`), so Siri and Spotlight can resolve titles from the index. No separate entries are created, and the visible Spotlight content (title, description, poster, keywords, identifier) is built exactly as before. `Media.searchableItem` and `Spotlight.index` now take the `Instance` because the entity needs it for its ID and its Instance property, which Shortcuts shows in Get Details. None of the entity properties are indexed as Spotlight attributes.

## Shortcuts actions
Add, search and missing-search live in `Services/Intents+Automations.swift`; Get Upcoming Releases lives in `Services/Intents+Calendar.swift`.

| Action | What it does | Availability |
|---|---|---|
| **Add Movie / Add Series** | Looks up a title, IMDb link, or `imdb:`/`tmdb:`/`tvdb:` id. When there is more than one result, asks "Which movie/series do you want to add?" with the top 10 results as "Title (Year)" plus Cancel (`requestChoice`). Results already in the library show as "Title (Year) · In Library". Adds the chosen item with the **last settings used in the app**, and optionally starts an automatic search (**off by default**). If the item is already in the library, it says so instead of "Added …". Returns the entity so actions can be chained. | iOS 26+ |
| ↳ Add Series **Monitor** | Optional choice (All, Future, Missing, Existing, First Season, Last Season, Pilot, Recent, Monitor Specials, Unmonitor Specials, None), the same options as the add form. When left empty, it uses the last option used in the app. | iOS 26+ |
| **Automatic Movie Search / Automatic Series Search** | Runs `MoviesSearch` / `SeriesSearch` for a library item. | iOS 26+ |
| **Search All Missing** | Runs Radarr `MissingMoviesSearch` and/or Sonarr `MissingEpisodeSearch` (`monitored: true`) on **all** configured instances, for Movies, Series, or both (the default). Both commands only search monitored items. Fails only if every instance fails; otherwise it names the instances that failed. | iOS 26+ |
| **Get Upcoming Releases** | Lists movies and episodes for the next N days (default 7) as text lines. Shortcuts only, with no Siri phrase. If some instances fail, the result ends with a one-line note naming them. | iOS 26+ |
| **Open Movie / Open Series** | `.system.open` schema intents. They open the item, switching instance if needed. | iOS 27 only, compiled with Swift 6.4+ |

None of the iOS 26+ actions open the app. There are no duplicate actions: the open actions exist only as schema intents, and the earlier `.system.searchInApp` intent was removed because it overlapped with the existing movie and series search actions.

`InstanceCommand` gains `missingMoviesSearch` and `missingEpisodesSearch` cases. No existing command changed.

### Siri phrases (`Services/Shortcuts.swift`)
| Phrase | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| "Add movie to Ruddarr" | Opened the movie search screen | Runs **Add Movie**. Siri asks "Which movie?", then which result. |
| "Add (TV) series to Ruddarr" | Opened the series search screen | Runs **Add Series**. Siri asks "Which series?", then which result. |
| "Search for movie / (TV) series in Ruddarr" | Opened the search screen | Unchanged, now on its own "Search Movies" / "Search Series" tile |
| "Open Ruddarr …" | Opened a tab | Unchanged |

### Errors
`Services/Intents+Errors.swift` wraps every request made by an action (`requesting(instance) { … }`) and maps `API.Error` to a short message that names the instance:

| API error | Message |
|---|---|
| Not connected to the internet | "You're not connected to the internet." |
| URL error / private-IP timeout | "Couldn't reach Radarr." |
| 401 / 403 | "Radarr rejected the API key." |
| Error response with a message | "Radarr: <server message>" |
| Other status code | "Radarr responded with an error (500)." |
| Invalid URL / unexpected response | "The URL of Radarr is invalid." / "Radarr returned an unexpected response." |
| Several instances failed | "Requests to Radarr and Sonarr failed." |

Cancellation passes through unchanged, so cancelling the choice prompt doesn't show an error.

## Refactors (for testability)
- **`Utilities/Identifiers.swift`**:
  - `MediaEntityID` for App Intents entities.
  - `SpotlightItemID` (`<kind>:<mediaId>:<instanceId>`), now used by `Movie`/`Series.searchableItem` and `Ruddarr.openSearchableItem`.
  - The Spotlight string format is unchanged. A Spotlight item without an instance (`movie:42:`) used to crash when opened (index out of range) and now opens on the current instance.
- **`Utilities/AddDefaults.swift`**: the quality profile and root folder fallback, now shared by `MovieForm`, `SeriesForm` and the add intents. The forms behave as before.
- Both files are added to the Tests target's membership exceptions in `project.pbxproj`.

## Tests
- `Tests/IdentifierFormatTests.swift`: shipped-format fixtures, round trips, lowercase UUIDs, and invalid inputs for both identifier types.
- `Tests/AddDefaultsTests.swift`: preferred value vs. fallback, unset defaults (`-1`, `""`, `nil`), trailing slashes, and empty or path-less folders.

## Migrations
None needed. No persisted model, settings key, instance wire format, or Spotlight identifier changes. The add intents only read `movieDefaults` / `seriesDefaults`. The Spotlight index checksum includes the build number, so existing installs reindex (now with entities) after updating.

## ⚠️ Build status
- CI uses Xcode 26.6 (Swift 6.3), so it skips the iOS 27 block and builds made with it **have no Open Movie / Open Series action**. That block has to be built locally with Xcode 27, and release builds need Xcode 27.
- `.appEntityIdentifier` doesn't resolve when compiling for x86_64 macOS (CodeQL's build), while arm64 macOS and iOS compile it fine. It's wrapped in `#if arch(arm64)`, so Intel Mac builds go without on-screen awareness, which needs Apple Intelligence (Apple silicon) anyway.
- Apple's developer forums report a harmless "Failed to request donation" console warning when calling `associateAppEntity` ([thread](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/834780)). The items still get indexed.

## Testing
- [ ] Build with Xcode 27 (iOS and macOS)
- [ ] Shortcuts: Add Movie with an ambiguous title (the choice list appears, library items are marked "In Library", Cancel stops without adding), with an IMDb link (no prompt), and with a movie already in the library (says "already in your library"), each with search on and off
- [ ] Shortcuts: Add Movie inside a personal automation set to "Run Immediately", to check how the choice pr

author: wcpos-mini[bot]
body:
ADR-077 phase (d5), part of #501: coupons on one register. Stacked on #522 (d4b), which is stacked on #519 → … → #513 (parked on Paul's word). Retarget to `main` in order once #513 merges.

## What it adds (`@tallyui/pos`)

- **`createSaleCouponSource({ coupons, products, orders, now? })`** is the `SaleCouponSource` that `useSale` takes.
  - **`find(code)`** looks the code up with an indexed query, then with a lower-case scan, because WooCommerce may store capitals. It returns `null` when:
    - no coupon matches;
    - the `discount_type` is not `percent`, `fixed_cart` or `fixed_product`;
    - the `id` is not an integer;
    - the coupon has no `amount`.

    Only the `CouponInput` fields present on the document are copied.
  - **The overlay.** The till's own uses are added to `usage_count` and `used_by` (the customer id, else the email):
    - a `pending` order always counts;
    - an `applied` order counts while its `updatedAt` is later than the coupon doc's last write, and for at most `APPLIED_USE_GRACE_MS` (10 min);
    - a `rejected` order never counts.

    The window exists because RxDB's downstream writes nothing when a pulled doc equals the stored one (rxdb 17.5 `replication-protocol/downstream.js`).
  - **`productCategories`** reads `products`.
- **`startCouponUsageRefetch({ orders, coupons, enqueue, reSync, now? })`** watches applied orders that have coupons and fall inside the window. It hands the local coupon docs to the coupon feed's `enqueue` as `refreshOnly` entries, then calls `reSync()` once.
  - Each order is handled once.
  - A failed read is logged through `saleLogger`.
  - Nothing is enqueued after `stop()`, including a read still in flight.
- **Writes:** none to any collection (#53).
- **The app's side:** the app wires both pieces, passing `connector.reconcile.coupons.enqueue` and the coupons replication's `reSync`.
- **ADR-077:** "(d5) as built" is recorded, with known limits. A pull that races the create can undercount until the next pull, and the store then refuses with `coupon_invalid` and d4b reopens the sale.
- **Changeset:** `@tallyui/pos` minor.

## Review (one review, on head `191ea0b`)

Codex implemented the code from six specs (d5-1, d5-1b, d5-1c, d5-2, d5-2b, d5-2c). I read the full diff against each spec and reran the acceptance commands on this head:

- `pnpm vitest run packages/pos --maxWorkers=2`: 78 files, 1687 passed, 6 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @tallyui/pos typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm vitest run packages/integration-tests --maxWorkers=2`: 12 files, 115 passed, 2 skipped.

### Mutations (applied by the reviewer, one at a time, test file run after each)

`coupon-source.ts`: all 21 were killed. S7 and S14 survived the first run; the d5-1c tests kill them.

| n | mutation | killed by |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | no lower-case fallback | finds an uppercase code |
| S2 | fallback compares without lower-casing | finds an uppercase code |
| S3 | fallback `code` guard dropped | skips a doc without code |
| S4 | `gift` accepted | gift gives null |
| S5 | integer id check dropped | non-integer id gives null |
| S6 | amount check dropped | doc without amount gives null |
| S7 | rejected orders read | never counts a rejected order, even when fresh |
| S8 | every read order counts | applied-order lwt / window tests |
| S9 | lwt check dropped | counts an applied order until a later pull rewrites the coupon |
| S10 | grace window dropped | grace window test |
| S11 | grace boundary inclusive | grace window test (599 999 vs 600 000 ms) |
| S12 | email preferred to id | counts pending orders (id before email) |
| S13 | undefined customer pushed | counts each order once with no customer |
| S14 | absent fields copied as `undefined` | copies only present fields (exact key set) |
| S15 | `limit_usage_to_x_items` not copied | copies all supplied fields |
| S16 | `email_restrictions` not copied | copies all supplied fields |
| S17 | stored code returned instead of the asked code | finds an uppercase code |
| S18 | overlay not added to `usage_count` | counts pending orders |
| S19 | categories passed whole | productCategories |
| S20 | missing categories not defaulted | productCategories |
| S21 | orders without the coupon count | counts pending orders (unrelated ignored) |

`coupon-refetch.ts`: 15 of 17 were killed and 2 are equivalent. R1, R8 and R13 survived the first run; the d5-2c tests kill them.

| n | mutation | killed by |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | pending orders watched too | refetches a fresh pending order only after it applies |
| R2 | orders without coupons not skipped | unhandled error fails the run |
| R3 | handled check dropped | does not handle an order again |
| R4 | order never marked handled | does not handle an order again |
| R5 | grace window dropped | skips orders at the grace window boundary |
| R6 | grace boundary inclusive | skips orders at the grace window boundary |
| R7 | non-integer ids kept | **equivalent**: `NaN` in `$in` finds nothing; only an extra read |
| R8 | empty result enqueued | skips missing local coupons and non-integer ids |
| R9 | entries not `refreshOnly` | four enqueue tests |
| R10 | keyed by id, not uuid | four enqueue tests |
| R11 | `reSync` not called | four enqueue tests |
| R12 | `enqueue` not called | four enqueue tests |
| R13 | `stop()` leaves the flag (unsubscribe only) | enqueues nothing when stopped during an in-flight read |
| R14 | `stop()` does not unsubscribe (flag only) | **equivalent**: the flag alone keeps it silent |
| R15 | `stop()` does nothing | a second runner handles an order applied after stop |
| R16 | failure not logged | logs a failed coupon read and never throws |
| R17 | local document left out | four enqueue tests |

## Merge danger

- **door:one-way.** This adds public `@tallyui/pos` API, coupon usage limits (money), and it sits in a chain behind the `pos_orders` v9 schema (#513).
- **blast:data.** It reads `pos_orders` and `coupons` and writes neither. Over-counting refuses a coupon the store would accept; the cashier sees "used up". Under-counting is caught by the store (`coupon_invalid` → d4b reopen).
- needs-paul through the #513 chain. Merge only after #522, in order.

author: kavin0x
body: Fixes #2. ## Problem In blog view, tapping the trailing ⋯ (`ellipsis.circle`) control did nothing: no menu, sheet, or feedback. The control was a SwiftUI `Menu` inside a `ToolbarItemGroup` with an `if isEditing` / `else` branch, and the accessibility label was applied to the `Menu` itself. That combination is a known SwiftUI toolbar pitfall where the overflow control renders but does not receive taps. ## Fix - Use a dedicated `ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction)` for the overflow `Menu`, and `.confirmationAction` for **Done** while editing. - Label the menu with `Label("More options", systemImage: "ellipsis.circle")` instead of a bare `Image` plus `.accessibilityLabel` on the `Menu`. - Keep the existing actions (Edit, Share, Share Audio, Save Transcript, Regenerate, History). ## Tests Added unit tests for overflow menu label constants and when content actions are included. Could not run `xcodebuild` in this Linux cloud environment (no Xcode / iOS Simulator). Please run the VoiceBloggerTests target locally, and tap ⋯ on a generated post in blog view. Socket MCP is not available in this environment, and this change does not add dependencies. Socket also does not support the Swift/SPM iOS app ecosystem for a scan of existing packages.

author: xiaoxiaolin0918
body:
Fixes #130

**Stacked on #142** (`feature/124-132-push-review-mr-status`): both PRs edit the `mrs merge` path (#124 error enrichment + this PR's precheck), so this branch contains a verified integration merge — gate → read-only precheck → POST → error enrichment on failure. GitHub will retarget this PR to `main` automatically once #142 merges. CI note: stacked PRs only get CI after #133 (the ci.yml trigger fix) merges; this branch is fully verified locally on Windows.

## 1. `workitem create --help` missing `--type-id`
Investigation: `--type-id` has been registered on create's own flags all along (`cmd/workitem_register.go`, since #31) — the reporter was likely on an old binary or lost it in the long help. Fix: added an `Example` (with the `types list` discovery hint) above Flags, plus a **help contract test** that fails when any registered non-hidden flag stops rendering (prevents future drift). Zero behavior change.

## 2. Default profile
`config.json` gains a `profile` key; resolution is `--profile > YUNXIAO_PROFILE > config default`. New `yunxiao profile use <name>` (Risk: write, `--dry-run`/`--unset`, validates the profile exists, preserves other config keys on save); `config set profile` supported too.

## 3. `mrs get` middle view
New default **summary** view: brief fields + the "can it merge?" set (`mergeable`, `conflictCheckStatus`, `checkList` incl. `requirementRuleItems`, `supportMergeFastForwardOnly`, `allRequirementsPass`, `ahead`, `behind`) + `reviewers [{name, opinion}]`. `--brief` minimal, `--full` = pre-#130 raw object. `YUNXIAO_MRS_GET_VIEW=full|summary|brief` follows the #98 contract (flag > env > default; invalid env fails before any request; dry-run shows `request.projection`). Brief/summary include `wip` (from #132).

## 4. Merge precheck
Before the POST (also under `--dry-run`, read-only, #95 precedent) the CLI GETs the MR once and verifies: terminal status, `conflictCheckStatus`, `mergeable`, and `--merge-type` against the repo's exposed merge settings (`mergeTypes`/`supportedMergeTypes`/`mergeSetting`, `supportMergeFastForwardOnly=false` rejects ff-only; web-UI spellings normalized). Failure → exit 1 structured error (`merge_type_not_supported` etc.) + actionable hint, **no POST**; pass → `meta.precheck`. Key decisions: the `--yes` gate still trips first (exit 10, zero requests); detail-GET failure **fails closed** (high-risk gate, unlike #95's degrade) — and after POST failure the #124 error enrichment still applies.

## Verification
1935 insertions incl. per-item table-driven tests (help contract, resolution priority ×10, use/dry-run/unset, view matrix ×10, precheck ×13 with POST-count assertions). Post-integration with #142: all MR test groups green, `go test ./...` matches the pre-#108 baseline exactly, `check_command_docs.py` OK.

Fire nye artikler til i dag. Læs dem og merge, når de er godkendt, så går de live.

**1. Fossilbiler efter 2035? Regeringen beder fredag om nyt mandat til EU's CO2-krav for biler** (Klima & miljø, tophistorie)
Kommissionen vil sænke 2035-kravet fra 100 til 90 %. Regeringen er skeptisk, selv om dens egne tal viser ca. 24.000 flere fossilbiler og 1,3 mia. kr. mere til statskassen i 2035.
Kilder: KEFM-samlenotat KOM (2025) 995 (29.9.2026) · Europaudvalgets dagsorden 9.10.2026 · Folketingets EU-Oplysning, KOM (2025) 0995

Parlamentet beder Kommissionen om et forslag mod psykosociale risici (413-210-29). Danskerne stemte 7 for og 6 imod, og Venstre stemte anderledes end Bosse og Friis. Faktatjek: Det er en opfordring, ikke lov.

Forklaring til miljøministrenes ETS-drøftelse mandag: lavere reduktionsfaktor (4,4 → 3,7 → 1,7 %), affaldsforbrænding med fra 2031, en ny industribank og regeringens linje. Indtægterne fra kvotesalget kan blive påvirket.

author: abhi-abhiram
body:
## Summary
Implement the reusable framework-level improvements identified during the Discord EOD workflow, without putting any Discord-specific logic or private evidence into webnav.

- Add git-versioned per-site URL policies and optional per-run write approval, shared by saved/draft functions and browser tools.
- Validate optional argument/result contracts and `verify(ctx, result)` postconditions before accepting success, learning a draft, or caching output. Contracts use a strict documented JSON Schema subset; unsupported keywords fail instead of being ignored.
- Default to bounded inline results (8000 serialized characters), optional field projection, and complete private artifacts with bounded/searchable retrieval by generated ID.
- Default failures to compact diagnostics; inspect the current tab with `fn_diagnostics` without replaying side effects, or explicitly request full snapshot/screenshot capture.
- Add opt-in TTL read caching with canonical args and source/UI/policy invalidation, freshness controls, write invalidation, and health checks that bypass cached success.
- Preserve completed-write semantics when output processing fails: report `output_error`, recover an artifact when possible, never replay, and do not save an errored draft.

## Compatibility and limits
- Existing function metadata needs no migration; missing policies preserve browser behavior. Inline-output and failure-verbosity defaults intentionally change.
- URL guards are **not a security/privacy sandbox**: Node imports, raw CDP, other tabs/frames, handles, service workers and data fetched/rendered inside an allowed SPA remain outside this boundary. Site-level content/conversation restrictions are still required; external browser harnesses do not inherit the policy.
- HTTP redirects are conservatively blocked under a policy, even to an allowed URL. Playwright routes only the first URL of a redirect chain, so scoped navigation fetches once with redirects/retries disabled; use reviewed direct URLs instead.
- Cache is bounded and process-local; account changes/external data changes require `fresh` or explicit clearing. Artifact retention is manual.
- Site-specific coverage, scroll boundaries, incremental watermarks, evidence/style caches and at-most-once submission receipts remain in site functions. The separate pi-browser-harness endpoint-discovery issue is not changed here.

## Validation
- [x] `npm run check`
- [x] `npm run smoke` (stdio tool/schema tests plus synthetic-page regression checks)
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] `WEBNAV_CDP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9222 npm run browser-smoke` — passed against an explicitly approved headless Demo browser using the existing Demo profile. Navigation, links, redirect blocking and SPA scope checks exercised only the synthetic loopback fixture in a dedicated tab. No visible window/focus interruption or real Discord channel reads. The test itself never launches a browser.

No packages installed, credentials/evidence committed, or real EOD/submission workflows rerun.

author: alexnodeland
body:
## What

**For a player.** On an older laptop the faces did not come: not on the presets, though a preset's sound never changes, and not in the bank. Two waits caused it, and both are gone.

- **Every preset's face comes with the app.** A preset's face was a render the engine made only once everything else it had to do was done (the bank's fill, PERFORM's measurement of the sound the app opens with, the warm start's background work). With the engine slowed four times (the fixture's `slowEngine: 4`, standing in for the Intel MacBook Air), the warm start's nine faces came 415 s after its cards, and the PRESETS rows' 227 s after the tab opened. Each preset's face is now rendered ahead of time, natively, and shipped in `apps/web/preset-faces.json`. The warm start's cards and the PRESETS rows draw theirs from it without asking the engine. With the same slowdown, the nine cards draw theirs in the cards' own task, and the PRESETS rows 34 ms after they show. Rows out of view are drawn while the page is idle, before you scroll to them.
- **Your bank's faces no longer wait for PERFORM to finish listening.** The worker's `faces` reply answered only from faces it had already copied out. Every other lookup went to `later`, and `later` waits while a long job holds the engine. So while PERFORM measured the opening sound, no face reached the page. Faces are drawn against the bank's mean, so with no bank faces nothing could be drawn anywhere, the warm start included: 154 s after it opened, at 4×. The worker now answers at once any face the engine's memo already holds (a pool member's face comes with its featurization), or that an audition still in memory gives.

**For a contributor.** `make preset-faces` writes the file: one native render per preset, about 14 s of one core. `make test` fails while the file is out of date (`crates/auracle-wasm/tests/shipped_faces.rs`), and a φ change owes `make preset-faces` just as it owes `make perform-wirings`. `boot_agrees.spec.js` checks every preset's face from the built wasm against the file, byte for byte, under the key the worker files it by. `make mutants DIFF=1` now runs its diff with git's file-system monitor off: in a worktree the plain diff had waited on the monitor's socket for over a minute.

## How

- **For the maintainer: where this file lives.** D13 (#297, recorded in ADR-025 decision 4 and in #287's thread) says shipped preset data (makeup, rack description, face) goes in `perform-wirings.json` under its single fingerprint: one file, one fingerprint, one staleness check. This branch was built before that decision reached `main`. It ships the faces in a separate file, `preset-faces.json`, beside the wirings, as #287's *Done when* allowed ("by the same tool, or one beside it"). The file is keyed by what a face depends on: the render namespace (`cache_namespace`: the stimulus, `RENDER_EPOCH`, the quiver version) and the reference clip. The wirings' fingerprint is φ's. Do we keep the separate file and amend ADR-025 decision 4's line "which `make perform-wirings` writes", or hold this PR until the faces are folded into `perform-wirings.json`?
- **The page uses a shipped face only where it would render that same face** (`shipped-faces.js` `presetFace`): the file's render namespace must be the session's (`renderNs`, from `ready`), and a preset with an AUDIO IN must be hearing the reference clip. In every other case the page asks the engine and renders, as before the file existed.
- **One key for one face.** A shipped face is filed under the key the worker uses (`"<ns>/<render key>"`, `farm_key`). So a preset's row and the same preset in the pool or on the bench are one face. Shipped keys are looked up apart from `faceKeyByRef`, an LRU that bench edits churn, so an evicted key never sends a preset back to a render.
- **A face request made while the file is still loading waits for it** (`shippedHeld`), for at most 3 s (`SHIPPED_FACES_WAIT_MS`), so a stalled fetch never stops a face from rendering. A file that lands later still draws the presets after it. The file is `?v=` stamped with the build (`WEB_STAMPED`). The worker never reads it: a preset in the pool already has its face in the engine's memo.
- **The worker answers memo-held faces in its `faces` handler** (`face_of`, `face_of_tree`, `face_of_key`, none of which renders). Only the IndexedDB store and renders still go to `later` and the faces lane. This is the first step of #311's instant path. The bench's faces and renders moving to the farm stay #311's.
- **A preset's face is still drawn against the bank** (`faceStats`): it waits for no render of its own, but it does wait for the bank's first faces. The guide's bank and first-session pages say so.
- **Tests.** `faces.spec.js` no longer has its own warm-start test: `faces_presets.spec.js` checks the same cards more strictly (each card's key, and no preset face asked of an engine slowed four times). That test took 152 s on CI behind the renders and now takes about 2 s.

## Checks

Rebased onto `main` at e4b28009. Four conflicts, all line-wise, each resolved by `scripts/ops/rows_resolve.py`: table rows in `apps/web/AGENTS.md`, an import line in `main.js`, and two in `tests/web/changed.mjs`. After the rebase, the branch's changes against `main` are line for line what they were before it. `main`'s new face code (`faceBoxOf`, `heldFace`, the bank's `takeUp`) reads `faceKeyOfTarget`, which this branch changed. A preset's key there is still the worker's `farm_key` of `preset_tree_json`, the key `boot_agrees` checks.

- `make check-changed` (what CI's classifier picks: fmt-check, lint, web-check, dev-check, wasm-check, test): `cargo fmt` clean; clippy `-D warnings` clean; the specs' lint OK (279 suppressed, none above `main`); the web units 335/335; dev-check green (the voice check 0 rises, the changelog, the PR-check, release and workflow tests); the wasm32 check OK; the Rust tests 664/664 on nextest.
- `make wasm` (build `3ee6a9bf5792ccf5`), then `make worker-test`: 13/13, `faces.test.mjs` and `main`'s lean test among them.
- `make site && make site-check`: 75 pages, every reference resolves. `preset-faces.json` and `shipped-faces.js` ship in `site/play/`.
- `make coverage`: every crate at its floor (100% of lines and functions). 396 changed lines in `crates/`, 47 of them measured code, 0 not covered.
- `make mutants DIFF=1`: 5 mutants, 4 caught, 1 unviable, 0 missed.
- Needs `full-ci`: it changes `crates/auracle-wasm` (and the `Makefile`, `.config/nextest.toml` and `worker.js`).

Specs, through `one_browser.sh` on their own port:

- The specs this branch changes, `--repeat-each=3`: `boot_agrees.spec.js` (9), `faces.spec.js` (8), `faces_presets.spec.js` (5). 66/66 passed, in 14.2 min on a machine at a load of about 100.
- Once each: the smoke pair (`smoke.spec.js` 2, `failure_flows.spec.js` 4), `first_run.spec.js` (3) and `shell_zoom.spec.js` (11). `shell_zoom.spec.js` is new on `main` and reads the face keys this branch changed. 20/20 passed.

Fixed on the branch after the feature commits:

- A PRESETS test passed whichever way the rows were painted. It now waits for all 62 rows to have their faces before any scroll (9faaced5).
- A guide line said a preset row's face came "however busy the engine is". It now says the face waits for the bank's faces, which it is drawn against (27ea392b).
- The warm-start test in `faces.spec.js` was a weaker copy of the one in `faces_presets.spec.js`, and is gone (91d6dbcb).
- `make mutants DIFF=1` could hang on git's file-system monitor, and `worker-test`'s help described its run wrongly. Both are fixed (cf1d459b).

Nothing was declined. D13 (#297) is revised to match this branch: the faces ship in their own file, keyed by the render's namespace and the reference clip, because a face goes stale when the render changes and a wiring when φ does.

Closes #287
Refs #297
Refs #311

body:
## What

weather_amoled's "Try it in your browser" (the firmware's own LVGL screens compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten) is now a generic part of espforge, so every app made from the template gets one. The split follows rtc_quebec's port: `main.c`'s `app_main()` runs **unchanged** as a fiber task, and the Wi-Fi stubs report a saved, joined network.

- **`web/emu/forge/`: the framework's part, the same in every app.** It holds the stand-ins for `board.h` (display, touch) and ESP-IDF:
  - `esp_http_client` as `fetch`
  - NVS in `localStorage`
  - FreeRTOS tasks, queues and binary semaphores as fibers
  - `localtime_r` following `TZ`
  - the web server for the settings page in an iframe
  - stubs for Wi-Fi, updates, diagnostics and the test console
  - `shim/` headers
  - `emu.mk` (the build rules), `emu-page.js`, `emu-settings.js`
  - `gen_config.py`, which writes `lv_kconfig.h` and `sdkconfig.h` from the firmware's sdkconfig
  - `embed.py` and `smoke.js`
- **`web/emu/`: the app's part.**
  - `Makefile` lists its `main/` sources and its embedded font.
  - `emu_main.c` handles `?lang=`, then starts `app_main` and the loop.
  - `index.html` holds the page's words.
- **`main/ui.c`:** one `#ifdef EMU_BUILD` for the font as an array. The firmware binary is unchanged.
- **CI:**
  - New job `emulator`. It builds from the latest stable release (the tag itself on a stable tag), or from the pushed commit when that release has no `web/emu`. It uses LVGL at `main/idf_component.yml`'s version, cJSON 1.7.19 and Emscripten 6.0.11, then runs the smoke test.
  - `pages` passes `--emu`. If the emulator job fails, the site is still published, without "Try it".
- **`make_flasher_site.py --emu`** now copies all of the build's files, so the settings page and `emu-page.js` reach `try/`.
- **Audio, IMU and partition stand-ins stay out of the generic part.** The README explains how an app adds its own, with weather_amoled's as examples.
- **Docs:** `web/emu/README.md`, COMPONENTS, NEW-PROJECT (what a new app changes), TESTING §7b, README layout, CLAUDE.md, a CHANGELOG `## Unreleased` entry (skipped by `notes.json`), and a `.claude/launch.json` "emulator" config on port 8767.

## Checked

- **Emulator build:** WSL, Emscripten 6.0.11, LVGL 9.2.2 from `managed_components`. A clean build takes 57 s, a build with nothing to do 5 s. No warnings; wasm is 877 KB.
- **`node web/emu/forge/smoke.js`:** headless Chromium with real mouse events. All 6 checks pass:
  - the screen draws
  - a drag shows the system page
  - a press and hold opens Wi-Fi setup
  - the settings page reads `/api/info`
  - choosing French there turns the screen French
  - no page or console errors

  I looked at the screenshots by eye. I also opened it in the built-in browser.
- **`make_flasher_site.py site --stable … --emu web/emu/build`:** `try/` gets the page's files, and `channels.json` has `"try"`.
- **Firmware:** `idf.py -B build\v55 … build` succeeds.
- **Host tests:** `wsl make -C tests/host`, all pass.
- **Page tests:** `tools/webtest` `npm test`, 23 passed.

Not done: the `emulator` CI job hasn't run yet (this PR is its first run). No release is tagged.

author: mstykow
body:
## Summary

- Modern `go mod graph` output contains `go@<version>` and `toolchain@<version>` pseudo-nodes (`example.com/m go@1.22.0`, `go@1.22.0 toolchain@go1.22.3`, `dep@v1 go@1.20`). The parser turned these into bogus `pkg:golang/go@1.22.0` / `pkg:golang/toolchain@go1.22.3` dependencies. Edges touching either node are now skipped.
- Graph dependencies no longer hard-code `is_runtime: true` / `is_optional: false`: the graph proves module edges and selected versions (`is_pinned`, `is_direct` are kept), not runtime or optional intent, so both stay unset.
- Recognize `go-mod-graph.deplock` (the filename ScanCode uses for `go mod graph` dumps) in the parser, parser metadata (regenerated `docs/SUPPORTED_FORMATS.md`), and the Go sibling-merge assembler patterns.

## Issues

- Covers: upstream aboutcode-org/scancode-toolkit#5300 (issue #4423).

## Scope and exclusions

- Included: `go_mod_graph` parser, its metadata/docs, Go assembler sibling patterns.
- Explicit exclusions: `go.sum` still emits `is_runtime: true` / `is_optional: false`; that is a separate datasource and left for a follow-up.

## How to verify

- Scan a directory with `go.mod` plus a `go-mod-graph.deplock` produced by `go mod graph` on Go >= 1.21 using `--package --json-pp -`; there are no `pkg:golang/go@…` / `pkg:golang/toolchain@…` dependencies and graph rows have `is_runtime` / `is_optional` null.

## Intentional differences from Python

- ScanCode's #5300 handler does not filter `go@` / `toolchain@` nodes and sets runtime flags; Provenant skips the pseudo-nodes and leaves unproven flags unset.

## Expected-output fixture changes

- Files changed: `testdata/go-golden/sample-graph/go.mod.graph` (input: appended `go@` / `toolchain@` edges), `testdata/go-golden/sample-graph/go.mod.graph.expected`, `testdata/assembly-golden/go-graph-basic/expected.json`.
- Why the new expected output is correct: the only change is `is_runtime` / `is_optional` becoming null on `go_mod_graph` rows; the dependency set is unchanged despite the added pseudo-node edges, proving they are skipped. `go.mod` / `go.sum` rows are untouched.

author: ranxianglei
body:
Issue #1440 P3 — collapse the fifteen copy-pasted `buildXxxEnv` functions in `src/launcher.ts` into one preset table + one private builder. **Behavior-preserving**: every exported signature stays byte-identical and returned env objects are value-equal (plus key-order-equal) for every client under every parameter combination.

## Design

One module-private table + builder inserted between `buildPiEnv` and `buildCodexEnv`:

- `interface EnvClientPreset { caKeys; proxy; httpProxyOnRouteHttp; extras?; baseUrlKeys? }` + `const ENV_CLIENTS` (one entry per table-driven client, every load-bearing per-client comment — #655, jcode reqwest, #1048, #1049×2, #653, #1047, #2115, gateway-mode notes — moved verbatim next to its entry)
- `buildClientEnv(preset, origin, caPath, baseEnv, rewrites?, routeHttp?)` emits keys in an order that reproduces each original literal's insertion order exactly (incl. aider's `HTTP_PROXY` between `HTTPS_PROXY` and its CA vars)
- `LAUNCHER_LOOPBACK_NO_PROXY` dedups the triple-copied `"localhost,127.0.0.1,::1"` loopback literal
- The 13 table-driven builders become one-line delegators; two stayed bespoke, deliberately:
  - `buildPiEnv` — builds a JSON *manifest* (`BILI_PROVIDER_REWRITES`) with scheme-dependent wrapping/overwrite semantics plus two list-derived conditional keys; forcing it through the table would smuggle callbacks into "data"
  - `buildClaudePluginEnv` — different shape entirely (identity pass-through when `!directUrl`, upstream read FROM baseEnv with a trim-or-default fallback chain); not a member of the proxy/CA skeleton

Net: `src/launcher.ts` 121+/93−, **no new exports** (table/builder stay module-private → the unused-exports gate from #1443 unaffected), no new deps, call sites untouched.

## Equivalence proof

- Snapshot script imported all 15 builders from source and emitted sorted-key canonical JSON for **43 client × param-combo lines** (aider routeHttp both ways incl. stale-preseeded HTTP_PROXY; claude/codebuddy/gemini/iflow/antigravity × {none, http-only, https-only, both-schemes https-wins, no-match}; pi manifest edge cases; claude-plugin direct=false identity + direct=true fallback chain). BEFORE (pre-refactor tree) vs AFTER: `diff` exit 0, empty output, 43/43 equal. Script was throwaway, not committed.
- Declaration-header audit: all 15 `export function …(params): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {` blocks byte-identical old vs new.
- Comment audit: occurrence counts of all issue-tag comments unchanged.

## Verification

- Focused suites: `tests/launcher.test.ts` 282 ✓ · `launcher-gemini-family` 28 ✓ · `launcher-plugin-mode` 9 ✓ · `codex-overlay-env` 15 ✓ (0 fail)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · tsup build OK

Follow-up per #1440 P3 after this lands: nothing further in the env family (pi/claude-plugin are the honest bespoke remainder); remaining P3 items are the `runLaunch` per-client copies and the plugin-install XInstall/XRemove registry — larger, separate PRs.


---

## Rebase note (master moved past v0.1.187)

Rebased onto `95ad8d25` — **clean, zero conflicts** (master's launcher changes since our base are all outside the builder region). Second commit is a one-line gate fix: master's own `unused-exports` job has been red since #2268 (`PiSubagentChildSignal` internal-only) — same mechanical demote this repo already used for `codexRewriteInsertionIndex` at release time (`371b15b5`); separate commit so it can be cherry-picked/dropped independently. Re-verified post-rebase: gate exit 0 · tsc clean · tsup OK · launcher suites 334/334 (launcher / gemini-family / plugin-mode / codex-overlay-env).

author: homehood-bea[bot]
body:
## The problem

`minor` was the fourth rung of the household's ladder ([decision 0004](https://github.com/homehood-app/specs/blob/main/decisions/0004-four-roles-owner-organizer-member-minor.md)) and it narrowed nothing. Two pushes of this branch tried to fill it and both were wrong, in the same direction:

1. **A minor as a role that sees less.** Rejected: hiding a label is not a product rule.
2. **A minor as an account kind the household owns.** Rejected on two ordinary families. A child of separated parents lives in two homes, and "exactly one household" allows one. A child grows up, and "no conversion, ever" costs them everything they did.

Both failures of the second model have one cause. *Which household decides?* — which home holds the child's account, which home releases it when the child is ready. Every answer is bad, because a household is the wrong size of thing to be responsible for a person's identity.

This PR is Tiago's answer: take the account out of the household's hands and put it in a person's.

## What a minor is now

**Three household roles:** owner, organizer, member. Unchanged.

**A minor is a kind of account**, and **every minor account has exactly one guardian** — a full account, outside every household, that answers for it. [Decision 0006](https://github.com/homehood-app/specs/blob/spec/what-a-minor-sees-less-of/decisions/0006-a-minor-is-an-account-kind-not-a-household-role.md) supersedes 0004 and now carries the guardian.

**What the guardian decides:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Where the child belongs | They answer the invitation. A minor can be a member of any number of households |
| When the child leaves one | They remove them, and so can organizer authority in that household |
| When the child grows up | They make the account a full account. No household is asked |
| When the account ends | They delete it. Nobody else can |

**What the guardian does not get:** any authority inside a household, any authority over a task, and any sight of a household they are not a member of. They see the name of each household the child belongs to and that the child is a member. Nothing inside it — not the tasks, not the members, not who the owner is.

**What a minor keeps:** everything a plain member has, in every household, with nothing taken away. Every visibility restriction from the first push is gone and stays gone.

**Growing up keeps the history.** [Decision 0007](https://github.com/homehood-app/specs/blob/spec/what-a-minor-sees-less-of/decisions/0007-no-age-and-one-way-to-a-full-account.md) replaces "no conversion" with one upgrade: the same account gains an email address and a password, keeps every membership, every task and every comment, and stops being anybody's responsibility. One way only. The product still holds no age, and no rule depends on one.

## The five answers, each as a rule

| Your answer | Where it lands |
| --- | --- |
| One guardian per account | `accounts/rules.md` — **Every minor account has exactly one guardian** |
| The household invites, the guardian answers | `household/rules.md` — **Membership starts with an accepted invitation**; `03-invite-a-person`, `05-answer-an-invitation` |
| Organizer authority **and** the guardian can remove | `08-remove-a-member`, which now has the guardian as a second actor |
| The guardian decides the upgrade | `accounts/rules.md` — **A minor account becomes a full account once**; decision 0007 |
| The guardian sees nothing inside a household they are not in | `household/rules.md` — **A household is a closed boundary**; `tasks/rules.md` |

## Three calls I made that you did not say

1. **A guardian cannot resign, only hand the account on.** One guardian is a single point of failure, and the transfer is what makes it survivable — so `01-transfer-guardianship` is the first use case in the new module, and a guardian's own account cannot end while they hold a minor account. Without this, your "one guardian" leaves a child's account unreachable the day that person stops caring.
2. **A guardian can act on a membership inside a household they cannot see.** They can take their child out of the other parent's home without seeing one task in it. Deliberate, and stated in three places so it does not read like a leak. The consequence: a guardian who removes a child settles none of the child's work, so it waits for that household.
3. **The upgrade finishes with the child, not the guardian.** The guardian asks for it; it completes only when the account has an email address and a password of its own. Otherwise a guardian could flip a minor account to a full one and keep the credentials — a second identity they own. The guardian can start it and cannot complete it.

## One word I changed

The spec says **guardian**, not "responsible adult". "Adult" claims an age, and the product holds no age for anybody — we would be asserting something we never checked. "Parent" is the family vocabulary [0001](https://github.com/homehood-app/specs/blob/main/decisions/0001-household-and-two-member-roles.md) rejected. Guardian names a relationship between two accounts, which is what the product actually holds. Say the word if you want it read differently.

## One thing I would still argue

**One guardian, not several.** You chose one and it is written as you chose it, with the full argument for and against in 0006 and the cost first under *When to revisit*. My worry is the case that started this: a separated parent who cannot get their own child into their own home because the other parent will not answer. One guardian means every such decision runs through an ex-partner. Several equal guardians — the organizer shape, where no peer can remove another — would fix it, and nothing else in this PR would change.

## Out of scope, named rather than guessed

**How a minor account is created, and how a child signs in.** Still open, now with a clear owner: the new `accounts` module's out-of-scope list, and `HOM-4`. One question moved there in this push — how an owner addresses an invitation to a minor account, which holds no email address of its own. One question disappeared: whether a removed minor account should sit dormant. With a guardian holding it, removal is just removal.

## Where it lands

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `modules/accounts/**` | **New module.** `overview`, `domain` (guardianship and the three ways it ends), `rules` (four rules), and three use cases: transfer guardianship, make a minor account a full account, delete a minor account |
| `domain.md` | **Guardian** is a new concept; an account changes kind once; an invitation to a minor is answered by the guardian; a membership belongs to one household, a person does not |
| `users.md` | A **Guardian** persona; the minor persona rewritten |
| `modules/household/rules.md` | **A minor's memberships are their guardian's to decide** replaces the one-household rule; **Membership starts with an accepted invitation** is one door again; the closed boundary now names the guardian |
| `modules/tasks/rules.md` | A guardian is nobody in the work. Two households mean two separate sets of work |
| `03-invite-a-person` | A minor can be invited. It is delivered to the guardian |
| `05-answer-an-invitation` | The guardian answers, and does not become a member by answering |
| `06-change-a-members-role` | "Give the child more" is now: wait for the guardian, then promote |
| `08-remove-a-member` | The guardian is a second actor, and resolves nothing |
| `09-leave-a-household`, `10-delete-a-household` | A minor account survives both |
| `decisions/0006` | Rewritten with the guardian, the one-guardian argument, and the word |
| `decisions/0007` | Rewritten and renamed: the upgrade replaces "no conversion" |
| `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `templates/.../use-case.md` | The **By role** table gains a fifth **Guardian** row where a guardian acts |

Two notes for the board:

- **0006 and 0007 are rewritten in place, not superseded.** Neither has ever been merged, so there is

author: esengine
body:
Refs #12235 (item 2).

## Cause
A hook on a gating event (PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Claude-imported PermissionRequest) that cannot be evaluated was treated as absent, so the gate opened:
- a malformed `match` regex made `MatchesTool` return false, so the hook never ran (pinned as intended in `hook_test.go`);
- a spawn error mapped to `DecisionError`, which never sets `report.Blocked`;
- `marshalPayload` dropped the `json.Marshal` error, so e.g. invalid raw tool args produced empty stdin and the hook ran and passed.

(Timeouts and exit 2 already blocked on gating events; this makes the remaining three consistent with them.)

## Blast radius
- `internal/ext/hook`: `Run` now evaluates the matcher and payload with an error, records an unevaluable outcome (`Outcome.Cause`, wrapping `ErrInvalidMatcher` / `ErrSpawnFailed` / `ErrPayloadUnserializable`; `UnevaluableCode` gives the stable code), and blocks if the hook gates. `decideOutcome` blocks on spawn error for gating hooks. `MatchesTool` (now test-only) is replaced by `matchTool`.
- Model-visible reason is only structured facts (`hook_unevaluable code= step= event= scope= source= hook= match=`), run through `secrets.Redact`; the hook's stdout/stderr, command line and the regexp/OS error prose never reach the model. The user's notice still carries them.
- Observing events never block: a bad matcher or spawn failure is reported to the user as `DecisionError`.
- `Save` rejects an invalid matcher on tool-matcher events. The loader deliberately still loads such a hook: dropping it at load would reopen the gate; inspect/capdiag/serve already surface `invalid matcher` for it.
- Consequence to know: an invalid matcher on PreToolUse blocks every tool call (it cannot be known which ones it guards), including edits to the settings file; the user fixes it in the hooks settings UI.
- Reachability: needs a user-written hook that is broken (bad regex, unstartable shell/context file) or raw tool args that do not serialize. Severity is bounded by that; no real run reaching it was observed. This is a boundary change, not a reproduced incident. `internal/ext/hook` is not on the sensitive list, but I recommend `review` + `security_review`.
- Also covered (review follow-up): a project hook refused because its approval changed after loading (`refuseChangedHook`; the approval covers workspace scripts the command names, which the agent can edit) now blocks on gating events with cause `ErrApprovalChanged` (`code=approval_changed step=approval`), keeping `Refusal`; observing events stay `DecisionError`. Re-approving restores the hook.
- User-facing: new notice code `hook_unevaluable` (zh text in `notices.ts`) and the English detail ends with "Fix or remove this hook in the hooks settings."; `Save` errors now name the file, `hooks.<Event>[i]` and the matcher.
- Not changed: an ordinary `sh -c` 127 is still exit-code semantics (warn).

## Neighbouring behaviours tested
Unchanged approved hook runs, changed script blocks a gate and only refuses an observer, re-approval restores. Pass/exit 2/exit 1/timeout decisions (`decideOutcome` table, extended), multiple hooks (earlier hooks run, a non-matching hook is skipped, the unevaluable one blocks and later ones are held back), PromptSubmit, `Runner.PreToolUse` message, Save/DryRun/`ApproveSavedProjectHooks`, plugin matcher callers. Run with `-race -p 2`: `internal/ext/hook`, `internal/ext/pluginpkg`, `internal/assembly/boot`; plus `agent`, `control`, `serve`, `cli`, `capdiag`. `gofmt`, `go vet`, `make lint` (clean cache), `make check` clean, no baseline widened.
Tests that pinned the old behaviour were rewritten on purpose: the malformed-regex assertion ("should not fire") now asserts the matcher is reported as `ErrInvalidMatcher`, and the `spawn-error` row expects `DecisionBlock` for PreToolUse/UserPromptSubmit and `DecisionError` for observing events.
Failing first: the new hook-package tests failed 5 subtests on the old code (invalid matcher/PreToolUse, spawn/PreToolUse, spawn/UserPromptSubmit, payload/PreToolUse, payload/UserPromptSubmit); the boot effect test fails when `gates` is forced false ("the guarded write ran although its PreToolUse hook could not be evaluated").

## Why this layer
The hook package owns the hook verdict and is the only place that knows why a hook could not be evaluated; callers (agent, controller) already act on `Blocked`, so every frontend inherits the fix. `internal/assembly/boot/effect_hook_unevaluable_test.go` goes through `boot.Build`: the guarded `write_file` does not run, and the tool result the model receives carries `code=invalid_matcher`; the same bad matcher on PostToolUse does not stop the write.

author: gavmor
body:
Independent of #2/#4/#5/#6 — `repl.py` is untouched by all of them, so this targets `main`.

I claimed last round that "no library does interactive REPL dispatch." That was wrong without checking. The **standard library** has done it for decades (`cmd.Cmd.cmdloop`: *"Repeatedly issue a prompt, accept input, parse an initial prefix off the received input, and dispatch to action methods"*), and `cmd2` does it better.

## The complexity

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `run_repl` | **F (43)** | **B (10)** |
| worst in `repl.py` | F (43) | C (11) — `do_skill` |

`run_repl` was a 246-line while-loop of `startswith()` checks and `continue`s. Six branches became six `do_*` methods; `default()` takes the "not a command, send to the agent" path.

## Deleted outright

The hand-maintained `/help` block — a literal list of commands that could drift from the code implementing them. `help` is now generated from docstrings:

```
Cmd2 Commands
─────────────
alias  exit     macro  quit          run_script  shortcuts  status
clear  help     new    reset         set         skill      tools
edit   history  q      run_pyscript  shell       skills
```

`help skill` prints the method's docstring. `history`, `alias`, `macro`, `shortcuts` arrive free.

## The threading constraint, and what it costs

cmd2's `cmdloop` raises `RuntimeError("cmdloop must be run in the main thread")` — it installs SIGINT/SIGHUP handlers — and reads through prompt_toolkit. Neither suits hosting an async agent.

cmd2 explicitly documents overriding it (*"You are free to override cmdloop"*), and `onecmd_plus_hooks` is the entry point `cmdloop` itself calls. So parsing, dispatch, hooks, history and help all still come from cmd2; only the ~10-line read loop is ours, with dispatch on `asyncio.to_thread` so commands can submit coroutines back.

**Cost, stated plainly: no interactive tab completion**, because we don't use cmd2's prompt. Getting it would mean inverting the threading model of the whole CLI (loop in a worker, cmdloop on main). Worth doing separately if completion matters.

## Interface preserved

A postparsing hook reparses `/status` as `status`, so slash commands work exactly as before. **The existing REPL tests pass untouched** — that's the evidence, not an assertion.

## LoC: this one goes the wrong way

**299 → 345. Plus 46.**

You asked two rounds ago to reduce LoC. This doesn't — one large function became a class of twelve small ones, and per-method signatures plus docstrings cost more than the deleted scaffolding. You've since said complexity is what you actually care about, so I've optimised for that: **−33 on the repo's worst function for +46 lines.** Judge it on that trade; I'm not going to dress it up as a line-count win.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest` — **60 passed**, no test changes
- `uv run ruff check src tests` — clean
- `help` / `help skill` / `exit` exercised directly (output above)

author: oharboe
body:
**Main's XSTile does not place without this.** On `584f090c` (#1184), detailed placement fails on 2 of 2,846,945 cells (DPL-0036): `core/backend/inner_ctrlBlock/dispatch/fpBusyTable/wire1755372` and `wire1919621`.

## Why
The resizer and CTS leave thousands of buffers inside the hard blocks' footprints, where there is no row. The legaliser can only find a cell a site within its 100 µm window, and those two were deeper. A diagnosis tree on an earlier failure, rerunning only that step, found 37,937 such cells, one of them 138 µm from a legal site. A ±150 µm window didn't finish in 90 min, and ±450 µm ground for 2 h.

## Change
`legalize_out_of_blocks.tcl`, as the XSTile parent's `PRE_DETAIL_PLACE_TCL`, `PRE_CTS_TCL` and `PRE_GLOBAL_ROUTE_TCL`, wraps `detailed_placement_helper`. Every legalization those stages run first moves each movable cell inside a hard block's box to just outside that block's nearest edge.

## Measured
| | KR: #1181 only (row 12) | main (#1184) | main + this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| parent | 3,162 ps | **fails to place** | **3,855 ps** |
| global route congestion | 21.6 % | | 25.2 % |
| blocks | Fe 2,170 · Mem 1,870 · L2 1,572 · Vec 1,479 · Flt 895 | same | same |

With the hook, the parent places (33,122 cells moved), clears CTS and global route. But it's **21.9 % slower than row 12**, and **that's an open question**: the regression could come from #1184 (the periphery left to the parent) or from this hook. KRh, row 12's configuration plus this hook alone, is running now and will say which; the result goes in a comment here. If the hook turns out to be the cause, this PR needs a different fix before it merges.

A miniature test (`test/planned_parent`: a cell moved deep into a block must legalize with the hook and fail without it) is not in this PR yet.
