author: neutrinic
body:
Closes #199

## Summary
The driver exported metrics only on the 60s interval or at shutdown, so a driver that died lost up to a minute of job, stage and executor-lifecycle metrics, and all of them in its first minute (lab: a driver killed 50s in exported none).

- `FlareDriverState` owns a `QuietPeriodAction`, as the executor plugin does: one per initialization, closed at shutdown and reset. `TracingSparkListener.onJobEnd` requests it, so the driver flushes 1s after its last job ends.
- Same throttle as executors (#139), sharing `FlareExecutorPlugin.IdleFlushIntervalMs` / `IdleFlushThrottledQuietMs`: within 30s of a flush the next needs 3s of quiet, so back-to-back jobs (173 in a 3-minute TPC-H-derived run) do not flush on every gap. 3s still beats a Databricks job cluster's teardown, about 8.6s after the last job.
- Docs: `exporting.md` and `volume.md` describe the driver flush and name `otel.metric.export.interval` for a JVM killed while still busy, which no idle flush covers (the Lakeflow timeout case on #199).

Found on the way, left out of scope: without the agent, `TelemetryFlush`'s plain-SDK fallback never matches, because `GlobalOpenTelemetry` wraps the SDK it is given. The agent path, which deployments use, is unaffected. So the test injects the flush action rather than observing an SDK export.

## Test plan
- [x] `FlareDriverStateTest`: three job ends in quick succession, no flush while they come, exactly one within 5s once they stop. **Fails with the listener's request removed**
- [x] `FlareDriverStateTest`: shutdown inside the quiet period stops the pending flush (thread gone, flush never runs), and a job end after shutdown starts none. **Fails with `closeIdleFlush()` removed from `endOpenSpans`**
- [x] `sbt test` 234/234 on 2.13.16 and 2.12.18; `AgentTest / test` 16/16

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Driver metrics are now flushed shortly after the last job ends, helping capture final job, stage, and executor metrics without waiting for the next scheduled export or shutdown.
  * Flushes may be delayed when another flush occurred recently, and metrics can still be lost if the JVM stops before a pending flush or while work is running.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated metrics guidance to cover driver and executor flush timing, unexpected termination, and how export frequency affects the window for unexported metrics.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: l4ci
body:
Closes #394

Adds `rota worker done <slot> [--base <ref>]`, the step before the PR. It exits 4 (`changed: false`, `data.missing`, hint naming `rota proof record`) unless the slot's item has a PASS proof row at the slot branch's current HEAD for `test.fast`. With the row it records the slot `done` and exits 0. When `test.fast` is unset it warns, sets `proofSkipped` and never refuses on that half.

A row counts when result is PASS, its sha abbreviates HEAD (7+ chars) and its check is either `rota test run fast` or each `test.fast` command as `rota proof record` writes it (`{files}` expanded). FAIL rows and PASS rows at an older sha do not count.

Contract entry in `docs/design/contract/workers.md` (+ README exit-4 list, `cli-helpers.md` row), worker-contract checklist step 4, smoke section 121, Go test `TestWorkerDone` (refuse, FAIL row, stale sha, accept, whole-tier row, unset test.fast, unknown slot).

Verification: `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/worker ./internal/config` green; `SECTION_LIST=test/sections/121_worker_done.sh bash test/runner.sh` green; `rota review scaffolding` clean. No RED row: the test and verb were written together, so the pre-change run was "unknown command", not a failed assertion. No frozen/golden records touched. Full gate not run (orchestrator's).

File scope: only the files the issue names plus `docs/design/contract/README.md` (exit-4 list) and `docs/reference/cli-helpers.md` (verb table). No overlap with #411's keys; did not touch `gate.go`, `train.go`, `ci.go`.

Worker tier: standard (sonnet)

## Approvals
None

## Rulings
- Accept `rota test run fast` as a whole-tier check alongside per-command rows — the contract tells workers to record that command, so refusing it would bounce compliant workers — cost if wrong: one-line change in `missingFastProof`.
- With several `test.fast` commands, require a PASS row for each — "the test.fast command" is singular in the ticket — cost if wrong: same one-line change.
- `worker done` writes `done` to the registry on every host, not only solo — the poll records the same state from the pane — cost if wrong: revert the PR.

Door: two-way. Blast radius: new verb and docs only; no existing verb changes behavior.

author: tagnabieouezena
body:
## Résumé

Défense en profondeur : la RLS n'est plus la seule barrière contre `anon`, et le comportement local est aligné sur la CI (donc sur la future prod). Origine : lors de la PR #9, le test « anon refusé » a échoué en CI seulement, parce que l'image Postgres du CLI de la CI accorde des droits par défaut à `anon` sur le schéma `public`.

Cette PR touche aux droits de **toutes** les tables : relecture et merge par Ouezz uniquement.

## 1. Version du CLI Supabase : 2.120.0, en local et en CI

- Avant : CI épinglée à 2.117.0 (image Postgres `17.6.1.167`), local en 2.115.0 (image `17.6.1.159`). C'est cet écart qui masquait le problème en local.
- Retenue : **2.120.0**, la dernière version stable disponible (installée en local par `brew upgrade supabase/tap/supabase`, image Postgres `17.11.0.004`). Raison : c'est la plus proche des défauts actuels de la plateforme ; avec elle le local reproduit exactement le problème de la CI (9 tables et 11 fonctions accordées à `anon`), et l'écart de version ne peut plus masquer un droit. La CI passe en 2.120.0 dans cette même PR, donc la CI verte la valide. La version attendue est documentée dans le `README.md`.
- Conséquence pour l'environnement : le stack local a été recréé (`supabase stop --no-backup` puis `start`), les données locales sont celles du seed.

## 2. Migration `20260928100000_durcissement_droits_anon.sql`

```sql
-- Durcissement : le rôle anon n'a aucun droit sur le schéma public.
-- Défense en profondeur : la RLS ne doit pas être la seule barrière contre
-- anon, et le comportement local doit être identique à la CI (donc à la
-- prod) quelle que soit la version du CLI Supabase, dont l'image Postgres
-- accorde des droits par défaut à anon sur les objets du schéma public.
--
-- Ne touche ni aux droits d'authenticated ni à ceux de service_role.

-- 1. Objets existants (tables, vues, séquences, fonctions du schéma public).
revoke all on all tables in schema public from anon;
revoke all on all sequences in schema public from anon;
revoke all on all functions in schema public from anon;

-- 2. Objets futurs : ils naissent sans droit pour anon. S'applique aux objets
--    créés par le rôle qui exécute les migrations (postgres).
alter default privileges in schema public revoke all on tables from anon;
alter default privileges in schema public revoke all on sequences from anon;
alter default privileges in schema public revoke execute on functions from anon;

-- 3. Fonctions : plus aucune n'est exécutable via le pseudo-rôle PUBLIC.
--    Une fonction Postgres est exécutable par PUBLIC dès sa création ;
--    anon en héritait donc malgré le revoke direct ci-dessus. Les droits
--    nécessaires sont accordés explicitement (idempotent : ils existent déjà
--    via les privilèges par défaut de l'image, mais ne doivent plus en dépendre).
revoke execute on all functions in schema public from public;

-- Fonctions appelées par les policies RLS (tables et Storage) et les vues :
-- évaluées avec les droits de l'appelant, donc authenticated en a besoin.
grant execute on function public.current_entreprise_id() to authenticated, service_role;
grant execute on function public.current_role_utilisateur() to authenticated, service_role;
grant execute on function public.is_super_admin_be_smart() to authenticated, service_role;

-- Les fonctions de trigger n'ont besoin d'aucun EXECUTE pour fonctionner
-- (le droit n'est vérifié qu'à la création du trigger). Les RPC applicatives
-- (creer_entreprise_et_ceo, dupliquer_charges_fixes_mois_precedent,
-- ecarts_mensuels, creances_situation, creances_balance_agee,
-- seuil_ecart_significatif) ont déjà leur grant explicite à authenticated.

-- Futures fonctions : naissent sans EXECUTE pour PUBLIC. La forme
-- « in schema public » ne suffit pas : Postgres n'y retire pas le droit par
-- défaut GLOBAL (EXECUTE pour PUBLIC sur toute fonction créée), il faut donc
-- la forme globale, limitée au rôle qui exécute les migrations (postgres).
-- Elle ne touche ni les schémas gérés par Supabase (autres propriétaires) ni
-- les fonctions existantes.
alter default privileges in schema public revoke execute on functions from public;
alter default privileges for role postgres revoke execute on functions from public;
```

Les droits d'`authenticated` et de `service_role` ne sont pas touchés : comparaison des ACL (`information_schema.role_table_grants` + `routine_privileges`) pour ces deux rôles avant et après la migration : **186 lignes, `diff` vide**.

## 3. Audit ajouté à `supabase/tests/isolation_multi_tenant.sql`

Échoue si `anon` a un droit explicite (`role_table_grants`, `routine_privileges`) ou effectif (`has_table_privilege`, `has_sequence_privilege`) sur une table, vue, séquence ou fonction du schéma `public`, et vérifie qu'une future table, vue, séquence et fonction (créées dans le test, annulées par `ROLLBACK`) naissent sans droit pour `anon`. Une future migration qui réintroduirait un droit fait donc échouer la CI.

## 4. Preuve avant / après

**Avant la migration** (droits présents), erreur de l'audit, en local avec le CLI 2.120.0 :

```
ERROR:  DROITS ANON SUR TABLES/VUES :
   budgets_mensuels [DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE]
   categories [DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE]
   entreprises [DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE]
   lignes_charge_prevue [DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE]
   lignes_revenu_prevu [DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE]
   objectifs_ca [DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE]
   transactions [DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE]
   utilisateurs [DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE]
   v_budget_mensuel_totaux [DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE]
```
(`creances` n'y figure pas : déjà révoquée en PR #9. Côté fonctions, 11 fonctions du schéma avaient `EXECUTE` pour `anon`, dont `creer_entreprise_et_ceo`.)

**Sans la migration, la CI échoue** : le commit de test seul (première version de cette PR) a donné une CI rouge sur l'étape « Test d'isolation multi-tenant » :

```
psql:supabase/tests/isolation_multi_tenant.sql:241: ERROR:  DROITS ANON SUR TABLES/VUES : budgets_mensuels [DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE] ; categories [...] ; ...
##[error]Process completed with exit code 3.
```

**Après la migration** : droits `anon` sur les tables/vues = 0, sur les fonctions = 0, l'audit passe (y compris le contrôle des futurs objets). Vérification par l'API REST réelle :

- `anon` : `GET /rest/v1/transactions`, `/entreprises`, `/creances`, `/v_budget_mensuel_totaux` → **401, code 42501 (permission denied)** ; `rpc/creer_entreprise_et_ceo` → fonction introuvable (non exposée à `anon`).
- Comptable A connecté : `transactions`, `creances` et `rpc/creances_situation` répondent normalement (200).

## 5. Régression

`supabase db reset` (10 migrations + seed), les 7 scripts SQL, le test de concurrence à deux sessions, `tsc --noEmit`, `lint`, `build` : tout passe en local.

## 6. Suites demandées en relecture (commit `005558f`)

### 6.1 Inscription : quelle fonction, appelée quand ?

`anon` ne voit plus **`creer_entreprise_et_ceo(p_nom, p_secteur, p_nom_utilisateur)`** (elle avait `EXECUTE` pour `anon` par les privilèges par défaut de l'image ; la migration d'origine ne la donnait qu'à `authenticated`, mais le droit `anon` hérité de l'image subsistait). Elle commence d'ailleurs par `if auth.uid() is null then raise exception`. L'inscription n'a donc besoin d'aucun droit pour `anon` : rien à corriger.

author: konard
body:
Caught virtual `exit 7` failures previously populated stderr with `Command failed with exit code 7` and mirrored that text to the parent process. Under `set('e')`, even `exit 0` rejected. This change makes both statuses silent and lets successful exits resolve.

Fixes #213.

## Changes

- Throw only for nonzero statuses, with explicit empty stderr. The runner retains the existing status aliases and decides whether to reject according to errexit.
- Remove the exit handler's dependency on global shell settings.
- Preserve sequence stopping after a failing exit under errexit, including when capture is disabled; unexpected virtual-handler failures still report their diagnostic stderr.
- Add eight regression tests to the existing Bun suite and Node 22/24/26 CI jobs.
- Add a reusable reproduction and a patch changeset for the next npm release.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

```sh
node experiments/issue-213/virtual-exit.mjs 2>stderr.txt
bun experiments/issue-213/virtual-exit.mjs 2>stderr.txt
node --test js/tests/virtual-exit.test.mjs
bun test js/tests/virtual-exit.test.mjs --timeout 10000
```

Before implementation, six of eight tests failed under both runtimes. The nine-case probe showed bogus stderr for caught nonzero exits and rejected status 0 under errexit. After the fix, all observations have empty stderr and `stderr.txt` is empty. `exit 7` rejects under errexit, while `exit 0` and argumentless `exit` resolve. A real child process provides the silent-status comparison.

Tests also verify result/error status aliases, output and exit events, stopping a sequence after `exit 3`, default mirroring, disabled mirroring/capture, non-errexit results, and unexpected-handler diagnostics.

## Validation

- Focused Bun suite: 61 passed; Node exit regression suite: 8 passed.
- Existing Node regression suites plus the new exit tests: 104 passed.
- `bun run check`: ESLint, repository formatting, duplication, and TypeScript declarations passed.
- Documentation/workflow regression checks: 386 passed.
- All 29 executable features agree under Node and Bun and run in Rust.
- Full Bun suite: 2,574 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed across 153 files.
- Full Rust suite, including doc tests: 830 passed, 5 ignored, 0 failed.
- Node zx compatibility: 490 passed, 2 skipped; Execa compatibility: 38 passed.
- Generated documentation and changeset/version validation passed.
- All seven CI workflows pass on `f9f55a0`, including Bun on Linux/macOS/Windows, Node 22/24/26, process-tree checks, security, quality, dependency freshness, executable parity, and benchmark smoke checks: [JavaScript checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/37572496651).

The first macOS Node 24 process-tree job observed one extra heartbeat byte (`6 !== 5`) in the existing `exec: stubborn` test at `js/tests/windows-tree-kill.test.mjs:87` (preserved run log, line 1806). Its 19 tests passed on a single rerun of the same commit: [successful rerun](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/37572496651/job/112635408432). The initial failure and rerun logs are preserved in `ci-logs/`. The new exit regressions passed in every runtime job on the first attempt.

## Scope and release

This is JavaScript-specific and carries `parity-exempt`: Rust's exit handler already returns the requested code with empty stderr. Executable language parity remains enabled. Existing argument parsing and non-errexit sequence behavior are preserved; full POSIX shell termination semantics are outside this issue's fix.

`js/.changeset/issue-213-virtual-exit.md` prepares the next patch release. Package versions remain managed by the release workflow.

  - `.github/workflows/js.yml`

author: hardcoreerik
body:
## What this changes
- **Home tunes the whole range.** Rotating the knob sends step counts; the Tab5 applies the step and raster of the band it is in, so a spin that crosses a band edge changes step and snaps to the next band's raster.
- **Home shows what it is tuned to.** Common band name (FM RADIO, 70 CM HAM, AIR BAND...), mode, frequency, step and volume, over a decorative waveform.
- **Controls.** Press cycles frequency, step and volume. A long press (0.9 to 4 s) opens the dashboards. Tapping the mode area cycles NFM, AM, WFM, USB and LSB.
- **Direct tuning keypad.** A long press on the frequency opens a numeric keypad (24 to 1766 MHz); TUNE sends an absolute tune that the Tab5 validates again.
- **Protocol.** The band id (Tab5 band profile id + 1) rides in the previously reserved packet byte 7. No version bump: an older Tab5 sends 0 and the Dial shows "RADIO".

## Testing
- Host tests: controller and protocol tests updated (Home step counts, focus order, band byte round trip).
- `pio run -e dial` builds. Flashed on COM14 and exercised against a Tab5 running the matching OrcSDR branch (`claude/home-smart-vfo`, not yet merged): linked, tuned, changed mode, keypad tune, survived an unplug and reboot.

## Notes
- Needs the matching Tab5 firmware: an older Tab5 rejects Home tuning commands (it only accepts them on tunable dashboards), so Home on the Dial will not tune against it.
- The band names table (`src/band_names.hpp`) must match the Tab5's band profile ids; OrcSDR's host test checks this.

author: rollroyces
body:
## Summary

Adds v0.5.0: the **write-side counterpart** to the existing read-side `WorksheetClient` / `AsyncWorksheetClient`.

- `WorksheetWriter` (sync) — `add_rows` / `update_rows` / `upsert_rows` / `delete_rows`
- `AsyncWorksheetWriter` (async) — same four operations, dispatched concurrently with a shared `TokenBucket` (same plumbing as `AsyncWorksheetClient`)
- 4 input formats per call: `List[Dict]`, `pandas.DataFrame`, `pyarrow.Table`/`RecordBatch`, file path (`.csv` / `.tsv` / `.json` / `.jsonl` / `.ndjson` / `.parquet` / `.arrow` / `.ipc`)
- Rows chunked at `batch_size` (default 500, hard cap 1000 — matches the documented read-side `MAX_PAGE_SIZE`)
- Shares `RetryPolicy`, `compute_backoff`, `parse_retry_after`, `Retry-After` honoring, and `TokenBucket` rate-limiting with the read side

## Commits in this PR

1. **`fecabed`** — `feat(errors): add NocolyWriteError + WriteValidationError + WriteBatchError`
2. **`2d715a6`** — `feat(writer): add sync WorksheetWriter with add/update/upsert/delete`
3. **`d9131d5`** — `feat(async-writer): add AsyncWorksheetWriter + AsyncWriteConfig + public exports`

## What's new for users

```python
from nocoly_explorer import WorksheetWriter, AsyncWorksheetWriter
from nocoly_explorer.auth import CredentialPair

# Sync
writer = WorksheetWriter(
    host="https://nocoly.example.com",
    worksheet_id="ws_123",
    credentials=CredentialPair(app_key="...", app_sign="..."),
)
writer.add_rows([{"id": 1, "name": "alice"}])
writer.upsert_rows([{"id": 1, "region": "HK"}], key_column="id")
writer.delete_rows(row_ids=[1, 2, 3])

# Async
async with AsyncWorksheetWriter(
    base_url="https://nocoly.example.com",
    auth_token="<app_key>:<app_sign>",
    worksheet_id="ws_123",
    batch_size=500,
) as writer:
    await writer.add_rows(my_pandas_dataframe)
```

## Tests

- **52 new tests** across `tests/test_writer.py` (30) and `tests/test_async_writer.py` (22)
- **Full suite: 362/362 passing** (`python3 -m pytest tests/`)

Coverage:
- All 4 operations (add / update / upsert / delete)
- All 4 input formats including CSV/JSONL file paths
- Batching chunk boundaries
- `fail_fast=True` (raises) vs `fail_fast=False` (collects failures)
- 429 `Retry-After` honoring
- 5xx retry with exponential backoff
- 4xx non-retriable
- HAP header verification on the async path
- Cooperative cancellation (`cancel_check`) on async
- Endpoint override (per instance `*_endpoint=` argument)
- Error inheritance chain (`WriteValidationError` → `WriteBatchError` → `NocolyWriteError`)

## Caveat (honest gap, called out in README)

The default endpoint paths (`/rows`, `/rows/upsert`, `/rows/delete`) and payload shapes (`{"rows": [...]}`, `{"rows": [...], "keyColumn": ...}`, `{"rowIds": [...]}`, `{"filter": ...}`) are **educated guesses**. Nocoly v3 only documents the read endpoint `POST /api/v3/app/worksheets/{id}/rows/list` in this repository. The auth headers and HAP-AppKey/HAP-Sign shape match the read side which **is** verified against the documented contract.

All endpoints are overridable per instance:
```python
WorksheetWriter(..., add_endpoint="/api/v3/app/worksheets/{worksheet_id}/rows/create")
AsyncWorksheetWriter(..., delete_endpoint="/api/v3/app/worksheets/{worksheet_id}/rows/bulk-delete")
```

A new "Write endpoints" bullet has been added to the README's "Honest gaps" section so users see this caveat before relying on the defaults.

## README

New section "Writing rows back to a worksheet (`WorksheetWriter`) (v0.5.0)" added between Layer 2 and Layer 3, covering:
- Operation matrix (add/update/upsert/delete with required args)
- All four input formats
- Sync example, async example
- Error model (`WriteValidationError`, `WriteBatchError`, `fail_fast=False`)
- Endpoint override caveat

## Files changed

```
 README.md                            | 148 ++++++++++
 src/nocoly_explorer/__init__.py      |  28 ++
 src/nocoly_explorer/async_writer.py  | 491 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 src/nocoly_explorer/exceptions.py    |  66 +++++
 src/nocoly_explorer/writer.py        | 538 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 src/nocoly_explorer/writer_inputs.py | 167 +++++++++++
 tests/test_async_writer.py           | 474 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 tests/test_writer.py                 | 445 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 8 files changed, 2357 insertions(+)
```

## Breaking changes

None. All additions are backward-compatible: existing imports and APIs are unchanged. The exception hierarchy gains three new subclasses that existing `except NocolyError` handlers will continue to catch (they live under `NocolyError` → `NocolyWriteError`).

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`12.8.1` → `12.8.2`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/12.8.1/12.8.2) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/12.8.2?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/12.8.1/12.8.2?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v12.8.2`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.8.2): pnpm 12.8.2

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.8.1...v12.8.2)

pnpm 12.8.2 fixes a startup crash on Linux ppc64le and `UnknownIssuer` errors on systems without CA certificates. `pnpm run` no longer installs before every script on CI when `autoDedupe` is enabled, and resolution and hoisted installs on macOS are faster.

##### Patch Changes

##### Platforms and environments

- Fixed pnpm crashing on startup on Linux ppc64le [#​16380](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16380).

- Fixed installs failing with `UnknownIssuer` on Linux systems without CA certificates, such as `node:24-slim`, when `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is set. The extra certificates now extend the bundled CA roots [#​16365](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16365).

- pnpm now creates its store operation locks and other per-user lock files in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` when it points to a directory only the user can write to. Otherwise, pnpm still uses `/tmp` on Linux and macOS. Sandboxes that block writes to `/tmp` can point `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` at a writable directory [#​16390](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16390).

- POSIX bin shims and the `pnpm`, `pn`, `pnpx`, and `pnx` launchers now run inside a Nix build, where the system default path holds none of the utilities they call. Installing again replaces the shims already in `node_modules` [#​16377](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16377).

- In a project that pins another pnpm version, pnpm now passes a command with an option it does not know to the pinned version. Before, pnpm rejected the option before switching, so `pnpm install --auto-dedupe` failed with "Unknown option" even though the pinned pnpm supports it [#​16353](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16353).

##### Installing and resolving dependencies

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now fails when `Cargo.lock` does not satisfy a dependency requirement in `Cargo.toml`. The error names the crate and the version the lockfile holds [#​16355](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16355).

- `pnpm install` returns "Already up to date" again in a workspace with injected workspace dependencies and a shared lockfile. Since 12.7.0 every repeat install in such a workspace ran the full install and copied the injected projects again.

- With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a fresh `pnpm install` now records a workspace dependency as `link:` when its injected copy differs from the project only by an optional peer that peer-dependent dedupe merges. It was recorded as a peer-suffixed `file:` copy [#​16354](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16354).

- `pnpm dedupe --check` now passes right after `pnpm dedupe` when deduplication merges variants of a package that differ only in their peers. A lockfile key whose peer suffix named a merged variant now names the variant that replaced it [#​16356](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16356).

- When `minimumReleaseAge` hides the version that `latest` points to, pnpm now falls back to a prerelease of the same major before a stable version of an older major. A stable version of the same major is still preferred. Before, while a new `1.0.0` was too new, `latest` fell back to an old `0.0.1` even though `1.0.0-beta.4` had been `latest` until then [#​16388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16388).

- Git-hosted dependencies now respect `pmOnFail`. If it is set to anything other than `download`, a git-hosted dependency that pins a pnpm version is prepared by the running pnpm, and pnpm does not download the pinned version [#​16376](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16376).

- pnpmfile hooks such as `readPackage` now run once for a dependency that several packages request at the same time. They could run twice for it before.

- `childConcurrency` now defaults to 5, the documented value. It used to be capped at 4 and to follow the host's CPU count.

##### Running scripts

- `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` no longer install dependencies before every script on CI when `autoDedupe` is enabled. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now keeps the deduplication record left by an earlier install [#​16374](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16374).

- On macOS and Linux, lifecycle scripts and `pnpm run` now always get `PATH` from the `PATH` variable. When the environment also held a `Path` variable, a script sometimes got `Path`'s value, and failed with `node: not found` [#​16308](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16308).

- `pnpm run` now exits after a `SIGTERM` in a container where pnpm is PID 1 and the script runs pnpm again, as `"start": "pnpm serve"` does. Since 12.6.0 it kept waiting after the script had shut down, until the container runtime killed it.

##### Other commands and settings

- `pnpm config get globalShims`, `pnpm shim list`, and global installs no longer read `globalShims` from a project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Only the global config file, the pnpm home's own `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and `PNPM_CONFIG_GLOBAL_SHIMS` set it, so a repository cannot choose which globally installed packages get project-aware shims.

- `pnpm config set --location=project` refuses a machine-level setting such as `stateDir` or `scope` with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_SET_NOT_A_PROJECT_SETTING`, which names where the setting belongs. `pnpm config delete` still clears such a key from a project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

- `pnpm deploy` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_DEPLOY_AMBIGUOUS_PEER` in a workspace with `injectWorkspacePackages: true` when a workspace package lists its peer dependency as a dev dependency too [#​16375](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16375).

- `pnpm deploy` no longer copies the workspace root's `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` fields into the deployed `package.json` [#​16403](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16403).

- `pnpm publish` now includes bare `README` files and README files with Markdown extensions such as `readme.markdown` in registry metadata [#​12704](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12704).

- `pnpm store prune` now removes the packages that only expired `pnpm dlx` cache entries used. They were left in the store until the next `pnpm store prune` [#​16383](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/16383).

##### Performance

- Sped up dependency resolution in large workspaces, and when many dependencies request different ranges of the same package. Resolution also uses less memory.

- Sped up `pnpm install` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` on macOS when the lockfile is re-resolved, such as with `autoDedupe` enabled [#​16397](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16397).

- Sped up extracting package tarballs.

- `pnpm install` without `--frozen-lockfile` is faster on some machines in projects with a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Those installs linked with one worker thread per core, half of what a frozen install uses.

- On Windows, warm `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` runs are 4-5% faster on 4- and 8-core machines. pnpm now links with one worker thread per core on Windows, between 4 and 16. This changes frozen installs and installs in projects without a `pnpm-wor

author: sonystone
body:
Stacked on #12. Brings the inspector's fields to GodSVG's behavior.

## Changes
- **Expressions** in number fields: `10*3+2`, `-2.2 + 4`, `sqrt(2)`, `max(1, 4)`, `tau/4`, comma decimals — a safe recursive-descent evaluator (no `eval`) with GodSVG's constants and the Godot math functions that make sense here. Invalid text puts the previous value back; values with units or `%` are kept; results are clamped to the attribute range.
- **Set vs unset**: unset attributes show an empty field with the inherited value (propagated attributes from the nearest ancestor) or the element default as placeholder; a set value equal to it is shown as redundant (warning color). Enum selects get a "(default)" entry; color swatches show the inherited color.
- **Opacity sliders** for 0–1 attributes: GodSVG's gauge beside the field, vertical drag in 0.01 steps (one undo step per drag), arrow keys. The card's native drag no longer steals the gesture.
- **id validation** while typing (GodSVG rules); invalid ids are not committed.
- Attribute rows keyed by name, so fields keep focus and pointer capture across edits.
- Fix: color swatches never showed their color (a color as the first `background` layer invalidated the declaration).

## Verification
- 70 unit tests (expression evaluator incl. rejection cases, id rules, ancestor/inheritance lookup, unset attributes)
- Chrome: placeholders `fill=blue` from `<g>` and `stroke=red` from the root, redundant `stroke-width=1` flagged, `10*3+2` → 32, invalid text reverted, slider drag 0.8 → 0.5 then one undo, invalid id refused, swatch shows the inherited blue

Tafuta Kazi stage goes from placeholders to live Supabase-backed job browsing:

- **Soma zaidi / Omba as Stages**: dynamic `job_detail:{id}` / `job_apply:{id}` payloads; detail shows full description (capped at 1000 chars for the 1024 message limit); **Omba shares the poster's contact** (`✅ … Phone:+255…` from new `created_by_phone` column) as button-less text and **clears Redis state**, so the next free text starts a fresh get-started menu while old card buttons keep working statelessly.

Completes the Tafuta Kazi branch scope: searchable, browsable, appliable job listings over WhatsApp with working pagination, replacing all placeholders.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm test` 40/40 pass.
- Live against production WABA: carousels delivered+read, Tizama pagination verified, Omba confirmation delivered, post-clear fresh menu verified. (Also survived real Meta rejections along the way: 139000 integrity, 131009 card-length, 131053 dead banner.)

## Follow-ups

- #3 — proper full-text/typo-tolerant search (current ILIKE matching is naive).
- `Omba` write path to `applicants[]` once identity mapping exists.

author: olinesn
body:
## Problem

Moving a view to another session (`moveVideosToSession`, `ui/sessions-panes.js`) removes that camera from every group in the origin session and re-triangulates each group from the remaining views.

On a lazy project, a group member on a frame that isn't loaded in memory is a `_lazy2d` placeholder, and its 2D reads as all-NaN. That was already true after a lazy reopen. Since #280 it is also true after Track All and Triangulate All.

Triangulating placeholders produces no 3D, so each such group:
- silently **kept its old 3D**, which was still solved with the view that had just moved;
- and was still marked clean.

No error was raised, and a later save writes the stale 3D.

## Fix

Before re-solving a frame whose groups lose the view, the function now loads that frame's members' 2D from the store (`hydrateFrameMembers2d`). After the re-solve it gives the 2D back (`releaseFrameMembers2d`). This is the same pairing the image ID-switch check already uses. Eager sessions and frames already in memory are unaffected, because both helpers do nothing there.

**Unchanged, and now documented in MODULES.md:** the function's first step moves the camera's 2D only for frames currently in memory. That camera's 2D for every other frame stays in the origin session's lazy store. This limitation predates #280.

## Test

`tests/e2e/move-video-lazy-members.mjs` (new):
1. Builds a synthetic project: 4 calibrated cameras, 2 animals, 300 frames. Its stored 3D deliberately doesn't match its 2D, so keeping the old 3D and re-solving can never give the same answer.
2. Reopens it lazily, adds a second session, and moves one camera to it through the real "Move videos" modal.
3. Compares each sampled group's 3D with what the app's own solver gives from that group's real 2D without the moved camera.

| | Not in memory: groups re-solved | Kept stale 3D | In memory (current frame) | Members back to placeholders |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| without the fix | **0/10** | **10** | 2/2 | — |
| with the fix | 10/10 | 0 | 2/2 | 10/10 |

## Test runs

- `node tests/run-mjs-tests.mjs`: 34/34 files.
- `node tests/e2e/run-unit-tests.mjs`: 1619/1619.
- `tests/run-node.js`: identical to `main` (1133/1234, the same failures that already exist there).
- Playwright: 110/114. The 4 failures (`occlusion-roundtrip`, `reopen-project-calibration`, `session-video-scoping`, `switchsource-mediabunny-refresh`) need `sample_session/` videos that aren't on this machine. They fail the same way on `main`.

## Scope

**Question.** Is the release path complete and proven end to end before the first real run? That covers:
- the production runner from the bank to the public archive;
- the remaining publication-gate checks;
- the Stage63 precision setting;
- James's blocs;
- a full-size rehearsal.

Authorized by James on 2026-10-07. The coordinator's notes are applied:
- precision from Stage63 #91 (M = 16);
- the config file is shared with Stage70, and main, including #94's adoption and #96 Stage69, is merged;
- the rehearsal says which inputs are stand-ins;
- stand-ins are labelled synthetic and kept out of `public/`;
- the decision number is the next free one on main (D113).

**What it adds.**
- **Precision** (`config/nowcast-2026.json` `simulation`): 4,096 national draws × 16 layer replicates = 65,536 rows, with the precision wording from #91. `simulation.draws` and `precisionPolicy` are no longer pending.
- **Assembly.**
  - Layer replication (`replicates=M`). Local-party conditional locations are solved once per national draw by the frozen solver's exact-row reuse.
  - Grouped per-seat Sobol noise banks (a shared bank for election-wide keys), so memory stays bounded at 65,536 rows.
  - Bank schema 3: winner indices, party votes per national draw. Batch-means MCSE keeps each draw's replicates in one batch.
- **Gate completion.**
  - New Python check `nationalReconciliation`.
  - Staleness labels go into the snapshot's limitations.
  - TypeScript release gate (`src/release/releaseGate.ts`): model provenance, nowcast, `uncalibrated`, no unavailable seat, available seat layer and MMP, and every probability's MCSE ≤ the limit.
- **Publisher** (`src/release/publish.ts`, `cli.ts`; `npm run release:build`, `npm run release:publish`).
  - Bank → v2 snapshot → gate → append-only archive.
  - Writes nothing on failure and refuses a duplicate id.
  - A model release goes only to `public/forecasts`; synthetic data never goes under `public/`.
- **Blocs (James).** NAT+ACT, NAT+ACT+NZF, LAB+GRN and LAB+GRN+TPM, plus hung-parliament scenarios in `seatLayer.summary.scenarios`. Each scenario has MCSE and is described as seat arithmetic:
  - `hung`: neither NAT+ACT+NZF nor LAB+GRN+TPM has a majority;
  - TOP kingmaker (either side);
  - only NAT+ACT+NZF with TOP;
  - only LAB+GRN+TPM with TOP.
- **Release settings** (`release`): MCSE ≤ 0.01, reconciliation ≤ 1.0pp, staleness 14/60 days. These are proposals; `release.policyApprovedBy` is pending, so the gate fails closed until James approves.
- **Rehearsal** (`scripts/release_rehearsal/run.py`) and a deterministic report `data/processed/release-rehearsal/report.json`.
- **Other changes.**
  - `scripts/nominations_2026/synthetic.py` (the shared stand-in roster).
  - `.gitignore` gains `node_modules` as a file (the cause of the Stage74 symlink slip) and `.release-build/`.
  - Docs: `docs/stage77-release-steps.md`, export contract, spec §2/§9, checklist items 10–14 and the gate section.
  - Fragment `handoff.d/2026-10-07-stage77.md` (changelog, state, D113, roadmap).

**Not done.**
- No real release.
- No Stage69 adoption (James's decision).
- No UI for the new fields.
- The release settings are proposals.
- No change to frozen stages, `data/sources.json` or CI.

## Findings and recommendation

**Rehearsal at production size.**
- **Real inputs:** the adopted Stage70 7 October refresh, the Stage64 baseline, the Stage72 scales and D107, the Stage75 fit, and Stage66 for the three polled Māori seats.
- **Labelled synthetic stand-ins:** the candidate list, the classification, the four unpolled Māori seats and the MMP rules label.

**Results.**
- 65,536 rows; 71/71 seats.
- Python gate: all structural checks pass (reconciliation 0.373pp against 1.0pp). It fails only `configComplete` (pending decisions) and `provenanceLive` (synthetic), as it should.
- TypeScript release gate at MCSE ≤ 0.01: passes, published to a gitignored archive and read back by the site loader.
  - 390 probabilities. The largest MCSE is 0.0051 (Opportunity qualifying by party vote, a national-driven quantity, ESS about 2,900).
  - Snapshot 0.63 MB; bank 10.4 MB.
- Runtime: 31.5 minutes on 4 cores, with the Stage76 speed-up included; publishing takes 7 seconds.
- No rehearsal figure describes 2026 seat outcomes.

**Recommendation.** The release path is ready. The first real run needs:
- the official roster (Stage50 part 2, after 8 October);
- James's classification, unpolled-Māori, rules-version and release-policy decisions;
- optionally, Stage69 adoption.

## Local validation

- Python: `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_stage50_nominations scripts.tests.test_stage72_nowcast_config scripts.tests.test_stage73_nowcast_assembly scripts.tests.test_stage74_nowcast_snapshot scripts.tests.test_stage75_candidate_fit scripts.tests.test_stage76_assembly_speed scripts.tests.test_stage77_release scripts.tests.test_weekly_refresh scripts.tests.test_historical_flag_isolation`: pass.
- `npm run test`: 140 pass. `npm run typecheck`: pass. `npm run build`: pass. `npm run check:dist`: no synthetic content in dist.
- `python3 -m scripts.nowcast_assembly.run --check` and `python3 -m scripts.nowcast_assembly.fixture --check`: reproduced.
- `python3 -m scripts.release_rehearsal.run`: run at full size. Its `--check` takes about 30 minutes, so it is local only.
- `npm run release:build` plus `release:publish` in rehearsal mode: published and read back.
- `python3 -m scripts.fold_doc_fragments --check`: valid. `python3 scripts/validate/source_files.py`: passed (926).
- Frozen selector with the attested runtime: all five `integrity`.
- Not run locally: the full Python suite (the changes are in the nowcast, release and rehearsal packages and their tests).

## CI and boundaries

New paths make Stage39 run in full once; no frozen replay. Earlier branch commits carry `[skip ci]` as work-in-progress checkpoints; the head does not. One intermediate merge commit was pushed with unresolved conflict markers in two files. It was never run by CI (no PR was open) and was fixed in the next commit, `1f63dc5`.

## Final published head and hosted validation

Head `4f0b73829ce4955f91970734b3b5490ca0e12b86`. [Verify run 37571977865](https://github.com/jamesfeng24/nz-election-model-2026/actions/runs/37571977865) passed:

The branch merges cleanly with main, and there are no review comments.

author: mitchross
body:
ArgoCD's `controller.sync.timeout.seconds` is 1800. On 2026-10-07 it terminated the geocoder sync at 03:43 and killed the `geocoder-initial-load` hook Job mid-load. That run committed 10 s before the kill, so 99,226,102 addresses are loaded now. Any later full reload would hit the same limit.

This PR removes the PostSync hook and runs `geocoder-ingest` hourly (`17 * * * *`) instead of monthly. Each run checks the source sizes and skips in seconds when nothing changed. A new or empty cluster still loads within the hour, without kubectl. These existing guards stay: `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`, the advisory lock (v0.1.5), and the 4 h `activeDeadlineSeconds`.

**Validation:**
- `kustomize build` passes.
- `gitops-risk-check.py` passes.

**Limitation:** each hourly run starts a pod that requests 4 CPU for a few seconds, and sends HEAD requests to census.gov and transportation.gov.

The choice the recommendation names comes first, labelled "Recommended:", and is preselected: it's the form's submit button, with `aria-pressed` and autofocus. Merged with main after GY-1408, which moved `park` into `src/cli/park-command.ts` and added ASK/STEP/WHY. GY-1408's WHY becomes the recommendation's one sentence of why. body:
## Repair update — 2026-10-07

Batch preclaiming marked notifications as possibly submitted before sending them, and inverted completion/sweep row locks could deadlock. This update claims one notification immediately before submission and uses notification-before-attempt locks. It also refreshes persistence inventory and rejects incomplete acceptance evidence.

- Current repair head: `69640dfa0529ee104d32bb481c4d06f71a378d9a`.
- Synchronized with `main@d41c63daac1c51175c89fc21a27d4c2f1181c17a` without rewriting PR history.
- Hosted acceptance passed: 26 domain/worker/Nest/HTTP specifications, 16 PostgreSQL delivery/lock-order regressions and the 338-test foundation integration suite, with no skipped tests.
- All 62 GitHub checks succeeded on this exact repair head, including the Foundation release gate, security, images and real infrastructure acceptance. Ready for the owner's final review and manual merge.
- All six repaired branches merge together locally without conflicts; the combined source passed 43 focused guard/inventory/acceptance-plan tests. This is local static evidence, not a deployed system.
- Existing business contracts, external providers and production-readiness blockers remain in scope as documented below. Readiness was not promoted; no automatic merge or deployment was performed.

<details>
<summary>Original implementation description and historical evidence (before this repair)</summary>

## P01-D2: Communications notification intent and delivery state

Child 2 of P01-D (Lane D). Parent status: **INTEGRATION_PENDING**. This is not a working SMS/push/email channel.

**Base** `f875d31bf62b153b6d36ac7a607949f8c4e29389` · **Head** `710a9e7` · **Tree** `b90cfb8`. It is independent of #97 (no stacking), and the shared runner file is byte-identical.

### What changes
- **Domain**: closed channels and states, validated requests (opaque recipient UUID, bounded parameters, TTL of at most 7 days), request fingerprint, full-jitter backoff, and submission/receipt/lease-expiry rules. **A timeout is `UNKNOWN`**, never success. It is resubmitted only when the provider is declared idempotent on our stable key `cw-notification:<id>`.
- **Application**: `EnqueueNotification` (idempotent on `(source_service, idempotency_key)`; a changed request is `CONFLICT`), `DeliveryWorker` (fence compare-and-set claims, deadline-bound submit, fenced completion), and receipts/cancel/find.
- **Infrastructure**: Prisma intake, which joins a caller transaction (the inbox seam), and repository; an HTTPS provider adapter with conservative classification.
- **Worker** `src/delivery/delivery.runner.ts` refuses to start without an explicitly declared provider. There is no fake production provider.

### Migration
`services/communications/prisma/migrations/20261007100000_p01d_notification_delivery_state`: additive only. CHECKs enforce states, channels, "lease only while SENDING", "provider id only when accepted/delivered/failed" and attempt outcome/finish consistency. Rollback: the previous build ignores the new tables.

### Evidence (exact head)
| Family | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Domain + real-socket HTTP provider + Nest specs | **PASSED** 40/40 (the worktree run includes the other D services' specs) |
| Real PostgreSQL (`run-real-infra.mjs`) | **PASSED** 13/13: idempotent and concurrent enqueue, inbox-atomic intent, accepted→delivered, timeout→UNKNOWN never resent, idempotent resubmission, attempt exhaustion, 4-worker claim race (each intent exactly once), stale-worker fencing, lapsed lease→UNKNOWN resolved by its own late answer, expiry/cancel, DB CHECKs via the runtime role, real HTTP adapter timeout end to end |
| layers / boundaries / append-only migrations / design reference / eslint / prettier | **PASSED** |
| Combined merge candidate D1+D2+D3 (`ab3ba45`) | **PASSED** 45/45 |

Real versus scripted: PostgreSQL and HTTP sockets are real. C4–C11 use a scripted `NotificationProvider` port (declared in each test) to force exact answers. No external provider was contacted.

### Security and privacy
Recipients are opaque references, never phone numbers or addresses. The token and recipient never appear in errors or logs, the worker logs counts and outcome kinds only, and the provider needs HTTPS (HTTP only on loopback).

### Remaining blockers / next consumer
- **External**: a real provider account, credentials, documented idempotency and verified receipts (signature verification belongs in its adapter); `UNKNOWN` reconciliation needs its lookup API.
- **E**: business event contracts/topology (CR-D-P01-04), `communications.read` plus a gateway route (CR-D-P01-01/05), deployment env for the worker.
- The next consumers are business producers (Booking/Billing) through accepted events, and the admin delivery view.

## 배경
2GB Lightsail 서버에서 `deploy.sh`로 이미지를 빌드하면 메모리 부족(스왑)과 CPU 크레딧 소진이 겹쳐 수십 분이 걸렸습니다(`Running TypeScript` 단계에서 37분 이상).

## 변경
### ① GitHub에서 이미지 빌드, 서버는 받기만
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: main 병합(및 `v*` 태그) 때 운영 이미지를 빌드해 GHCR에 올립니다. 태그는 `ghcr.io/ictact-coop/taeil-space:<커밋 SHA>`와 `:main`이고, GitHub Actions 캐시를 씁니다.
- `deploy/deploy.sh`: `.env`에 `REGISTRY_IMAGE`가 있으면 서버가 받은 커밋과 같은 이미지를 받습니다.
  - 이미지가 아직 없으면 30초마다 다시 시도하며 최대 15분(`PULL_WAIT`) 기다립니다.
  - 권한 오류는 따로 안내합니다.
  - `BUILD_ON_SERVER=1`이면 예전처럼 서버에서 빌드합니다.
  - 이미지 준비를 백업보다 먼저 해서, 이미지를 받지 못하면 백업·교체 전에 멈춥니다.
- `deploy/setup-server.sh`: GitHub 저장소면 `REGISTRY_IMAGE`를 자동으로 채웁니다. `env.prod.example`에도 이 항목을 넣었습니다.

### ② 이미지 빌드에서 타입 검사 생략
- `Dockerfile`이 `SKIP_BUILD_TYPECHECK=1`을 넘기면 `next.config.ts`에서 `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors`를 켭니다.
- CI의 `pnpm typecheck`와 일반 `pnpm build`는 그대로 검사합니다.

### 문서
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` 2.6(신규): 이미지 받기 권한 준비(패키지 공개 권장, 또는 `docker login ghcr.io`), 대기 동작, 서버 빌드 대안. 리허설 결과도 추가했습니다.
- `docs/DEPLOY_AWS.md`: 첫 배포·운영 표 갱신.

## 검증
- 운영 이미지 빌드: 108초, 타입 검사 단계를 건너뛰는 것을 확인했습니다.
- 로컬 이미지 저장소로 GHCR을 대신해 배포 리허설을 했습니다.
  - 첫 배포 26초(서버 빌드 없음)
  - 이미지가 아직 없는 커밋은 30초마다 다시 시도하다가, 올라오자 받아서 백업·교체 완료
  - 없는 이미지는 대기 후 백업 전에 멈추고 사이트는 계속 응답

- GitHub Packages의 `taeil-space` 패키지를 공개로 바꿉니다(또는 서버에서 `docker login ghcr.io`).
- 기존 서버의 `deploy/.env`에 `REGISTRY_IMAGE=ghcr.io/ictact-coop/taeil-space`를 추가합니다.

author: goyaladitay11
body:
## Summary

Preserves all fields of `functionResponse` (such as multimodal `parts`) and `functionCall` (such as `partialArgs` and streaming metadata) when `stripToolCallIdPrefixes()` removes tool name prefixes from IDs.

## Details

In `packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts`, `stripToolCallIdPrefixes()` stripped `<toolName>__` prefixes from `functionResponse` and `functionCall` IDs by manually reconstructing objects with hardcoded `{ name, response, id }` and `{ name, args, id }` subsets.

When `read_file` or other tools return multimodal payloads (images, screenshots, inline data), `convertToFunctionResponse` attaches them to `functionResponse.parts` if multimodal tool use is supported. Because `stripToolCallIdPrefixes()` reconstructed `newPart.functionResponse` without `parts`, all binary/image content was discarded prior to sending the request to Gemini / Vertex AI, causing models to hallucinate descriptions of unseen images. Similarly, extra fields on `functionCall` were dropped.

This PR uses object spread (`...fr` and `...fc`) to preserve all existing properties while updating the stripped `id`.

## Related Issues

Closes #29589

## How to Validate

Run unit tests:
```bash
npx vitest run packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.test.ts -t "stripToolCallIdPrefixes"
```

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [x] MacOS
    - [x] npm run

author: kesslerio
body:
## TL;DR

Your Mac now shows up in sparkDash as a first-class node with a **Mac** badge, a **Model runtimes** panel built from a data-driven inventory of the engines you actually start (`omlx`, `qflash`, `splash`, `mtplx` and its variants, the `:8200` mux, `tensorfold`, …), and tiles it genuinely cannot measure rendered as **unavailable** instead of a fake `0W`.

## What Problem This Solves

A MacBook joining a fleet of DGX Sparks is a different platform, and the dashboard had only ever read one platform. Two things went wrong:

- **Nothing about what is serving.** Reading a Mac over SSH yields vitals, but the one thing you want from a machine running your own inference engines — which engines are up, on which ports, serving which model — was invisible. You had to remember which `model-start()` function you had run.
- **Zeros that were not zeros.** A DGX-only tile read over SSH on a Mac reports `0W` or `0%`. Idle GPU, or a counter macOS only hands to root? The dashboard could not tell you, and neither could I.

A third problem surfaced while building it: the detection rules cannot live in code, because my engines are not yours. Anything hardcoded rots the moment a new launcher appears in `~/.zshrc`.

## Why This Change Was Made

An on-device agent is the only place that can answer "what is running here" honestly, so `agents/macos/` now ships a stdlib-only collector (optional `psutil`, nothing heavier — no pip install) that runs `--once` for debugging or `--serve` as a LaunchAgent, plus a plist and a one-line install.

Detection is data, not code. `agents/macos/runtimes.json` declares engines, ports, argv matchers, health paths, model flags, and watchdog roles — seeded from the owner's real model-start functions. Order is precedence, so the `:8200` mux is named `mtplx-mux` rather than whichever variant launched it, and a mux with no children reports `degraded` rather than "serving". **A listener no entry claims comes back as `other-runtime` with its own command basename — an unknown server is never renamed into an engine it merely resembles.**

Honesty is a wire format, not a UI trick. The agent emits `unavailable: [{metric, reason}]`, so macOS root-only counters (`gpu.power`, `gpu.utilization`, `cpu.power`, `ane.power`, thermal pressure) are *declared* instead of guessed. `MacAgentCollector` maps the snapshot onto the existing collector shapes — no panel needed a new data path — and keeps SSH as the fallback when the agent is not answering, with the runtime state explicitly reporting that fact rather than going blank.

Two build notes worth knowing:
- CPU usage uses `iostat -w 1 -c 2`, because macOS `top -l 2` blocks indefinitely when sampled from a pipe with no TTY — the agent hung on first contact.
- `powermetrics` runs only when already root or under passwordless sudo. On my laptop both fail, which is exactly why the "unavailable" path exists and is exercised by a fixture.

DGX Spark behaviour is untouched apart from carrying the new platform badge.

## User Impact

**Overview card** — Mac badge next to the cluster-role badge, `unavailable` where a DGX number would be, and a runtime row with port and model:

![Mac node on the overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kesslerio/sparkDash/refs/heads/fm/sparkdash-mac-node/assets/mac-node-overview.png)

**Mac node page** — GPU usage/power and CPU temperature/power say `unavailable`; the Model runtimes panel names both engines, their ports, and the model being served:

![Mac node detail page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kesslerio/sparkDash/refs/heads/fm/sparkdash-mac-node/assets/mac-node-detail.png)

From the dashboard's point of view nothing about a DGX changed. To add a Mac: add a Mac unit, tick "Mac node agent", set the port (8790 default), and install the LaunchAgent:

```
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) agents/macos/ai.onyx.sparkdash-mac-agent.plist
```

To teach sparkDash a new engine, add one entry to `runtimes.json`. No rebuild, no code.

## Evidence

Commands I ran, and what they returned:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `python3 -m unittest discover -s agents/macos/tests` | `Ran 24 tests … OK` — including parity against the SSH collector's own macOS fixtures, so both transports must agree on the same capture |
| `npm run test:server` | 675 tests, 674 pass, 1 fail: `fleet-energy.test.js` UTC-minute boundary, **pre-existing** (fails identically with this branch stashed) |
| `npx vitest run` | 79/79 pass. `metricsStore.test.ts` wall-clock case flaked once in four runs, unrelated to this diff |
| `npm run typecheck` | clean |
| `npm run build` | `✓ built in 633ms` |
| `python3 agents/macos/sparkdash_mac_agent.py --serve --port 8790` + live dashboard | `/health` → `{"ok":true,"schema":"sparkdash.mac-agent/1"}`; API reported `mtplx-mux` :8200 and `tensorfold` :8300 (`qwen3.8-27b`), `agentOnline: true`, `unavailable: [gpu.power, gpu.utilization, ane.power, cpu.perCore]` |

Live capture from the M5 Max, at the moment both screenshots were taken:

```json
{"runtimes": [
  {"name": "mtplx-mux", "port": 8200, "state": "serving", "detectedBy": "port+argv"},
  {"name": "tensorfold", "port": 8300, "model": "qwen3.8-27b", "state": "serving", "detectedBy": "port+health"}
 ],
 "unavailable": [{"metric": "gpu.power", "reason": "powermetrics requires root (run the agent as root or via sudo -n)"}]}
```

The unsupported-metric claim is proven twice: `MacAgentCollector.test.js` feeds a real M5 Max capture (`fixtures/mac/agent-snapshot.json`) through the collector, and `OverviewPage.macNode.test.tsx` renders that card and asserts `unavailable` with the node's own reason — and that no `0W` appears anywhere on it. The screenshots above are the same data through the real UI.

**Risk and Rollout:** the agent is opt-in and the collector falls back to today's SSH path whenever the agent is unreachable, so upgrading changes nothing until a Mac unit ticks the agent box. GPU counters stay unavailable unless the LaunchAgent is booted as root — that is a deliberate choice, not a TODO; the plist documents the swap. Two things I chose not to touch and am flagging: the existing SSH `MacSystemCollector` samples CPU with `top -l 1 -s 0`, which reports a single instantaneous sample rather than a window (the agent uses `iostat` for that reason), and the agent binds `0.0.0.0` with no auth, so port 8790 should stay on a trusted LAN.

author: chukeaa
body:
Worker rejected explicit targets solely because an exchange was Input or its exact Flow revision was Waste. This change accepts unique Input/Output targets whose authored exact UUID/version resolves to Product or Waste, using the same normal snapshot and Review overlay validation. Missing metadata, another revision, unknown/Elementary targets and malformed vectors still fail closed. Legacy shares, SparseZero, reference normalization, residual attribution and signed-flow linking remain unchanged.

Allocation semantics advance to `tidas-reference-allocation-v5`. Snapshot/source and Review fingerprints bind this marker; persisted artifacts are independently checked before new compute/reuse, and certificate input requires v5 in both requested and frozen scope. Historical v4 artifacts remain readable but cannot masquerade as newly validated v5 evidence.

Validation:
- `make check` (full workspace fmt, 17 Python qualification tests, Clippy and Rust tests), with escalation only for local loopback fixtures denied by sandbox.
- `cargo clippy -p solver-worker --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.
- 30 allocation semantic tests and 13 snapshot allocation regressions, including four Product/Waste direction combinations, exact revision versus wrong/latest metadata, signed pivots/residuals, no double allocation, malformed/legacy modes, v4 fingerprints/reuse and certificate input rejection.
- Hermetic synthetic Waste/Input → residual parsing → sparse HDF5/closure-binding roundtrip, immutable process identity `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000137`, snapshot `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000138`, exact Flow revisions `01.00.000`, expected biosphere coefficient 4.0. This verifies local compilation/artifact binding; no DB/S3 integrated runtime or deployed binary is claimed.
- Enforced Docpact lint and diff checks.

Rollout requires paired [Database #789](https://github.com/tiangong-lca/database/issues/789) and [Edge #454](https://github.com/tiangong-lca/edge-functions/issues/454); Worker must not deploy alone while those producers author/admit v4. No production operation, Process rewrite, deployment, restart, closure resubmission or calculation was performed. Source merge, exact workspace gitlink integration and deployed-runtime qualification remain separate steps.

Closes #311

body:
Closes #40.

The `temperature_to_vs` and `gadopt_loading_field` examples computed the isotropic shear speed as `sqrt((2 vsh² + vsv²)/3)`, which gives vsh the double weight. The Voigt average puts it on vsv, `sqrt((2 vsv² + vsh²)/3)`, as `voigt_vs` in `scripts/convert_seismic_models.py` already does. The same swap was in `temperature_to_vs/generate_expected.py` and, written with column indices, in `temperature_to_vs/generate_thumbnail.py`, so those are fixed too. The third place listed in the issue, the text of `tomography_models/demo.py`, turned out to be correct already, and so are `tomography_cross_section` and the tomography thumbnail script. The only remaining swapped formula is in `tests/test_dataset_fixes.py`, where it is used on purpose to build a non-Voigt field for a negative test.

The demo text now also explains where the weights come from. With L = ρ vsv² and N = ρ vsh², the Voigt shear modulus of a transversely isotropic medium is (A + C − 2F + 5N + 6L)/15, and since REVEAL only gives the S-wave speeds we use the S-wave form (2L + N)/3, which is what the full form reduces to when A + C − 2F = 4L.

Both `expected.pkl` files are regenerated, the gadopt one with the Firedrake environment. Only values that go through the isotropic speed change. At 200 km in REVEAL vsh is larger than vsv at most points, so the mean isotropic Vs drops from 4449 to 4397 m/s and the mean converted temperature rises by about 94 K. The maximum Vs goes up (4836 to 4940 m/s) and the minimum converted temperature drops from 1264 to 900 K, but both of those come from a single point at 45°S, 170°E where vsv exceeds vsh by about 800 m/s. In the gadopt example the converted temperatures move by 15 K in the mean and up to 140 K at the extremes. Running the generator with the old formula on the current code reproduces the old stored values exactly, so the formula is the only cause.

body:
## Problem

The optional usage payload queries singular post and board tables that do not exist. Its catch then reports zero scale brackets. Reporting also currently starts by default without an explicit opt-in.

## Solution

Require literal `ENABLE_TELEMETRY=true` before collecting or scheduling optional upstream reports, and keep `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true` or `1` authoritative. Bind all three count queries to the existing Drizzle schema objects.

## Changes

- Add the strict opt-in getter and preserve disable precedence.
- Correct schema-bound counts for users, posts and boards.
- Document the endpoint, cadence and actual payload categories in the existing environment example.
- Add consent and real PostgreSQL regression coverage with network sends intercepted.

## Validation

On VSH, with an isolated migrated loopback test database:

- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run apps/web/src/lib/server/telemetry/__tests__`: eighteen passed. The same tests against the original source produced thirteen failures and five passes, including PostgreSQL's missing-table error.
- `node node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js apps/web/src/lib/server/config.ts apps/web/src/lib/server/telemetry`: passed.
- `node node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs --check apps/web/src/lib/server/config.ts apps/web/src/lib/server/telemetry`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

PostgreSQL fixtures use temporary copies of the migrated schema and transaction-local synthetic rows. All fetch calls are intercepted. No actual telemetry endpoint call or production mutation was performed. Required repository CI and independent exact-head review remain release gates.

## Risk and rollback

Optional upstream statistics now require explicit opt-in, so existing installations stop sending by default after this source is deployed. Existing application functionality, UI, authentication and user data are unchanged. Restore only the prior source through a reviewed release if a regression is demonstrated; do not enable reporting as a rollback shortcut.

author: srgarciavel
body:
## Summary

Phase 5.3B adds the **SST Brand Flag**: a compact broadcast-style tab with the **official SST mark**, physically attached to the side of the overlay (`[ OVERLAY ][ SST ]` / `[ SST ][ OVERLAY ]`).

- **Modes:** a periodic tab (slides out, stays, retracts) or a fixed badge.
- **Access:** Creator Beta, behind the new independent entitlement `overlays.brandFlag`.

## Official assets

No new or approximated logo. The mark is the shared brand geometry (`components/brand/geometry.ts`, the same source as `public/brand/*.svg`):

- **monogram:** `<Monogram>`;
- **full:** the official lockup composition (monogram + divider + "Session Stats Tracker" in Barlow Condensed, as `<BrandMark variant="lockup">` / `sst-lockup.svg`), drawn with overlay CSS because the dashboard component uses Tailwind, which isn't CEF-safe.

It is inline vector: no image request, no base64. It uses the official **monochrome** form (letters only) in the overlay's text colour, so it is always legible. `colorMode` tints the tab's accent edge (theme accent, or the Creator secondary accent).

## Architecture

- **Structure:** `root > .ov-brand-row > [panel | rotation stage] + .ov-brand-slot > .ov-brand-flag`, only when enabled. Without it the DOM is exactly the pre-5.3B structure.
- **Containment:** the **slot** is static, reserved space (3.3em monogram / 8.4em full, scaling with the overlay). **Fit-to-box measures the panel (the 5.2 fix is preserved) plus the slot**, so panel + flag always fit the OBS canvas: the flag is never clipped and never covers a statistic.
- **No layout shift:** the **tab** moves with `transform`/`opacity` inside its slot (it emerges from behind the panel's edge), so nothing is re-measured while it animates.
- **Controller** `useBrandFlag`:
  - one `setTimeout` chain at most, independent of the live data, rotation, priority and Creator Motion;
  - schedule changes restart from hidden; cosmetic changes don't;
  - **"Probar aparición"** reveals through the same controller (a local preview signal).
- **Timing definition:** `intervalSeconds` is the time **between reveal starts**; the first reveal starts one full interval after the overlay appears. The static badge schedules nothing.
- **Animation:** slide / fade / instant (320 ms). Animations off or reduced motion ⇒ instant (also enforced in CSS).

## Config & entitlement

| Key | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | false |
| `mode` | timed-tab · static-badge | timed-tab |
| `position` | left · right | right |
| `intervalSeconds` | 30 · 60 · 120 · 300 | 60 |
| `visibleSeconds` | 2 · 3 · 5 | 3 |
| `animation` | slide · fade · instant | slide |
| `logoVariant` | monogram · full | monogram |
| `colorMode` | theme · creator-accent | theme |

- **Validation:** strict writes (no URLs, uploads, text or CSS); per-field safe defaults on read.
- **Entitlements:** stored vs effective and the save merge follow the existing Creator blocks.
  - A forged Free request is ignored.
  - Downgrade keeps the preferences; renewal restores them.
  - The public payload carries only the effective block.
- **Presets** carry it inside the Creator block (`statsScope` stays out).
- Integration-tested against Postgres. No migration.

## Builder

- **"Marca SST"** (Creator tab) with progressive disclosure:
  - only the switch while off;
  - frequency, visible time and animation only for the periodic tab;
  - a note when overlay animations are off;
  - logo and colour;
  - a note about the reserved space.
- Free sees it disabled with "Creator Beta requerido".
- **"Probar aparición"** appears in the preview for an effective periodic tab.

## Validation

- `pnpm typecheck` ✓, `pnpm lint` ✓, `pnpm format:check` ✓, `git diff --check` ✓.
- `pnpm test`: **76 files, 820 tests passed**, integration included.
- `pnpm build` ✓ (clean), `pnpm companion:build` ✓.

## Browser QA (production build, Chromium)

- **Builder** at 1440 / 1280 / 1024 / 768 / 390: no overflow.
  - Progressive disclosure verified; the save persists the block.
- **Probar aparición:** the tab goes out, then retracts after the visible time. Root font-size 27.6 → 27.6 → 27.6 px and panel width 695 → 695 → 695 px **before / during / after** (no re-fit, no layout shift).
- **Geometry:** six themes × supported canvases (600×120, 800×180, 900×240) × right/monogram, left/full (Creator accent) and right/full at 100 % zoom: **0 issues**.
  - Panel and slot always inside the canvas, the tab inside its slot, **0 px overlap** with the panel, mark ≥ 12 px.
  - A 1–3 px `scrollWidth` excess is the existing fit-to-box tolerance.
- **Long runs** (Playwright clock in 1 s steps, CDP after forced GC):
  - **without rotation:** 110 reveals in 3300 s, period between starts **exactly 30 s** (min = max); listeners 497 → 497, overlay DOM 51 → 51, one tab, heap 5.89 → 7.08 MB;
  - **with session-all rotation:** 109 reveals in the same window (first at 31 s), exact 30 s period, overlay DOM 53 → 53.

QA notes on measurement:
- Playwright's clock keeps flowing in real time after `install()`.
- React commits through `MessageChannel`, which the clock doesn't fake, so large `runFor` jumps under-counted reveals.
- At 1 s resolution the schedule is exact. The unit tests (fake timers) confirm the same semantics.

## Scope

- No changes to tracking, Companion, statistics algorithms, the SSE protocol, the DB schema, auth or billing.
- Phase 5.3A presentation semantics and Creator Motion detection unchanged.
- DB pool `max: 5`.
- No new dependencies.

## Docs

`docs/creator-overlays.md` (new section, including rollback SQL), `docs/overlay-builder.md`, `docs/creator-presets.md`, `docs/entitlements.md`, `docs/architecture.md`.

author: obra
body:
Fixes #3906

Last PR in the stack. This branch merges #3938 (the fold accepts several deliveries per call), #3941 (transcripts render earlier results) and #3945 (reply shape). Their commits leave this diff as each one lands. This PR's own change is in `agent/delegate_delivery.go`, `agent/delegate_runtime.go`, `agent/session_tools.go`, the tool description, and the tests.

## The bug

A delegate's earlier generation can finish while its parent is mid-turn, after the parent's last delivery flush. The parent then holds that result for its next round. If the parent's very next tool call is a `delegate_send` with `max_wait_ms` to the same delegate, three waits close a loop:
- the new generation's result queues behind the held one,
- the held one waits on the parent's tool round,
- the tool round waits on the new result.

The send sat out its whole wait and answered timed out, even though the delegate had finished. CI hit this by chance in `TestRunServeInterruptSettlesClaimedPositiveWaitDelegateSend` ("waiting for delivery acceptance"). `TestDelegateSendWaitAnswersWhileAnEarlierResultIsDeferred` forces the same interleaving every time; before this fix it failed after 30s.

## The fix (Jesse's ruling)

The waiting reply carries the held result and the new one, in order. The held result is consumed and is never delivered again as a notification.

- **Marking held results.** A plan its receiver defers marks its claim `held`.
- **Carrying the held result.** When the waiter's delivery is next in line behind a held head for the same owner, its plan takes over the head's claim and carries it. `BeginDelivery` admits the held head under the receiver's own claim token, then admits its own delivery. The waiter resolves with both. The reply's tool round acknowledges the held result first, then its own, and the turn records both commits on the one call.
- **Refused or abandoned replies.** If the carrying plan is refused, or the reply's tool round is abandoned, the receiver's claim comes back to its held plan, but only while that plan could still be admitted. A stop or close that has taken the delivery drops the claim, the same as `BeginDelivery` does. One rule (`deliveryStoppedLocked`) now covers both paths and `BeginDelivery`'s own refusals.
- **Failed acknowledgements.** A tool call's acknowledgements complete in order. After one fails, the rest are left retryable for the same inline retry rather than abandoned. They are already in the reply, so they must never come back as notifications.
- **Shared replay helper.** `ReplayDeliveries` and the per-owner replay after an acknowledgement now share one head-plan helper. The per-owner path therefore also retries a retryable receipt at the new head. Before, only `ReplayDeliveries` did that, via requeue. This is a small behaviour change outside the feature, and it's harmless: a duplicate retry is refused under the lock.

## Known gap

Only a held head directly ahead of the waiter's delivery is carried. With two results queued ahead of it (the head held and a second one unclaimed behind it), the send still sits out its wait, as before. A probe shows this is reachable but rare: it needs two completions inside one parent round. I'll file it as an issue.

## Tests

- `TestDelegateSendWaitAnswersWhileAnEarlierResultIsDeferred`, through a real `ProcessInput`, asserts that:
  - the reply carries the first result and then the second,
  - the parent's next request carries the first exactly once,
  - both deliveries are acknowledged,
  - the root transcript still folds with both commits on the send call.
- New controller tests in `agent/delegate_delivery_held_test.go`:
  - a carrier refused on a head mismatch hands the held result back;
  - a carrier refused by a pending stop drops the claim;
  - an abandoned reply hands it back;
  - a stop covering the owner, followed by an abandoned reply, leaves no claim behind;
  - a failed acknowledgement retries both inline with no notification.
- Each test fails with its fix removed.
- `-race -count=3` passes on all of these.
- The targeted delegate, delivery, attention, stop and fold suites pass.
- vet passes plain, with `evenerfuzz`, and with `evenerfuzz` on Windows. golangci-lint reports 0 issues.

## Review

- **First review (earlier design):**
  - Critical: the transcript fold refused two deliveries on one call (fixed in #3938).
  - Important: aborts stranded the held result, a partial ack failure duplicated the newest result, and only the happy path was tested. All fixed here.
  - Important: web and phone don't show `earlier_results`. That's a client PR, and the scope is with the coordinator.
- **Second review (rework):** Important: an abandoned reply restored the held claim after a stop had taken the delivery, leaking it for good. Fixed, with a regression test.
- **Re-review:** no Critical or Important findings. Its Minor about two encodings of the restore rule is unified.
- **/simplify:** brought net non-test code from about 174 lines to about 102. It shares one stop check across the new and existing refusal paths, uses one restore function, shares one replay head helper, and drops a field and two helpers.

author: parkerhdavis
body:
One page at `/status`, and everything a status page needs to be truthful, hand-rolled: error tracking, a deepened `/health`, the resource alerts the app spec has owed since #325, an outside-of-the-platform uptime check from the anthers.social droplet, per-IP rate limits on the open doors, and the browser error beacon.

**The reframe that shaped it** (task: *Build a public status page at /status and wire the observability behind it*, Parker 2026-10-06): the public page is the forcing function; the operator-facing Admin module is deliberately its own follow-up task, parked until the page has been live through an incident or two.

**What ships:**

- `error_events` + `services/error-tracker.ts` — an `app.onError` capture fingerprinted and deduped (a row is an issue, not an occurrence), token/email/id shapes redacted at normalize, first-seen-then-24h-resurface alerts through the existing `sendOperationalAlert`. Error data stays in our Postgres rather than a third party's event stream — that was the tooling decision.
- Deepened `/health`: per-component (database by `SELECT 1`; queue by a SQL read of the `pgboss` schema, because `boss.start()` is the *worker's* act and a process-local read would report down on every healthy deployment). Headline `down` only for the database — restarting the API cannot fix a queue.
- `/api/status` composing the public answer — states and sentences, never a number — rendered by `StatusPage.tsx`, polled every 30s, linked in both footers.
- The droplet heartbeat: `heartbeat-check.sh` in `anthers-node` checks the hub from a failure domain App Platform does not share, emails `OPS_ALERT_EMAIL` on a verdict *change* through the node's own restricted Resend key, and reports the verdict into `POST /api/status/heartbeat` (bearer `HEARTBEAT_TOKEN`, timing-safe). Laid in, cron installed, both halves proven live on `anthers-pds` — including one real DOWN alert landing and the repeat suppressed.
- The shared per-IP rate limiter (`rate_limits`, fixed window, atomic upsert, fails-open-logged-loudly): auth code sends and verifies, the parental pin, DMCA intake, and the abuse/issue intakes migrated off their per-instance Maps.
- The browser beacon: one POST per fingerprint per session, a five-beacon cap, a day-budget that samples past rather than walls, Origin re-checked at the route, and a hard never-500.

**Migration note:** 0120 is #383's; this branch's tables are 0121 (regenerated against merged main after the pre-push gate caught the fork). The `RATE_LIMITS_DISABLED=1` knob follows the `SIGNUP_POW_DIFFICULTY` opt-in shape — set by test sessions, never by the app spec — with the two refusal-asserting suites stripping it for their own run.

**Operator follow-ups after merge** (runbook § *The outside check on the droplet*): the promote, then one check that the outside row on `/status` reads operational with a fresh `lastReportAt`.

받은 `ogimage_taja.png`(2400x1260, 1200x630 의 2배)를 공유 미리보기 이미지로 넣었습니다.

## JPEG 가 아니라 PNG 로 넣은 이유
픽셀 아트라 JPEG 로 구우면 글자 가장자리와 격자에 번짐이 생깁니다. 팔레트 PNG 는 가장자리가 그대로 남습니다.

| | 용량 |
|---|---|
| JPEG q92 | 101KB |
| **팔레트 PNG (적용)** | **131KB** |

30KB 차이로 선명도를 지킬 수 있어 PNG 를 골랐습니다. WebP 가 55KB 로 가장 작지만, 공유 미리보기는 앱마다 지원이 달라 PNG 가 안전합니다.

- `public/og.jpg` → `public/og.png` (경로가 바뀌어 `lib/seo.ts` 도 같이 고쳤습니다)
- `og:image:alt` 을 새 그림에 맞게 바꿨습니다 — 전에는 서울을 달리는 배경 그림 설명이었습니다

로컬에서 `og:image` 가 `/og.png` 로 나가고 그 주소가 200(PNG)으로 응답하는 것을 확인했습니다. `npm test` 297 passed, `npm run build` 통과.
