author: wirsteve
body:
## What
A full user-acceptance pass drove the game in a browser. It covered:
- **Careers:** new careers in karting, asphalt, dirt and club road, every family background, and start years 1995, 2005, 2016 and 2026.
- **Seasons:** 1–7 seasons each, including owner mode.
- **Pages and actions:** every page, plus every Garage and Race Shop action.
- **Display:** light and dark themes and phone width.
- **Navigation:** back and forward, reloads and odd URLs.

It recorded no JS errors and found the issues below; all are fixed here.

**Money**
- **Season dollars:** messages, ledger lines and labels showed 2025 dollars while every number on screen used season dollars. For example, a 1995 freshen button said "$81" and the toast said "$250". Owner mode quoted $62,500 and charged $40,187. All of these now go through `nominal_usd(year, x)`: garage, owner mode, off-season actions, sponsors, scholarships, fines, jewels.
- **Budget shown:** the sidebar and dashboard "Budget" ignored the racing account, so it showed $631k when $4.6k was left. It now shows what you can spend: the account plus savings in season, next season's money in the off-season.
- **Ledger totals:** the starter-car purchase was paid before the account opened and then counted again. It is now a record-only line.
- **Jewel entries:** crown-jewel entry and travel now get a ledger line.
- **Garage costs:** freshen and repair buttons now show the real cost, including the engine-room and fabrication discounts.

**Sim and navigation**
- **Double clicks:** a double-click on "Go racing" or "Next race" ran two races. Sims now run one at a time and every sim button is disabled meanwhile.
- **Fast navigation:** clicking quickly between pages could leave the wrong page on screen (URL on News, page showing Tracks). Page loads that finish after you've moved on are now dropped.

**Messages**
- **Failed actions:** failures such as "more than you have" or "no room" now come back with `ok: false` and show as error toasts (`rules/fail.py`).
- **Freshen:** you can no longer freshen a brand-new engine.
- **Confirmations:** selling the team, buying or trading a hauler, and selling off a facility now ask first.
- **Off-season message:** last winter's decision no longer shows as current.
- **Preseason standings:** now titled "2016 final standings" instead of looking like this season's.
- **New career:** blank names, a non-numeric seed or an unknown background are rejected with a clear message before the world is built.
- **Server errors:** bad numbers in URLs give a readable 400, not Python's text.

**Layout**
- **Wrapped text:** results links and garage crew names were broken one letter per line. The crew list now has the price and Hire under each name.
- **Recent races:** the week links to the results.
- **Off-season page:** no sideways scroll at 1400px (forms are capped at their column).
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - "shocks shocks" in the ledger;
  - car numbers skipping (Car 2, Car 9);
  - "Own car" on a retired player's card;
  - settings Save/Defaults now confirm;
  - the viewer ticker explains a caution as the flag comes out;
  - the theme toggle works on phones;
  - the saves page names the real folder.

**Left as is:** a few balance observations, for example the cost of a karting start for a modest family and the losses of a one-car MX-5 team. They're design calls, not bugs.

## Testing
- **Full suite:** 145 passed.
- **New `tests/test_uat.py`:**
  - season-dollar messages;
  - failures reported as `ok: false` through the API;
  - the budget shown;
  - the starter-car ledger line;
  - new-career validation;
  - a fresh off-season message.
- **Browser re-check (Playwright), with no JS errors:**
  - triple-clicking "Go racing" makes one `/api/sim` call and opens the viewer;
  - Tracks→News in quick succession shows News;
  - the garage freshen button is disabled on a fresh engine;
  - dismissing the hauler confirm leaves the rig unchanged;
  - no table overflows in the garage;
  - the off-season page is 1400px wide at a 1400px window;
  - the preseason title reads "2026 final standings".

body:
What: X17's decision-free remainder, in four parts.
1. The census keeps its results file. .github/workflows/seo-census.yml uploaded the hidden .seo-census folder, which actions/upload-artifact skips by default, so no run kept its per-page table. The step now sets include-hidden-files: true; the input is read from the action's own action.yml at v7.
2. Canonicals on two of the four live, indexable pages outside the census. /information/map and /teams/<slug> answer "index, follow" on prod with no canonical, and are not in the sitemap, so the census could not see them. Their base metadata now names their own address, as #1143 did for the census's 155; findTeamBySlug matches exactly. /contribute and /feedback are noindex and need none. /social and /social/threads, the other two, are noted for X17's next PR.
3. The author photos. The census counted the empty alt of the author photo on the blog bylines, the authors index and the author pages as missing. Empty was the accessibility rule, because each photo stands beside the author's name. They now carry the name and aria-hidden="true", so screen readers hear exactly what they heard before, while search engines and Seobility see a description.
4. The calendar's ?s= deep links. The series pages and their tabs still link /calendar?s=<series>, which prod answers noindex with a canonical to /calendar. app/robots.ts now keeps crawlers off them, as R15 did for the filter addresses. app/robots.test.ts follows the intended change (R15 had listed /calendar?s=f1 as allowed) and guards /calendar?series= and /calendar?sessions= from the new rule.

Why: X17's acceptance is the next crawl's counts at zero, and the operator pays per crawl; every part here is code, needs no wording from the operator and no write to the live database. The 21 weekend-family pages the census counts with an image without a description were not found in a sample of one weekend and one session page per series; they wait for the census's results file, which part 1 makes possible.

How verified: tsc 0; eslint 0 on the changed files; the robots and blog tests green. The full suite, the build's pages checked, the testing Worker probed, the review, and the same checks plus the census workflow's results file on prod after the merge are recorded in docs/pull-requests.md.

body:
# MedSynth Guard v0.6.0 Release Candidate

This pull request merges the completed MedSynth Guard professionalization work into `main`.

## Highlights

- FastAPI platform with PostgreSQL persistence and asynchronous workers
- Clinical tabular synthesis using Gaussian Copula, CTGAN and TVAE; ECG generation workflow
- Structural validation, provenance and SHA-256 artifact integrity
- Statistical fidelity, DCR privacy diagnostics and Disclosure Protection analysis
- Declared TRTR / TSTR ML utility evaluation
- Versioned release policies and HTML governance reports
- React product workflow
- OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE with opaque application sessions
- OWNER / EDITOR / VIEWER authorization and organization-level tenant isolation
- Private S3-compatible artifact storage, retention/deletion lifecycle and audit trail
- Operational logging/metrics and verified backup/restore
- Production container recipes, CI, dependency/secret scans, SBOMs and individual container CVE review

## Verification

Phase 6 release-candidate verification completed successfully for source commit:

`aea2637f239e623641be4771e2147d327e89154e`

[Remote GitHub Actions quality run 37583306149](https://github.com/Stevemeg/Synthetic-Data/actions/runs/37583306149) passed all four jobs: backend, frontend, containers-security and oidc-storage-browser.

Evidence includes unit/model/PostgreSQL integration tests, real OIDC authentication, tenant authorization, private S3 workflows, browser E2E, visual/accessibility/responsive checks, container builds/runtime probes, full container scans, dependency audits, secret scanning and six CycloneDX SBOMs.

The PR merge result and subsequent main commit must pass their own full CI before tagging.

The publication branch also merges existing main history in commit `f6993eb3f15094db5a2a1b6785650b382d5e1ca3`. It preserves main's assets and resolves README/legacy requirements conflicts using the verified implementation. Two stale README statements now reflect Linux CI and link to the releases page. Application, container, security and workflow contents remain identical to the verified Phase 6 source; fresh PR CI verifies the combined tree.

## Security posture

Remaining container CVEs are retained transparently with individual, configuration-specific dispositions. No vulnerability was hidden using blanket scanner exclusions. There are no unresolved BLOCKING findings or unresolved Critical findings within the verified configuration; raw Critical findings remain visible.

The archived MinIO build is a restricted, loopback-only development fixture with trusted raw credentials, not approval for public/shared production storage. PostgreSQL base migration requires logical backup/restore into a new volume. Individual CVE reviews expire 2026-11-06 or earlier upon relevant changes.

See [security scan review](docs/SECURITY_SCAN_REVIEW.md) and [Phase 6 verification](docs/PHASE_6_VERIFICATION.md).

## Important limitations

MedSynth Guard does not claim HIPAA/GDPR compliance, formal anonymization, zero re-identification risk, differential privacy or clinical validation.

Current clinical tabular synthesis/evaluation supports single-table workflows. CTGAN/TVAE and ECG are Beta; medical imaging is experimental and disabled in production.

This is a release candidate, not a regulatory certification.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary Ports the POSTTRAN batch job to Java on the UNT51-11 harness (ADR-0015). Stacked on #62. Do not merge. **`posttran` stream** (`com.carddemo.batch.posttran.PosttranJobConfiguration`). It is a new harness `JobStream`: the batch CLI resolves `--job=` to a single job first, then to a stream, and runs the stream as a `JobChain`. The process exit code is the highest step RC. ``` posttran: STEP10 cbtrn01c (CBTRN01C, read-only check, RC 0) STEP15 cbtrn02c COND=(4,LT,STEP10) (CBTRN02C posting engine, RC 4 if any reject) --STEP10.SYSOUT=... / --STEP15.
=... step-qualified parameters (JobStream.forStep) ``` - **DDs** go through `DdParameters`. DALYTRAN / XREFFILE / ACCTFILE / TCATBALF / TRANFILE (and CUSTFILE / CARDFILE for STEP10) each take either a file path or `table`. `KeyedDataset` models a KSDS opened INPUT, I-O or OUTPUT, backed by a file or by JPA, and returns COBOL file statuses (`22` duplicate, `23` not found, …). - **TRANFILE is opened OUTPUT**, as in the JCL, so the transaction master is replaced on every run. - **FILLER preserved:** file-mode rewrites keep the FILLER of the record that was read, as COBOL `READ … INTO` does. Without this, TCATBALF differs from the baseline. - **DALYREJS** is written by default as the dated generation `DALYREJS/DALYREJS..`, through `DatedOutputFiles`, with a `batch_output_file` row (ADR-0012). It is written only when the step ends normally, matching `DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE)`. `--DALYREJS=` writes a plain file instead. - **`Cbtrn02c` rules:** - Validation order is 100 → 101 → 102 → 103, and 103 overwrites 102. - `WS-TEMP-BAL` is truncated to `S9(09)V99`. Reaching the limit exactly passes, and so does expiring on the transaction date. - Negative amounts are added to the cycle debit bucket. - A missing TCATBALF row is created. - `PROC-TS` comes from the injected `Clock` (`golden` = 2022-07-06) in `YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.hh0000` format. - All arithmetic is `BigDecimal` with no rounding. - **One database transaction per accepted record** (`TransactionTemplate`, `REQUIRES_NEW`) covers the TCATBALF, ACCTFILE and TRANFILE updates. If the TRANFILE write fails, that record's TCATBALF and account updates are rolled back. COBOL leaves them applied, as the rules doc notes. - **New `unload` job** (`--DATASET=ACCTDATA|CARDXREF|TRANSACT|TCATBALF|DALYTRAN --OUTFILE=`): an IDCAMS REPRO equivalent that writes a table to a file in key order. It is used for the table-mode comparison. - **Rules docs:** `docs/modernization/rules/CBTRN01C.md` and `CBTRN02C.md`, derived from the source plus the harvested business spec branch `devin/1790171286-posttran-business-spec`. **Equivalence** follows the existing pattern. `scripts/batch/run_posttran.sh file|table` runs the packaged jar and calls `compare_posttran.py`, which compares field by field using the copybook layouts: - SYSOUT of both steps - RC - DALYREJS records and the reason-code tally - TRANSACT, ACCTDATA and TCATBALF after-images Both modes are added to `make batch-equivalence`, which the CI job `batch-equivalence` runs. The script also checks: - the `batch_run` and `batch_output_file` rows; - the COND path: when STEP10 abends, STEP15 is bypassed, the exit code is 16 and no generation is written. Table mode starts from `initial-load` of the EBCDIC samples. Its differences are reported in `REPORT.md`, not hidden: - **ACCTDATA record 49 `ACCT-ADDR-ZIP`:** `A000000000` in the baseline vs `ZEROAPR` in Java. This is the known sample-input difference, listed in `scripts/batch/posttran-table-mode-expected-diffs.txt`, and each listed entry must match exactly once. - **TCATBALF FILLER:** differs in all 100 rows because FILLER is not persisted (ADR-0011). This is counted and reported. The DISCGRP record 34 difference does not reach POSTTRAN. Local results (packaged jar, PostgreSQL 16): ``` | CBTRN01C SYSOUT | 1807 lines, match | | TRANSACT after-image | 262 records, match | | POSTTRAN SYSOUT | 54 lines, match | | ACCTDATA after-image | 50 records, match | | RC | Java 4 / baseline 4 | | TCATBALF after-image | 100 records, match | | DALYREJS | 38 records, match; reason codes 0102: 38, match | RESULT: PASS (file) RESULT: PASS (table, with the 2 documented differences above) batch_run: cbtrn01c COMPLETED 0 300/0, cbtrn02c COMPLETED 4 300/262; batch_output_file DALYREJS 2022-07-06 38 ``` `mvn verify` (Java 21): 394 unit tests and 77 ITs pass, and the JaCoCo checks pass. New tests: - `Cbtrn02cTest`: every reject path, limit reached exactly, expiring today, negative and zero amounts, missing TCATBALF row, PROC-TS, unit of work, temp-balance truncation. - `PosttranBaselineTest`: file mode vs the baseline. - `PosttranJobIT`: table mode on Testcontainers, plus rollback of a failed posting. - `JobStreamTest`. - `DatedOutputFilesTest.generationIsNamedAndCataloguedByTheGivenBusinessDate`. **Changes from review** (487f2b8, f520fc3): - **File mode abend:** on an abend, including a failed CLOSE, TRANFILE / ACCTFILE / TCATBALF are still written with every update made so far, as VSAM keeps them. DALYREJS is not written, matching `DISP=(…,DELETE)`. - **OPEN OUTPUT:** creates or empties TRANFILE at open, so a destination that cannot be written fails before any posting. - **DALYREJS business date:** the generation name and catalogue date come from `--run-date` (`DatedOutputFiles.write(gdgBase, businessDate, …)`). - **No restart of `cbtrn02c`:** the job uses `preventRestart()`. Postings commit one record at a time, so restarting a failed instance would post them twice. Recovery is restore ACCTDATA/TCATBALF, then run a new instance (rules doc R-14). _Requested by **Maythee** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018HWmb5wuUnNNRbmem9bKoh?thread=cmsg_018HWmb5wuUnNNRbmem9bKohK1dfErKVjt4sJohjZ24oYP)_

## Summary

Before: the new Fitness overview (#2207) uses plain section headings, flat bordered tables with a faint header band, a hairline stat strip, and its own error and empty states, while Gear, a gear's page, Files, Heatmaps, Privacy and Connections still used shadowed `Card`s, separate stat tiles, centred "Loading..." text and plain red error lines.

After: every fitness page reads like the overview. Gear lists each kind as a heading with its count and Add button over a bordered table; a bike, shoe or device page shows its totals on the overview's stat strip; Files shows Used / Quota / File count on the strip, puts the import between storage and the list, and lists each file as a compact row; Heatmaps and Privacy use the same section headings; the Strava and Wahoo forms sit in flat panels with overview-sized headings. Loading is static skeleton bars, errors are the overview's alert (with Retry where a read failed) and empties are its icon panel.

How: the overview's pieces are pulled into shared primitives in `lib/components/fitness/` (`FitnessSection`, `FitnessAlert`, `FitnessEmptyState`, `FitnessStatCell`, plus `FITNESS_TABLE_HEAD_ROW_CLASS`), and the overview itself now renders its error, empty state and stat strip through them, so there is one copy of each. `FitnessStatGrid`'s `summary` variant gains a `columns` prop so a two- or three-value strip has no empty cell (three values go 2+1 on a phone). Gear tables now sit on the page, so the pinned column paints `bg-background` and the pinned header paints the header band's tint opaque (`STICKY_HEAD_CELL`).

Also fixed on the way: Files rendered upload times with `toLocaleString()` during render, which threw a hydration mismatch; it now uses the viewer's zone after hydration. Deleting a file now counts it out of the totals, and a gear page that fails to load says so and offers Retry instead of claiming the gear was deleted.

Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (fitness section primitives, pinned column surface), `docs/fitness-file-storage.md` (pinned column surface), `docs/maintenance.md` (Files heading).

## Screenshots

Before/after for each page, from a local build with seeded mock data: https://claude.ai/artifact/BDQbf8pqkjN5rrfYSrYNZ3 (the mock seed bypasses the storage counters, so Used and the file count read 0 there).

author: marcwimmer
body:
Odoo-Ticket 5650.

Beim Restore neutralisiert zodoo die Datenbank jetzt über Odoos eigenen Weg `odoo-bin neutralize`, statt die `data/neutralize.sql` der Module selbst einzusammeln (#263). Damit greift jedes installierte Modul mit eigenem Neutralize-Skript genau so, wie Odoo es vorsieht – Core, Enterprise und auch zSYNC (Odoo-Ninjas/zebroo-sync, Branch `feat/zbsync-neutralize-sql`).

**Änderungen**
- `odoo/bin/neutralize.py` + `exec_odoo(..., command=...)`: `odoo-bin neutralize -c … -d …` im Einmal-Container; im Standard-Image-Modus direkt das Odoo-CLI.
- Restore: die DB heißt währenddessen noch `<db>_restoring` und liegt auf dem Hilfs-Postgres → `DBNAME`/`DB_HOST` werden übergeben, die Kopie ist also schon neutralisiert, bevor sie ihren endgültigen Namen bekommt. Schlägt die Neutralisierung fehl, bricht der Restore ab.
- Neu: `odoo restore odoo-db --neutralize` (nur Odoos Neutralisierung, ohne DEVMODE – z.B. Staging) und `odoo dev-env neutralize`.
- `turndb2dev.sql` 16–20: Cron-Abschaltung macht jetzt Odoo (lässt den Autovacuum-Cron an). TOTP, neue `database.uuid` und `enterprise_code` bleiben zodoo-Ergänzung – das macht Odoo beim Neutralisieren nicht.
- MANIFEST `neutralize`: Einträge auf `<modul>/data/neutralize.sql` werden ab Odoo 16 übersprungen (sonst doppelt).
- Doku: Command-Reference mit Tabelle „was macht Odoo / was ergänzt zodoo“, Settings- und MANIFEST-Referenz.

author: huypqfinhay
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 (Shadow MVP) of #6: a native router that, for a virtual model (`auto/jev`, configurable), picks which model and reasoning effort it **would** use from the models reachable right now, validates the answer in code, and records it. In shadow mode the request is always served by a deterministic `fallbackTarget`; the router's choice is metadata only.

Refs #6 (Phase 1 only, so this does not close the issue).

## What changed

- **Candidates are discovered, not configured.** Models of connected providers (minus disabled ones) with quality, latency and cost tier inferred from name and price; `include`, `exclude` and per-model `overrides` correct the guess; pool capped at `maxCandidates`.
- **Per-request filtering** before anything reaches the decision model: required vision, tools or structured output, context size, API key provider allowlist, DLP provider filter, provider availability. A choice that was not offered is rejected in code.
- **Decision**: one typed request to TypeSafe Jev for model plus reasoning effort; confidence gate, effort validated against the profile and the chosen model. Timeout, HTTP error, bad response, missing key, low confidence and no eligible candidate all fall back with a reason.
- **Observability**: `requestDetails.routing` (no prompt text) and `X-Smart-Routing-*` response headers, including the model that actually answered.
- **Admin**: Profile page, Smart router card (detected models, weights, confidence, timeout, include/exclude/overrides, API key per decision provider with test). The key can come from admin (write-only, never returned by `GET /api/settings`) or `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, environment wins. Decision providers are pluggable.
- **Offline evaluation**: `scripts/smart-routing-eval.mjs` compares the router with a fixed-model baseline on fallback rate, selection, confidence, decision latency, estimated cost and labelled quality.
- Plan and design notes: `docs/SMART_ROUTING_PLAN.md`.

The first commits add a tag and route-table version that the later commits replace with the candidate-based design from the issue; squash on merge if a single commit is preferred.

## Behaviour to know

- Disabled by default. Needs `fallbackTarget` to enable.
- Shadow mode waits for the decision (default 800 ms timeout) before serving the request, so it only affects requests that use the virtual model.
- Truncated conversation text is sent to the decision provider; it is never logged or persisted. Restrict with `apiKeyIds` where needed.
- Not in this PR (Phase 2/3): executing the chosen model and effort, rollout percentage, session stickiness, dashboard metrics, multiple profiles, combos and compatible providers as candidates.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/unit/smartRouting.test.js`: 31 tests (pool inference, filtering, confidence gate, invalid choice, every fallback path, headers, validation, keys, evaluation maths), run with vitest
- [x] Offline evaluation script run end to end against a local stand-in for the decision API
- [ ] Open the Profile page, save a key, press **Test key**, check the model list, switch the router on
- [ ] Send `model: "auto/jev"` through `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages`, streaming and not, and check the `X-Smart-Routing-*` headers and `requestDetails.routing`
- [ ] Run a real evaluation against real prompts before enabling routing

Not verified: `next build` fails locally on an unrelated Windows `EPERM` while scanning `Application Data`, so the UI and the three endpoints have not been exercised in a running app. 25 other unit tests fail in the repo for unrelated reasons (RTK, sqlite driver, translator normalisation); the routing tests are not among them.

author: nicopennec
body:
**Problem**
- Deleting a metadata column wipes a same-named column of another entity type.
- Renaming a metadata column onto another one overwrites its values, then fails.
- Updating a production metadata column without a name fails.
- When durations display in hours, the estimations CSV import reads days.
- Kitsu cannot tell when the pictures of a new preview are ready.
- A preview that just turned ready can still answer 404 for a few minutes.

**Solution**
- Scope the removal or rename to the entity type of the column.
- Refuse such a rename.
- Keep the current name.
- Read them in hours.
- Send the preview status with the concept list, the update and set-main events, and the set-main answers.
- Check a processing status again before answering 404.

author: graemerocher
body:
`JMSListenerRegistry` takes a connection from the `JMSConnectionPool` for every listener it registers and never returns it. `shutdown()` stops the listeners but keeps their pooled connections out of the pool, so each stop and re-registration of listeners leaks one connection, until the pool fails with `IllegalStateException: Maximum pool size reached`.

The fix:

- `register(Connection, …)` remembers the pooled connection of each listener it creates.
- `shutdown()` returns those connections to their pool once their listeners have stopped. A connection shared by several listeners is returned once.
- If a listener fails to stop, its connection stays out of the pool, because it may still hold that listener's session. This is what released code already does for every connection.

`ListenerConnectionPoolTest` (Testcontainers Artemis, `micronaut.jms.max-pool-size: 4`) registers and shuts down a listener 12 times. It then checks that a re-registered listener on a re-lent connection still receives messages. Without the fix it fails with `Maximum pool size reached`.

This targets `5.1.x`, the line the platform ships (5.1.0), and merges forward. The dev-mode adoption PR micronaut-projects/micronaut-jms#791 includes the same `JMSListenerRegistry` change, and will rebase onto this once it has been merged forward.

author: justinhelmer
body:
A requester-selected preset can no longer end as a repository listing or another registry command. Grounding reads remain available; the model still interprets the work and PR.

**Why:** Standalone Review with PR, head and focus reached the model path. Its unrestricted terminal command projection accepted repo.list and finished without a Review bind.

**Where to look**

1. [Preset action boundary](https://github.com/coreplanelabs/switchboard/blob/540c232f42d51b9ef10e53cfc1ef1bb0f50baa55/src/core/dispatch/operator.ts#L567-L578) Reuse the registered leading directive syntax to filter terminal commands only on unowned, authorized preset requests.
2. [Parse shares the projection](https://github.com/coreplanelabs/switchboard/blob/540c232f42d51b9ef10e53cfc1ef1bb0f50baa55/src/core/dispatch/operator.ts#L2346-L2353) Reject filtered commands on normal and exhausted multi-call paths, while retaining the full owned-thread fold.
3. [Actual failed probe as a local control](https://github.com/coreplanelabs/switchboard/blob/540c232f42d51b9ef10e53cfc1ef1bb0f50baa55/src/core/dispatch/operator.test.ts#L1628-L1660) The unchanged standalone request rejects repo.list and repairs to a PR-evidenced Review bind with its full constraints.

**Feedback wanted:** Check terminal action filtering, grounding helpers and original owned-thread precedence.

**Risk:** Applies to offered leading preset directives on unowned threads. Live model variability and new-candidate routing/deployment acceptance remain unproved.

**Verified:** 1,182 scoped tests pass. Types, lint, format, fix, consistency, specs, coverage and title pass. Current-head PR CI pending.

<details>
<summary>Decisions (2)</summary>

- **Preserve syntax without inferring intent.** Use the existing registered leading preset directive and current projection, not review words, reasons or a new semantic regex. Preset and PR interpretation stay with the model.
- **Share action boundaries.** Prompt/tool offerings and the parse use the same command filter, including bounded multi-call repair. Helper reads and full registry-help data remain available; ownership retains its existing precedence.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Validation (3 criteria)</summary>

| Criterion | Proof |
|---|---|
| The exact standalone probe cannot complete as a terminal repository listing | Six qualified RED controls become GREEN: actual failed request repairs to Review; ordinary and exhausted multi-call paths reject filtered commands. |
| Grounding and original behavior remain available | Helper-read then Review bind, exact head/focus text, ordinary/quoted/unknown markers, owned-thread projection and existing PR quote repair controls pass. |
| No release acceptance is manufactured | Smoke case and assertion unchanged. No model, native Review, deployment, variable, permission or retry-budget changes. A containing candidate must pass its normal live gate. |

</details>

<details>
<summary>For agents</summary>

Original source owner, separate coherent follow-up on actual released 3c9b74d. Root owns next containing release and one candidate/deploy cycle. No bootstrap approval is claimed; native review currently unavailable. Prior RED attempts retained but corrected fixture assumptions are excluded from causal credit. Production impact lookup found no connected Switchboard resource.

</details>

- 修后表现：判卷框架是 `tests/_*` 这一条 glob，五个框架文件都罩住，以后新建的 `tests/_*` 也罩住。被测的 `_panel-roster-lib.sh` 不在判卷面。家族登记表仍要求 `bin/_review_result.py` 在判卷面或 high。
- 根源 → 修法：框架不是“被多少套件 import 到”，而是约定放在 `tests/_*`。删掉 source/exec/import 解析。`tests/` 里除了总跑登记的套件、套件用 `node --test` 点名的判据、`fixtures/`、`mutation-*.sh`，其他文件必须是 `tests/_*`。框架文件去掉注释后如果点名了 `bin/` 里的文件，那个文件也必须在判卷面。
- 钉住它的测试：`tests/test_aiwork_gate_workflow.mjs`「判卷框架按 tests/_* 约定，并且都在判卷面」。修前在当时的策略上失败，缺 `tests/_mutation-guard.sh`。

body:
Closes #36

## 意図

#34 で一時フォルダを導入したことで、`--no-part` の単一フォーマット（TwitchのHLSなど）で中止した後に、**同名の別動画や、同じURLの別フォーマット**を取ると、一時フォルダに残った途中ファイルの続きとして取られ、混ざったファイルが「完了」になる（exit 0）おそれがあった。変更前は途中ファイルが出力先に残り、`MakeUniquePath` が別名を選んでいたので起きなかった。

## 再現（計画の調査）

ローカルのHLS（ffmpeg で作った40断片のA・B）と `E:\tube\yt-dlp.exe`（2026.08.19）で、`--no-part -P home:O -P temp:T -o Same.mp4` を共通にして確認した。

- 中止後は `T\Same.mp4` と `Same.mp4.ytdl`（`current_fragment` 12）が残る。
- 同名の別動画を続けて取ると、exit 0 で完成し警告も無い。中身は冒頭12秒がA、残りがBの連結。
- 同じURLの別フォーマットも、混ざる。
- 同じURL・同じ名前の再実行は、`frag 12/40` から再開し、A単独と一致する（意図した再開）。
- サブフォルダで分けると混ざらない。

## 変更

- 一時フォルダを設定したとき（ライブ録画を除く）、`-P temp:<一時フォルダ>\<ハッシュ12桁>` を渡す。ハッシュは SHA-256 の先頭6バイトで、元は「`NormalizeUrl` を通したURL・`SelectedFormat`・音声のみ・`Codec`」（`Codec` は常に入れる。Issueの確定要件どおり）。
- 同じ項目（同じURL・同じフォーマット）は同じサブフォルダになり、再開できる。別の動画・別のフォーマットは別のサブフォルダ。
- 成功（exit 0）したら、空のサブフォルダだけを（再帰なしで）削除する。失敗・中止のものは、再開用に残す（#34 の「掃除しない」を保つ）。削除に失敗しても取得の成否には影響しない（ADR 0001）。
- 一時フォルダが空欄、またはライブ録画のときは、渡す引数は今までと同じ。`BuildOutputArgs` は変えていない。
- 新規 ADR 0007。ADR 0006・CLAUDE.md・CONTEXT.md を更新。

## 既知の制約（ADR 0007）

- #34 の版で一時フォルダの直下に残った途中ファイルは、更新後は再開に使わず、自動でも消さない。
- 成功直後の削除が、ウイルス対策ソフトなどのハンドルでまれに失敗し、空のサブフォルダが残ることがある。
- `SelectedFormat` が `bestaudio+bestvideo` のような指定のとき、同じ文字列でも実際に選ばれるフォーマットが変わりうる。同じサブフォルダで再開しようとする（Issueの「同じURL・同じフォーマット」の範囲内として許容）。
- `[MoveFiles]` 中の中断の問題（#34 の既知の制約）は、このPRの範囲外。

## 動作確認

- `dotnet build yt.slnx`：0警告0エラー（`--no-incremental` も）。
- ハッシュ・サブフォルダ・削除の関数を、スクラッチのハーネスで検証：39件すべて通過（ハッシュの期待値は Python の `hashlib` で独立に計算）。
- 実機のyt-dlp（ローカルHLS）：Aを中止してBを別サブフォルダで取ると、Bは混ざらない。Aを同じサブフォルダで再実行すると、途中から再開して完走する。
- **未確認（人が行う）**：GUIでの確認（一時フォルダ設定・空欄・ライブ録画）、実際のTwitch・YouTube、`-N 4` ありでの再現、長いパス、削除失敗時の挙動。

body:
## Why

Um pai Codex pode bloquear a rede dos CLIs externos. O runner passa a explicar essa causa na falha final, e o setup recusa probes bloqueados antes de produzir efeitos. A escrita também verifica o acesso antes de alterar os arquivos.

## What changed

- Captura o estado do pai e acrescenta a pista somente à falha final de CLI sem motivo tipado do provedor.
- Deriva a recusa do mapa completo, inclusive famílias já verificadas, e admite os dois destinos e o ledger alterado antes de escrever.
- Atualiza pré-requisitos, proveniência e os carriers da versão 0.5.23.

## Scope

Cobre runner, setup e a documentação correspondente. Preserva o classificador de B, as rotas e o schema público; ACP mantém seus motivos originais.

## Blast Radius

O setup verifica permissões antes da primeira mutação. Readback e rollback continuam necessários porque o estado do sistema pode mudar depois dessa checagem.

## Verification

- Sete gates do head commitado passaram: 1.482 testes Node sem skips, 74 testes Bun e TypeScript estrito, matriz, agentes, colisões e os dois diff checks.
- Focos de runner/setup: 52 testes passaram, incluindo ACP literal, ELOOP, referent somente leitura e rollback. Interrogate encerrou sem correção obrigatória; a tentativa Claude teve API 429.
- [CI do head](https://github.com/byvict/pstack-vic/actions/runs/37599243835) passou. Root concedeu CLEAN: 14 scopes passaram em 17 contextos independentes; as provas 2, 6 e 9 tiveram uma repetição fresca por falha de método, sem alteração de fonte.

- Performance: duas chamadas de warmup e 20 chamadas medidas, sem reposição; medianas base/head de 66,5/66,5 ms. O intervalo inclui o corpo fake, sem alegar decomposição causal. Permissões foram provadas em macOS sem privilégios.

body:
## Fixed source

HEAD `47c768a366ff5517039ecc428eee30280fde5410`, branch `codex/official-fixed-sale-contract-oct07`.

Fix the official fixed-odds HAD sale contract: CBT selling/allUp is the pool admission evidence; INT/single-pool flags do not veto it. Signed receipt V2 is used for new publications, while V1 is restricted to explicit historical replay. Existing frozen decisions are preserved.

## Actual deployment and acceptance

Normal signed full r806 completed on 2026-10-07, archive SHA256 `ed0e3c63aa21392d8451a8844ec4e70ecb00af6a35a2ed4f339ab3d3952f4c7c`. The third normal same-bundle deploy exited 0 after the two preserved SSH/transport failures. No duplicate controller or source hot copy.

Fresh independent runtime acceptance at 10:56:57 UTC passed: 1,885 immutable source entries, all 218 dist files / 14,315,214 bytes, PG/current-read, services, source health, integrity/parity, and a natural full cycle started 10:32:01 and finished 10:51:50 after release completion. Public TLS at 11:02:17 matched all 217 static files and the unique dynamic runtime-config contract.

Six current business-day 2026-10-07 HAD receipts were independently replayed as new/open/fresh/signed after completion. This batch took 13.153 seconds from receipt arrival to these immutable decision publications; this is not first-quote discovery latency or an end-to-end SLA. HHAD price provenance is a separate scope and is not proved by HAD receipt replay.

Frozen continuity observed at 10:43:26 UTC: all 44,513 baseline decisionId/recordHash pairs preserved, no missing/changed, 3,348 additional records, four sealed original files byte-identical. This is not a full historical-payload rehash.

## Product and model boundary

Actual Chrome recommendation center shows six published reference directions and one reference candidate. The final pressed 2/3-combo tabs show no combination because two/three distinct qualified candidates are required. Limited desktop/mobile DOM and native viewports were recorded; a failed full-page screenshot is excluded. Normal 900-second QA was revoked and its stored code cleared at 11:09:45 UTC. Whole-page/all-matches visual acceptance and all browser-storage-empty proof are not claimed.

All six primary directions still select the lower handicap side. Actual frozen probabilities reproduce naked cross-market probability selection: +1 handicap home win covers HAD home/draw; -1 handicap away win covers HAD draw/away. These broader events win against a single HAD result. This PR fixes collection/publication admission, not that selection rule. The model still includes market priors and manual adjustments, formal calibration remains unavailable, and no training, improved accuracy or qualified combination claim is made. Ordinary pipeline model recomputation did occur.

## Follow-up

PR #115 contains time-based backup/log retention and resource monitoring, not yet deployed at this update. Follow-up recommendation work needs separate market calibration, trustworthy team features available before decision time, rolling out-of-sample evaluation and frozen prospective comparisons.

body:
Closes #614.
Closes #485.

An Ahrefs audit found the word pages orphaned: the word sitemaps list them, but no page links to
them. This adds browse pages under `/dictionary/browse/`, built from the #614 mockups, so every
word is a few links from the dictionary home. It follows the plan in the decision comment on #614,
in order, one commit per step, then the commits that answer the reviews, add the kanji JLPT levels
decided on #614, close what was left open, merge `main`, and fix what an audit of the branch
against the issue and its mockups found (items 12 to 23).

**It includes `chore/dictionary-image-layers`.** Its one commit, `Put the dictionary image's data
first and its code last` (5a36a4f), is this branch's first, and that branch was never pushed or
opened as its own pull request, so it ships here. The dictionary service's image now puts its
language-data layers first and its code last, so a deploy that changes only code pulls one small
layer instead of the ~1 GB of data again. The ranked lists this branch adds
(`RankedLists.sqlite3`) go in that data layer.

## What changed

1. **Language data** (`Keep JMdict's subject fields, dialects, and usage labels, and rebuild the language data`)
   - `apps/ios/Tools/jmdict_labels.py` maps every JMdict usage (`misc`), subject-field, and dialect
     code on a sense to an app-owned identifier. It keeps them in the sense's `usage`, `fields`,
     and `dialects`, which are absent when empty. An unmapped code fails the import.
   - They're not in note identities or the semantic fingerprint, so saved notes and ranking don't
     change. The app doesn't decode them (item 12); the website's browse pages read them.
   - The rebuild now keeps the Wikipedia and six Jiten packs' mapped ranks in
     `Resources/RankedLists.sqlite3` (19.6 MB, `build_ranked_lists.py`). Until now the rebuild
     discarded them.
     - `build_jiten_frequency_packs.py` keeps each pack's evidence beside its ZIP.
     - Each list must hash to the `mappingSHA256` its catalog manifest pins. The app's installer
       makes the same check, so the service ranks words exactly as the app does.
     - `Package.swift` leaves the file out of the app bundle.
     - `tests/test_ranked_lists_contract.py` checks it.
   - The Jiten and Wikipedia sources and their CDN URLs are unchanged. As on every rebuild, their
     old manifests moved into `trustedHistoricalManifests` (16 → 23).
2. **The service reads the ranked lists** (`Read the Wikipedia and Jiten ranked lists in the dictionary service`)
   - The file is attached as `ranked`, and `checkArtifact` refuses a file built for other data, or
     one that lacks a list. With TUBELEX, the service has all eight ranked dictionaries.
   - The Dockerfile copies it in the image's language-data layer (above).
3. **Browse routes** (`Add browse routes to the dictionary service`)
   - `DictionaryBrowse` in the core (`packages/dictionary-core/src/artifact/browse*.ts`,
     `src/browse/`) answers eleven routes under `/v1/browse` and `/v1/sitemaps/browse`, listed
     below with their shapes and counts. Contract 4 (3 was this branch's first shape, never
     deployed; item 13 changed it).
   - None of the routes are under `/v1/auth`, `/v1/me`, `/v1/sync`, or `/v1/health`.
4. **ADR 0010 amended** (`Amend ADR 0010 with the browse pages`)
   - The ADR now covers the browse pages, and `routes.test.ts` lists their routes and
     `/sitemaps/browse.xml`. The routes test fails on this commit alone, until the next commit adds
     the pages.
5. **Website** (`Build the browse pages`)
   - Pages: the browse hub, the kana charts, each script's kana, a kana's two-kana groups and their
     words, the kanji lists, the frequency dictionaries and each list, and the category lists and
     each category.
   - Site-wide: the dictionary home's browse sections; the footer's Browse by kana and Kanji by
     grade links; `/sitemap/` as a tree; and `/sitemaps/browse.xml` in the sitemap index.
   - Each behavior is in `apps/web/docs/product/browse.md`, with its check.
   - Rows reuse the search results' `WordRow`, which moved to `components/dictionary/word-row.tsx`.
   - Licences: pages showing Jiten rankings credit it under CC BY-SA 4.0, with a share-alike
     notice. Wikipedia and TUBELEX are credited under BSD-3-Clause.
6. **Reviews** (`Answer the fresh review of the browse pages`, `Link only the kana that start a word`)
   - Page numbers past 10,000, `…/1/` of an unknown list, and a two-kana group that doesn't exist
     are 404s. Every browse page renders per request, and a test holds them to it.
   - The home shows its search box alone when the service can't answer.
   - Long breadcrumb trails wrap on phones. The kana charts draw ぢ and ヂ, which start no word,
     unlinked, and a hiragana's page links its katakana only when words start with it.
7. **Kanji by JLPT level**, from Jonathan Waller's kanji lists, as decided on #614 (four commits:
   `Give each kanji Waller's JLPT level, and rebuild the language data`, `List kanji by JLPT level
   in the dictionary service`, `Add the JLPT kanji lists to the browse pages`, and `Answer the
   review of the JLPT kanji lists`).
   - tanos.co.uk no longer resolves, so his five kanji pages are pinned as the Wayback Machine
     captured them in 2020, in `apps/ios/LanguageData/Sources/Kanji-JLPT-Waller-2020-08-06/` (Git
     LFS). The record names each capture's timestamped URL, size, SHA-256, and Wayback digest, and
     his sharing page, which licenses the site under CC BY. Each page holds its whole level in one
     table, and every 2019–2020 capture of a level has the same digest.
   - `davidluzgouveia/kanji-data` (commit `00fd707`), whose `jlpt_new` names Waller as its source,
     lists the same 2,211 kanji at the same levels. The record keeps the cross-check; the
     compilation isn't imported.
   - `import_jlpt_kanji_levels.py` reads the pages, and `import_kanjidic.py` writes each kanji's
     level as `wallerJlptLevel` in `KanjiReferenceData.json`. A page that doesn't match its
     record, or a kanji KANJIDIC2 lacks, fails the import. `tests/test_jlpt_kanji_contract.py`
     checks the levels against the record.
   - The service lists each level (`/v1/browse/kanji/jlpt-n5` … `jlpt-n1`), and the website adds
     the kanji lists page's "By JLPT level" cards, a page for each level, N5 and N4 chips on the
     hub, and the five in both sitemaps. The pages say the levels are estimates and credit Waller
     under CC BY, and so do the app's Credits.
   - Waller's lists give no level to 172 jōyō kanji, such as 分 and 可. No modern list does: the
     JLPT has published none since 2010. They're in no JLPT list, and their details show no JLPT
     level.
8. **Kanji details show Waller's level** (`Show Waller's JLPT level in kanji details`). This
   replaces a value learners see, as the decision comment on #614 (2026-10-06) says: "Kanji JLPT
   levels come from Jonathan Waller's kanji lists … This settles #485's level scale."
   - The app's kanji detail and the website's kanji details show Waller's level, N5 to N1, and a
     kanji outside his lists shows no JLPT stat, never KANJIDIC2's pre-2010 level. 一 and 日 show
     N5 (they showed N4), 要 N3 (it showed N2), and 分 none (it showed N4).
   - The app builds its metrics in one place (`KanjiReferenceEntry.stats`), and the kanji detail
     suite now records the JLPT stat, with 分 as a new case; the service replays it.
     `KanjiStatTests` and `kanji-data.test.ts` pin 一 and 日 to N5 and 分 to none.
   - A search or word page whose kanji details show a JLPT level credits Waller's lists under CC
     BY, beside KANJIDIC2.
   - KANJIDIC2's own `jlpt` stays in `KanjiReferenceData.json` (removing it would change the
     release's `zenbu.kanji-reference.v1` format); nothing reads it.
9. **The language-data release is complete** (`Put the ranked lists and their notices in the
   language-data release`). See "The language-data release" below.

# PR-S1: site status and purchase calls to action after the 3.1.1 rejection; release records

Branch `claude/ios-311-site`, from `main` 691fdb6. Six commits: four for the change and two from review (§5). Plan steps 11, 5, and the repo-record parts of 4.

Apple rejected AwardGrid 1.0 (3) on 2026-10-05 under Guideline 3.1.1. Two things on the public site were wrong after that:

- It said the app "is waiting for Apple's review". The review is over: the build was rejected.
- It had calls to buy something outside the app: "Check your seats.aero settings show an API tab before you subscribe" (in Chinese, 订阅之前…), and "your own paid seats.aero Pro subscription". Guideline 3.1.3 does not allow these on the 173 storefronts outside the US, and App Review reads the support and marketing pages.

The reply sent to App Review on 2026-10-06 says our support pages will have no purchase links or calls to action **by Thursday, October 8**. So deploy 1 of this PR has to be live by then.

## What changes

### 1. Registry and gate (`0bdad75`, plus the registry part of `6662f81`)

- **`release_status`** (submitted_not_live):
  - en: "AwardGrid for iPhone is submitted to the App Store and not available there yet."
  - zh: "AwardGrid iPhone 版已提交 App Store，目前还不能在那里下载。"
- **`dependency`**: the call-to-action sentence and its Chinese are gone. What remains is AwardGrid's own paraphrase, with no quotation marks: "AwardGrid depends on seats.aero's Partner API, which seats.aero licenses for non-commercial use and can limit or withdraw."
- **`prerequisite`**:
  - `allowed_copy` is the owner's D6 sentence, word for word. A Chinese version is added.
  - The extra sentences lose "paid" and "subscription". They use D6's words instead: "a seats.aero account with API access (part of seats.aero Pro, which AwardGrid does not sell)".
  - Evidence for "sample data": build 3's Welcome › "View an example" shows made-up results labelled "Illustrative data — not live availability".
- **`price`, `grid` and `released`**: the notes no longer call the prerequisite "paid". They record the rejection, Manual release (D9) and the D15 release rule.
- **Gate (`scripts/growth/validate-public-claims.mjs`)**:
  - FREE_WITHOUT_PRO now looks 160 characters around "free" (was 120) and 100 around 免费 (was 60). The D6 sentence names "seats.aero Pro" about 145 characters after the "free" of the price sentence (about 90 in Chinese).
  - STALE_STATUS now treats "is submitted to the App Store" as submission wording.
  - New tests cover both. "seats.aero Pro" further away than the window still fails.

### 2. Pages (`6662f81`)

| File | Lines changed |
|---|---|
| `support/index.html` | What it needs; "Where do I find my seats.aero API key?"; "…no API tab…", in en and zh |
| `ios/index.html` | What you need; FAQ "Is AwardGrid free?" and "Could AwardGrid stop working?", with their JSON-LD; the **status section**: the new status sentence plus the **D7** wording ("AwardGrid is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by seats.aero. Each user connects their own seats.aero account."), replacing the "question for them, not for us to assume" sentence |
| `ios/zh-hans/index.html` | 使用前提; FAQ 免费吗 / 会不会用不了 / 哪里能下载, with their JSON-LD |
| `ios/award-grid/index.html` | Lead; dependency limit; status section |
| `index.html` | Status line |
| `public/llms.txt` | Summary; Facts date (now checked 2026-10-06); "Price and status"; Dependency |
| `README.md` | Public-claims section; line 134 drops "paid" |
| `growth/geo/accuracy-answer.md` | The "free" answer and line 40 |

Other changes in this commit:

- `pages.json`: lastmod set to 2026-10-06 for `/`, `/ios/`, `/ios/award-grid/`, `/ios/zh-hans/` and `/support/`.
- The FAQ JSON-LD was regenerated with `sync-faq-schema --write`.

### 3. Release records (`7ab0ac4`, plan step 4)

`docs/release/IOS_1.0_RELEASE.md` (facts only, no licence reasoning):

- **§0 P16**, the rejection:
  - 2026-10-05 23:49 PT, submission c6c3b469-875a-48bd-b19e-7f47eace8672;
  - Guideline 3.1.1, "the app uses Pro key to unlock or enable digital features";
  - reviewed on an iPad Air 11-inch (M3);
  - Apple's screenshot is the `#/settings/seats` screen.
- **§0 P17 and the new §0.1**: the owner's decisions D1–D16 ("follow the recommendations"). D9 sets Manual release. D15 releases a build only with seats.aero's written permission. D16 is decided before resubmission.
- **§0 P18–P24**, what was done on 2026-10-06:
  - reply sent at 17:45 PDT;
  - seats.aero asked for written permission;
  - membership renews 2027-10-10;
  - internal TestFlight group created;
  - GitHub description updated;
  - PR #115 (PR-P) open;
  - Meet with App Review slots checked.
- **Stale rows fixed or marked**: P1, P3, P4, P9, P10, P11, P12, §2 D8 and D9, §6 step 10. §7.4 and §7.6 are marked superseded; §7.6 stays as the record of 1.0 as submitted, and the ASO tests still read it. §9 records the Acknowledgements artifact from D3.
- **`APP_STORE_HANDOFF.md`**: D9 (review access) and "State the prerequisites" are marked superseded, in place.

### 4. Reply record (`7271e26`, plan step 5)

body:
caisson reads the overlay registries from caisson-core under their new names, and its own view of the package overlay registry is removed. The caisson-core side is nix-caisson/caisson-core#42.

**Breaking** for a package config that selects package overlays:

```nix
# before
caisson.nixpkgs.overlays = [ lib.caisson.nixpkgs.overlays.default ];
# now
caisson.nixpkgs.overlays = [ lib.caisson-core.pkgOverlays.default ];
```

- `lib.caisson.nixpkgs.overlays` is gone. caisson-core holds the registry and now has the view, `lib.caisson-core.pkgOverlays`, so there is one spelling.
- The option `caisson.nixpkgs.overlays` of a package config keeps its name. It belongs to the nixpkgs integration and configures a nixpkgs package set.
- The lib overlay registry is read as `lib.caisson-core.libOverlays.<name>`, where it was `lib.caisson-core.nixpkgs-lib.overlays.<name>`. Only a unit test wrote it.

caisson-core is pinned at its main, which has nix-caisson/caisson-core#42, in `flake.lock` and in `tests/dependencies/flake.lock`.

Verified: the full `nix flake check` passes with those pins.

body:
## What this changes

A `send` / `public_send` through a Symbol variable naming a method the receiver lacks raised a NoMethodError that did not name the receiver:

```ruby
x = [true, 1][0]
%i[with].each { |m| p((x.public_send(m) rescue $!.message)) }   # CRuby: "undefined method 'with' for true"
%i[zork].each { |m| p((5.send(m) rescue $!.message)) }          # CRuby: "undefined method 'zork' for an instance of Integer"
```

On master these say `"undefined method 'with'"` and `"undefined method 'zork'"`.

`emit_dynamic_send` (`codegen_call.c`) expands the send over the names the Symbol can hold and ends with an arm for any other name, which built its message with no receiver. That arm now raises through `sp_nomethod_msg` on the receiver, as a literal `x.zork` does. A receiver with side effects was already read once into a temp ahead of the arms, and that temp is what the message reads (the test checks a receiver that prints). A receiverless `send(m)` keeps its message.

author: resolut1onedl
body:
## Problem

Since Dota 2 build **6951** (first seen 2026-10-07), the flattened serializers declare the var encoder `fixed8` on ~25k fields: `uint8`, `int8`, enums such as `MoveType_t` / `RenderMode_t` / `SolidType_t`, attachment handles, and `CNetworkUtlVectorBase< uint8 >`. Build 6944 declared none. The server writes these fields as 8 raw bits, but manta picks decoders by type name only and reads them as varints. The two only agree while the value is below 128.

The `CParticleSystem` instance baseline has `m_iServerControlPointAssignments` (`uint8[4]`) = 255 ×4. Read as a varint, the first `0xFF` consumes five bytes, every later field shifts, and parsing stops at `m_hControlPointEnts.0062` with

```
nextByte: insufficient buffer (380 of 379)
```

That happens on every build-6951 replay we tried, as soon as the first `CParticleSystem` is created (e.g. match 9032897977, a league lobby, and 9033035139, a public turbo game). `int8` fixed8 fields were also misread (zig-zag: 41 came out as -21).

## Fix

- `findDecoder` picks `fixed8Decoder` before the type tables: 8 bits, sign-extended for `int8`, unsigned otherwise.
- Values keep the cell kind the type-name decoders produced (`int32` for int8, `uint64` for uint8, `uint32` for everything else), so `Entity.Get` callers see the same types.
- Variable arrays tagged fixed8 decode their elements with it; the length stays a varint.

This is the same rule clarity adopted in skadistats/clarity@17b33df ("fix: honor fixed8 encoder on any S2 field type").

## Testing

- New `TestFixed8Encoder`: on master it fails with `0xffffffff` instead of `0xff`, then runs out of buffer; with the patch it passes. The existing decoder, huffman, reader, lzss and util tests pass, and so does the golden `TestMatchNew8552595443`.
- I ran a manta-only parse loop (`Start()` + `OnEntity`) on master and on this branch:

| match | build | master | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9032897977 | 6951 | error at tick 2200 | ok, tick 26908, 2510 entities created |
| 9033035139 | 6951 | error (same) | ok |
| 9032697419 | 6944 | ok, 14445 entities | identical |
| 9032516247 | 6944 | ok, 16002 entities | identical |
| 9031923491 | 6944 | ok, 12295 entities | identical |

- With the patch, the `CParticleSystem` baseline of 9032897977 decodes bit-exactly: 100 field paths, ending 5 bits before the end of the 379-byte buffer (byte padding).
- Builds older than 6951 declare no fixed8 fields, so their decoding does not change.

Replays: `http://replay151.valve.net/570/9032897977_1496998234.dem.bz2` and `http://replay153.valve.net/570/9033035139_579811620.dem.bz2`. Both are zstd-compressed despite the `.bz2` name.

body:
## Summary

- Mirrors the hardcoded tier enum from A-Guy-Admin (`TIER_SLUGS`, `TIER_RANK`, `TIER_LABEL_HE`, `TIER_PRICE_ILS`, `TIER_AI_COST_CAP_ILS`, `DEFAULT_TIER`, `isTierSlug`) into `src/lib/tiers/constants.ts`. Byte-identical with Admin; the parent-folder `TIERS.md` is the shared contract.
- Adds gate helpers for content access (learning / practice / exam), per-tier daily AI-question quota, LLM monthly cost cap reconciliation, and a Gemini model selector stub.
- Introduces `TIER_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED` kill switch (env var, default **off**). While off every gate is permissive — no content locked by tier, no cost cap enforced, no daily quota applied, no premium downgrade. Subscriptions aren't live yet, so this ships inert.
- Wires `reconcileUserLlmLimit` as fire-and-forget inside `getSessionFromToken` so `users.llmTokensLimit` tracks the admin-set `currentTier` automatically after login. Short-circuits when the switch is off so admin-tuned caps aren't clobbered during the off period.
- `checkTokenLimit` now short-circuits to `{ withinLimit: true }` when the switch is off.

## What's **not** in this PR (deferred, safe because the switch is off)

- Lesson-roadmap wiring — `useLessonGrouping` still produces locks from enrollments only. The new tier gates exist as helpers; no caller imports them yet.
- `chat-quota.ts` per-tier swap — still reads the global ConfigValues quota.
- `selectGeminiModel` adoption — adapters still resolve model names directly from `PROVIDER_MODEL_NAMES`.

See `TIERS.md` → "Web implementation" for the flip-on checklist and the full deferred list.

## Decisions needing sign-off before flipping the switch

- **Daily AI-question numbers** (free 10 / basic 50 / advanced 150 / premium `null`) — my pick vs. the current global 15 per 12h. Open to tuning.
- **ILS → tokens unit mismatch** on `llmTokensLimit` — reconciler currently writes the ILS integer as-is into the token field. Admin owns the semantic; flag before enabling.

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirm `TIER_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED` is unset (or `false`) in dev/prod Vercel env before merge.
- [ ] Deploy to `dev.aguy.co.il`, log in, hit `/api/agent/chat` — behavior unchanged vs. main (no 429 from new code, existing global quota still enforces).
- [ ] Flip switch on in a scratch preview env, confirm `/api/agent/chat` returns 429 when `llmTokensUsed >= llmTokensLimit`.
- [ ] Flip switch off again, confirm `checkTokenLimit` returns `withinLimit: true` even for over-cap users.
- [ ] Pre-push verify (typecheck / lint / build / unit tests) passes locally. ✅

kyverno도 같은 조건이다. NodePool이 지워진 뒤 wave 1에서 삭제 훅을 돌려야 한다.

## Summary

Data release 0.4.0 (schema 1.3.0). Classifications go from 526 to 946.

**Tables**
- Added 40 catalog tables from Learn and the Log Analytics metadata, 19 CrowdStrike API/FDR tables, 238 Corelight v3 tables, 121 Corelight v2 tables (legacy, replaced by v3), and 5 CrowdStrike `*V2_CL` tables.
- `Corelight_CL` and the CrowdStrike V1 API tables are legacy with `replacedBy`.
- Corrected parser aliases and missing `_CL` names: `BitwardenEventLogs_CL`, `IllumioInsightsGraph_CL`, `TheHiveData_CL`, `TrellixEvents_CL`, `ImpervaWAFCloudV2_CL`, `ElasticAgentLogs_CL`, `OktaV2_CL`, `Corelight_CL`. Removed `CrowdStrikeReplicatorV2` (a parser).
- New optional `defenderNative` field on 67 tables.

**Shared-table sources (new file)**
- `shared-table-sources.json`: 57 reviewed sources inside `CommonSecurityLog` and `Syslog`, each with a filter, optional parser, and table-style classification.
- Optional `splitHints` for data lake sources (PAN-OS, Cisco ASA/FTD, Zscaler, Infoblox, vArmour).
- All filters and hints use only operators that transformations support. Top-level `or` is parenthesized. Negated action predicates are guarded with `isnotempty()`.
- The `CommonSecurityLog` and `Syslog` records now classify only rows that match no source.
- The README explains that a table has one split rule, how to compose its condition from all deployed sources, and that `_SPLT` retention is per table.

**Field analysis**
- `New-FieldAnalysis.ps1` keeps only real columns (`-TableSchemaPath`), attributes parser calls to source tables (`parsers` section), and writes shared-source candidates.
- Fixed two bugs: case-sensitive schema filtering dropped mis-cased rule fields, and field casing depended on hash order.
- Field statistics regenerated from Azure-Sentinel `2e3336d`. Curated high-value fields cleaned (parser-alias keys and non-columns removed). `EntraIdSignInEvents` fields verified against Learn. 9 table split hints rewritten without `has_any`/`in~`.

**Reclassifications**
- `AzureDiagnostics` and `OracleWebLogicServer_CL` to C5. `prancer_CL` to C1. `CloudAuditEvents` to Defender for Cloud C3.
- `DeviceInfo` and `Tailscale_Devices_CL` to T2.
- 24 C9 tables from 365 to 180 days.
- `isFree: false` for `SecurityIncident`, `Watchlist`, `ConfidentialWatchlist`.

**Consumer impact**
- Renamed and removed `tableName` values affect consumers that pin names. Log Horizon tests reference `OktaSSO` as a replacement target (now `OktaV2_CL`).
- `shared-table-sources.json` is a new optional file. No existing contract field changed.

## Evidence

- Learn: [table plan support](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/tables-features), [Defender XDR schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-schema-tables), [EntraIdSignInEvents](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-entraidsigninevents-table), [Defender XDR connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/connect-microsoft-365-defender), [filter and split transformations](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/transformation-filter-split), [supported transformation KQL](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/data-collection/data-collection-transformations-kql), [ISOC overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/isoc-overview)
- [ISOC announcement (Tech Community)](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftthreatprotectionblog/integrated-security-operations-center-in-microsoft-defender/4559097)
- [Azure-Sentinel @ 2e3336d](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/commit/2e3336d0520681d277d1fa7b2fbc7730242f1d88): Corelight connector and parsers, CrowdStrike API CCF connector 3.4.0, vendor parsers and rules for shared-table filters and split hints
- [corelight/CorelightForCrowdStrike @ 2bf3ad4](https://github.com/corelight/CorelightForCrowdStrike/blob/2bf3ad4f110287f0c9ab8a435b5c998e613e05b7/parsers/corelight-investigator.yaml): `corelight_ad_*` = anomaly detection
- Every new source is recorded in `data/sources.json`.

- [x] New or removed table
- [x] Source or plan metadata update
- [ ] Taxonomy update
- [x] Schema or tooling change
- [x] Documentation update

- [x] `pwsh ./tests/Test-Baseline.Tests.ps1` passes (23 checks, verified in a clean clone because of the uncommitted-input guard).

author: ok
body:
Backup and recovery become one concept: a backup, opened with a passphrase.

- **One screen:** Settings → Backup holds the status, the automatic-backup switch, the folder and the passphrase. The Protection screen is gone; Profile → Backup, the stale toast and the restore banner open it.
- **Setup in two steps** (where, passphrase), ending in a toast. **One restore dialog** from onboarding and the locked screen.
- **No recovery key file:** key-only save, "save a copy", key-file restore and their IPC/main dialogs removed. The key stays sealed in the backup folder.
- **Locked computer unlocks in place** with the backup's key (`identity:unlock-from-backup`), keeping newer local data; another identity's data goes to a snapshot restore.
- **Fewer, labelled backups:** bookkeeping alone writes no snapshot; retention keeps ~7 (newest, 1/2 days, 1/2 weeks, 1/2 months) plus pins before a loss or leaving a space. The loss check no longer fires on an Activity Log purge or a rewrite.
- Also: Title Case English headings; one dialog-footer layout; a guard that every literal `t()` key exists.

Tests: typecheck, lint:ci, test:unit 3308/3308; integration backup-* and restore-* green; flow backup-restore and identity-lockout green. FE s157, s160–s164 rewritten — not yet run here (agent-desktop can't read the windows on this machine).

body:
The home screen froze for 1–2 seconds after it appeared.

After every sync — including the quick sync each time the home screen appears, when the app returns to the foreground, and hourly — `RadicalCharacterImages.downloadAll()` called `getAllSubjects()`, loading and decoding every subject (~9,000) inside a single database call just to find radicals with images. On an iPhone 13 that held the database for about 1.7 s, and the home screen's main-thread queries waited for it:

```
[background] DB query LocalCachingClient.swift:getAllSubjects() took 1658 ms
[main] DB query LocalCachingClient.swift:getUserInfo() waited 1654 ms for the database queue
Main thread was blocked for 1726 ms.
```

(Measured with temporary timing instrumentation that isn't part of this PR.)

Changes:
- New `getRadicalsWithCharacterImages()` only loads radicals (filtered on `type` in SQL), a few hundred rows instead of every subject.
- `downloadAll()` only looks for missing images once per launch, and again when a subject sync brings in new or changed subjects (a new `lccSubjectsChanged` notification).

Tested on an iPhone 13: after the change the radical query no longer shows up (under the 250 ms logging threshold) and the 1.7 s freeze is gone. Smaller freezes from the home screen's other main-thread queries remain and aren't addressed here.

author: enjay27
body:
A defect found while taking baseline screenshots for the S6d split of `ChatRow`; its own task and PR, not part of the S6 plan.

**Symptom.** With compact mode on, clicking anywhere logged `panicked at ... title_bar.rs:39:25 ... a reactive value ... has already been disposed` (and the ui's wasm hit `unreachable`) on every mouse press.

**Cause.** The title bar registers a window-wide `mousedown` listener for its picker with leptos's `window_event_listener`. In leptos_dom 0.8.8 that listener is **not** removed when the component is disposed (the returned handle has to be `remove()`d by the caller), and compact mode removes the title bar (`<Show when=!compact_mode>`). The listener stayed on the window and every later press ran its closure, which reads `picker_open`, a signal that went with the component. Toggling compact mode also added a new listener each time the bar came back.

**Change.** `utils::window_listener(event, cb)` registers the listener and removes it with the component (`on_cleanup`). The title bar's one and the nav bar's two (Ctrl+F, click outside; the nav bar goes whenever the setup wizard shows instead of the chat) use it. The other three window listeners (`app/mod.rs`, the two popup windows) live as long as their window and are unchanged.

**Test.** Not unit-testable: it needs a DOM and the reactive owner's disposal (leptos glue). `ui-preview` (headless Chromium, mock bridge, compact mode on, clicks on the sender and on the text): before the change the console shows the panic on each click, after it only the unrelated 404 for a missing asset.

**Verified.** ui tests (167), wasm check of the ui crate, core + llama + types tests, `cargo fmt --check`, memory check. No src-tauri change.

**NOT VERIFIED.** `cargo tauri dev` on Windows (the real window in compact mode).

author: laduwan
body:
## What
Moves PRP's email from Brevo to Resend, and receives email sent to PRP's Resend receiving domain.

### Sending — `utils/mailer.js`
- `sendMail` sends through **Resend** when `PRP_RESEND_API_KEY` is set, falls back to Brevo while only `BREVO_API_KEY` is set, and logs to the console with neither. Deploying before the key is in Render changes nothing.
- A 429 from Resend is waited out (honouring `retry-after`) and retried up to twice, so the broadcast loops (paced at ~5/s) don't drop recipients if the account's rate limit is lower.
- Optional `replyTo` on `sendMail`.
- SMS alerts (`sendSms`) stay on Brevo — Resend has no SMS.
- Every PRP sender (auth, payment, trial reminders, digests, broadcasts, alerts) already goes through `sendMail`, so no caller changes.
- `PRP_RESEND_API_KEY` is named apart from `RESEND_API_KEY`, which stays CounselorReady's key for `jobs/broadcast-prp-crosspromo.js`.

### Receiving — `routes/inboundEmail.js`
`POST /api/inbound-email/webhook`:
- verifies Resend's Svix signature by hand (no new dependency), with a 5-minute replay window and support for secret rotation; fails closed (503) if `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset
- answers 200 right away, then processes the `email.received` event
- logs an `email.received` activity event (shows in the admin panel)
- fetches the body from Resend's Received emails API with `PRP_RESEND_API_KEY` and forwards it to `INBOUND_FORWARD_TO` (default `ADMIN_ALERT_EMAIL`), with Reply-To set to the sender; the HTML is cleaned with `sanitize-html`
- skips redelivered events so a Resend retry doesn't forward the same email twice

`server.js` gives the route `express.raw()` before `express.json()`, like the Stripe webhook.

### Docs and copy
- `.env.example` / `render.yaml`: `PRP_RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `INBOUND_FORWARD_TO`; Brevo documented as SMS plus fallback.
- `public/privacy.html`: Resend added as an email processor; Brevo kept as backup. **The policy's effective date is not changed** — the owner should decide that.
- Admin dashboard broadcast text and job comments no longer name Brevo.

## Setup
1. Resend → Domains: verify the domain of `MAIL_FROM_EMAIL` (passreadyprep.com) and enable receiving.
2. Resend → API Keys: create a key and set `PRP_RESEND_API_KEY` on Render.
3. Resend → Webhooks → Add Webhook → URL `https://www.passreadyprep.com/api/inbound-email/webhook`, event `email.received`; set its signing secret as `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

## Testing
Local scripts against a fake Resend/Brevo endpoint:
- No key: the email is logged, not sent.
- Brevo only: sends via Brevo, `replyTo` included.
- Resend key: the first call gets a 429, the retry succeeds, and the payload carries `from`, `to`, `html`, `text` and `reply_to`.
- SMS still goes to Brevo.
- Webhook: a valid signature returns 200, a bad one returns 400, and a valid one next to a rotated-out old one returns 200.
- `node --check` passes on all server, route, util and job files.

Not tested: real Resend calls, because resend.com isn't reachable from the dev container.

body:
webapi binds SVG's 71 element interfaces (`SVGElement`, `SVGGraphicsElement`, `SVGGeometryElement`, `SVGSVGElement`, `SVGCircleElement`, the filter primitives, …) from the SVG, svg-paths, svg-animations, filter-effects and css-masking specs.

Each of SVG's 63 tags is a type of `svg_tags`, whose element `SVGTag` gives, as TypeScript's `SVGElementTagNameMap`:

```rust
document::create_element_ns(document, namespaces::Svg, svg_tags::Circle)
// document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "circle"): &'static SVGCircleElement
```

Not `Tag`'s, as `createElement("circle")` makes an `HTMLUnknownElement`. The string form is `create_element_ns_named`, as `create_element_named` is (ADR 0223). This is what the react crate needs next, to give each SVG tag its element.

ADRs 0024 and 0223 amended.

Ao abrir o mapa de uma empresa ou selecionar o botão Mapa nos resultados, o mapa passa a desenhar o trajeto de carro em azul, usando a localização real do visitante e as coordenadas da empresa. Um cartão permite abrir o Google Maps com origem e destino preenchidos.

Acrescenta GET /api/map-route para obter a geometria das ruas pelo serviço público OSRM, com validação de coordenadas e timeout. Não altera banco, autenticação, pesquisa por ponto, agrupamento de marcadores ou ações existentes. Requisições antigas são canceladas ao trocar o destino; sem GPS ou em caso de falha, o mapa permanece disponível e o botão Google Maps continua acessível.

Validação: npm run lint e npm run build passaram; sete testes existentes de marcadores passaram; seis verificações locais do endpoint cobriram entrada inválida, ordem das coordenadas e falha do provedor. Ainda falta validação visual no navegador com GPS real. O serviço público OSRM é uma dependência externa sem garantia de disponibilidade; o Google Maps recalcula o percurso ao abrir.

Alterações limitadas a src/components/ProductMap.tsx e server.ts.
