author: mtaraszewski
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds hosted platform E2E tests for the latest VLM block versions, using the Roboflow managed key (`rf_key:account`). Hosted E2E previously covered only OpenAI, Claude and Gemini, mostly pinned to v1 and each needing its own provider secret. xAI, Qwen, Meta, Z.ai, Kimi, Gemma and the generic OpenRouter block had no E2E coverage at all. The new tests need only `HOSTED_PLATFORM_TESTS_API_KEY` and also exercise the managed-key proxy path customers get by default.

- Follows the existing per-provider layout in `tests/inference/hosted_platform_tests/workflows_examples/`. Claude v5, Gemini v6 and OpenAI v7 tests are appended to the existing provider files; the other providers get one new file each. Existing v1 tests are untouched.
- Each provider gets the same tests and asserts as the existing ones: classification (`top_class == "dog"`), structured answering (`"2"` dogs), object detection (exactly 2 dogs) and secondary classifier (no `dog` class after replacement). The new secondary-classifier tests also assert that at least one detection is kept, because the class-replacement step drops detections whose crops got no classification, so an empty list would otherwise pass. Every test runs in both auth modes with the existing `flaky(retries=4)` marker.
- Reads `$steps.<model>.predictions` directly instead of chaining `vlm_as_classifier@v2` / `vlm_as_detector@v2`, because the latest blocks decode internally and their docs say the parser steps are no longer needed.
- Adds `ROBOFLOW_MANAGED_API_KEY = "rf_key:account"` to the hosted conftest; it is passed as the `api_key` workflow parameter, so no `skipif` is needed.
- Kimi, Gemma and OpenRouter have no detection test because `vlm_as_detector@v2` has no model type for them. Kimi steps set `max_tokens: 2048`, since the block default let the reasoning model run out of tokens on the secondary classifier.

| File | Block | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_workflow_with_claude.py` (appended) | `anthropic_claude@v5` | 4 |
| `test_workflow_with_gemini.py` (appended) | `google_gemini@v6` | 4 |
| `test_workflow_with_openai.py` (appended) | `open_ai@v7` | 4 |
| `test_workflow_with_spacexai.py` | `spacexai@v3` | 4 |
| `test_workflow_with_qwen_vlm.py` | `qwen_vlm@v4` (OpenRouter backend) | 4 |
| `test_workflow_with_meta_vlm.py` | `meta_vlm@v3` | 4 |
| `test_workflow_with_zai_vlm.py` | `zai_vlm@v2` | 4 |
| `test_workflow_with_kimi_openrouter.py` | `kimi_openrouter@v3` | 3 |
| `test_workflow_with_google_gemma.py` | `google_gemma@v4` | 3 |
| `test_workflow_with_openrouter.py` | `openrouter@v3` | 3 |

## Type of Change

- Tests only. No library or block code changes.

## Testing

- **Staging E2E, all 37 new tests passed** on the first attempt: [run 37618894087](https://github.com/roboflow/inference/actions/runs/37618894087), `hosted_inference_e2e_test_staging.yml` on this branch with `test_target=serverless-v2`. The 10 failures in that run are pre-existing and come from staging lagging `main`: `test_get_versions_of_execution_engine` (1.15.2 vs 1.16.1), `test_gpt_6_1_sol_*` (model not deployed on staging) and `test_describing_workload_*` (404/405).
- An earlier run ([37617125308](https://github.com/roboflow/inference/actions/runs/37617125308)) failed the Kimi secondary classifier with "reasoning model ran out of tokens"; fixed by `max_tokens: 2048`.
- Compiled all 51 workflow specs in the touched files with `compile_workflow_graph`: 51/51 OK.
- The non-empty check in the secondary-classifier tests (9d74f7d) was added after these staging runs and has not run on staging yet. All 100 tests in the changed modules collect with `pytest --collect-only`.
- `black` and `isort` clean on changed files; `flake8` reports nothing new. Pre-existing F541/F811/F401 findings in untouched code remain, including the duplicate `test_structured_prompting_workflow` name in the OpenAI file.

## Additional Context

Each staging run makes about 94 managed-key VLM calls, billed to the staging workspace. Model answers can vary, so the strict asserts (exactly 2 dogs) rely on the existing retries.

Next steps, in separate PRs:
- Add Kimi, Gemma and OpenRouter model types to `vlm_as_detector@v2`, then add detection tests for them.
- Consider raising the `kimi_openrouter` block's default `max_tokens`, since customers hit the same token exhaustion.
- Pass provider keys (or the managed key) to `integration_tests_workflows_x86.yml`; about 45 `WORKFLOWS_TEST_*`-gated VLM integration tests are always skipped today.
- Schedule the hosted E2E (e.g. nightly on staging) with Slack reporting, instead of `workflow_dispatch` only, and add a `test_path` input to run a subset.
- Cover the remaining blocks: Llama 3.2 Vision v2, Qwen 3.5/3.6 (OpenRouter), OpenAI-compatible, Cosmos 3.
- Rename the duplicate `test_structured_prompting_workflow` in `test_workflow_with_openai.py` (F811 shadows one test).

author: mritd
body:
## Summary

A module-by-module review of the iOS code found async races, lifecycle bugs, and swallowed errors left over from feature work. This PR fixes the user-visible and lifecycle findings. The large structural refactors are left for a later phase. It also makes the web tasks install their dependencies, so `task server` works in a fresh worktree.

### Session and API
- Every transition that leaves the session bumps an epoch. A bootstrap, connect, or 401 that returns afterwards no longer changes the new session.
- A 401 signs the user out only when the request carried the current token. The SSE client uses the same 401 and error mapping as other requests.
- An expired saved token reports "Session expired" instead of "Anonymous access is disabled".
- Connect sends the network request before replacing the stored server.
  - A failed connect keeps the previous server and token.
  - The timeout message shows, and cancellation stops the login.
  - A login that finishes after the user chose offline mode no longer leaves offline mode.
- Each sync scope has a single `SyncStore`.
- Dead API methods are removed.

### Player
- A source switch fetches the new detail before changing the selection, and a generation counter guards it. A slower earlier reply, including the page's opening load, cannot override the user's pick.
- Coordinator callbacks carry their item, so a stale item's error no longer triggers a fallback.
- iOS resumes on appear only if the video was playing. The error message clears after recovery. tvOS shows a failure screen when every source fails.
- Scrubbing goes through view model methods, and a cancelled drag resets correctly.
- `PlaybackProgressPolicy` holds the progress rules for both players. The online player now throttles saves by wall clock.

### Browse and screens
- Searches can be cancelled, and an older search can no longer overwrite a newer one.
  - A search keeps running when the user leaves the page.
  - The search context lives in `SearchViewModel`.
- A failed first Categories load can be retried. The first Home and Categories loads keep running when the user switches tabs.
- Admin:
  - A failed add keeps the form input.
  - A failed setting change rolls back.
  - Batch deletes reload once.
  - Tabs and setting keys use enums.
- Clearing watch history asks for confirmation. Downloads list and show screens share one edit-mode modifier.

### Downloads
- Scope transitions run one at a time. `beginDeactivate()` queues its transition as soon as it is called.
- Concurrent `LocalMediaServer.start()` calls share one start. Readiness comes from state callbacks, and `stop()` cancels a start in progress.
- Bulk deletes move directories into `Downloads/.trash` and delete them on a background queue. Transport cancellation and manifest decoding run off the main actor.
- A present but malformed IV now fails the playlist. One `KMTVProxyURL` rule decides what counts as a proxy URL.
- Storage reports a single `usedBytes`. Dead per-scope API is removed.

### Sync (matches `web/src/sync`)
- Ported from web:
  - start waiters, so a sync requested before `start()` waits for the first cycle
  - the `login` and `online` reasons, plus an online trigger that resets the retry backoff
  - stored-row validation
- SwiftData read and save failures are now visible: an unreadable scope is not treated as empty.
- `requestSync(_:waitingAtMost:)` uses a task group. `resetForNewEpoch` is renamed to web's `resetForServerLoss`.

### Build
- `web:install` is skipped while `node_modules` matches `package.json` and `bun.lock`. The `web:*` tasks depend on it, so `task server` and `task build` install dependencies when they are missing.

## Compatibility
- No server or API changes, and no new SwiftData fields.
- Downloads created before this change are unaffected. The trash folder is created on first use and swept at launch.

## Verification
- `KMTVTests`: 475 of 475 pass on the iPhone 17 Pro iOS 26.5 simulator, up from 403.
- iOS and tvOS builds pass, and so does `task bilingual-check`.
- Screenshot tours against the dev server:
  - iPhone: anonymous connect, home, search, playback, categories with back to top, favorites, downloads, and profile.
  - iPad: the "Session expired" prompt after a database reset, home, categories, the downloads swipe and edit mode, and profile.
- A final review of the whole change found 8 issues, and all were fixed:
  - the opening load could override a source the user picked
  - a search, or a first Home or Categories load, was cancelled when the user left the page
  - the offline sync engine kept sync requests waiting
  - logout waited for an activation to finish
  - a deactivation could run after a later activation
  - an interrupted bootstrap was never retried
  - a server stop test could pass without checking anything

## Not covered
- Signed-in flows: the dev admin credentials are not available here.
- Not checked on a device:
  - fullscreen playback rate sync
  - `LocalMediaServer` restarts across background and foreground
- Structural refactors left for later:
  - splitting `DownloadManager` and `PlayerViewModel`
  - a `PlaybackEngine` protocol
  - tvOS design tokens
  - a shared poster grid and badges

author: christhomas
body:
## What

The part of #52 that can be done without an observation. `extent::parse_entries` now refuses an entry kind it cannot decode by name (crc128, stripe_ptr, flags, reconcile, numbered by S1 9.1.3's order of the remaining kinds, which the code says is inferred from that order alone) and points at the open question. A `bgcompress` fixture (`--background_compression=lz4`) is added to the guest build so that a reconcile entry, if the formatter writes one on such a filesystem, appears in a lister output a later change can learn the layout from.

Decoding or skipping those entries is still blocked on seeing one: only crc128's size (24 bytes) is documented, and S1 gives no sizes for the others, so skipping by a guessed size would be exactly the kind of guess the clean-room record forbids. #52 stays open for that half.

Stacked on #73. Not compiled locally; CI is the first run.

Refs #52.

author: raashish1601
body:
`posthoc_tamhane` applies the Dunn-Sidak adjustment as `1 - (1 - p) ** groups.size`, so the exponent is the number of groups k instead of the number of pairwise comparisons m = k(k-1)/2 that the docstring describes. For three groups k = m, which is why the existing tests (all with three groups) pass. From four groups on the p values are too small.

```python
import scikit_posthocs as sp

x = [[1, 2, 3, 5, 1], [12, 31, 54, 62, 12], [10, 12, 6, 74, 11], [4, 8, 6, 9, 7]]
sp.posthoc_tamhane(x).iloc[0, 1]
# master: 0.1416, PMCMRplus::tamhaneT2Test: 0.2047
```

The fix uses m = k(k-1)/2 as the exponent, for both `welch=True` and `welch=False`.

I added `test_posthoc_tamhane_four_groups`, which checks both variants against `PMCMRplus::tamhaneT2Test` (PMCMRplus 1.9.12, R 4.6.1) on four groups. It fails on master and passes with the change. The full test suite passes (`pytest .`), and `ruff format --check` is clean on the changed files.

While checking this I compared most of the all-pairs tests against PMCMRplus on a four-group data set and a 10x4 block design. Everything else matched except `posthoc_dunnett_t3`, which I'll send separately.

author: pluveto
body:
**Background**
Previously, `JS_SetPromiseHook` only emitted `BEFORE` and `AFTER` hooks during thenable assimilation. Consequently, neither ordinary `.then()` callbacks nor native `await` resumptions triggered these hooks.

**Impact**
Embedders hosting QuickJS (e.g., Node-like runtimes) were unable to track execution context around asynchronous operations or trace async call chains (similar to `async_hooks`).

**Changes Summary**
Fixes the limitation in `JS_SetPromiseHook` by emitting `BEFORE` and `AFTER` hooks around `.then()` callbacks and native `await` continuations, allowing embedders to reliably track async context transitions.

Preserves all existing public C API function signatures and enum values without breaking changes.

**Detailed Changes**
1. **Emit hooks for ordinary reactions & ensure balanced exit:**
   * Captures the associated promise when a reaction job is enqueued.
   * Emits the `BEFORE` hook before execution and the `AFTER` hook upon completion.
   * Guarantees that the `AFTER` hook is also invoked on uncatchable-exception exit paths (e.g., OOM, host interruption), ensuring entries and exits remain strictly balanced.

2. **Isolate native `await` continuation context:**
   * **When hooks are enabled**: Creates a dedicated continuation capability for native `await` resumptions, setting the awaited promise as its parent. This gives each `await` point its own identity, preventing multiple async functions awaiting the same shared promise from conflating.
   * **When hooks are disabled**: Retains the existing capability-elision optimization with zero performance overhead.

**Testing**
1. **Documentation & Assertions:**
   * Updated the C API documentation and existing promise-hook count assertions.

2. **Covered 18 Regression Scenarios:**
   * Settled and pending fulfillments/rejections;
   * Absent handlers, handlers throwing exceptions, and `finally` callbacks;
   * The `JS_PromiseThen` C API and custom `species` constructors;
   * Reentrant job execution;
   * Native `await` scenarios (single await, sequential awaits, and shared awaited promises);
   * Interruptions within both reaction jobs and async continuations;
   * Verified active promise identities, `await` parent-child links, and balanced hook entry/exit pairs.

3. **Validation Results:**
   * **Environment**: Windows x64 / MinGW GCC 13.2.0 / `QJS_BUILD_WERROR=ON`.
   * **Test Suites**: `api-test`, `lre-test`, and built-in Test262 passed in both Debug and Release configurations (`0/120 errors, 9 excluded`).
   * **GC Stress**: `api-test` passed in Debug mode with `QJS_ENABLE_GC_STRESS=ON`.
   * **Negative Check**: The new tests fail as expected on the unpatched engine due to the missing `BEFORE` hook, confirming the regression coverage is effective.
   * *(Note: The full external Test262 suite and other platform configurations were not tested locally).*

author: raaaas
body:
## What

Adds `plugin-catalog/agent-batch.yaml` — **Agent Batch**, a parallel AI task orchestrator: paste a task list, Hermes phases it, each task dispatches an independent GitHub Actions agent on its own branch, PRs tracked from a desktop panel. Free-tier runners (opencode/kilo keyless) or BYOK (cline / claude-code / codex / dsh + provider keys).

## Owner submission (rule 5)

I (`raaaas`) own and maintain https://github.com/raaaas/hermes-agent-batch — this is the plugin author's own submission.

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- **Network calls:** the backend router (`plugin/dashboard/plugin_api.py`) makes HTTPS calls to `api.github.com` only — list workflow runs, trigger `workflow_dispatch`, read PR status. No third-party endpoints.
- **Credentials:** reads `GITHUB_TOKEN` from the environment, falling back to the `GITHUB_TOKEN=` line in `~/.hermes/.env` (the shared Hermes env the user configures for GitHub access). It does not read any other tool's token files, and never writes or refreshes credentials.
- **No self-updating code (rule 3):** `desktop/plugin.js` is static; its only `fetch` targets its own local backend router. No downloads, no remote loaders, no update checkers.
- **SDK surface (rule 8):** `plugin.js` imports only `@hermes/plugin-sdk` and `react`. No prototype patching, no eval, no MutationObserver, no reaching into app internals.
- **No core overrides (rule 9):** the plugin registers a FastAPI router + a desktop page only; it does not monkey-patch anything.
- **Shell/processes:** the plugin itself spawns no processes; all agent execution happens in GitHub Actions workflows in the author's repo, on the user's own GitHub account.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate plugin/ --install-deps` at the pinned SHA:

```
✓ manifest — plugin.yaml parses
✓ loadable — entry: desktop/plugin.js
✓ security scan — safe
✓ desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface
Validation passed.
```

## Pin

`sha: 70fc4df633fc414d48ff2c759e3b0f30251802de` (main @ 2026-10-07), `subdir: plugin`. The repo's workflows and docs live outside `subdir` and are never installed.

The end-to-end pipeline behind this (dispatch → sandboxed agent → commit → PR) was verified live today: Actions run https://github.com/raaaas/hermes-agent-batch/actions/runs/37605204560 and issue-agent run https://github.com/raaaas/hermes-agent-batch/pull/4.

author: rajnandan1
body:
Picks shipped in 0.7.0, but in big repos they never ran: the memory list alone passed the 32,000-character limit of a pick request, so the job logged `too_big` and made no call (#23). Two of the owner's repos have 212 and 184 memories, with lists of 37,788 and 39,611 characters.

Now a request lists at most 50 memories. A repo with 50 or fewer sends every memory, as before. A bigger repo sends the 50 that the word search scores best for the prompt plus the newest turn. The list keeps its form and order (by address, `m1`, `m2`, …), so the model sees the same request shape that 0.7.0 measured.

```diff
 pick()
   memories = ix.all(scopes)
+  if memories > 50
+    memories = ix.search(terms(prompt + newest turn), scopes, 50), sorted by address
   message(memories, turns, prompt)       # 32,000-character guard and too_big stay
```

The `pick` log line gets two counts, `memories` (in the repo) and `listed` (in the request), so the live log shows when the cut happens. The transcript is now read once per job. Version 0.7.1.

How I checked it:
- `cargo test --release --locked`: 40 unit tests and 33 hook tests. The new hook test lists all 50 memories at 50, and 50 of 60 at 60: a memory that matches only the newest turn is in, and one that matches only an older turn is out.
- `python3 eval/harness.py report --picks` on the frozen cases (97 pick jobs, $1.82): 19 injections, 15 useful (79%), 2 false. 0.7.0 gave 23 injections, 18 useful (78%), 3 false. The goals are 67% or more and 13 or more useful.
- The cut ran in 19 of the 97 cases. Only 4 cases picked differently from 0.7.0, and the cut does not explain any of them: 3 had 50 memories or fewer (same request as 0.7.0), and in the 4th the search matched 21 of 70 memories, so the cut left out only memories that share no word with the query. The difference is the model choosing differently between two runs.
- Replay of the prompt path with picks on: p50 9.5 ms, p95 14.8 ms.

Risk: low and easy to roll back. Picks are off by default. The change touches only the pick job, which runs off the prompt path.

Closes #23

author: mr-tz
body:
compute_macho_layout named a thin Mach-O by running a full
machofile.UniversalMachO parse and reading cputype/cpusubtype from its
result. Any failure in that parse, for example load commands truncated
after the header or a corrupt command, made the node "macho: macho" even
though the two header fields were intact. machofile also iterates
ncmds load commands without a bound, so a header with ncmds 0xFFFFFFFF
on a 39 KB file allocated past 16 GB before floss got control.

The arch name now comes from cputype and cpusubtype at offsets 4 and 8
of the header, read with the same magic, endianness and header size
checks that _parse_macho_endian_and_cmds already applies. A header
shorter than 28 (32 for 64-bit) bytes still yields "macho: macho".
With that, nothing in floss uses machofile anymore, so the import and
the dependency in pyproject.toml, requirements.txt and the pyinstaller
spec are removed; the ncmds exposure goes with it, since floss's own
load command loop stops at the end of the slice.

Output change: thin Mach-O files whose load commands machofile could
not parse are now named by arch. No file in tests/data or the runs
corpus is affected.

## What this PR now carries (3 commits, 3 themes)
This PR started as the eval gate; it now also carries two follow-ups requested on the same branch. Commits are separate so each can be reviewed alone.

### 1. Eval gate (`cdae131`)
- **Credential-free gate on the Eligibility Agent's decisions** — `apps/api/evals/test_grant_agent.py` + `grant_agent_cases.jsonl` (38 golden cases) running the real `analyst_node`, `grant_compatibility_check` and `verification.assess_results`: zero false "eligible" results, no unverified pair ever reported `stackable`, no `confirmed` without supporting evidence. Three sensitivity tests prove each gate can fail.
- **`FAITHFULNESS_GATE` 0.7 → 0.75**, and the gate now prints `NOT MEASURED` instead of a bare `n/a`.
- Why: the repo has **no RAGAS runner**; the gate only reads a `FAITHFULNESS_SCORE` secret, which is empty (confirmed in this PR's CI log: `NOT MEASURED`).

### 2. Nightly grant refresh (`f3d9c95`)
Scheduled crawling already exists (`ingest-sources`, `ingest-madani`, `deadline-monitor`), so I built only what was missing: the Tavily deadline check ran live per query, and nothing re-checked grants nobody asked about.
- `apps/api/scripts/agents/grant_refresh.py` runs the agent's own classifier over every active `grant_database` row. **`confirmed` → sets `last_verified` (live mode only, the only column ever written). `changed`/`closed` → reported, database untouched.** `application_deadline` is never edited (migration 023 mirrors it into deadline alerts).
- `.github/workflows/grant-refresh.yml`: 17:30 UTC nightly, hosted on GitHub like `deadline-monitor.yml`. **Scheduled runs are dry-run unless the repository variable `GRANT_REFRESH_LIVE` is `'true'`**, so merging this writes nothing to production.
- Exit 1 only for infrastructure failure (database unreachable/placeholder, or *every* check failing — e.g. bad Tavily key). No `TAVILY_API_KEY` → skips with a notice.

### 3. Faithfulness-judge pilot — scaffold (`5473b91`)
`scripts/evals/faithfulness/`: claim splitter, a lexical baseline judge, a client for a self-hosted `autotrust/JEV-27B-VL` `/v1/decide`, calibration metrics with a verdict that returns **`insufficient_data` below 30 labelled examples per language** and requires beating the baseline, and a scorer that writes the `--scores-json` file the deploy gate reads (and refuses to emit a score if >10% of claims fail). 18 **synthetic** seed rows; plumbing only.

- **The workflow has not run on GitHub Actions**, and nothing has hit live Tavily or Supabase (no credentials in the sandbox). First step after merge: dispatch it manually in dry-run and read the step summary.
- **No model has been run for the pilot** (no GPU, no route to Hugging Face). Request/response shapes come from the model card; it lists **English only**, so BM/ZH accuracy is unknown. Real labelled data, a pipeline exporter, hosting and Nebius packaging are still to do (see `scripts/evals/faithfulness/README.md`). There is deliberately no cron for the pilot: hosted runners have no GPU.
- The new Eligibility Agent fixtures are synthetic programmes: they test the rules, not what any agency currently requires.

1. **Secrets** for the refresh: `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `TAVILY_API_KEY` (the first two already exist for other workflows).
2. Dispatch **Grant Refresh** once in `dry-run` and review the summary. Only then set the repo variable `GRANT_REFRESH_LIVE=true` if you want nightly stamping.

author: dennisosrm
body:
## What

Each MQTT output now publishes its availability: a retained `online` whenever it (re)connects, and a retained `offline` registered as MQTT last will, which the broker publishes once the connection is lost.

| Output         | Availability topic |
|----------------|--------------------|
| Home Assistant | `solar/hms_<device id>/availability`, without a device id `solar/<client id>/availability` |
| Simple MQTT    | `hms800wt2/availability`, with a device id `<device id>/availability` |

Home Assistant discovery sets `availability_topic` on every sensor and on the power limit number, so the entities show as unavailable when the publisher is gone instead of keeping their last values.

## Why

Without it, a stopped or crashed publisher is indistinguishable from an inverter that stopped changing its values.

## How

- Based on koskev/hms-mqtt-publisher@ceef500 by @koskev, cherry-picked as the first commit with Kevin as author. The conflict with the current wrapper (client id handling, renewed subscriptions, receive channel) was resolved keeping his last will and birth message.
- Follow-up adaptations: the topic is no longer a fixed `<base>/status` but derived per output from its configuration before connecting (the last will must be set in `MqttOptions`), so several instances with different `DEVICE_ID`s don't share it. Without a device id the Home Assistant output uses its client id, since the DTU serial number is only known after the first reading.
- `MqttConfig` gets an internal `availability_topic` (not read from `config.toml`), filled by `HomeAssistant::new` and `SimpleMqtt::new` before they create the client, so the topic layout stays in the output modules and any `MqttWrapper` sees it.
- The rumqttc wrapper sets the last will when a topic is given and publishes `online` on every ConnAck, so it is restored after reconnects (also after the broker already sent the will). Building the `MqttOptions` moved into a function so it can be tested.
- README documents the topics.

Platform (small, fabrics 1.2.1 with `RT_PRIORITY=50` and `capabilities.add: [IPC_LOCK, SYS_NICE]`): all three agents logged `rt_priority_failed "Operation not permitted"`. Kubernetes/containerd put added capabilities only into the bounding set; the agent runs as uid 1000 and gets no ambient caps, so it had no effective `SYS_NICE`.

- Image: `setcap cap_sys_nice,cap_ipc_lock+p /usr/local/bin/mxl-fabrics-agent` (permitted only). With `+ep`, execve fails with EPERM wherever the runtime doesn't grant them (plain `docker run`, CI); with `+p` a missing capability just stays missing.
- `raisePermittedCapabilities()` at the very start of `main` (before any thread) raises the permitted set into the effective set via capget/capset; the `startup` log has `capabilities` (e.g. `sys_nice,ipc_lock`).
- deploy example adds `SYS_NICE`; README notes the requirement; CHANGELOG 1.2.2.

Lab: see comment (with `--cap-add SYS_NICE` the fabric thread runs SCHED_FIFO 50; without it the agent still starts and logs `rt_priority_failed`).

author: guimartins
body:
A câmera de perseguição (modo padrão) se afastava da moto conforme ela acelerava: de 6,4 m parada para quase 14 m no talo, e a moto ficava com menos da metade do tamanho na tela.

## Por quê

A câmera seguia a **posição da moto no mundo** com um filtro exponencial (`cam_follow = 7`). Um filtro assim fica para trás na proporção da velocidade (`v / k`): a 52 m/s são 7,4 m de atraso.

## O que muda

- **`scripts/chase_camera.gd`**: a câmera passa a seguir o **deslocamento em relação à moto**. A distância é a do slider em qualquer velocidade. O atraso continua onde servia: o deslocamento gira atrasado na curva, então a moto ainda escapa na saída dela, e a altura segue suavizada, então ladeira e quique continuam amortecidos.
- **`cam_fov_speed_gain` de 16 para 8**: abrir a lente no talo também encolhia a moto, porque de 50° para 66° ela perdia mais de um quarto do tamanho. 8 é o valor que o `docs/REFERENCIA_VIDEO.md` já propunha.
- **Slider novo `cam_recuo`** (padrão 0, no F3): metros a mais de distância na velocidade máxima, para testar um respiro pequeno se a distância fixa ficar dura.
- **`tests/unit/test_chase_camera.gd`**: `test_distancia_fixa_no_talo`. No código antigo ele reprova (13,4 m contra 6,4 m).

GARUPA, CAPACETE e DIAGNÓSTICO não mudam de comportamento.

## Verificação

- `test` (81 casos), `selftest` e `lint` verdes depois do merge com a `master`. O baseline não varia, porque o banco de provas não roda câmera.
- `regressao-visual`: o céu caiu de 0,329 para 0,245, mais que os 20% de tolerância. É o enquadramento novo: comparando os quadros do CI da master com os da branch, é a mesma cena, com moto e prédios maiores e menos céu. O `baseline_visual.json` foi atualizado com os valores do CI no commit `154d2a1`, que explica a mudança.

body:
# Description

Closes #2439.

`SnowflakeEmbed` loaded `Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-long` with `trust_remote_code=True`. The repository's remote code looks for `pytorch_model.bin` (the repository ships only `model.safetensors`; the `use_safetensors=True` we pass is not the kwarg it reads), and when the weights are made available its forward pass fails on transformers 5 (`'NomicBertModel' object has no attribute 'get_extended_attention_mask'`). `library/jailbreak_detection/requirements.txt` pins `transformers>=5.3.0`, so the documented in-process setup for the `jailbreak detection model` rail could not load the embedding model and every request through the rail ended in an internal error.

The architecture is native to transformers (`NomicBert`), so the tokenizer and model are now loaded without remote code. Everything else is unchanged (`add_pooling_layer=False`, `use_safetensors=True`, the CLS embedding).

Verified in a clean `python:3.12-slim` container with torch 2.14.1 (CPU) and transformers 5.19.0:

| load | result |
|---|---|
| `trust_remote_code=True` (before) | `OSError: Model name Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-long was not found.` |
| native, `use_safetensors=True` | `NomicBertModel`, embedding shape (1, 768), 29 s including download |
| native, `add_pooling_layer=False, use_safetensors=True` (this PR) | same class, same embedding (allclose) |

A side effect operators will notice: no `trust_remote_code` prompt or remote code execution when the rail starts.

# Test plan

- New `tests/test_jailbreak_model_based.py::test_snowflake_embed_loads_without_remote_code`: asserts neither `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` nor `AutoModel.from_pretrained` is asked for remote code and that `use_safetensors=True` is kept. Fails on the previous loader, passes now.
- `pytest tests/test_jailbreak_model_based.py`: 18 passed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both files.

author: tokuda99
body:
## Background

camxiom ships two implementations of the same projection math: a 4-wide one
(`CAMXIOM_HAS_SSE2`, which also serves aarch64 through the `__m128` → NEON
mapping in `simd_neon_compat.hpp`) and an 8-wide AVX2 one. Which one is used was
decided **at compile time**, by `#if defined(__AVX2__)`.

A compiler only defines `__AVX2__` when the whole build is given `-mavx2`.
Neither this CMakeLists nor a consumer's default build does that. So outside the
one CI variant that sets the flag explicitly, **the AVX2 kernels compiled to
nothing** — every package built and installed the normal way ran 4-wide code on
every machine, including the machines the AVX2 kernels were written for. The CI
`avx2` variant proved the kernels worked, and nothing shipped them.

Raising the baseline is not an option for a library that gets distributed as a
binary: the result would execute an illegal instruction on any CPU without AVX2.

## Approach, and what was rejected

**Rejected — a `CAMXIOM_ENABLE_AVX2` CMake option.** Small, but it leaves the
default exactly as broken and produces a binary that faults on older CPUs. Users
who install through colcon/ament or a `.deb` never touch compiler flags, so
opt-in means "off" in practice.

**Rejected — splitting each `simd_*.{hpp,cpp}` into an SSE and an AVX2
translation unit and compiling only the latter with `-mavx2 -mfma`.** This is the
textbook approach, but it is a trap here: `batch/float.cpp` includes all five
SIMD headers, which hold ~43 `inline` kernel bodies. Compiling one TU with
`-mavx2` and another without gives those inline functions two different
definitions — an **ODR violation**. The linker picks one arbitrarily, and if it
picks the AVX2 one, the binary faults on a CPU without AVX2. Avoiding it means
splitting every header into declarations and kernel bodies first.

**Chosen — per-function `__attribute__((target("avx2,fma")))`.** The compiler
emits AVX2 for the attributed function alone while the rest of the translation
unit stays baseline. No header split, no TU split, no mixed flags, therefore no
ODR hazard: every TU is compiled the same way. Selection moves to run time via
`cpuHasAvx2()` (`__builtin_cpu_supports`, resolved once and cached).

One binary, fast where the CPU allows it, correct where it does not. Building
with `-mavx2 -mfma` still works and is unchanged — the attribute then matches the
command line and becomes a no-op, which is why the CI `avx2-native` variant is
kept.

The attribute is a GCC/Clang extension. On any other x86 compiler the AVX2
kernels stay out of the build and `cpuHasAvx2()` returns false, which is the
behaviour that exists today.

## Results

Same binary, default flags, one 5.5 GHz core, 2M points, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`,
best of 5. The "SSE2" column is what a normally-built camxiom has been doing
until now:

| | SSE2 | AVX2 | |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| pinhole forward | 3.36 ms | **2.41 ms** | 1.39x |
| pinhole inverse | 40.68 ms | **39.20 ms** | 1.04x |
| fisheye forward | 7.02 ms | **4.12 ms** | 1.70x |
| double sphere forward | 6.42 ms | **3.89 ms** | 1.65x |
| double sphere inverse | 7.27 ms | **4.29 ms** | 1.70x |

No path regresses.

## A 2.7x regression this nearly shipped

Turning the AVX2 kernels on by default surfaced something the compile-time gate
had been hiding: **the KB4-family fisheye inverse is 2.7x SLOWER on AVX2 than on
SSE2** (51.0 vs 19.0 ms per million pixels, reproducible across runs). Merging
the dispatch alone would have made that the new default for every fisheye user.

Two things were going on:

1. The AVX2 kernel was **missing the SSE4 kernel's Newton early exit**, so it
   always ran its full 15 iterations while the 4-wide one converged in a handful.
   That is a defect in its own right and is fixed here: 101.9 → 75.8 ns/pixel.
2. It still does not close the gap (SSE2 is at 37.9). Every lane of a group must
   converge before the shared Newton loop can exit, so widening the group makes
   a slow lane likelier, and that more than eats the width.

So this one path is **excluded from AVX2 dispatch** and stays on the 4-wide
kernel. The carve-out sits directly below an existing aarch64 carve-out that
exists for the same reason, and follows its shape. The AVX2 fisheye *forward*
kernel is unaffected and stays selected — it is 1.70x faster.

## Consequences reviewers should know about

**1. The same binary can now produce slightly different batch results on two
machines**, because the AVX2 kernels use FMA and the 4-wide ones do not. This is
the same spread that already existed between a baseline build and an `-mavx2`
build; it stays inside the tolerance the scalar-vs-SIMD parity tests assert, and
the documented determinism guarantee — repeated calls within one process are
bit-identical — is unaffected.

**2. Without an override, the 4-wide kernels would lose all automated
coverage.** Every GitHub-hosted runner supports AVX2, and camxiom has no aarch64
CI job, so after this change every CI job would take the AVX2 path and the
4-wide kernels — which are the kernels that actually run on Jetson through the
NEON mapping — would be compiled and never executed.

`CAMXIOM_DISABLE_AVX2=1` pins a process to the 4-wide path. The CI matrix
becomes three variants covering the three combinations that matter:

| variant | flags | `CAMXIOM_DISABLE_AVX2` | exercises |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sse2-baseline` | — | `1` | 4-wide kernels |
| `avx2-runtime` | — | — | AVX2 via `cpuHasAvx2()` — what consumers get |
| `avx2-native` | `-mavx2 -mfma` | — | whole-TU AVX2, attribute is a no-op |

The switch is also the first diagnostic step when a result differs between
machines, which is standard for libraries doing runtime dispatch (OpenCV's
`OPENCV_CPU_DISABLE`, NumPy's `NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES`, oneDNN's
`ONEDNN_MAX_CPU_ISA`). It earned its keep during this PR: the fisheye inverse
regression above was found by A/B-ing both paths in one binary.

## A failure mode no functional test can catch

If AVX2 instructions escape the `target`-attributed functions into code that
runs unconditionally, the library faults **only on a CPU without AVX2**. No CI
runner has one, so every test would pass and the break would reach users.

`tests/simd_containment/check_avx2_containment.py` disassembles the built
archive and fails if either (a) no AVX2 instructions are present at all — the
kernels did not make it into the build and the dispatch selects dead code, the
exact bug this PR fixes — or (b) AVX2 instructions appear in a function without
the attribute. It is not registered for an `-mavx2` build, where the whole
library is AVX2 by construction and containment is not meaningful.

## Test plan

- [x] 18/18 tests pass, default build, AVX2 selected at run time
- [x] 18/18 tests pass, default build, `CAMXIOM_DISABLE_AVX2=1`
- [x] 17/17 tests pass, `-mavx2 -mfma` build (containment test not registered)
- [x] AVX2 containment verified: 14 attributed functions carry AVX2
      instructions, zero leaks into baseline code
- [x] No path slower than before on any of the six measured kernels
- [x] clang-format clean, no new warnings under `-Wall -Wextra`
- [ ] Review on aarch64: `CAMXIOM_HAS_AVX2` is guarded on `CAMXIOM_X86`, so the
      NEON path should be untouched, but CI cannot confirm it
- [ ] Worth confirming on a pre-AVX2 x86 machine if one is available — the
      containment test is a static proxy for that

body:
## What changes
New `utils/socket-auth.ts`: `verifySocketToken` (valid JWT **and** live session **and** account `ACTIVE` and not banned — PENDING_VERIFICATION, SUSPENDED, SUSPENDED_REVIEW all refused) + `socketAuthMiddleware`.
- **Main namespace** (chat, ai-review, ai-assistant, assessment, proposal-audit, setup-test, help-assistant): `io.use(...)` at the handshake. A valid token of a non-active account / revoked session is **refused at connect** (`connect_error`, `data.code = ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE | SESSION_REVOKED | NOT_FOUND`). **Compatibility:** the namespace also serves public pages, so a connection with *no token or a token that is not a valid JWT* still connects as an anonymous socket (no `userId`, no user rooms) exactly as before.
- **/assessments:** the same check, mandatory (no token = refused).
- **Token-in-payload paths** now use the same check: `join_user_room { token }`, every `setup_test:*` event (the old code only verified the JWT signature). `chat.gateway` no longer parses the token itself (it used to set `userId` from a bare `jwt.verify`); it relies on the handshake. help-assistant's own gate now also blocks SUSPENDED_REVIEW.
- **Mid-session cut:** `utils/socket-registry.ts` (`disconnectUserSockets`) — `AdminUsersService.updateUserStatus` calls it when the new status is not ACTIVE: the user's live sockets (main + /assessments) receive `account_not_active { code, message }` and are disconnected; other users are untouched; moving to ACTIVE cuts nothing.

## Limits (stated, not hidden)
- The cut happens when the status is changed **through the admin status endpoint** (the only status writer in the codebase besides OTP activation). A status changed directly in the database, or a session revoked elsewhere (logout / password change), does not push a disconnect; such a socket is refused on its next connect, and its HTTP calls are already refused by `requireActiveUser` (PR #51).
- Events on an already-open socket are not re-checked per message.
- Frontend: show `account_not_active` / `connect_error.data.code` (a message + back to login) — not done in this PR.

## Tests
`socket-auth.test.ts` (6, **real Socket.IO server + client**): token verification per account state; main namespace — ACTIVE connects; PENDING / SUSPENDED / SUSPENDED_REVIEW / banned / revoked-session refused with the code; no-token / garbage / foreign-secret tokens still connect anonymously; /assessments stricter; mid-session cut (main + /assessments told and disconnected, bystander untouched, cannot reconnect, ACTIVE change cuts nothing); no-op without live sockets. Plus a setup-test case (suspended/pending/review tokens → error, no profile write, no WaseetAI call) and a SUSPENDED_REVIEW case for help-assistant. Full suite 2054 tests, 0 failures. Disclosed edit: `setup-test.gateway.test.ts` mocks now provide an ACTIVE user + session (its tokens go through the shared check).

Dev only, not deployed.

author: surrealroad
body:
## Summary

Adds the cross-adapter conformance suite from `docs/plans/doc-implied-features.md`, plus the parity bugs it found.

**Suite**
- `runStorageAdapterConformance` is exported from a new `@critical-path/core/testing` entry. Test-runner functions are passed in, so core has no vitest dependency, and authors of custom adapters (Postgres, Prisma and so on) can verify against the same contract.
- It covers:
  - round-tripping every field of every entity
  - partial updates and clearing fields with `undefined`
  - not-found contracts
  - combined filters
  - sort orders
- It runs against InMemory, SQLite and Firestore.

**Bugs it found, now fixed**
- **SQLite silently dropped 10 fields:**
  - tasks: `key`, `semanticStatus`, `todos`
  - projects: `schedule`, `startDate`, `targetEndDate`
  - teams: `weeklyCapacityHours`, `schedule`
  - attachments: `artifactType`

  Rather than adding more hand-maintained columns, which is how they got lost, these tables now store any field without a dedicated column in a JSON `extra` column. It's worked out from `PRAGMA table_info`, so future fields round-trip without schema changes. Existing databases get the column automatically.
- **Firestore:**
  - `getAttachments` and `getActivities` only applied their first filter.
  - Activities weren't ordered.
  - Comments relied on insertion order.

**Docs**
- The docs site's "Custom Storage Adapters" page documented a non-existent `CriticalPathStore` interface. It's rewritten with the real repositories, the behavioural contracts, and how to run the suite.

**Known gap (documented in GOTCHAS):** `InMemoryStore` returns live references. Copy-on-read touches ~60 methods, so it's left as a follow-up.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm run build && pnpm run test` (439 tests passing)
- [x] `pnpm docs:build`

These changes are AI-assisted and need human review before merging.

author: glarivie
body:
## Pourquoi

Story 26.3 de l'épic 26. Un assistant branché sur `/api/mcp` lit les comptes, les budgets et les factures, mais aucun objectif d'épargne. Pour savoir où en est un objectif, ou pour en créer un qu'il vient de décrire, le propriétaire doit ouvrir « Objectifs ». Cette pull request ajoute `get_goals`, que Sure n'a pas, et reprend `create_goal` de Sure.

## Ce qu'elle fait

- `get_goals` (`archant:read`) liste tous les objectifs dans l'ordre de `/goals`. Pour chacun, il donne la cible, ce que ses comptes lui réservent, ce qui reste, le montant mensuel nécessaire et la part de chaque compte, en chaînes décimales. Suivent les totaux de la carte du tableau de bord, calculés sur la même lecture par une nouvelle fonction `getGoalsOverview`. Les objectifs dans une autre devise sont nommés à part.
- `create_goal` (`archant:write`) crée un objectif ou une réserve comme « Nouvel objectif ». Les comptes sont donnés par identifiant, chacun avec un montant fixe ou son solde entier. Comme Sure, la couleur est tirée au hasard parmi les teintes des catégories, par `sampleGoalColor` dans `@archant/data/goals`, et la réponse donne l'adresse de la page de l'objectif. L'icône reste la tirelire de la fenêtre, car `goals.icon` est obligatoire là où Sure la laisse vide. La cible d'une réserve est un montant ou un nombre de mois de dépenses.
- Les refus sont ceux du service, avec le chemin et le code de chaque champ : un compte qui ne peut pas financer un objectif, deux devises, un compte déjà pris en entier par un autre objectif. L'entrée de l'outil refuse aussi l'absence de cible, deux cibles à la fois, des mois pour un objectif ponctuel et une date sur une réserve, que le service effacerait sans rien dire.
- Les instructions du serveur demandent à l'assistant de reformuler le nom, la cible, la date et chaque compte avec ce qu'il réserve, puis d'attendre l'accord. Elles expliquent qu'un lien sans montant sur un objectif actif ou en pause prend le compte entier.
- « Nouvel objectif » tire aussi sa couleur au hasard à chaque ouverture, comme le formulaire de Sure, au lieu de toujours partir de l'orange.
- Modifier, mettre en pause, terminer, archiver ou supprimer un objectif reste dans l'interface.
- Les deux libellés de la page de consentement nomment les objectifs : « …, vos factures et vos objectifs » en lecture, « …, définir vos budgets, vos soldes et vos objectifs, … » en écriture. `docs/deployment.md`, `docs/security-model.md` et `docs/sure-parity.md` sont à jour.

Aucune nouvelle dépendance, aucune migration.

## Vérification

- `pnpm format`, `pnpm lint:code`, `pnpm lint:format` et `pnpm typecheck` ne signalent rien.
- `pnpm test` passe : 3 598 tests pour l'API, 368 pour l'interface, 300 pour `@archant/data` et 14 pour le test de volume.
- `pnpm test:e2e` passe : 420 tests.
- `packages/api/src/mcp/goals.spec.ts` couvre chaque cas du tableau de la spec en passant par le serveur MCP, dont le refus d'un jeton en lecture seule et l'inscription de chaque appel dans `assistant_calls`.

body:
Automated implementation. Closes https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/6629

## Auto-decisions

Decisions the pipeline took from the issue's clarification questions:

- **AD-1** (clarify comment 6037509656, clarify-respond on claude, Q1) The poller's four review-run matchers on current `main` don't check `head_branch == <default branch>`. `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` doesn't even ask GitHub for `head_branch`, and there's no default-branch cache to reuse. Should this issue harden them too? → **A**: The facts show PR #⁠5109 (#⁠5094's fix) was merged into `claude/implement-plan-issue-5094-verify-pr-named-review-run-provenance`, not `main`. On `main`, `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19098`) still requests only `{databaseId, event, status, conclusion, displayTitle, createdAt, startedAt}` at line 19147, with no `head_branch` and no `path`. The issue asks to ap Alternatives: B (No. Harden only `_mt_inflight_review_branches` and the sweep's `dispatch_pr` matcher, plus spoof tests for `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs`. File a separate issue for the poller.), C (Harden only the poller's four matchers here, and file the merge train and sweep as a follow-up.).
- **AD-2** (clarify comment 6037509656, clarify-respond on claude, Q2) GitHub can report `head_branch: null` on a real default-branch `workflow_dispatch` review run (issue #⁠4928). The sweep keeps such runs by their `pr:<N>` title on purpose, because dropping them let the next tick dispatch again and replace the pending review. How should every hardened matcher treat a null `head_branch`? → **A**: Only a real default-branch `workflow_dispatch` run can have a null `head_branch`. A spoof from a branch copy always reports its own non-empty branch, so accepting null still rejects that spoof. It also keeps the #⁠4928 protection the sweep comment documents at `review_autofix_sweep.yml:247-251`. Option B brings back duplicate dispatches. Option C turns a normal GitHub quirk into a release hold or s Alternatives: B (Strict: require `head_branch` to equal the default branch and drop null runs. This reverts the #⁠4928 protection, so the sweep may dispatch duplicates again.), C (Strict match, but a null `head_branch` makes the listing "incomplete". Each caller then uses its existing fail-closed path (skip dispatch or hold release this tick).).
- **AD-3** (clarify comment 6037509656, clarify-respond on claude, Q3) In `_mt_inflight_review_branches`, any review-path `workflow_dispatch` run without a PR-named title currently marks the whole listing `unattributed_run` and holds every merge-train release. After hardening, what happens to a review-wrapper dispatch run on a non-default branch, or one whose title and path don't pair? → **A**: A run that fails the trust rule is by definition not a trusted review run. Today `review_merge_train.sh:676-679` turns it into `unattributed_run`, which marks the listing incomplete and holds every release. That is exactly the spoof's effect. Ignoring the run removes the stall. Keeping `unattributed_run` for trusted default-branch dispatches with no PR title (`review_autofix.yml` self-dispatches)  Alternatives: B (Keep treating it as `unattributed_run`, which marks the listing incomplete and holds every release this tick. That keeps the availability stall the issue is trying to remove.).

devledger-six.vercel.app served a 404. People have no reason to trust an unsigned `.exe` from a repo with one star. The site gives them two things to look at before they download anything.

**`/demo`: the real app in the browser, on made-up data.**

- A download table read live from the GitHub releases API, showing the SHA-256 GitHub computed for each file. If the API can't be reached, the page falls back to a link to the release page.

**`vercel.json`**
- Builds `apps/desktop` with `npm run build:web` and serves `dist-web`.
- Sets a strict CSP (only `api.github.com` may be fetched), `nosniff`, `frame-ancestors 'none'` and immutable caching for hashed assets.

**README**
- Now leads with the demo, the download, install and verification steps, and an honest status line.

- `vite.config.ts`, `index.html`, every component, Rust, the schema, crypto and the workflows are unchanged.

author: r-log
body:
A tools-only PR for both tracks. The verbatim proof's member reader names a class's data members from its header, and it split a qualified declaration such as `std::string m_name;` at the scope operator, so it listed `std`, `proto` and `Motion` as members and missed the member on that line. Both proofs read members through it: the verbatim proof's member check and the handler proof's bare-member check, which refused a local named like a false member even after the earlier lookahead. The reader now names a member by the last name before its initialiser, array bound or bit-field colon, and a scope operator is not that colon.

## Why the fix is here and not in the handler proof

The first handler-tools ruling kept the two tracks' tools apart and put the qualified-name fix in the handler proof's own reader. The measurement that followed showed the shared reader misses nine real session members today, so a handler-local fix would have left a hole in both tracks. The lane rule yields to a shared bug once: one fix in one place, measured clean on every class a tool reads, with both tracks rebasing onto it before their next tool change.

## What

- **The session's member list** goes from 561 to 567 names: `Motion`, `proto` and `std` out; `m_Address`, `m_Socket`, `m_accountName`, `m_deferredLogin`, `m_mailbox`, `m_movers`, `m_secondStreamDeadline`, `m_sessionId` and `m_timeBase` in. The two classes the site data names, the aura and the cast, and the aura holder read the same before and after. A sweep of every class in the tree shows 126 whose lists change the same way; the session is the only one a tool reads.
- **Fixtures:** the handler proof's fixture session declares a member named `std` and a qualified member, so the row that a bare member named `std` fails keeps its meaning and a reverted fix is caught; the verbatim fixture gains a qualified member. Two new rows: a qualified member used bare fails while a local named its qualifier passes, and a local named `proto` used through an arrow passes when `proto` is not a member. The handler proof's scope lookahead stays.

## Proof

Self-tests 226 to 227 and 65 to 66 rows; six tool mutants killed, among them the fix reverted, the split kept at the first colon of the scope operator and the split at any colon, each by the member-count row and the two new rows. Every mode of all four tools on the real tree is byte-equal to the tools on master in output, error stream and exit code; the handler proof's 25 functions and 2 residues are unchanged. A probe on the one body the old reader refused, a local named `proto` used through an arrow, passes now and failed before.

## What it does not close

Nothing moves. The handler proof's next forms, residue edits and multi-line heads, and the verbatim proof's valued-pair derivation rebase onto this before they land.

body:
Slice 4a of the engine-owned runtime session: the narrow reads the Player and its debugger need, so that the Player migration (slice 4b) never exports the whole state for an ordinary update.

Refs #512
Refs #494

## What changes (`src/runtime/session.ts`)

| Player need (today's read) | Session read | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Camera placement per publication (`snapshot.cameraView`) | `view().cameraView` | O(1) |
| Scene-clock hold while a storage write and a queued block coexist (`snapshot.pendingTimerHandlers.length`) | `view().queuedBlocks` | O(1) |
| Date/time presentation for form text and appended messages (`currentTemporalContext(snapshot).presentation`) | `temporalPresentation()` | size of the presentation settings |
| Debug Now call chain; Variables grouping (`snapshot.callFrames`: kind, function, call site, return position, scope depth, interruption) | `callStack()` | O(call depth), no arguments, captures, or temporaries |
| Debug Variables and live values (`globals`, `frames`, `retainedScopes`, `liveMessages`) | `variables()` | O(variables and their values), on demand |

All results are deeply frozen copies; reads go through the session's ended/re-entry guard. `RuntimeSessionCall`, `RuntimeSessionVariables`, `RuntimeCameraViewSnapshot` and `RuntimeLiveMessageSnapshot` are exported types. Docs: RUNTIME.md "Runtime sessions" Results bullet. No format change.

Script storage is not added: the Player reads it only at storage adoption and debug export, both existing explicit export boundaries (Player map, section 2).

## Evidence and checks

- The shared resume-equivalence helper's session pass compares the extended view (including `cameraView` and `queuedBlocks`) with the snapshot API's state at every boundary of every scenario, including the camera-view and timer suites.
- `tests/runtime-session.test.ts`: with a timer block interrupting a function's wait, `queuedBlocks` is 1 before the block starts and 0 after; `callStack()` gives the function then the block (`interruption: "timer"`) and matches the exported call frames; `variables()` equals the exported globals/frames/kept scopes/live messages (a message handle's updated text included) and is frozen; `temporalPresentation()` equals the session's temporal context presentation.
- `flock /tmp/agent-work/npm-check.lock npm run check` at a8908313 (rebased onto main c37df73e): pass, 1,809 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped. `git diff --check` clean.

`callReturnInstructions()` (#682) stays as merged (coordinator decision); `callStack()` serves the debugger.

author: benhuddart
body:
## Summary

The `global_fit_wizard_result` screenshot failed about 40 % of docs-pages runs with `StopIteration`: the recommendation held no split with exactly Δ and B_L local. **The cause is host floating point, not scheduling.** On runners whose NumPy dispatches AVX-512 kernels, the role search takes a different path and never fits that split. This PR changes the scenario's data so every host gives the same answer, and records the root cause.

### Evidence (temporary probe workflow on this branch, since removed)

- 8 × `ubuntu-latest` runners, 3 fresh processes each: every runner was self-consistent. Pass or fail split exactly on `numpy.__cpu_features__`: AVX-512 hosts failed (Xeon 8370C, 8573C, 6973P-C, EPYC 9V74 with AVX-512 exposed); AVX2 hosts passed (EPYC 7763, EPYC 9V74 without AVX-512).
- **Causal test:** on the same AVX-512 host, the old fields fail with native dispatch and pass with `NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES` set to the host's AVX-512 features.

### Mechanism

The separable engine starts from independent per-run LF-KT + Constant fits. At 50 G and 100 G (γ_μB_L/Δ ≈ 11, 22) the signal is decoupled, so A_1, A_bg, Δ and B_L are nearly degenerate within one run:

- Migrad reports failure on every seed, even where it reaches χ² ≈ 508 / 447.
- The ladder keeps the Simplex fallback at χ² ≈ 635 / 476.
- Simplex stops on a flat valley, and where it stops moves with the last bits of `exp`/`sin`/`cos` (AVX2 vs AVX-512 kernels).

From the AVX-512 anchor the surrogate shares Δ first instead of A_1. The greedy chain then ends at a mis-converged AICc 2124 and never visits {B_L, Δ} local. Full trace and tables: `docs/investigations/wizard-result-screenshot-flake.md`.

### Change

- **Scenario data:** fields 0, 5, 10, 25 G (γ_μB_L/Δ ≈ 0, 1, 2, 5; the textbook sweep without its 50 G point). Every per-run fit converges under Migrad from every seed.
- **Verified on CI:** the 8-row ranking is identical to ~1e-9 AICc on AVX-512 and AVX2 hosts. The narrowest decision in the chain is 0.02 AICc, about four orders of magnitude above the cross-host spread.
- **Caption** in `reference/global_fit_wizard.rst` rewritten to match the new figure. B (Δ also local) now scores **+4.0 AICc** and passes every check, and its per-run Δ sits on A's shared value: a parsimony story rather than the old "+34, fails at 100 G" one.
- No `StopIteration` handling was added.

### Not fixed here (core, follow-ups)

1. `_best_single_run_fit_result` prefers a "successful" Simplex over a failed Migrad endpoint 127 χ² lower.
2. The elimination chain can accept a node whose χ² exceeds a nested, less flexible node's. The certificate check only compares a child with its direct parent.
3. `RunEstimate.at_bound` is documented as parameter names, but callers pass `_bound_hit_names` display strings (`"Delta at lower bound"`). The "never propose a railed parameter" rule therefore never fires.

The other Ag LF scenarios still use 0/15/50/100 G. They don't assert on the verdict, so they don't crash, but their wizard images may differ between hosts.

## Test plan

- [x] `python tools/harness.py validate`: 9695 passed
- [x] `python tools/harness.py docs`: build succeeded, no new warnings on the touched pages
- [x] `python -m docs.screenshots.capture --only global_fit_wizard_result` renders locally (macOS arm64)
- [x] CI probe: new fields pass with an identical ranking on 8 runners, 2 of them AVX-512

author: misja-pronk
body:
**mise tasks.** stevin, lely and caland each had a `mise.toml` with nearly the same tasks; the template had none. A new tool now gets one — Python and uv, and the tasks under the names every Kostavo tool uses:

`dev` · `test` · `test:lowest` · `lint` · `fmt` · `fix` · `typecheck` · `check` · `build` · `docs` · `docs:build` · `ci` · `clean`

`check` is the gate before a commit, `fix` repairs what ruff can, `ci` is everything CI runs (gate, docs site, package), `test:lowest` runs the tests on the lowest dependencies as CI's job does, `clean` removes build output and caches.

**mise's MCP server.** `.mcp.json` gives Claude Code `mise mcp`, so an assistant runs those tasks (`run_task`) instead of guessing at commands; a starter `CLAUDE.md` names them. The server is experimental in mise, so the file sets `MISE_EXPERIMENTAL=1` for it, and mise only starts in a folder whose `mise.toml` you have trusted (`mise trust`).

What the server shows of the environment is what `mise.toml` sets under `[env]` — not what the shell holds. A test starts the server exactly as `.mcp.json` says, with a secret in the shell's environment, and holds it to that. So the rule is: no secret in `mise.toml`.

**Also**
- CI gets the `test (lowest dependencies)` job the three tools have.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are a tool's own from now on: made once, left alone by `copier update`.

Tests: 20 passed here, five of them new — the tasks are there, they run through mise (`fix`, `ci`, `test:lowest`, `clean` on a tool made from this checkout), and the server starts and shows no secret. The two that need mise skip where it isn't installed, which is CI.

**A tool that was there already keeps its code and its ci** (second commit). Two answers say what a tool takes: `starter_code` (a starter `src/` and `tests/`) and `shared_ci` (the `ci.yml` that calls the shared workflow). Both are yes for a new tool and are recorded. Without them, an update wrote the template's starter test beside a tool's own tests — and a rehearsal on scratch copies showed worse: adopting a tool by updating it from the template as it was *before* these answers deletes the tool's own `cli.py`, `__init__.py` and `ci.yml`, because the old template had files by those names.

So stevin, lely and caland are not adopted by an update from the old version. Each gets an answers file at this version, with the files this version generates for it; from then on `copier update` moves them like any other tool.

author: myrmidon-vm-core[bot]
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - The GitHub shared-identity subsystem gives an agent run a short-lived GitHub App token instead of a long-lived personal token
> - Adapters that run on the board host or over SSH receive that token through a staged launcher: a `git-credential-paperclip` helper, a `gh` wrapper, and a broker capability
> - An agent that starts through the `hermes_gateway` adapter runs outside that path. The board does not build an execution target for such a run, so the launcher is never staged and the agent keeps falling back to a static token
> - A gateway run can only carry data in the request body that the board sends to the gateway
> - This pull request therefore sends the launcher as request content, and the gateway materializes the programs and the broker environment inside the run
> - The benefit is one shared-identity path for every adapter: gateway runs obtain a GitHub App token like container runs, and no static GitHub token stays in the environment

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

**Subsystem affected**

`packages/adapters` (the `hermes` gateway adapter) together with `packages/adapter-utils` (the shared Git launcher) and `docker/bot-runtime` (the Hermes image and its upstream patches).

**Problem or motivation**

After the container launcher work landed, a release agent that starts through the gateway still pushed with a static `MYRMIDON_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Its run record showed `run_identity_contexts.github = null`, the `git-credential-paperclip` helper was absent from `PATH`, and `PAPERCLIP_GITHUB_BROKER_TOKEN` was absent from the environment. The reason is structural: `prepareGitHubOperationLaunchers` stages files into an execution target, and a gateway run has no such target on the board side. The gateway adapter sent only the provider payload, so the App capability could not reach the agent.

**Proposed solution**

Send the managed launcher to the gateway as request content, and stage it in the Hermes image.

1. `packages/adapter-utils/src/github-launcher.ts` exports `githubLauncherPayload`, which carries the launcher profile file names and the program bodies (the `git` wrapper, the `gh` wrapper, the credential helper, and the profile snippets).
2. `packages/adapters/hermes/src/gateway/server/execute.ts` puts that payload in the run body as the `github_launcher` field. The field is set after the payload template is spread, so an injected template cannot forge or remove it. The field follows the same rule as the existing `github_broker` field.
3. `docker/bot-runtime` gains patch `11-run-scoped-github-launcher.patch`, which writes the launcher programs from the request body into a run-private directory, adds that directory to `PATH`, and points Git at the staged credential helper.
4. A build-time regression test, `docker/bot-runtime/tests/github_launcher_run_scope.py`, checks the staged layout and the run scope.

**Alternatives considered**

- Put the launcher files into the image at build time. Rejected: the files must stay per run, because the credential helper resolves the credential per repository and per run.
- Reuse `paperclipSecrets` or the context snapshot. Rejected: those channels carry values, not executable programs, and they cannot set `PATH` for the run.

**Roadmap alignment**

This continues the shared-identity work for agents that live outside the container host. It removes the last static GitHub token from the agent environment.

**Additional context**

The patch is numbered `11-` because `10-run-workspace-open.patch` already exists upstream. The `gh` wrapper talks to the broker with the run capability token and never writes a token to disk.

## What Changed

- `packages/adapter-utils/src/github-launcher.ts` — export the launcher payload (profile file names plus program bodies) and reuse the credential-helper source in the program map.
- `packages/adapter-utils/src/execution-target.ts` — import the shared file-name list and the credential helper, so one list serves both the execution-target staging path and the gateway path.
- `packages/adapters/hermes/src/gateway/server/execute.ts` — add the `github_launcher` field to the run body and set it unconditionally after the payload template spread.
- `packages/adapters/hermes/src/gateway/server/execute.test.ts` — two tests: the body carries the launcher payload, and the field stays absent without broker configuration while a forged template value is ignored.
- `docker/bot-runtime/patches/11-run-scoped-github-launcher.patch` — stage the launcher programs in the run and wire `PATH` plus the Git credential helper.
- `docker/bot-runtime/tests/github_launcher_run_scope.py` — build-time regression for the staged launcher.
- `docker/bot-runtime/Dockerfile` — run the new regression and import the new context module in the lazy-import check.
- `scripts/myrmidon/hermes-upstream/deltas.json` and `docker/bot-runtime/patches/README.md` — register patch `11-`.
- `docs/myrmidon/changes/myr-1-6-5-github-gateway-launcher.md` — change fragment for release notes.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/adapter-utils run typecheck` — pass.
- `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/hermes-paperclip-adapter run typecheck` — pass.
- `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/hermes-paperclip-adapter exec vitest run src/gateway/server/execute.test.ts` — 109 passed on this branch against 107 passed on `main`.
- New tests by name: `forwards the managed Git launcher as the github_launcher body field`, and `omits the github_launcher field when no broker env is configured, and ignores payloadTemplate attempts to forge one`.
- `docker/bot-runtime/tests/github_launcher_run_scope.py` against the patched Hermes tree — pass.
- The patch applies with `git apply -p1` to the image tree that already carries patches `01`–`10`.
- Known unrelated failures: `src/server/detect-model.test.ts` fails 3 tests on `main` as well (`3 failed | 4 passed`), so the failures do not come from this change.

## Risks

- The launcher payload adds a few kilobytes to every gateway run body. The run body already carries the broker field, so the increase is small.
- The `PATH` change comes from the image patch and applies to every gateway run. A run without broker configuration receives no launcher content, and the patch then leaves the environment unchanged.
- The gateway stages programs from the request body. The board is the only writer of that body field, and the adapter sets the field after the template spread, so a card cannot replace it.

## Model Used

- Provider: Aliyun DashScope (custom endpoint), through the Hermes Agent harness.
- Model ID: `dashscope-deepseek-v4.1-flash`.
- Reasoning mode: standard chat completions; no extended thinking mode.
- Capabilities used: tool use (shell, file edit, HTTP calls). Context window: not advertised in the run metadata.

## Checklist

- [x] I have included a thinking path that traces from project context to this change
- [x] I have specified the model used (with version and capability details)
- [x] I have checked ROADMAP.md and confirmed this PR does not duplicate planned core work
- [x] I have searched GitHub for duplicate or related PRs and linked them above
- [x] I have either (a) linked existing issues with `Fixes: #` / `Closes #` / `Refs #` OR (b) described the issue in-PR following the relevant issue template
- [x] I have not referenced internal/instance-local Paperclip issues or links (only public GitHub `#NNN` / `github.com/paperclipai/paperclip` URLs)
- [x] My branch name describes the change (e.g. `docs/...`, `fix/...`) and contains no internal Paperclip ticket id or instance-derived details
- [x] I have run tests locally and they pass
- [x] I have added or updated tests where applicable
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation to reflect my changes
- [x] I have considered and documented any risks above

author: ebbmango
vaggeliskls
body:
# Current Behaviour

On a host with a kernel older than 5.12 (Ubuntu 20.04 ships 5.4) the first start ends right after "Booting Windows using QEMU":

```
qemu-system-x86_64: Failed to initialize io_uring: Cannot allocate memory
❯ ERROR: QEMU exited unexpectedly!
```

and the container restarts in a loop. dockur 6.06 lets QEMU 11 choose io_uring for disk I/O, whose buffers are charged against the container's locked-memory limit on those kernels, and Docker caps that at 64 KB.

Also, `storage/` and `shared/` are written by the container as root, so the README's "delete storage/" instructions fail for a normal user.

# Expected Behaviour

- `docker-compose.yml` sets `DISK_IO` to `native`, the Linux AIO backend that works on every kernel. It can be overridden from `.env`; `io_uring` remains available on kernels 5.12 and newer.
- `.env.example` and the README table document the three values and when `io_uring` is safe.
- The "start over" and Development instructions use `sudo rm -rf storage shared`.

`docker compose config` passes. The setting maps to QEMU's `aio=native`, confirmed in dockur's disk.sh. Not yet confirmed on the affected host at the time of merging; the host is being re-run with this setting.

author: sanjaysrinivas
body:
### What

`sceLibcMspaceRealloc` and `sceLibcMspaceReallocalign` round sizes to 16 bytes before checking whether an existing chunk can hold them. Near `SIZE_MAX`, that rounding wraps to zero: both exports return the original pointer as success and replace its requested-size metadata with a value the allocation cannot hold. A later relocating resize uses that metadata as a copy length.

Reject rounding overflow with guest ENOMEM before either fast path updates the chunk. This follows the overflow check already present in `Allocate`, without changing normal allocation, zero-size or alignment handling.

Extend the existing Mspace regression to reject `SIZE_MAX` through `SIZE_MAX - 15` for both resize exports, checking errno, original contents, usable capacity and usage/peak statistics. Its existing relocating growth immediately afterward also verifies the allocation remains usable.

### Tested

Earlier focused validation of the unchanged contribution patch:

Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2, GCC 13.3.0, x86-64:

- Against the original full libc, a focused maximum-size check shows both resize exports returning success; the extended Mspace regression fails.
- Complete libc built using its repository CMake source list in a local, untracked harness. `mspace` and `guest_reallocalign` pass three consecutive runs each. Five neighboring native save tests also pass.
- The actual modified `Mspace.cpp` and regression pass with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -pthread`, and a local thread-local errno provider.
- `git diff --check` passes.

With the full repository configured and built with `BUILD_TESTING=ON`:

```sh
ctest --test-dir build -R '^(mspace|guest_reallocalign)$' --output-on-failure
```

No affected retail title or exploitation is claimed. Local validation helpers and investigation notes are excluded from the patch. Full-build results and remaining platform limits are recorded below.

### PR overlap (earlier checks)

Direct per-file three-way merge checks confirm a conflict with the whole-tree formatting PR #1128 in `core/libs/prx/libc/src/Mspace.cpp`. That PR does not implement this bug fix. #1128 currently conflicts with upstream in `StdioExtras.cpp`, so the repository overlap tool skips its pairwise conflict check; its empty result does not clear this overlap. This PR merges cleanly into upstream `1e5bb880`; merging it and #1128 will require rebasing whichever lands second.

### Earlier local validation after rebase

Rebased onto upstream `main` at `cea1ef13`. Tested head: `bc1f7e694e02f4bd63fa718295860a71dfe7a07b`.

- Focused CTest regression selection: 6 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed (6 registered).

Title/homebrew execution remains untested. The GitHub-hosted fork checks below are separate from these local results.

### Independent fork CI

[Build run 37676602286](https://github.com/Sanjaysrinivas/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37676602286) passed on exact PR head `131e05a26bea1775cbb990224501aa255c7389d7`.
Rebased onto upstream `main` at `4764e59c37b1fc6c89284fdecaef5a5718b6119e`. The unchanged contribution's source tree matches the checked automatic merge result; conventions and `git diff --check` passed.
Both jobs completed the full Release CMake build with `BUILD_TESTING=ON`, the `libs` target and the full CTest suite with `--timeout 120 --repeat until-fail:3`.

- Native Windows: WinLibs GCC 15.2: **239 passed, 156 skipped, 0 failed** (395 registered).
- The newly merged upstream `guest_force_tls_destructor` regression passed in all three Linux repetitions.

These fork checks do not replace upstream workflow approval or maintainer review. No title/homebrew execution or RDNA hardware measurement is claimed.

author: lsx-ink
body:
Before: a scene's key words (the name, the number, the twist word) were only drawn bigger in the captions.

After: in lore videos those words also land with a soft, low sub-bass hit as they're spoken, felt more than heard, so the word sticks. Each scene gets at most two, never on top of the scene's own sound effect.

How: `thump_times` finds when each punch word is first spoken, from the voice's word timings or the estimate. `render_scene` gains a `thumps` list that mixes in a short `THUMP` sine burst at each time. It is lore only (`THUMP_STYLES`) and skipped when a scene has no voice. A new test covers the timing rules, the wiring in `make`, and the thump in a real render.

body: ## 📄 Description - The fallback variables for browsers without `light-dark()` support are now defined in one place and pulled in with `@extend`. body:
## What changed
- `download()`: a `text/html` response whose file name isn't `.html/.htm` is no longer `LoginRequired`. It raises a per-item `ApiError` (item skipped with a warning, nothing written to state, retried next run). If the server names the file via `Content-Disposition` (e.g. `lab.php`), it is saved normally, so a real file is never dropped.
- `get_json()`: a 200 + non-JSON page (e.g. maintenance) is a transient `ApiError` instead of `LoginRequired`.
- `LoginRequired` is now raised only for 401, a redirect to another host, or a final URL with a login marker (`_check_login`, unchanged).
- Tests: audit probe P3 inverted into a regression test, plus tests for named HTML files, real login redirects, JSON-endpoint HTML, and a full sync continuing past an HTML attachment.

## Why
Audit B3/S3: an extensionless/.php/.xhtml upload or a maintenance page stopped the whole sync, showed "Blackboard oturumu sona erdi", and signing in again never helped, so it repeated every run.

## Risk
Low. Builds on the per-item warning handling from #25. Trade-off: an HTML file with no server-provided name and a non-html expected name is skipped with a warning (still on Blackboard) rather than saved.

## How to test locally
`./scripts/setup.sh && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` (336 pass), or run `tests/test_session.py -k html`.

author: syed-bipul-rahman
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Syed-Bipul-Rahman"} -->
_Requested by **Bipul** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016AMx6a7ajyGKNhuJf4EHey?thread=cmsg_016AMx6a7ajyGKNhuJf4EHey8wJt2Bo2trJXno4FfYc8wb)_

Before: Guard ships 15 JSON rules and loads YARA rules only from files the user drops into `~/.guard/av`.

After: 2,333 community YARA rules are built into the binary and run on every scan, next to the JSON rules. They come from ReversingLabs (MIT: ransomware, backdoors, stealers), Neo23x0 signature-base (DRL 1.1: hacktools, APT and malware), ESET (BSD-2-Clause), Google GCTI (Apache 2.0: Cobalt Strike) and Airbnb BinaryAlert (Apache 2.0). Hits are reported as suspicious, with rule ids like `yara:reversinglabs.Win32_Ransomware_GandCrab`. Each engine start takes about 3 s longer (release build). `GUARD_COMMUNITY_RULES=0` leaves the rules out, and an allowlist entry silences a single rule. `guard av rules --licenses` prints the licenses.

YARA Forge's release packages couldn't be downloaded from this environment. They also mix in sources whose licenses are share-alike, non-commercial or missing. So this PR pulls YARA Forge's highest-rated sources that can be bundled straight from upstream, pinned to specific commits, and filters them the way YARA Forge builds its core package: score ≥ 65, modified in the last 2,500 days, no external variables. It also leaves out files that are slow to compile or aren't malware detections (the certificate blocklist, vulnerable drivers, web shells and log rules). `data/yara/README.md` records the sources, commits and every selection step.

How:
- `data/yara/*.yar` hold the rule sets in plain text, like `data/av-rules.json`. `cli/build.rs` gzips them into the binary, so the binary never contains rule text and can't flag itself. The engine allowlists the rule files by hash.
- The Detection Rule License asks that alerts name the rule's author. So every signature-base rule's description ends with `(author: …)`, which shows with each hit. The license texts are in `data/yara/LICENSES.txt`, and the binary carries a copy.
- The engine now compiles YARA once, after all rule files load. Before, it compiled once per directory.
- False positives: before trimming, the full candidate set of 5,953 rules scanned 125,000 files (`/usr`, the Cargo registry, parts of this repo) with zero hits. The repo's own sweeps in `cli/tests/detection.rs` now run with the community rules on, on Linux, macOS and Windows. A one-off sweep of all of System32 also ran on Windows x64. Together they caught four rules, all now left out:
  - `SUSP_shellpop_Bash` (flags docs)
