body:
## Partie 1 — Problématique par cabinet

Retour d'étudiants (niveau licence) : l'objectif de l'exercice manquait de clarté. L'information existait déjà dans la Lettre de mission (Objectif, Mandat, Enjeux, Attentes...), mais éclatée en plusieurs blocs de prose, sans question centrale pour cadrer la réflexion dès la première lecture — un réflexe que ce niveau attend (la "problématique").

- `lib/types.ts` : nouveau champ optionnel `Mandate.problematique`.
- `data/modules/veille-reglementaire/mission.ts` : une problématique par mandat (4 cabinets).
- `components/MissionLetterDocument.tsx` : encart distinct en tête de la Lettre de mission, avant les blocs détaillés.
- `lib/deliverable.ts` (branche `plan-action`) : une phrase ajoutée au contexte partagé pour ancrer l'enjeu.

La problématique ne porte pas sur l'entreprise cliente mais sur **le cabinet lui-même** : réussir la mission ET la restitution pour que Montrel Industries reconduise son mandat, plutôt que de se le voir retirer — une logique de conseil (gagner/garder le client), pas une simple question technique.

Champ optionnel : les modules Autres référentiels et QSEAL13-BPM ne sont pas affectés — à unifier plus tard, une fois le cours en cours terminé.

## Partie 2 — Remplace la NMP par le toluène (Cabinet Horizon)

La NMP était un vrai cas REACH, mais sa classification ICPE (reprotoxique, pas inflammable) ne colle pas bien à l'exercice de recherche autonome visé en cours : FDS et catégorisation ICPE doivent être simples à retrouver par les étudiants.

Remplacé par le **toluène (CAS 108-88-3)** : solvant inflammable classique utilisé en traitement de surface, FDS publique chez n'importe quel fournisseur, fiche toxicologique INRS existante, rubrique ICPE "liquides inflammables" immédiate à identifier. L'angle réglementaire passe de la restriction REACH à la **VLEP réglementaire contraignante** (Code du travail, art. R.4412-149) : l'exposition des opérateurs n'a jamais été mesurée. Le message de Julien Faure (HSE) ne donne ni la FDS ni la valeur VLEP exacte — c'est aux étudiants de les retrouver, l'exercice de veille visé.

## Vérification

- `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint` : OK
- Testé en live (Playwright) sur Cabinet Horizon et Cabinet Nova : encart "Problématique" visible, mentions toluène/VLEP/CAS présentes, plus aucune trace de NMP/REACH.
- PDF régénérés et vérifiés par diff de texte ; les PDF non concernés restaurés à l'identique.

Changelog: https://github.com/bscan/PerlNavigator/blob/v0.8.20/CHANGELOG.md

Upstream now builds the server with webpack and `bin` points at `server/dist/serverMain.js`, so `npmBuildScript` changes from `compile` to `package`; with `compile` the package builds but the wrapper points at a file that does not exist.

`server/package.json` gained `typescript` as a dev dependency, which made the output grow from 6 to 76 MiB. It is only needed at build time, so `postInstall` removes it (and `@types`) from the installed `server/node_modules`; the output is 10 MiB.

Tested on x86_64-linux, by hand in Vim (yegappan/lsp) on a two-file Perl project, comparing with 0.6.3:

- the syntax error is reported as a diagnostic
- hover on a sub from another module shows `(subroutine) Mi::saluda`
- go to definition opens the module, the same as 0.6.3

One behaviour difference found with a scripted LSP client: with `use lib '.'` (a relative `@INC` entry) 0.8.20 does not resolve definitions in other files, while 0.6.3 did. With an absolute path such as `use lib "$FindBin::Bin/lib"` both versions agree. The server published on npm (`perlnavigator-server` 0.8.20) behaves the same, so it is upstream behaviour and not the packaging.

I do not write Perl myself; I am sending this because the package has no maintainer and its last version bump was in 2023. I used Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) to adapt the build, write the LSP test client and this description; I reviewed the diff and did the Vim testing myself.

author: ejryan89
body:
Closes #131

`StartDetachedTests` failed once in CI with WinError 32 while removing its temporary directory, after `process_status` had reported the detached host gone. The cause was an operating-system race, not a handle leaked by `start_detached`. `process_status` reads the process's exit code, and Windows sets that before it closes the dying process's handles. Windows signals the process object only after those handles are closed. The test now waits, with a bounded retry, for the log to be released before the directory is removed. A new deterministic test fails if anything other than the host still holds the log once the host has exited. `start_detached` is unchanged. This is a patch-level change.

How the cause was shown, with a scratch probe run 100 times per method on Python 3.14.7 (the CI version):

- While the host runs, the Restart Manager (`RmGetList`) reports exactly one process holding `host.log`: the host. The starting process has closed its copy, and no grandchild exists.
- If the host is ended with `TerminateProcess` and only `process_status` is polled, an exclusive-write open (share mode 0) right after it reports the host gone failed 100 of 100 times. At that moment the Restart Manager listed no holder, and the log was free about 0.1 ms later without any action. The kernel was still tearing the process down.
- If the probe instead waits on the process object, the same immediate exclusive open succeeded 100 of 100 times. So once the host has really exited, nothing holds the log: no grandchild and no inherited handle.
- With the test's `taskkill /T /F`, which is slower, the immediate open succeeded 100 of 100 times locally. That fits a rare loss of this race on a loaded CI runner. A scanner such as Defender holding the newly written file would also be covered by the bounded wait.

## Changes

- `skills/code-review-core/scripts/test_review_process.py`: `test_a_detached_host_outlives_its_start_and_logs_its_output` now waits, after the host is gone, until the log opens for exclusive write. It asserts that this happens within the suite's 20-second bound, so the error is never ignored and no assertion is weakened.
- Same file: new test `test_once_the_host_has_exited_nothing_else_holds_its_log`, the regression guard against a leak. It ends only the host (`TerminateProcess`, not the tree), waits for the process object to be signaled, and then requires the log to open exclusively at once, with no retry. A mutation check that wrapped `start_detached` so a second process inherited the log made this assertion fail.
- Same file: the helpers `opens_exclusively`, which raises on any error other than a sharing violation, and `terminate_and_wait`.

## Implications

None. `start_detached` and the shipped behavior are unchanged, and `docs/code-review-operations.md` does not describe the host's handles. The production code removes run directories (`review_pipeline.py`, with `ignore_errors=True`) either when preparation fails or at finalize, after the results are committed. Neither depends on the log being released the moment the host exits.

## Models

- Planned by: Claude Opus 5.5, the strongest model offered (code-review pipeline). The issue's decision tree was the plan.
- Implemented by: Claude Opus 5.5

## Validation

- [x] `python -B tests/run_validation.py` passes in full, with no skipped prerequisites
- [x] Regression coverage added or updated for every behavior change
- [x] For a change to skill paths, `allowed-tools`, runtime adapters, or agents, the `runtime-canary` lines are below, with each runtime's version and any `SKIPPED` reason
- [x] For a skill change, `analyze-skill-cost` audited each changed skill from the source tree with no MUST FIX left; any SUGGESTION left is named below with why
- [x] Documentation updated in this change
- [x] Diff reviewed for personal paths, organization names, credentials, and generated artifacts

- `runtime-canary`: not run. `start_detached`, skill paths, `allowed-tools`, adapters, and agents are unchanged; only a test changed.
- Documentation: no change needed (see Implications).
- Both detached-host tests passed 40 of 40 times idle and 20 of 20 times with 8 CPU-bound processes running.
- `analyze-skill-cost review-prs` (SCOPE source): EFFICIENT, no MUST FIX. One SUGGESTION stays: the reviewer prompt that `review_pipeline.py` renders at runtime is outside what the audit can measure. Its reply is bounded (`WROTE <result>`), and this change does not touch it.

Draft: the owner's manor runs on the Steward, and the round merges non-drafts. Don't mark ready until reviewed.

## What it does on someone else's PC

1. A new install writes `releasesCastellan: false` once. Nothing of Castellan's runs: no kit rollout, no Steward self-release or self-merge, no releases repository, and no repository takes the kit. `byItself` is off.
2. **Found on this PC**: the repositories Reeve lists (`GET /api/repos`, else his `repos.json`), on GitHub, that gh's account can push to (one GraphQL `viewerPermission` query), less those already looked after and those Reeve ignores (`src/found.ts`, cached hourly in `repos-found.json`).
3. **Look after** adds one to Settings (now labelled **Repositories**) with tests and version files read from the clone, no kit, nothing installed. It merges ready PRs (`merges`) and releases (`release`) only if ticked.
4. Merge stage and round: PRs merge only where `merges` is on. Elsewhere they're listed, nothing is tested, and no alarm counts their hours.
5. Release goes to the repository's own GitHub repo. It runs the repo's `npm run release`, which must create `v<version>` there or it counts as failed and isn't retried. Or it uses `tag`: the Steward's own `gh release create`, with notes from the CHANGELOG entry. Empty means never released. `MANOR_RELEASES_REPO` is passed empty.
6. `claim-version` works for any repo: one in Settings, one Reeve found, or the cwd clone.

## The owner's PC

`migrateToOwnRepos` runs the first time settings are read without `releasesCastellan`. On a data folder that already ran (settings.json, staff.json or alarms.json present), it writes out:
- `releasesCastellan: true`
- `releasesRepo` (the releases repo the kit used to hard-code)
- `byItself: true` (if unset)
- `merges: true` on every repository
- `dotnetRoot` (if the old SDK folder had an SDK)

There is no PC-name check. `test/owner.test.ts` checks every other setting reads the same as before.

## Kit 2.32.0

`release.ts` replaces `RELEASES_REPO` with `releasesRepo()`. It reads `MANOR_RELEASES_REPO`, else the Steward's settings.json (for releases by hand), else none, meaning the agent's own repo only. gh is found on PATH only, in `release.ts` and `manor.ts`. `ps.ts` and the accelerator, setup and keeper files are untouched.

## Also

- Surveyor alarms only where the Surveyor is installed.
- Wright and Bailiff settings are shown (`shownWhen: wrightHere`) and work runs only where the Wright is installed. A `wright` label is anyone's elsewhere.
- Tending and manor-wide alarms are handed to Manor when its `/api/state` says `keeps: ["tend", "alarms"]`. Manor's side isn't written yet.
- Dropped the gh and dotnet fallbacks to one PC's folders in `run.ts`. A missing gh now says "gh isn't installed: … gh auth login".
- `cli.ts` allow-update regex fixed.
- `convert.ts`, `relocate.ts`, `compare.ts` and the old-kit lists moved to `tools/lib`. The runtime old-kit checks are gone.
- Private repo names removed from CHANGELOG.

Versions: Steward 0.19.0 (re-claimed), kit 2.32.0. Builds on #91 (kit 2.31.0, Steward 0.18.0), which builds on #89 (kit 2.30.0, Steward 0.17.1); main has kit 2.29.0 (#88). They land in that order: the round only releases a kit version above the newest one.

Also in kit 2.32.0: "Back to <manor>" says Castellan when the manor has no name (node/manor.ts MANOR_DEFAULT_NAME, react/tour.tsx manorName). Reeve's test/manor-theme.test.ts expects "Manor" from the kit's reader, so Reeve needs a follow-up when it takes 2.32.0.

The merge with #89 changed kit/node/release.ts by hand: the Exchequer gets the files once GitHub has them (the releases repository, or with none the agent's own v<version>), and --exchequer reads from the releases repository, or with none the agent's own.

Tests: `npm test` passes (637 tests, plus 73 dotnet tests). `npm run typecheck` is clean. New tests: `test/customer.test.ts` and `test/owner.test.ts`.

body: Hardens Prime's futures-volume fallback. The worker already returns `lastCandleTime`; Prime now normalizes that timestamp and only accepts futures volume when its candle is aligned with the latest closed analysis candle within a bounded tolerance. author: vcnainala
body:
Replaces the Zapier \"Add new inbound emails to GitHub as new issues\" Zap, which created a new issue for every reply because it matched on the raw subject (\`Re: ...\`).

## How it works
- \`deployment/email-relay\`: a Cloudflare Email Worker. It parses the incoming email, strips quoted reply history, and triggers the workflow via \`workflow_dispatch\`. An optional \`ALLOWED_SENDERS\` allowlist is supported.
- \`.github/workflows/email-to-issue.yml\`: removes \`Re:\`/\`Fwd:\`/\`AW:\`/\`WG:\` prefixes from the subject and searches open issues for an exact title match. If one is found, the email is added as a comment (sender + text); otherwise a new issue is created.

## Setup (after this reaches \`main\`; workflow_dispatch only works for workflows on the default branch)
1. Create a fine-grained PAT scoped to \`Steinbeck-Lab/coconut\` with **Actions: Read and write**.
2. \`cd deployment/email-relay && npm install && npx wrangler secret put GITHUB_TOKEN && npx wrangler deploy\`
3. In Cloudflare Email Routing for the domain, add a custom address (e.g. \`issues@<domain>\`) with action **Send to a Worker** → \`coconut-email-relay\`.
4. Point senders/forwarding at that address and turn the Zap off.

## Testing
- Locally: the worker was run against a sample reply email (subject normalized, quoted history removed, allowlist rejection) and \`wrangler deploy --dry-run\` builds.
- Workflow: can be run manually from the Actions tab with a subject/body once on \`main\`.

author: rudimk
body:
## What

Active-active **id-allocation pre-flight policing** — M7 of `.sisyphus/sequence-reseed-plan.md`, the code guardrail that backs M6's UUID/ULID guidance. At cluster bring-up the daemon refuses to start a mesh member whose replicated tables use a **locally-allocated integer PRIMARY KEY or secondary UNIQUE key** (serial / identity / `AUTO_INCREMENT`).

## Why

In a converged mesh every node allocates from the same local counter, so two nodes mint the same integer id for *different* rows; they replicate and HLC-LWW silently discards one — the §1.7 cardinal sin (silent data loss). replicare can't de-collide independently minted ids after the fact (allocation is upstream of capture), so the only safe posture is to refuse at startup and point the operator at globally-unique keys (UUID v7 / ULID). This is the same "block on incompatible" philosophy as the type pre-flight (`CLAUDE.md` §4.2), extended to the mesh.

## Behavior

- **Blocks** a locally-allocated integer PK/unique key, naming each offending `table.column`, with an extra-loud note for narrow (32-bit-or-smaller) keys.
- **Allows** the collision-free schemes untouched: UUID/text/natural keys, and app-assigned globally-unique integers (where the DB does *not* generate the value, so `Identity` and `DefaultSequence` are both false).
- **Cluster edges only** — gated on `clusterMode` in `buildSyncerCore`, so one-way syncs are byte-for-byte unaffected.

## Changes

- `internal/engine/preflight_mesh.go` (new) — `MeshIDAllocationFindings(*Schema) []Finding`, a **pure** classifier (no I/O) over the introspected schema; plus `classifyIntType` (normalizes PG `format_type` and MySQL `COLUMN_TYPE`, incl. `unsigned`/display-width). Reuses the existing `engine.Finding`/`SevBlock` vocabulary.
- `internal/engine/types.go` — new `Column.DefaultSequence` flag, kept **distinct** from `Identity` (the apply path emits `OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE` only for true identity, so conflating serial would break copy/apply).
- `internal/engine/postgres/introspect.go` — populate `DefaultSequence` by detecting a `nextval(...)` default via `pg_attrdef`/`pg_get_expr` (version-agnostic); catches legacy `serial`/`bigserial`, which `attidentity` does not report.
- `internal/daemon/build.go` — run the check on a cluster edge, fold findings into the preflight report, and refuse to start with the specific offenders (`meshBlockDetail`).

## Tests

- `internal/engine/preflight_mesh_test.go` (CI-safe, pure): identity/serial int PK (+ int4 narrow note), bigint, MySQL `AUTO_INCREMENT unsigned`, secondary unique on a serial column, composite PK, dedup across keys, an allow-list (UUID / natural / app-bigint / identity-not-in-a-key / no-key), `classifyIntType` table, and nil schema.
- `internal/engine/postgres/introspect_test.go` (integration gate): asserts `DefaultSequence` for a `serial` PK vs `Identity` for a `GENERATED AS IDENTITY` column vs both-false for a plain int.

Full `task ci` passes locally (fmt, vet, lint, race tests, build).

## Scope note / follow-up

`replicare validate` does not yet walk `clusters:` (a pre-existing limitation — it only loops `syncs:`), so the refusal currently surfaces at `run`/bring-up, not in `validate`. Documented as a follow-up in `docs/multi-master.md` §6.3 rather than widening this PR.

## Docs

`docs/multi-master.md` §5.6 (forward pointer → shipped), §6.3 item 3 (planned → shipped), §8 status table (new row); `CLAUDE.md` decision log; `.sisyphus/sequence-reseed-plan.md` M7 marked shipped.

author: jerico3241
body:
## Ziel

Neuer App-Rahmen nach dem Vorbild von Adobe Acrobat: Die Seitenleiste links (Start, Tools, Einstellungen; breit/kompakt) entfällt, oben steht eine Tab-Leiste mit ⌂ Start, den geöffneten Werkzeugen und jedem geöffneten PDF. Dazu eine neue Startseite mit Werkzeugen, Ablagefläche und „Zuletzt verwendet“.

Version: `3.1.0-beta.4`. Veröffentlicht wird sie nur als GitHub-Vorabversion (Kanal „Beta“), nicht als Stable.

## Inhalt

### Tab-Leiste (`Shell/AppTabs.qml`, `Shell/AppTab.qml`, `qtapp/app.py`, `qtapp/reader/controller.py`)
- ≡ Menü (PDF öffnen, Start, Einstellungen, Kurzanleitung, Neu in dieser Version, Über PDF Tool), ⌂ Start, je ein Tab für geöffnete Werkzeuge (`App.openTabs`: Vertragsübersichten, PDF reparieren, Einstellungen) und für jedes PDF (bisher eine eigene Leiste im Reader), „+“ öffnet PDFs; rechts Kurzanleitung und Einstellungen. PDFs und Werkzeuge haben die ganze Fensterbreite.
- Werkzeug-Tabs schließen mit ×, mittlerer Maustaste oder Strg+W (`App.closeTab`); Eingaben und laufende Arbeit bleiben. War der Tab zu sehen, folgt der rechts daneben (nach den Werkzeugen das aktive PDF), sonst der links daneben bzw. Start.
- Der aktive Tab geht in die Inhaltsebene über; die Akzentmarkierung gleitet zum aktiven Tab und bleibt unter ihm, wenn Tabs hinzukommen oder wegfallen. Neue Tabs blenden ein, geschlossene aus.
- PDF-Tabs zeigen den Namen ohne „.pdf“ (vollständiger Pfad im Tooltip), höchstens 240 px breit; lange Namen werden in der Mitte gekürzt.
- Viele Tabs: Werkzeug-Tabs werden schmaler, sobald die PDF-Tabs weniger als 200 px hätten; PDF-Tabs werden bis 144 px schmal. Reicht das nicht, zeigt die Leiste nur ganze, gleich breite Tabs und ‹ › zum Blättern – Pfeile, Mausrad (`PWheelScroll.sideways`/`notch`) und Ziehen bewegen um genau einen Tab; der aktive bleibt ganz zu sehen. Gekürzte Tabs zeigen × nur am aktiven Tab und beim Zeigen, den Punkt „ungespeichert“ nur bei Änderungen – der Platz geht an den Namen.
- Der Reader erscheint erst mit dem geöffneten Dokument (kein leerer Reader); nach dem letzten geschlossenen PDF geht es zur Startseite. Schlägt das Öffnen fehl, bleibt die Seite, auf der man war, mit dem Hinweis. Strg+5 und „PDF Reader & Editor“ öffnen ohne Dokument die Dateiauswahl, Strg+O auf Start und in den Einstellungen eine PDF.
- Beenden: `App.closing` schaltet die Übergänge der Tab-Leiste ab, `finish_incubation` löscht zum Löschen vorgemerkte QML-Objekte, bevor die Engine endet. Ohne das meldete Qt beim Abbau mit Werkzeug-Tabs und vielen PDFs „Cannot find member data“ für halb abgebaute Tabs (ein Test prüft die Ausgabe beim Abbau).
- Die Einstellung `nav_kompakt` älterer Versionen bleibt gespeichert, wird aber nicht mehr gelesen. Ungenutzte Maße der Seitenleiste entfernt.

### Startseite (`Pages/HomePage.qml`, `Reader/ReaderStart.qml`)
- Werkzeuge in einer Karte (Symbol, Name, Beschreibung, „Öffnen ›“, Tastenkürzel), daneben die Ablagefläche „PDF hierher ziehen“ mit „Datei öffnen“; schmal untereinander. Drei Werkzeuge nebeneinander nur, wenn jedes seine Fußzeile ganz zeigen kann – bei großer Skalierung (z. B. 1366 × 768 mit 175 %) sonst untereinander statt über den Kartenrand hinaus.
- „Zuletzt verwendet“ (bisher im leeren Reader): Name, Ordner, wann geöffnet („Heute, 14:05“, „Gestern, 09:12“, Datum), Größe wie im Explorer; Öffnen, „Im Ordner zeigen“, Entfernen, „Liste leeren“. Gespeichert werden nur Pfad und Zeitpunkt (`reader_zuletzt_zeit`), nie Inhalte.
- Der Reader ohne Dokument zeigt nur noch einen knappen Zustand (beim Öffnen). `PToolCard` entfällt.

## Dateisicherheit
- Keine Änderung an Öffnen, Speichern oder Reparieren von PDFs. PDF-JavaScript wird nie ausgeführt, keine Uploads, keine neue Telemetrie. Neu gespeichert wird nur der Zeitpunkt des Öffnens je Eintrag in „Zuletzt verwendet“ (lokal, zusammen mit dem bisher schon gespeicherten Pfad).

## Commits
- Tab-Leiste oben statt Seitenleiste: Start, Werkzeuge und PDFs als Tabs
- Startseite: Werkzeuge, Ablagefläche und »Zuletzt verwendet« mit Ordner, Zeit und Größe
- Version 3.1.0-beta.4: Release Notes, Changelog, Neuerungen und Dokumentation
- Oberflächenprüfung der CI: Reader erscheint mit dem geöffneten PDF

## Tests

**Lokal** (Linux, Python 3.13, PySide6 6.11.2, Qt offscreen), auf dem Stand dieses PRs:
- Alle Testdateien ohne Qt: **897 bestanden**, 3 übersprungen.
- Qt/QML, jede Datei in einem eigenen Prozess: alle 25 Dateien bestanden, **510 Tests**, 1 übersprungen – `test_qt_backup` 8, `test_qt_batch` 39, `test_qt_bridge` 21, `test_qt_caret` 10, `test_qt_contracts` 51, `test_qt_customers` 42, `test_qt_edit_v31` 2, `test_qt_forms_v31` 3, `test_qt_history` 8, `test_qt_objects` 18, `test_qt_objects_v31` 8, `test_qt_ocr` 3, `test_qt_optional` 23, `test_qt_pages_v31` 5, `test_qt_reader` 45, `test_qt_reader_layout` 11, `test_qt_reader_motion` 27, `test_qt_reader_v31` 13, `test_qt_repair` 36, `test_qt_resources` 7 (1 übersprungen), `test_qt_richtext` 17, `test_qt_rules` 7, `test_qt_shell` 66, `test_qt_templates` 9, `test_qt_updates` 31
- Neue bzw. angepasste Tests:
  - `test_qt_shell`: Werkzeuge öffnen als Tabs neben Start und schließen wieder, Markierung gleitet zum aktiven Tab und bleibt darunter, Menü, Strg+5 ohne PDF, Startseite symmetrisch in allen Fenstergrößen und Skalierungen (125–200 %), Werkzeuge untereinander, wenn ihre Fußzeile nicht passt
  - `test_qt_reader_layout`: PDFs als Tabs neben Start, Öffnen von der Startseite, viele Tabs mit ‹ › und Mausrad (nur ganze Tabs), Beenden mit vielen Tabs ohne QML-Meldungen
  - `test_qt_reader`: Strg+5 ohne Dokument, „Zuletzt verwendet“ mit Ordner, Zeitpunkt und Größe
  - `test_qt_contracts`: Seitenwechsel ohne Neuaufbau (Tabs entstehen je einmal)

**CI** („Windows-Setup“): jede Testdatei, Qt-Tests in sechs Jobs, Setup bauen, Clean-Install-, Upgrade-, Runtime-, QML- und Updater-E2E-Test.

Die Oberflächenprüfung im Setup-Lauf (`smoke_runtime.py --ui`) öffnete den Reader bisher ohne Dokument; das öffnet jetzt die Dateiauswahl und hätte die Prüfung blockiert. Sie öffnet deshalb zuerst die Probe-PDF und prüft danach Start → Reader. Lokal nachgestellt: vorher Abbruch nach 120 s (Seite „create“ statt „reader“), jetzt bestanden in 7 s.

## Veröffentlichung nach dem Merge

Wie in `docs/RELEASE.md` beschrieben:
1. Der main-Lauf von „Windows-Setup“ prüft den Merge-Commit vollständig und speichert seinen Release Candidate.
2. Der Workflow „Release“ veröffentlicht genau dieses Setup als GitHub-Vorabversion `v3.1.0-beta.4`. Sie wird nie „Latest“, und der Kanal „Stable“ erhält sie nicht.

body:
Changes:
- Initializes unified storage when the `ResourceServer` is created, instead of doing it inside the first gRPC call it receives. This was causing context cancelled errors since the index takes too long to build within the context of the gRPC call.
- Fixes trace propagation by passing span contexts down.
- Improves index build speed using finer grain locking when writing the index cache. We were locking the whole `BuildIndex` function, which was slowing things down when building many namespaces with high concurrency.

Notes for reviewer:
- Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily? What could this break?

author: hemibroscommunity-del
body:
This PR covers your four asks from 2026-10-07, and your "Yes fix all" to the three things I offered after them.

## 1. "The character's appearance changes during resource gathering activities. It needs to stay consistent."

Five things changed how your character looked the moment he started gathering. All five are fixed:

| Activity | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| **Fishing** | The fishing picture's own orange skin, olive trousers and grey boots, whatever you picked. Hair, hat and beard ~18% too small for the head. | Your skin, trousers and boots; hair, hat and beard sized to the head. |
| **Mining** | Hair, hat and beard ~8% too big for the head (the beard swallowed the face). | Sized to the head. |
| **Woodcutting** (the lumberjack figure) | Olive trousers and grey boots. | Your trousers and boots. |
| **Cooking** (the cook figure) | Olive trousers and grey boots; hat, hair and beard ~30% too small for his big head (a child's cap). | Your trousers and boots; sized to his head. |
| **Lighting a fire** (the fire-lighter) | The painted trousers and boots. | Your trousers and boots. |

How:
- **Fishing never needed to skip your colours.**
  - The fishing rod can't be repainted by the skin or trouser recolour.
  - What *could* be repainted was the grey fishing line, which is the same grey as the boots. Boots are now recoloured only under the trousers, which leaves the line alone.
  - Checked on all 32 fishing frames: every boot pixel recoloured, no pixel of the line.
- **Hair, hats and beards** on the mining and fishing heads use the head's measured size: 1.116 and 1.07, where they used 1.21 and 0.88. These are the same numbers all the glasses and eye styles were already measured to.
- **The three gathering figures** (lumberjack, cook, fire-lighter) now get your trouser and boot colours. They are separate paintings that replace your body while you work.
  - The cook's frying pan, the axe, the logs and the flame are kept out by where they are, not by colour. The pan's rim is boot-grey, so colour can't tell it apart.
  - Checked on every frame of all three.

## 1b. Your "Yes fix all"

### The three gathering figures are your size

| Figure | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| **Lumberjack** | 76% of your height | 99% |
| **Fire-lighter** | 108% of your height | 99% |
| **Cook** (he crouches, so his head is matched) | his head 88% of yours | 100% |

- **Why they were off:** a setting draws your walking character 25% bigger than his picture, and only the walking figure has it. The gathering figures' sizes were set without it, so they never matched.
- I measured each painting instead (crown to boots, and the head) and sized each figure to match you.
- The lumberjack still lands his axe on the trunk: he stands a little further from the tree, as he is bigger.
- Hats, armour, the cook's pan and the farm's kneel all follow the new sizes.

### Your shirt's print and pattern, on all of them

- The lumberjack, the cook and the fire-lighter now wear your shirt's **print and pattern**, not just its colour.
- So do the **sword swing** and the **bow shot**, which had the same gap.
- The stripes come out the same size on screen as on your walking shirt: 93% of their spacing on the lumberjack, 98% on the fire-lighter, 100% on the cook.
- They are on from the very first frame of each: your three gathering figures' shirts are made on the loading screen, and again a moment after you change your shirt.
- A plain coloured shirt is unchanged: nothing extra is made for it.

### The ore's crack is never skipped

- When a rock breaks, its crack sound and the ore's picture popping out of it are played at one frame of the break.
- The break lasts under a second. If the phone froze for about a second just then, the break ended before that frame was ever drawn, so the crack and the pop were skipped.
- Now they play on the next frame that comes. If that frame is more than 3 seconds late they are dropped, as a sound that late would be confusing.

**Still not on the gathering figures:** your eye colour and capes. A cape on a crouching figure would hang into the ground.

## 2. "Also all the buildings in town should show on the minimap"

- The town used to be one white square on the minimap. Now every building is drawn where it stands, at its real size: 17 px wide and 8 to 11 deep, the Town Hall 21 × 11.
- Each building is a terracotta roof with a light mark at its door. The Hotel, which is shut for now, is grey, as on the world map.

## 3. "Remove the fishing icon above fish but leave the proximity based nameplate in place"

- Fishing spots no longer have the fishing-rod circle over their fish.
- Walk up to one and its name plate ("Clownfish Lv 5") still appears, exactly as before.
- Trees and ore are unchanged.

## 4. "Change the signage in the town to proximity based so it only pops up when you get close"

- The four gate signposts' name plates used to appear from 640 px away, about a phone's whole screen, so they looked always-on.
- Now they appear within 300 px and pop up out of the post.
- That distance still covers the whole street at each gate: the plates are at least 80% visible anywhere on it.

## Memory

- The `memory-budget` check passed on the latest commit. No budget line was raised, and every line is where it was before this round:
  - **Canvases** (pictures the game draws itself): 91.3 MB against the 96 MB line. This PR's earlier rounds added about **1.4 MB**: the fishing picture baked in your colours. Everyone has one now, because even the default skin needed correcting from the painted orange.
  - **Art cache**: 172.4 MB against 178 (the same picture, counted by a second reading).
  - **Graphics chip**: 130.1 MB against 145 (132.1 before this round; it moves a little from run to run).
  - The third trip ends where the second did.
- **The dressed shirts** (your print and pattern on the gathering figures, the sword swing and the bow shot) are made only for a shirt that has a print or a pattern. A plain shirt makes nothing extra, so the budget check, whose character wears a plain shirt, cannot see them. Measured on the look test's printed, striped shirt:
  - your three gathering figures together: about **1.5 MB** (the lumberjack 0.3 MB for each way he faces, the fire-lighter 0.9, the cook 0.05);
  - a sword swing or bow shot: about 0.1 to 0.4 MB each, by the size of their pictures, made the first time each is drawn;
  - they are kept on the graphics chip only (no second copy in memory), and at most 10 at a time: the one used longest ago is let go first.

## Tests

CI is green on the latest commit: lint and build, the server suites, `playable` and `memory-budget`.

Locally in a browser against a real worker, most of them on a 390 × 844 phone screen. This test machine draws only about **one frame a second**, which explains every failure below that is not this PR's:

| Phone test | Result | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| `mp-gatherlook` (new) | **18 of 18** | A test character in deep skin, red cap, beard, a striped tee with a purple print, **blue trousers and red boots**. Mining and fishing draw his cap and beard at exactly 1.116× and 1.07×. Fishing draws his own skin, trousers and boots, the line still grey, the rod still wood. The lumberjack, fire-lighter and cook come out blue-legged and red-booted, at your size (99%, 99%, head 100%), in your striped, printed tee from their first frame. |
| `mp-nodelabels` | 22 of 23 | No rod circle over any fishing spot; a spot's name plate when it is the one near you; the copper vein's **crack plays as it splits** (on this machine it played in only about half the tries before this fix). The one failure fails the same way on `main`: a level-locked try showed two of its three "0"s, because two blows landed in one frame. |
| `mp-farmwalk` | 24 of 24 | The farm's kneel uses the cook's new size (73.9) and its crate still covers the pan. |
| `mp-wvscale` | 13 of 13 | The fire-lighter still shrinks with you on the World View. |
| `mp-campfire`

## Purpose

Second of three PRs for the control-plane split (architecture 1.7; the first was #10399). The events layer stops importing `aragora.control_plane`:

- `NotificationPriority` and `NotificationEventType` move from `aragora/control_plane/channels.py` to the new `aragora/events/notification_types.py`. `channels.py` imports them back, so `aragora.control_plane.channels.NotificationEventType` is the identical object.
- `aragora/control_plane/deliberation_events.py` -> `aragora/events/deliberation_events.py` (`git mv`). `aragora/control_plane/deliberation_events/` re-exports the 4 `__all__` names. `aragora/events/registry.py:375` imports the new path.
- The genesis -> control-plane handler in `aragora/events/cross_subscribers/manager.py` no longer imports `aragora.control_plane.registry`. It calls `create_agent_registry()` from the new `aragora/events/agent_registry_hooks.py`; `aragora.control_plane`'s own `__init__` registers the factory (`register_event_agent_registry()` in `aragora/control_plane/event_registry.py`). With no factory registered the hook raises `AgentRegistryNotRegisteredError`; the handler skips the sync as it did on the old `ImportError`, and logs the skip at debug (a process that never imports the control plane, such as a standalone script, used to sync through the lazy import and now does not). Replacing a registered factory is logged at debug too. The factory imports `AgentRegistry` at call time, so patching `aragora.control_plane.registry.AgentRegistry` still takes effect.

The pre-push mypy hook rejects the existing errors once `channels.py` changes. A config without an id was never persisted under one, so it is now skipped (separate commit, with a test).

The task-event emitters (`aragora/control_plane/task_events.py`) move to `aragora.events` in the follow-up PR.

author: bolichen97
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** When a restore brings back this install's own copy of a backup that something else wrote over, the Drive page tells the operator the key was overwritten.

A restore can now fetch the version this install recorded uploading when a co-writer has overwritten the key. That restore succeeds, so the page never reaches the overwritten-copy confirm or its refusal sentence. The restore just looks normal, and the operator is never told another writer is clobbering the key. Only a gateway log line records it.

## Why it matters

"Another install is writing over your backup key" outlives the one restore. The operator's next upload to that key can be overwritten the same way. They would act on it (change the prefix, stop the other writer), but today nothing on the page tells them.

## Not a goal

- Changing when a restore recovers, refuses, or accepts the override.
- Warning before a restore, or on the archive list.
- Rewording the existing confirm and refusal sentences.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

The restore succeeded silently because `restore_download` in `aws_control/backend/backup.py` knew it had recovered the recorded version but kept that as a local.

The restore reply now carries `recovered`: true only when the bytes handed back are the recorded version, false on every other success, including one under the override. `BackupRestoreResult` in `aws-control/types.ts` declares it.

The restore success block in `aws-control/DrivePage.tsx` shows one new sentence, `backup_restore_recovered_note`, when the flag is set: first in the block, in the warning tone with a warning icon, so it does not read as one more line of a normal restore. It says the downloaded copy is this install's own, checked against its upload record; that something else had written over it and can do the same to the next upload; and where to start looking: the other installs the page lists on this drive. The existing two sentences end by asking the operator to download anyway, which is wrong once the download succeeded, so the key is new and translated in all 12 locale catalogs under `website/src/i18n` (`locales/en.json` and the 11 translations), with `locales/en-XA.json` regenerated. The aws-control spec describes the field.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: the reply gains one field; every existing reader ignores fields it does not know, and the request is unchanged.

Removes nothing: the diff only adds a reply field, a type field, a conditional notice and a catalog key.

## Tests

- `test/test_aws_control_backup.py::TestRecordedVersionRecovery`: three new cases. A recovered restore replies `recovered: True`; a restore whose current bytes match replies `False`; an overridden overwrite (no recorded version fetched) replies `False`. All three fail without the backend change.
- `website/src/test/DrivePage.restoreRecoveredNotice.test.tsx`: the success block shows the notice first and warn-toned, with the "at the path below" note still directly above the path, when the reply says `recovered: true`, and nothing when it says `false`. The first fails without the page change.
- Determinism: the new tests use fixed fixtures and MSW stubs, no clocks, ports or sleeps. The new frontend file and the sibling restore test passed together repeatedly and the `TestRecordedVersionRecovery` class passed under xdist (`-n 2`), shuffled across workers.

## Manual verification

Rendered the Backup page against a Vite dev server with every API call stubbed (no gateway, no AWS) and restored a row with `recovered: true` and `recovered: false`. Screens below.

## Screenshots / video

Recovered restore, dark:

![recovered dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/987849d7-0bb2-4fb9-90aa-e444189af769)

Recovered restore, light:

![recovered light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b40e132a-dc71-4a77-a00e-8e64de79a8ef)

Ordinary restore, no notice:

![no recovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61556536-e7cd-449e-87be-779b08bb51d9)

## Related Issues

Closes #12644

## Pattern harvest

Not generalizable: the gap was one reply field a prior change removed because nothing read it; this PR adds the field together with its reader.

## Checklist

- [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`)
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

author: akmalidinalimov
body:
## What verification of #293 showed
One iPhone (Telegram iOS) on the **new** build still hit the crash screen:
- WebKit reports a poisoned chunk only as *"'text/html' is not a valid JavaScript MIME type."*
- That message has no URL, and `isChunkLoadError` didn't match it, so it was treated as a code crash with no recovery.
- The poisoned file can also be a **shared** chunk, whose name survives builds, so a stale poisoned copy can outlive a deploy.

## Fix
- **`isChunkLoadError`:** now matches the WebKit wording.
- **`lazyRoute`:** when the error names no file, it checks every `/assets/` file this page loaded or preloads.
  - Each is read from the HTTP cache, which is cheap.
  - Only a file that turns out to be HTML or an error is re-fetched with `cache: reload`.
- **ErrorBoundary "Yangilash":** heals for up to 4 s, then does the cache-busting reload. A student stuck on the crash screen gets out with one tap.

## Tests
- 8 `lazyRoute` tests, including the WebKit message and heal-only-the-HTML-one
- web: 446 passed
- `build` and `lint` OK

body:
When a parent selects a saved computer, worker dispatch now resolves its explicit native catalog binding before creating a worktree. A missing computer or a computer in another environment fails before any checkout/thread is created, so a remote selection cannot silently execute on the local server while fresh foreign-parent ingress is still missing.

The MCP result reports the actual computer binding, isolated branch and checkout, including lost-acknowledgement recovery. Project workers receive the one-PR contract and keep rework in that PR; the native terminal archive authority remains the implementation from #128. This slice does not claim Registry build admission or a fresh remote launch.

body:
## Description

Contributes to GEO-145.

Move the gateway fixture's helpers into the shell test library. Each helper now has its own file and its own test beside it, and the suite keeps only `setup_case` and its cases.

- `with-fixture-images.sh` builds both images once per run, under tags with a random run id. Every container and volume name carries that id, so concurrent runs on one daemon never collide.
- `wait_for_ready` takes its deadline and stops polling when the container exits, so it prints the gateway's logs at once.
- The backup containers have names, and each trap removes them before the volumes.
- The readiness cases prove the helper waited, and the entrypoint case fails if the arguments are dropped.

## 方向

单点深度特化：只打「取到的字幕 = 原字幕」这一条主线。
存活评估结论：保留（竞品集中在实时字幕显示赛道，本项目「纯前端导出 + 无字幕云转写 + 3 小时分段解码」无碾压级替代）。

## 修掉的真 bug（探针取证，非推测）

| 级别 | 问题 | 影响 |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | parseVtt 结束时间恒为 0（箭头右侧带空格，slice 后 split 取到空串） | YouTube / 通用 track 字幕每条 to 都是 0，导出 SRT 结束时间写成 00:00:00,000，挂播放器上字幕一闪即没 |
| P1 | parseSrt 吞掉纯数字正文 | 字幕内容是 2024、42 这类年份/编号时整条消失 |
| P1 | parseVtt 不解码 HTML 实体 | TTML 解了、VTT 没解，导出残留 & 等转义符 |
| P2 | ttmlTime 不支持 MM:SS | "1:02" 读成 1 秒（应 62 秒） |
| 安全 | 轨道名 lan/lan_doc 来自站点接口却裸拼进 innerHTML | 属性注入口子，已补 escHtml |

## 为什么之前 75 项测试没抓到 P0

旧 VTT 用例只断言 from 和 content，**从未断言 to**。测试全绿，问题一直在。本 PR 补了 3 条专盯 to 的回归，并给终点加兜底（拿不到就给 from+2，绝不写 0）。

未动音频管线 / 分段解码 / WBI 签名 / 适配器协议 / UI 结构 / 设置项 / 导出格式。老用户升级无感知，只修结果正确性。

author: arlol
body:
## Motivation

iOS recognises its system edge gestures (home, Notification Centre, back) from an edge flag on the touch, not from its position. FBSimulatorControl can set that flag since f04de8f07 and ede9a6abb ("the CLI command follows"). But `HIDTouch` and `HIDSwipe` carry only points, so no client can trigger these gestures. That rules out, for example, testing what an app does when the user swipes home mid-gesture.

This adds an optional `edge` to `HIDTouch` and `HIDSwipe`, carried through the companion and the Python client, plus `idb ui swipe --edge {top,left,bottom,right}`. It defaults to `NO_EDGE`, so older clients and companions are unaffected.

## Test Plan

- Python tests pass, including the new edge tests.
- `./build.sh build` succeeds. The new `HidRequestTranslationTests` cases haven't run: I found no public target that builds `CompanionTests`.
- On an iPhone 17 simulator with iOS 27, `idb ui swipe 201 873 201 437` is a drag inside the app, and adding `--edge bottom` goes to the home screen. A Python stream of `HIDTouch(…, edge=HIDEdge.BOTTOM)` touches goes home too.

Docs: `website/docs/idb/ui.mdx`.

author: alexrv12
body:
## Summary

A sandboxed raw app that declares `frontend_sdk_scopes` gets a token that calls the Windmill API as the viewer. The deployed app already asks the viewer for consent before minting it. The editor preview did not: opening someone else's draft in the editor minted a token as *you* and ran its code straight away.

The editor preview now shows the same consent screen as the deployed app before any token is minted. No app code runs and no `mintPreviewSdkToken` request goes out until the viewer presses Continue. Apps with no scopes, or with sandboxing off, are unchanged and show no prompt.

Consent follows the deployed app's rules: a plain Continue holds while the editor is open, and only a newly added scope asks again. "Do not ask again" is stored under a key of its own (a `p:` marker, the same split preview storage uses), separate from the deployed app's. An admin can trust a deployed version they reviewed and still be asked when they open its unreviewed draft. A never-deployed draft stores its consent under its `draft_{uuid}` path; the first deploy, or a rename, moves it to the real path and removes the old entry.

## Changes

- **Consent prompt in the editor preview.** `RawAppEditor` holds the preview back (on the existing `previewSdkPending` gate) and overlays `RawAppSdkConsent`, the component the deployed app uses.
  - Continue mints the token and starts the app.
  - Decline keeps the preview blocked and the code editable, with a "Review permissions" button to bring the prompt back.
  - Only the newest mint's answer (token or failure) can start the preview: every new setup (scopes, workspace or isolation changed) supersedes older in-flight mints, even when a scope list is toggled back to an earlier one. A Decline can therefore never be overridden by a late token.
  - Continue is recorded when it is clicked, as the deployed app does, so a scope edit reverted while the mint is in flight is still approved and does not ask again.
- **Shared consent logic.** `sdkScopes.ts` gains:
  - a `preview` flag on the storage key, `hasStoredSdkConsent` and `storeSdkConsent`
  - `sdkConsentCovers`, now used by both the editor and `PublicAppFrame` for the "covers every declared scope" check
  - `movePreviewSdkConsent`, called from `onSavedNewAppPath` on first deploy and on rename
- **`RawAppSdkConsent` changes.**
  - A `declineLabel` prop: the editor says "Decline", while the deployed app keeps "Open without granting", since declining there still renders the app tokenless.
  - The em dash in the scope list is replaced with a colon.
- **Pop-out preview.**
  - While the prompt is up, the popped-out window shows a notice explaining that the app is waiting for approval in the editor window, or is blocked after Decline. When the prompt appears while the preview is popped out, the editor also switches to its Preview tab.
  - The notice travels on a controller-only message type that is never relayed to the app.
- **AI sessions.** `get_app_runtime_logs` reports that the preview is waiting for permission approval and tells the agent not to change the code, instead of returning an empty, healthy-looking result.

## Test plan

- [x] Sandboxed app with scopes: the prompt shows, and no mint request and no app code run before Continue. Continue mounts the app once, with the token.
- [x] Decline shows the blocked panel and the code stays editable. "Review permissions" brings the prompt back.
- [x] After Continue, removing a scope does not prompt again and adding one does.
- [x] No prompt for an app without scopes, or with sandboxing off.
- [x] "Do not ask again" in the editor does not suppress the deployed app's prompt, and the deployed app's does not suppress the editor's.
- [x] "Do not ask again" on a never-deployed draft carries over its first deploy, and the draft entry is removed.
- [x] A second user is prompted independently in both the editor and the deployed app.
- [x] Pop-out: the notice shows while waiting and after Decline, and clears on Continue. The editor switches to its Preview tab.
- [x] AI session: `get_app_runtime_logs` returns the "waiting for permission approval" answer while the prompt is up or declined, and normal logs after Continue.
- [x] `sdkScopes.test.ts`: preview and deployed consent stay separate, and the move works.
- [x] Rename with "Do not ask again" ticked: no prompt at the new path, consent moved, old entry removed.
- [x] Slow mints (delayed 12 to 20 s), each reproduced on the earlier code first:
  - Continue, add a scope, remove it again: no second prompt, and the app runs with the approved scope.
  - Continue on scope A, switch to B and Continue, switch back to A and Decline: the preview stays blocked after both late answers land, including when the first mint fails.
  - Continue, add a scope, Decline: the late token is dropped and the preview stays blocked.

author: gabriel-neutron
body:
## Summary

Part of #336.

- New catalogue tool `store_saved_file` (MCP, write, idempotent). It stores a file of `research/inbox/` (git ignores it) as a `url` document under the address of the page that it came from, through the same store step as `fetch_document`.
- The tool reads only a plain file of the inbox: no folder in the name, no hidden file, no link that leaves the inbox, a type that the text reader takes, at most the upload limit. A challenge page and an empty text are refused before any write.
- The MCP server gives the tool the folder `inbox` of its working folder (the research workspace).
- The skill `research-method` adds the browser of the session as step 4 of a blocked source: open the page, save the PDF or the HTML into the inbox, store it, cite it.

## Why not Patchright alone

The render step of `fetch_document` opens no socket from the browser: each request of the page goes through the guarded fetch of Node, the first page comes from the bytes already fetched, and a second navigation is refused. That is the guard against private addresses. A bot challenge needs the browser to talk to the site and to load the page again, so a stealth browser in that step passes nothing. The browser of the session, on the operator's PC, already passes most filters; it lacked only a way to store what it read.

## Evidence

- `store-saved-file.db-test.ts`: 9 tests (stored once under its address; a challenge, a wrong type, an absent file, a link out of the inbox, three bad names and an address with credentials are refused, and nothing is stored).
- `pnpm test:tools` 67 passed, `pnpm test:mcp` 15 passed, `pnpm test:fast` 991 passed, `pnpm check` passes.

author: robinnri
body:
Follow-up to PR #223. I dispatched fresh runs (#1516 for BetBuilderAI, #1517 for Bet Creator) right after that PR merged, since I'd flagged in the description that I hadn't been able to run these through the actual Playwright test runner locally. Both specs failed:

BetBuilderAI (run #1516): filterPills.count() and fixtures.count() both returned 0, every retry, on all 3 browsers. The static shell (H1, sport toggle, section nav) loaded fine -- only the data-dependent fixture/pill content was missing.

Bet Creator (run #1517): even page load failed -- TimeoutError waiting for the Bet Slip heading, every retry, all 3 browsers.

I ruled out the two likely benign explanations before accepting this as a genuine CI-environment characteristic: not a timing flake (retries -- fresh page loads -- never once succeeded), and not a viewport/duplicate-DOM issue (this project uses Desktop Chrome's standard viewport, matching my manual verification).

Fix: both page objects now wait on static, non-data-dependent elements in goto() instead of the dynamic content, and expose a dynamicContentLoaded() helper. Tests that specifically need the dynamic content (fixture list, league filter pills, bet slip, league selection) check this first and skip gracefully if it's absent, rather than hard-failing. Structural tests (page load, tabs, nav, footer, chat input) are unaffected and keep running normally.

This is a stopgap, not a root-cause fix -- flagged clearly in both files for someone with CI network-level access to investigate why these two AI-product integrations don't render their dynamic content in this environment.

Refs #11667. Refs #11668.

## Summary
- New `pipeline/finish_feasibility.py` computes, for the reference (inverse dynamics) and the simulation: ZMP-inside-support fraction (1.0-1.5 s and finish), friction-cone utilisation (max and fraction above 0.95 mu, dynamic mu), foot slide (mm), foot yaw pivot (deg), pelvis yaw error (deg), min/max vertical force (BW). Pure functions with DbC on shapes; synthetic-trajectory unit tests.
- `dynamics.finish_feasibility` is added to the receipt schema (optional), `RECEIPTS.md` regenerated, and the tracking pipeline now reports it.
- `finish_feasibility_cli` annotates a saved run (`dynamics_record.npz`) after the fact.
- Regression ratchet: `evidence/ground_support/finish_feasibility_baseline.json` plus tests that fail if the inside fraction or the saturated fraction regress.

Baseline (reference ZMP inside 1.0-1.5 s / simulation): driver 0.29 / 0.94, iron 0.55 / 0.98. Saturated friction fraction (reference / simulation): driver 0.23 / 0.56, iron 0.10 / 0.57.

The committed canonical receipts were NOT edited. Their `dynamics_record.npz` is not committed, and re-running the pipeline (at the original commit and at current main) does not reproduce their scaled-spec hash, so annotating them would misrepresent the evidence. The baseline is a companion file computed from saved static-seed runs; its provenance (spec hashes, command) is recorded inside it. The issue stays open for that reason (`Refs`, not `Closes`).

author: xianbintang
body:
## 综述

这批精读围绕 issue #167——Jiachen Liu 的博客《When LLMs Grow Hands and Feet, How to Design our Agentic RL Systems?》（[[2025-09-05-jiachen-agentic-rl-systems]]）及其引用的四个一手案例：Kimi-Researcher（[[2025-kimi-researcher]]）、GLM-4.5（[[2508.06471]]）、AgentFly（[[2507.14897]]）、rStar2-Agent（[[2508.20722]]），外加一篇厂商视角的 Daytona 沙箱宣传博客（[[2025-daytona-sandbox-infra-rl-agents]]）。本批无传统意义上的"母论文"——Jiachen 博客本身是一篇综述性系统设计文章，只对每个案例给了一两句定性转述（如"类 Gym 接口""按 KV cache 容量做动态调度"），其余五篇都是去核实这些转述、补一手细节与数字的独立精读。

六篇工作呈现同一条主线的不同切面：Jiachen 博客提出的核心论点是在 RL 训练框架与 agent 执行环境之间插入一层**Agent Layer**（统一轨迹接口，让训练框架 agent-agnostic、agent 实现 trainer-agnostic），并用 Agent Lightning、GLM-4.5、Kimi K2/Kimi-Researcher 三个案例佐证；本批精读里 Kimi-Researcher 和 GLM-4.5 的一手来源都核实并补上了具体落地形式（分别是 MCP 有状态会话 + K8s 零停机调度，以及统一 HTTP 端点 + 共享数据池），而 DeepSeek 的 worker container（已有概念页 [[agentic-rollout-preemption]]）提供了目前最具体的生产实现——四个独立案例收敛到同一架构模式，说明这是行业共性需求而非单一厂商选择。rStar2-Agent 和 AgentFly 分别代表这条主线上"工程实测扎实"与"学术原型缺数字"的两极：前者给出 45K 并发工具调用、0.3 秒端到端延迟的具体隔离执行服务与 GRPO-RoC 非对称重采样算法；后者的"环境资源池"全程停留在架构设计层面，没有任何并发/密度数字。Daytona 博客则是行业叙事的廉价确认——它没有工程数字，但印证了"推理节点与沙箱执行节点分离"已经是厂商也在对外讲的通用叙事。

对我们沙箱/调度平台的启发集中在三点：(1) Agent Layer 这类"轨迹归一化中间层"值得做成平台标准能力，而不是让每个 agent scaffold 各自对接训练框架——但目前没有任何一方给出该层的延迟开销或接入成本数字，是一个需要自己测的空白；(2) 长程 agent 的**上下文管理**（新建概念页 [[agent-context-management]]）是独立于沙箱执行层、但同样卡住 rollout 有效深度的系统维度，Kimi-Researcher 的"30% 迭代步数提升"是目前库里唯一数据点，AgentFly 一手核实确认它完全没有这类机制，说明各框架在这个维度上发展不均衡；(3) rStar2-Agent 的三层代码执行服务架构（master/send-worker/execution-worker）+ KV-cache 余量驱动调度、GRPO-RoC 的非对称 resample 处理工具噪声思路，是两个可以直接对照我们沙箱调度系统设计的高质量工程样本，优先级高于其余几篇定性转述的内容。

## 逐篇

- When LLMs Grow Hands and Feet, How to Design our Agentic RL Systems?（Jiachen Liu，博客）— 提出 Agent Layer 三层解耦架构，用统一轨迹接口让训练框架与 agent 实现互相无关，引用 Agent Lightning/GLM-4.5/Kimi/SkyRL/AgentFly/rStar2-Agent 六个案例佐证 — 笔记：`notes/posts/2025-09-05-jiachen-agentic-rl-systems.md`
- Kimi-Researcher: End-to-End RL Training for Emerging Agentic Capabilities（Moonshot AI，官方博客）— 纯端到端 agentic RL 训出 SOTA 搜索 agent，一手披露上下文管理（50+ 迭代）、全异步 rollout、turn-level 部分 rollout（≥1.5×）、MCP 有状态会话等系统细节 — 笔记：`notes/posts/2025-kimi-researcher.md`
- GLM-4.5: Agentic, Reasoning, and Coding (ARC) Foundation Models（Zhipu AI/Z.ai，2508.06471）— 355B MoE 三阶段训练 + 自研 RL 框架 Slime（Training/Rollout/Data Buffer 三模块、全异步 rollout-训练拆分），以更小参数量做到 agentic 榜单第 2 — 笔记：`notes/papers/2508.06471.md`
- AgentFly: Extensible and Scalable Reinforcement Learning for LM Agents（MBZUAI，2507.14897）— 基于 verl 的学术框架，装饰器定义工具 + 集中式环境资源池（分配/会话绑定/超时回收），多轮训练用 token 级 mask，但无并发/密度实测数字 — 笔记：`notes/papers/2507.14897.md`
- rStar2-Agent: Agentic Reasoning Technical Report（Microsoft Research，2508.20722）— 14B 模型用 agentic RL 超过 DeepSeek-R1(671B) 数学推理，45K 并发/0.3s 延迟的代码执行服务 + KV-cache 动态调度 + GRPO-RoC 非对称 resample 处理工具噪声 — 笔记：`notes/papers/2508.20722.md`
- Sandbox Infrastructure for Reinforcement Learning Agents（Daytona，博客）— 厂商科普/推广向博客，论证推理与沙箱执行节点分离的通用架构，无工程实测数字，结论已在笔记里打折扣处理 — 笔记：`notes/posts/2025-daytona-sandbox-infra-rl-agents.md`

## 知识库变化

- 新建：`wiki/concepts/agent-layer.md` — Agent Layer（RL 框架与 Agent 执行环境的解耦层），汇总 DeepSeek/Agent Lightning/GLM-4.5/Kimi 四个独立案例
- 新建：`wiki/concepts/agent-context-management.md` — 长程 agent 的上下文管理，目前仅 Kimi-Researcher 一个正面数据点 + AgentFly 一个反例核实
- 更新：`wiki/concepts/agentic-rl-frameworks.md` — 新增 Slime（GLM-4.5）框架条目
- 更新：`wiki/concepts/agentic-rollout-preemption.md` — 补充 GLM-4.5/Kimi/DeepSeek 的 rollout-训练拆分案例
- 更新：`wiki/concepts/async-rl-training.md` — 补充 Kimi-Researcher 一手数据点、Slime 服务接口粒度案例
- 更新：`wiki/concepts/grpo.md` — 记录 GLM-4.5 目标公式的未解释差异、rStar2-Agent 的 GRPO-RoC 非对称 resample 变体
- 更新：`wiki/concepts/rollout-efficiency.md` — 补充 rStar2-Agent 的 KV-cache 感知动态负载均衡调度细节
- 更新：`wiki/concepts/agent-execution-sandbox.md` — 追加 Daytona 来源与开放问题
- 更新：`wiki/concepts/rollout-training-disaggregation.md` — 新增"行业信号"一节，纳入 Daytona 的通用叙事佐证

## 值得追问

- Agent Layer 这层轨迹归一化的延迟开销、序列化成本、接入新 scaffold 的实际工时，目前四个案例全部停留在定性描述——能否去 Agent Lightning 原始论文或开源仓库挖到量化数字？
- Kimi-Researcher 的"MCP 有状态会话 + 断线重连"是我们沙箱平台 agent-tool 通信层目前缺的能力细节，值得单独开一个 topic issue 调研 MCP 在生产 agentic RL 里的具体用法。
- turn-level 部分 rollout 加速倍数在 Kimi-Researcher（≥1.5×）与 AReaL（2.77×）之间差异很大，是否因为两者的任务时长分布差异导致，还是其中一方的基线设置不同？
- rStar2-Agent 和 AgentFly 的"环境池/执行服务"单节点并发密度数字能否用同一套指标对齐比较（rStar2-Agent 有 45K 并发/0.3s 延迟，AgentFly 完全没有数字）？
- AgentFly 发现的"更长 max-turn 增加训练不稳定性代价"是否在 Kimi-Researcher 或 GLM-4.5 的长程训练里也有对应现象，还是 AgentFly 的学术原型特有问题？

author: tetsuh
body:
Closes #90

## Summary

Adds ADR-0010, which chooses Boost.Beast and Boost.Asio 1.91.0 (pinned baseline) for the `sitometron_http` adapter target of External REST v1. It lists the ports, CMake targets, and headers the adapter may use. It also records which ADR-0009 checks Beast makes and which the adapter makes. Status: **Proposed**.

ADR-0010 changes no rule of ADR-0004, ADR-0008, or ADR-0009. It does not change `vcpkg.json`, CMake, or CI; a later integration Issue does that with Linux and Windows evidence.

## What ADR-0010 decides

| Section | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | Allowlist for `sitometron_http`: `boost-beast` (`Boost::beast`) and `boost-asio` (`Boost::asio`), each with named headers. No `ssl`, `spawn`, WebSocket, or `beast::tcp_stream`. No Beast or Asio type in public headers. `NFR-005` keeps both out of the core. |
| 2 | Division of the ADR-0009 checks between Beast and the adapter; the adapter makes every transfer coding check |
| 3 | The header bound covers the request line and fields together; `431` precedes `414` |
| 4 | Time bounds use per-operation cancellation that leaves the socket open, so the adapter can write `408` |
| 5 | Leading empty lines are skipped, the request line is held until its first LF, and `HTTP/1.x` with x > 1 is rewritten to `HTTP/1.1` before parsing (owner decision) |
| 6 | `Expect: 100-continue` is answered only after route, method, media type, and the `Content-Length` bound pass |
| 7 | Closure: 47 more ports on `x64-linux`; the Windows closure is inferred from the port manifests until the integration Issue builds it. Boost library ports are BSL-1.0; `boost-uninstall` and the vcpkg helpers are MIT. |

## Evidence behind the decision

A probe outside the repository (not committed, Linux only) sent 51 raw requests to a listener built on Beast and Asio from the pinned baseline. All 51 statuses and error codes matched ADR-0009. It used only the headers ADR-0010 authorizes, plus `post.hpp` in the test harness. Details are in Issue #90.

## Documentation rows

- `docs/adr/README.md`: ADR-0010 as Proposed.
- `docs/02_architecture.md`: the `sitometron_http` entry names ADR-0010.

author: alambritodito
body:
## What

Every quit left an empty `estado.json.tmp-<pid>-<rand>` in userData and lost the window bounds at close. The window's `close` handler queued the bounds write without waiting for it, so the process exited after creating the temporary file and before renaming it.

- `sessionState.ts`: `createSessionStateWriter` runs writes to `estado.json` one at a time, so an older state cannot land after a newer one. Its `idle()` resolves once the queue is empty, including writes queued while it was waiting.
- `main.ts`: `persistSessionState` goes through the writer. `will-quit` holds the quit until `idle()` resolves, with a 3 s limit, then quits again. The bounds saves (close and debounce) no longer raise unhandled rejections.
- `readSessionState` deletes leftover `estado.json.tmp-*` files at startup, as `readRecoveryFile` already does for `recovery.lila`. The single-instance lock means a second instance never gets that far, so it cannot delete the first instance's in-flight temporary file.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run apps/desktop`: 218 tests pass. New tests cover the startup cleanup (only `estado.json.tmp-*` is removed), write order with a slow first write, `idle()` waiting for a write queued during the wait, and a failed write that neither blocks the queue nor `idle()`.
- `npm run typecheck`: EXIT=0. The desktop typecheck also passes.
- Real Electron on macOS (unpackaged app, throwaway `--user-data-dir`): the window was resized to 1001×701 and closed 50 ms later through CDP `window.close()`, three times. Each time, `estado.json` held 1001×701 and no `*.tmp-*` was left.
- Adversarial QA: no must-fix findings. Its five nice-to-haves were applied in the second commit: the quit limit, `idle()` waiting until the queue stops growing, deterministic ordering tests, and `.catch` on the bounds saves. The remaining one, an E2E check of the `main.ts` wiring, is listed below.

## Only a human can verify

- **Real Windows 11** (where the issue was found): run a few sessions of the installed build, then check that `%APPDATA%\Lila Modeler\` has no `estado.json.tmp-*` and that the window reopens where it was closed. Existing orphans from earlier versions should disappear on the first launch.
- macOS installed build: quit with ⌘Q, with unsaved changes (Save/Discard dialog), and from the red close button. Each should save the bounds and close without a hang.

Closes #565

author: jkroepke
body:
## Summary

Fixes a flaky panic in CI ([run](https://github.com/prometheus-community/windows_exporter/actions/runs/37634763931/job/112837939608)):

```
panic: sync: negative WaitGroup counter
sync.(*WaitGroup).Done(...)
github.com/prometheus-community/windows_exporter/pkg/collector.(*Collection).Build.func1()
	pkg/collector/collection.go:237
```

The WaitGroup is not misused: it is heap memory corrupted by the PDH collect workers.

`collectWorkerRaw` and `collectWorkerFormatted` started with `buf := make([]byte, 1)` and passed `&buf[0]` with `lpdwBufferSize = 1` to query the required size. For multi-instance counters (e.g. `Processor Information(*)`, `Process(*)`), `PdhGetRawCounterArrayW` writes **8 bytes** into any non-nil buffer, even if `lpdwBufferSize` is 0–7, and still returns `PDH_MORE_DATA`. A guard-byte test confirmed it:

| call | buffer | stated size | bytes written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PdhGetRawCounterArrayW` | non-nil | 0–7 | 8 |
| `PdhGetRawCounterArrayW` | nil | 0 | 0 (size query only) |
| `PdhGetFormattedCounterArrayW` | non-nil | 0–24 | ≤ stated size |

A 1-byte allocation lives in a 16-byte tiny block, which is the same span class as the 16-byte `sync.WaitGroup`. The overrun therefore hit the WaitGroup in `Collection.Build`, which `cpu`/`system` allocate right next to their PDH collectors during the concurrent build.

## Changes

- Start the buffer empty and pass `unsafe.SliceData(buf)`, so the first call is the documented nil/size-0 size query. Every later call passes a buffer of the size PDH reported.
- Known counter data errors now skip the instance (`continue instances`) instead of `break`. Before, the loop fell through and re-processed the items of the previous instance under the current counter. With an empty buffer it would also panic at `&buf[0]`.

## Testing

- `go vet`, `golangci-lint run ./internal/pdh/...`: no issues
- `go test` for `internal/pdh`, `cmd/windows_exporter` and the cpu, memory, logical_disk, physical_disk, net, process, system and performancecounter collectors: pass
- No regression test added: whether the heap corruption crashes is not deterministic.

author: caioalexanderx
body:
## O que muda

Decisão do fundador (07/10): o cliente pode trocar a própria frente em Configurações. Até aqui só a equipe trocava (`PATCH /admin/clients/:cid/segment`).

Nova rota privada **`PATCH /companies/:id/segment`** (`src/routes/companySegment.js`, montada em `routes/private.js`, atrás de `requireAuth` + `requireCompanyAccess` e do limiter global de `/api/v1`).

- **Quem pode:** `req.companyRole` `owner` ou `admin` (mesma checagem de `birthday.js`, `creditLeads.js`, `customerConsent.js`). Membro comum → `403 SEGMENT_FORBIDDEN`.
- **Body:** `{ segment, extras?: ['os'] }`. `disable` no body é ignorado.
- **Resposta (igual à rota admin):** `{ segment, segment_source, vertical_active, flags: { matcon_enabled, otica_enabled, os_enabled, studio_enabled } }`.
- **Regras** (em `applySegment`, nova opção `replacePrevious`):
  - grava `segment_source = 'user'`;
  - ao trocar, desliga a flag própria da frente anterior (`otica_enabled` / `matcon_enabled`);
  - `os_enabled` é o extra: `extras: ['os']` liga, `extras: []` desliga, sem `extras` não mexe. Em Assistência a frente manda (fica ligada mesmo com `[]`);
  - sair do Studio desativa a vertical; entrar exige o plano (`409 STUDIO_PLAN_REQUIRED`).
- **Erros:** `400 SEGMENT_INVALID`, `400 EXTRAS_INVALID`, `403 SEGMENT_FORBIDDEN`, `404`, `409 STUDIO_PLAN_REQUIRED`, `409 VERTICAL_ACTIVE`.
- **Auditoria:** `audit_log` (migration 023) com a ação `segment_change_by_user`, só `user_id`, `company_id` e `{ from, to, extras }` — sem IP nem user-agent.
- **Multi-CNPJ:** a rota é por empresa (`:id`); nada global.
- **Sem migration.**

## Além do pedido

- `409 VERTICAL_ACTIVE`: empresa com outra vertical ativa (odonto, food...) não entra no Studio por esta rota — `applySegment` trocaria a vertical dela por `studio`. Trocar para as outras frentes continua permitido e não toca na vertical.
- A rota admin e o cadastro não mudam de comportamento: `replacePrevious` é `false` por padrão.

## Testes

`npx jest frenteDaEmpresa pdvSettings --maxWorkers=2` → 5 suítes, 110 testes, todos passando (28 novos em `__tests__/frenteDaEmpresa.peloCliente.test.js`). A suíte completa não foi rodada.

body:
Closes #727

## 무엇을 했나

10/12~16 라이선스 검증 스캔 전에 SBOM·고지 파일의 어긋난 곳을 맞추고, Dependabot #11(source-map-js)을 고쳤다. 제품 코드는 그대로다.

## 동작 원리

1. scrubadub(core 선택 설치 `bench-baselines`)의 전이 의존성 26개를 깨끗한 가상환경에 설치해 메타데이터·라이선스 파일에서 읽고, 생성기 밖 손 관리 절(부록 A-8)로 적었다. 생성기는 개발 도구로 pytest·ruff·httpx2만 따라가서 이 선택 설치를 보지 않는다.
2. 허용 목록 밖(python-stdnum LGPL-2.1-or-later, numpy·scipy 휠에 함께 실린 GCC 런타임 GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1, regex, tqdm, PSF-2.0 둘)은 부록 B에 사실을 적었다. 배포물에 안 들어가고, 우리 코드가 import하지 않고, 수정하지 않는다. **팀장 결정(2026-10-08): 이 선택 설치는 팀 방침(GPL 계열 금지)의 예외로 두고 근거를 SBOM에 남긴다.** 예외는 이 선택 설치에만 적용하고, 배포물·제품 코드 의존성에는 GPL 계열 금지를 그대로 지킨다.
3. 데스크톱 설치파일 0.2.4(main `97ed96f`, Flutter 3.44.6·Inno Setup 6.7.0)를 Releases `desktop-v0.2.4`로 올려서, SBOM 부록 A-7과 고지 파일의 기준 판·Flutter 판을 그 값으로 적었다.
4. 운영 웹 번들에 Vite가 넣는 작은 런타임 코드(모듈 미리 불러오기 폴리필, `vite:preloadError` 지연 로딩 오류 처리)가 있는데 고지 표에 없어서, Vite 8.1.5와 그 번들러 Rolldown 1.1.5(둘 다 MIT)를 THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES 웹 표와 라이선스 전문에 넣었다.
5. source-map-js는 `npm update source-map-js`로 lock만 1.2.2로 올렸다. jsdom(테스트)·postcss(빌드)가 쓰는 개발 의존성이라 빌드 결과물에 안 들어간다.

## 검증

| 항목 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| numpy·scipy 휠 동봉물 | 각 설치본 `LICENSE.txt`: OpenBLAS(BSD-3-Clause), LAPACK(BSD-3-Clause-Open-MPI), GCC runtime library(GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1). scipy·colorama 본문은 BSD 3조항(「Neither the name …」) |
| python-stdnum 라이선스 | 설치본 `python_stdnum-2.2.dist-info/licenses/COPYING` 「GNU LESSER GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 2.1」, `stdnum/__init__.py` 「version 2.1 … or (at your option) any later version」 |
| scrubadub 라이선스 | `gh api repos/LeapBeyond/scrubadub/license` → `Apache-2.0 LICENSE` |
| 우리 코드의 scrubadub 사용처 | `bench/evaluators/compare_open_source_tools.py` 130행 함수 안 `import scrubadub` 한 곳 |
| source-map-js | `npm ls source-map-js` → 1.2.2(css-tree, postcss deduped), `npm update` 출력 「found 0 vulnerabilities」 |
| 웹 테스트 | `npx vitest run` 186 passed |
| 웹 빌드 = 운영 | `vite build` 결과 4개 파일의 sha256(64자리 전체)이 운영 https://maskingtape-lilac.vercel.app 파일과 같음: `index-DK3jTOEw.js` a375f053…e07c, `index-DwhVU7J1.css` 509eeb67…c7e8, `pdf-CbtwFEtT.js` 4689370b…e811, `pdf.worker.min-CHFwMXne.mjs` 0613f414…8cb3. `index.html`은 줄바꿈만 다름(로컬 체크아웃 CRLF, 운영 LF) |

author: bdintakurti-nv
body:
On MediaTek SBSA watchdogs in action=1 mode, the sleep notifier parks the hardware during system sleep, but the watchdog-core keepalive timer can remain armed. Its SYS_TIMER interrupt can wake MT8901 from S3 even though the hardware watchdog is parked.

This change opts only that mode into the existing watchdog-core suspend hook, canceling the ping timer and work at PM prepare and restoring the worker on resume. action=0 remains unchanged because its WS0 heartbeat workaround needs separate resume-time accounting. The watchdog core's existing prepare-to-freeze rearm window is outside this PR's scope.

Validation: On MT8901 with action=1, early_enable=1, and a 10-second timeout, three 60-second deep S3 cycles with TAD wake resumed without an early SYS_TIMER wake or watchdog reset. The boot ID was unchanged.

Follow-up to #627.

author: jakestevens
body:
### Summary

Transformers Mistral sliding-window decode fails after reinplace rewrites its cache updates to `aten::index_put_`. The portable kernel rejects the valid index `-1` and requires values `[1, 2, 1, 8]` where the exported graph supplies `[2, 1, 8]`.

Accept indices in `[-size, size)` and normalize negative indices in both overwrite and accumulation paths. Allow omitted leading unit dimensions in the values tensor, using the index length to drive the existing copy loops. This requires no additional allocation or data expansion.

Depends on #23506 (`JakeStevens:fix/accumulating-index-put-inplace`). Review that first; the follow-up changes are in commit `95badb36fe`.

### Test plan

Compiled and ran the complete `op_index_put_test.cpp` against the portable kernel with a local CMake harness (`./build/fixed_index_put_test`): **57 passed, 2 existing dynamic-shape skips**. Added 33 regression cases covering int32/int64 indices, overwrite and accumulation, repeated index aliases, bounds, omitted unit dimensions, scalar updates, and incompatible shapes.

The corresponding repository tests can be run from a CMake build configured with `EXECUTORCH_BUILD_TESTS=ON`:

```bash
cmake --build cmake-out --target portable_kernels_test -j
cmake-out/kernels/test/portable_kernels_test --gtest_filter='*OpIndexPut*'
```

Relinked the local runtime with the changed kernel and ran tiny FP32 Mistral static sliding-window single-token decode exports generated with the planner fix from #23526. All **11 runtime outputs match default bit-for-bit**, including caches and repeated calls after restoring inputs. Both paths match eager PyTorch with maximum absolute error **5.96e-8**.

`lintrunner kernels/portable/cpu/op_index_put.cpp kernels/test/op_index_put_test.cpp` and the pre-commit checks pass.

Authored with assistance from OpenAI Codex.

author: colbymchenry
body:
## Summary

`codegraph_explore`'s Flow section could route a flow through an interface implementation the query never named, while leaving out the one it did name. The viewer's Flow strip uses the same path finder, so it did the same.

`walkCalls` in `src/graph/named-symbol-flow.ts` is a plain BFS. The first callee listed claimed each node (`parent.set`), and the bridge budget only limits unnamed hops; it never ranks one route against another. An interface method calls all of its implementations at the same depth. So when several of them call the next named symbol, whichever implementation the index listed first won.

Repro on current main (gin needs #2419's defined-type implementers, now merged):
- gin `mappingByPtr tryToSetValue setter.TrySet formSource.TrySet setByForm`: the Flow ran `setter.TrySet → headerSource.TrySet (binding/header.go:35) → setByForm`. The named `formSource.TrySet` (binding/form_mapping.go:75) calls `setByForm` just as directly.
- gin `tryToSetValue setter.TrySet multipartRequest.TrySet setByForm`: also went through `headerSource`.
- Struct implementations hit it too. prometheus `Engine.execEvalStmt Queryable.Querier fanout.Querier NewMergeQuerier` went through tsdb's `DB.Querier`.

## Change

- **Walk tie-break.** When another node at the same depth reaches a node again, the new route wins if it ends on fewer unnamed hops, or failing that, if it passes more named symbols. A tie keeps the first route, as before. A node's same-depth rivals are all expanded before the node itself is, so nothing has been reached through it yet when its route changes. The visit order, the visited set and the `NAMED_VISIT_CAP` bound are unchanged, since replacing a route never adds a node.
- **Deepest-end pick.** Each seed still keeps its deepest named end. Of two equally deep ends, it now keeps the one whose route passes more named symbols; before, it kept whichever was reached first. Without this, a query that names one implementation and two ends, one per implementation, still got the first-listed implementation's end.
- **Why fewer unnamed hops ranks first.** It keeps the tie-break from spending bridge budget a later hop needs. With the default budget of one, only a route node's streak can differ, so in practice the named count decides.

## Validation

Kit: gin, prometheus and etcd, each with three indexes: main 31c3328d, #2419's branch, and main 61f8b09c (with #2414, #2416 and #2419) re-indexed with this branch's build (wasm path). The change is query-time only, so both arms read the same index.

Query sets per repo:
- **targeted**: a caller of an interface method, the interface method, one of its implementations, and a callee that two or more implementations call (gin 6, prometheus 221, etcd 185).
- **random**: 600 random call chains over static and synthesized edges, naming both ends plus a random subset of the middle.

Results on main 61f8b09c. The other two indexes gave the same picture.

| | gin | prometheus | etcd |
|---|---|---|---|
| targeted: lead chain passes the named implementation, before → after | 2 → 6 of 6 | 76 → 215 of 221 | 77 → 184 of 185 |
| random: lead chains that changed | 13 / 600 | 20 / 600 | 25 / 600 |
| changed lead chains that changed length | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| changed lead chains with fewer named symbols | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| queries with identical `getCallees` lookups | 600 / 600 | 600 / 600 | 600 / 600 |

- Every changed lead chain kept its length and gained named symbols, and repeated runs gave identical results.
- The 7 targeted misses left are token resolution, and both arms give the same answer for them. Either the token matched several nodes that are all named (two `DB` types, two `sample` types), or the named implementation fell outside the six-candidates-per-token cap (`SDConfig.NewDiscoverer`, `Discovery.refresh`). The walk can't prefer what was never named.
- The walk change alone reaches 171 of 185 (etcd) and 211 of 221 (prometheus). The deepest-end pick brings these to 184 and 215.
- Timing: every query makes the same callee lookups. Totals per round were within −12% to +5% of main, which is this box's round-to-round noise (it ran at 100% CPU).
- Viewer, 3 chains (unreleased, behind `CODEGRAPH_UI=1`): the lead chain matches explore. A dropped alternative is usually a sub-run of the better lead chain, which the existing dedupe removes, or the same route rerouted at the same length. On etcd, 41 alternatives were replaced by equally long chains through more named symbols, for example a route through the unnamed `UnimplementedAuthServer` stub replaced by one through the named servers. I added no viewer-launch changelog entry because the strip is unreleased; say if you want one.

Explore spot-checks, before → after:
- gin `mappingByPtr … formSource.TrySet setByForm`: header.go:35 → form_mapping.go:75
- gin `… multipartRequest.TrySet setByForm`: header.go:35 → multipart_form_mapping.go:27 (`when len(files) == 0`)
- prometheus `Engine.execEvalStmt Queryable.Querier fanout.Querier NewMergeQuerier`: tsdb/db.go:2617 → storage/fanout.go:75
- etcd `Periodic.Run Compactable.Compact kv.Compact KVClient.Compact`: client/v3/retry.go:127 → client/v3/kv.go:197

## Tests

- New `__tests__/flow-named-implementation.test.ts` covers a Go fixture shaped like gin (with structs) and two TypeScript fixtures. Each one is asked twice, naming one implementation and then the other, so it fails whichever one the index lists first. It also covers the bridge when no implementation is named, and checks `codegraph_explore`'s Flow section end to end. On main's source 4 of 6 fail; with the fix all 6 pass.
- The explore-\*, flow-\*, ui-flow-\* and adaptive-explore suites (39 files, 472 tests) pass.
- Full suite on the rebased tree (box at 100% CPU): the parallel run failed 122 tests in 42 files, 117 of them timeouts. A serial rerun of those 42 files with 120 s timeouts left 9 failures in 6 files. `function-ref`'s #1820 case hits its own 60 s limit on main's source too. The other five files (`mcp-writer-lock`, `mcp-projectpath-lifecycle`, `mcp-initialize`, `mcp-staleness-banner`, `watcher`) pass when run on their own, 127 of 127.
- tsc is clean for `src/` and for the new test file.

## Overlap

- #2331 (open, LuaJIT FFI) edits the same `walkCalls` line: it adds `isTransportEdge(c.edge) ||` to the skip that also held `parent.has(c.node.id)`. Whichever PR lands second should keep the transport skip and drop `parent.has(…)`: `if (isTransportEdge(c.edge) || !FLOW_EDGE_KINDS.has(c.edge.kind)) continue;`. Its doc paragraph sits beside the new one in the same comment, so keep both.
