body:
## ⚠️ Apply the migration to production BEFORE merging
This adds a table, `platform_events` (migration `20261007090000_add_platform_events`). Merging deploys automatically, and until the table exists in production, switching a school off or on and saving provider settings will fail. Order: apply the migration to production, then merge. It is already applied to the local dev database.

## Summary
**Find a user** (`/owner/users`)
- Search school admins, teachers and parents by name, email or school; filter by role. Defaults to the newest accounts.
- Two support actions per account: **Send password link** (confirm first; refused for switched-off accounts) and **Change email** (reuses the existing dialog, now for any non-owner account).
- Platform-owner accounts are never listed or acted on. Both actions and the page check the caller is the platform owner themselves, not just the proxy.

**Audit log** (`/owner/audit`)
- One newest-first timeline, filter by category and date range, 50 per page.
- Combines existing records: school sign-ups, sign-in email changes (with who did it), price changes, free-access grants, deletion requests and decisions, announcements.
- Plus a new append-only table, `platform_events` (database trigger blocks UPDATE; RLS enabled), for what nothing else recorded: school switched off/on (only when the status really changes, in the same transaction), provider settings saved/removed (which provider only, never keys), password links sent (and whether the email went out).

Menu: "Find a user" and "Audit log" added to the owner sidebar. No "last sign-in" shown — it isn't recorded anywhere today.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test`: 339 pass (new: audit rules and paging, complimentary-note parsing, and guard tests that the owner pages/actions check the role, never touch owner accounts, and never log provider keys)
- [x] eslint clean; `tsc` clean except the existing `LayoutProps` error in `layout.tsx`
- [x] Local app as platform owner: search by name/school/no-match, confirm prompt and change-email dialog (cancelled, nothing sent), switched the demo school off and on via the real button and saw both entries, plus temporary rows for every other source (removed afterwards). Found and fixed a bug where deletion-request entries were missing.

author: caioalexanderx
body:
## O que muda

Decisão do fundador (07/10): o cliente troca a própria frente em Configurações › Políticas do Caixa.

**Depende do backend:** CaioAlexanderx/aura-backend — PR `feat/segment-pelo-cliente` (`PATCH /companies/:id/segment`). Mergear o backend antes.

- A linha **"Sua frente: X"** ganha uma seta (`testID="pdv-settings-frente-trocar"`, `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel="Mudar a frente da loja"`). Ao tocar, abrem os quadros das frentes e o extra "Ordem de Serviço", com a frente atual marcada.
- Botão **"Trocar para <Frente>"** (desabilitado enquanto a seleção é a atual) → confirmação inline ("Sua Aura passa a abrir como <Frente>. O que a frente anterior ligava fica desligado." + "Você vai para o Aura Studio." quando for Studio) → `PATCH /companies/:id/segment` com `{ segment, extras }`.
- Sucesso: toast, invalida `pdv-settings` e `first-steps`, grava `company.segment` / `vertical_active` no store, `refreshMe()` e, se a nova frente for Studio, vai para `/studio`.
- Erros: `409 STUDIO_PLAN_REQUIRED` → "Studio exige plano Negócio ou superior"; `403` → "Só o dono da conta muda a frente"; demais → mensagem genérica.
- **Essencial:** o quadro Personalizados não aparece (nada desabilitado). Abrir a grade revalida o `/auth/me` (plano stale no JWT).
- **Permissão:** só dono/admin da empresa (`company.member_role`) ou staff vê a seta; membro comum lê a linha sem seta.
- Sai o "Pra mudar, fale com a gente". Atalhos de configuração por flag e switches de staff ficam como estavam.
- **Multi-CNPJ:** a frente é da empresa ativa; o card continua escondido na visão consolidada.

## Arquivos

- `components/onboarding/FrenteOpcoes.tsx` (novo) — quadros + extra, extraídos de `FrenteSection` com os mesmos estilos e testIDs.
- `components/screens/configuracoes/FrenteDaLoja.tsx` (novo) — a linha, a seta, a grade e a troca.
- `components/screens/configuracoes/PdvSettingsCard.tsx` — usa `FrenteDaLoja`.
- `components/admin/FrenteSection.tsx` — usa `FrenteOpcoes`.
- `services/primeirosPassosApi.ts` — `frenteApi.trocar`.
- `constants/primeirosPassos.ts` — `STUDIO_PLAN_MSG`.

## Além do pedido

- A confirmação é inline, não modal: overlay fixo dentro do shell fica preso atrás da página no RNW.
- Mudar só o extra "Ordem de Serviço" (sem trocar a frente) também habilita o botão, com o rótulo "Salvar".
- Personalizados também some para empresa com outra vertical ativa (o backend responde `409 VERTICAL_ACTIVE`).

## Saída do Studio (commit 2)

Empresa no Studio não chega em `/configuracoes`. O mesmo controle (`FrenteDaLoja`, com paleta do Studio) entrou em `app/studio/(estudio)/configuracoes.tsx`, no card "Frente da loja", antes de "Equipe & acessos". Trocar de Studio para outra frente: confirmação "Sua Aura volta a abrir como <Frente>. Você sai do Aura Studio; seu catálogo e seus pedidos continuam guardados.", mesma rota, store gravado com `vertical_active` nulo antes do `router.replace("/(tabs)")` e de novo depois do `/auth/me` (não depende do `refreshMe`, que pula na janela de 3 s). Testes em `__tests__/studioConfigFrente.test.tsx` (6).

## Verificação

- `npx jest` (`--maxWorkers=2`): suítes da frente e a nova do Studio passando (13 + 6 novos). `studioCelularTelasEnxutas` tem 3 falhas em "Início" que já existem em `origin/main`. Suíte completa não rodada.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: 419 erros na branch e 419 em `origin/main`, medidos no mesmo estado; contagem por arquivo idêntica; nenhum erro nos arquivos novos.
- Não verificado: render real no navegador (desktop e 375 px).

author: trevorhansen
body:
SMT-LIB splits a solver's output in two: the **regular output channel** carries command responses, the **diagnostic channel** carries everything the solver says about itself. STP honours that for most of its statistics — every `{Pass}` counter and `Difficulty Initially:` go to `cerr`, which `:diagnostic-output-channel` redirects — but six places wrote to `cout`, where they interleave with the replies:

```
$ stp -s query.smt2
[4ms:10MB]input asserts and query: Node size is: 4
[1ms:10MB]After Sharing-aware Flattening: Node size is: 4
...
sat
(
(define-fun |x| () (_ BitVec 8) #xFD)
)
```

A client reading responses from the regular channel cannot do anything with those lines, and cannot tell them from a reply it does not recognise. Pointing `:diagnostic-output-channel` at a file did not help — the file got 13 lines and stdout kept the rest.

### The split ran through single statistics

Of the three difficulty lines `STP.cpp` prints, two were on `cerr` and one on `cout`:

| line | channel before |
|---|---|
| `STP.cpp:1121` `Difficulty Initially:` | `cerr` |
| `STP.cpp:1439` `Difficulty After Size reducing:` | **`cout`** |
| `STP.cpp:1629` `(3) Initial/Final Difficulty Score:` | `cerr` |

Likewise `CounterExample.cpp` printed `checking counterexample` to `cout` and, two lines later, `checking <the input>` to `cerr`.

### The six

- `STPMgr::ASTNodeStats` — the per-pass node sizes, the bulk of it
- `STP.cpp:1439` — the difficulty line above
- `CountersAndStats` — the `Number of times the function:` table
- `CounterExample.cpp:1809` — `checking counterexample`
- `AbstractionRefinement.cpp:741` — the remaining-read-axioms note
- `PrintSATModel` — which exists to dump a SAT assignment for debugging

### After

`stdout` under `-s` is byte-identical to `stdout` without it, and the statistics still appear — on stderr, and in the file when `:diagnostic-output-channel` names one, which now takes 118 lines where it took 13.

**Not addressed:** the SAT backend's own `c ...` lines. Those are CaDiCaL printing to stdout from inside the library, which STP turns on through `Cadical::setVerbosity` and cannot redirect from here.

### Checked

Over all 1247 files in `tests/query-files`, against a **configuration-matched** build of `538f4dba` (same `STATICCOMPILE`, `ENABLE_ASSERTIONS`, allocator and backends), four files differ and all four differ only in `:cpu-time`, `:peak-memory-mb` or `(get-info :version)`. No test reads any of these lines from stdout.

### Why I went looking

A fuzzer cannot enable `-s` while the statistics are mixed into the replies, so the whole diagnostic layer was unreachable to it. With the replies clean it is worth **+930 covered lines** over a 250-case corpus (62.69% → 63.63%) — and not only print statements: the difficulty scoring at `STP.cpp:1121` and `:1439`, and every pass's counters, are computed only under the flag.

New test `statistics-are-not-command-replies.smt2` holds stdout under `-s` to the replies and checks the statistics still arrive on the other channel; it fails on `538f4dba`.

author: bbingz
body:
## ELI5

If your Windows terminal is set to Git Bash but Orca cannot find Git Bash, Orca quietly opens Windows PowerShell instead. Agent launches still wrote their start command in Bash syntax, so PowerShell rejected it and the agent never started. A fresh OMP launch hit this every time. Orca now writes the start command for PowerShell in exactly that case.

## What Changed

**Before**, issue #22664 reported that starting OMP opened Windows PowerShell 5.1 and failed with this:

```
At line:117 char:43
+ printenv ORCA_OMP_FRESH_CONFIG >/dev/null && test -f "$ORCA_OMP_FRESH ...
The token '&&' is not a valid statement separator in this version.
```

**After**, the same launch types the PowerShell form of the guard, `if ("$env:ORCA_OMP_FRESH_CONFIG" -and (Test-Path ...)) { omp --config ... }`, and OMP starts.

**Mechanism.** Two places decide the shell, and they disagreed:
- The terminal spawn (`local-pty-launch-plan.ts` and the daemon's `shell-launch-plan.ts`) checks whether Git Bash exists. When the setting is `git-bash` and none is found, it spawns literal `powershell.exe`.
- Agent startup quoting (`resolveLocalWindowsAgentStartupShell`) looked only at the setting. It classified `git-bash` as POSIX and built POSIX commands, including the `printenv ... && test -f ... || printf ... >&2` guard for a fresh OMP launch.

`resolveLocalWindowsAgentStartupShell` now takes an optional Git Bash probe result. When the setting is exactly `git-bash` and the probe says it is missing, it returns PowerShell, which is the shell the spawn actually starts.
- **Main process** fresh launches pass `isGitBashAvailable()`, the same lookup the spawn uses. These are worktree create with an agent, runtime and CLI terminal creates, agent sessions and mobile launches.
- **Renderer** fresh launches pass `getProbedLocalGitBashAvailability()`. These are the new-tab launch, the new-workspace composer, folder workspaces and background sessions. The function reads the existing Windows terminal capability cache. It answers only in the desktop app, only after the local probe has run, and only when the launch targets this machine rather than a runtime host. Otherwise it returns "unknown". Each call site checks the host the launch actually goes to. New-tab and background launches use the worktree's owning runtime. The composer uses the selected repo's execution host, and folder workspaces use their target runtime.

**Unchanged:**
- An unknown probe keeps today's POSIX classification. A working Git Bash setup cannot flip to PowerShell because a probe has not run yet, or because a probe over a web client or runtime connection failed.
- `powershell.exe`, `pwsh.exe`, `cmd.exe`, `wsl.exe` and explicit `bash` paths classify as before. An unresolved bare `bash.exe` still spawns that bash, not PowerShell.
- SSH and non-Windows launches are untouched.
- Agent resumes are left alone. Open PR #19286 moves resume command building into the spawn itself.

## Why

The setup-script runner already handles this case. `worktree-runner-script.ts` gates its POSIX choice on the same Git Bash lookup, with the comment "the PTY resolves Git Bash independently and falls back to PowerShell when it is missing". Agent startup quoting never got the same gate. I considered three alternatives:
- Rewriting the command at spawn time cannot work for arbitrary agent commands and prompts.
- A guard that parses in both Bash and PowerShell 5.1 is not possible, because 5.1 has no `&&` or `||`.
- Changing the user's setting when Git Bash disappears would lose their choice if they reinstall it.

The reporter wrote that their default shell is `powershell.exe`. With that setting, both 1.4.206 and current `main` already build the PowerShell guard. The only path I found that sends the POSIX guard into Windows PowerShell 5.1 is the missing Git Bash fallback. That fallback hardcodes `powershell.exe` even when PowerShell 7 is installed, and it shows the user a PowerShell prompt. The "At line:117" in the report also fits: Orca appends the startup command after its PowerShell bootstrap script.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #22664

## Visual Proof

N/A. This changes the text Orca types into a terminal when it starts an agent, with no UI change. The before output is quoted above, and the after command is pinned by a test.

## Testing

- [ ] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

I did not run this on a Windows host. I tested on macOS only, with the Windows platform simulated in unit tests.

- `src/shared/windows-terminal-shell.test.ts`: covers missing Git Bash, PowerShell 5.1, pwsh, cmd, wsl and bash, plus remote and non-Windows launches.
- `src/shared/agent-startup-plan-inputs.test.ts`: builds a fresh OMP launch with `git-bash` configured and missing, and asserts the PowerShell guard with no `printenv`.
- `src/renderer/src/lib/windows-terminal-capabilities.test.ts`: covers the probe reader before the probe, after it, and with a runtime environment active.

The new shared tests fail on `main` and pass with this change.

- `vitest run` on the focused files plus the existing launch suites: 39 files, 1699 tests passed and 1 skipped. The suites cover runtime worktree startup, agent sessions, the runtime spec aggregator `orca-runtime.test.ts`, new-tab Windows quoting, composer state and folder workspaces.
- `tsc --noEmit -p config/tsconfig.node.json`: clean.
- `tsc --noEmit -p config/tsconfig.tc.web.json`: clean.
- `oxlint`, the code-quality and anti-slop oxlint configs, and `oxfmt --check` on the 14 changed files: clean.

## AI Disclosure

Implemented with Claude (Anthropic) as a coding agent. Reviewed by OpenAI Codex (`codex exec`, read-only).

## Review

Codex reviewed three rounds read-only. Its final answer was "No actionable findings."
- **Round 1, failed probe:** a failed probe is cached as "missing", which could flip a working Git Bash. Fixed. The renderer now trusts the probe only in the desktop app, where it is an in-process call to the main process. A web client or runtime host gets "unknown". A test covers the web client.
- **Round 1, daemon environment:** the long-lived terminal daemon resolves Git Bash from the environment it started with, which can differ from the main process. Accepted as a residual risk. They disagree only when Git Bash is found through PATH alone and PATH changed after the daemon started. Before this change the same split already existed in the other direction for every user without Git Bash. Removing it fully means building the command after the spawn picks a shell, which is what PR #19286 does for resumes.
- **Round 2, background routing:** background launches used the focused runtime instead of the worktree's owning runtime. Fixed. New-tab and background launches now look up the worktree's owner, and the composer checks the selected repo's execution host.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable, or this change follows `docs/reference/agent-skill-sharing-upstream-boundary.md` and copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments, or documentation.

## Notes

- **Cross-platform:** the new branch runs only for a local `win32` launch with `git-bash` configured. macOS and Linux return early as before.
- **SSH and remote:** SSH launches return before the gate. Runtime-environment launches get "unknown" from the renderer, so they keep today's behavior. The known residual risk is the daemon-environment case described under Review.
- **Mobile:** mobile launches are planned on the host in the main process, which now passes the host's own probe.
- **Backwards compatibility:** there is no wire or settings change. The new parameter is optional.
- **Performance:** `isGitBashAvailable()` checks a few candidate paths once per launch. The renderer reads an in-memory cache.
- **Security:** no new inputs, commands or permissions.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is small and focus

Continues #502, which was closed when the branch moved to `poc/bunny`. Earlier review comments are there.

# Changes

- Hosts on-demand pages as a Bunny Edge Script via Bunny's Astro adapter (lab release, pinned exactly); built files go to Bunny Storage.
- Replaces Workers Builds with a GitHub Actions deploy workflow (`voorhoede/bunny-edge-deploy`). A DatoCMS build trigger starts it when editors publish.
- Upgrades to Astro 7.
- Keeps Shiki out of the Edge Script to stay under Bunny's 10 MB limit.
- Updates the docs and records the decision in `docs/decision-log/2026-09-30-workers-to-bunny.md`.

**Variant:** `poc/bunny-full-edge` is one commit on top of this branch. It deploys the adapter's middleware build to a separate full edge site with edge storage replication, using a vendored adapter build and an unreleased `bunny-edge-deploy` branch.

# Trade-offs

- The adapter and `bunny-edge-deploy` are pinned to unreleased versions.
- `/x` and `/x/` both return 200; canonical tags cover SEO.
- Files other than HTML get a one-year immutable `Cache-Control`. Deploys purge the CDN, not browsers.

None yet.

1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill it in.

author: oblomov-dev
body:
Three review passes over the AI Studio (`ai/`) and the AI Pilot (`pilot/`) found a series of problems; each one was traced through the code before it was fixed. The full Chromium suite passes locally, and the new tests below pass as well.

**Both chats**
- Tool input is now parsed by the page every 150 ms (`followStream( )`). The SDK's `inputJson` re-parsed the input on every delta and ended the stream as soon as one delta was unparsable.
- Rows of a retried attempt are marked finished.
- Failed and stopped requests are counted in usage.
- Stop ends a tool that is still running.
- A 529 error says what to do.
- `search_samples` and `find_apps` rank partial matches.
- The log follows the conversation only while the reader is at its end.
- Safari IME composition is handled.
- New chat during a running tool is handled.
- A key error restores the message and its files.
- Long conversations now clear old tool results on the server (`context_management`, beta `context-management-2025-06-27`). This kicks in from 200,000 input tokens; the last ten tool uses are kept and each clear removes at least 60,000 tokens. Before, a Pilot working through a list ended with "the conversation has filled the model's context". The clearing happens on the server, so the history stays append-only and the thinking blocks stay valid. It happens late and in large steps because every clear costs the cache.

**AI Studio**
- Linter hints are shown as optional advice.
- A failed run is marked as failed.
- A JavaScript error while the app starts is reported as a failed roundtrip.
- Auto is not restored on the studio's page.
- Ctrl+Enter sends only.
- Numbered lists keep their numbers.

**AI Pilot**
- The bridge clears the paths the Pilot's request carried. Before, typed values were sent again later.
- What the reader typed but did not send goes with the Pilot's step and shows in "What Claude sees".
- `restart_app` waits for every tab, and stale parked steps are refused.
- An act whose event cannot be pressed is refused before anything is typed.
- Told-tracking happens per screen read, and dumps reach the model.
- A failed open puts the files back.
- The Run shortcut and opening a draft no longer restart every tab.
- On a phone the chat comes back; the tab strip is rebuilt only on change.

**AI Pilot, third pass** (the bug classes fixed in abap2UI5/mcp-server#48)
- **Stale screens:** an event is pressed only on the screen the model saw. Before, two `act a1` in one answer pressed NEXT and then the next screen's a1. A click of the reader's while the model was thinking, or during the pause before the press, did the same. Such an act is now refused with the screen as it is, and nothing is typed or pressed.
- **Screen size:** screens are fitted to the budget as mcp-server's `fitSnapshot` does: long values are cut and made read-only, then table rows are dropped from the end. Before, they were cut mid-JSON at 30,000 characters, so a 120 KB TextArea pushed out every action and the app's answer.
- **Message size:** the `<screen>` of one message holds 60,000 characters for all apps together. A dump is at most 2,000 characters and comes after the screen.
- **Unknown arguments:** a tool argument the tool does not take is refused. Before, `act { value, event }` pressed without the values. `row` and `max_rows` must be whole numbers, and `beside` a boolean.
- **Echoed arguments:** errors and chat rows repeat at most 80 characters of an argument.
- **Closed tabs:** a closed tab's operator is released (it held its mirror for the rest of the chat).

**Files**
- Text is decoded via BOM, then UTF-8, then Windows-1252.
- A docx text box is read once.
- xlsx row numbers are kept.
- `_xHHHH_` escapes are decoded.
- New limits: 20 MB per message, 400k characters of text.
- Empty files are refused.
- Pastes from Excel and Word stay text.
- Duplicate files are deduplicated.

**Tests and docs**
- New tests in `pilot.spec.js` and `ai.spec.js`. Three are for the third pass, and one checks the request shape for context clearing.
- Fixtures `textbox.docx` and `gaps.xlsx`.
- `AGENTS.md` updated.

**Follow-up after abap2UI5/mcp-server#48 merges:** re-vendor `src/vendor/agent/` (`appclient`, `snapshot`, `viewxml`). That brings in the client's own fixes: LRU sessions, queued acts, argument echo and linear text handling.

jtranq
body:
A funded intent that never sends a packet cannot use an ICS-20 timeout refund. The owner cancellation builder existed but the dapp gave users no way to call it after resuming a saved request.

Saved transfer and swap requests now offer cancellation while funded. The Gateway builds an owner-authorized transaction and the connected funding wallet signs it. Status polling reports cancellation only after canonical inclusion. Cancelled requests show a recovery result and let the user start again. The API also accepts an output index and rejects ambiguous multi-output intents. Gateway and browser regression tests and TypeScript checks pass.

body:
## 変更内容

ゲームの選択に「桜ガーデン」を追加しました。短い文章を打って水と花びらを集め、桜を育てて庭を作るゲームです。既存のタイピング・検定・サクラダファミリアの判定・記録・画面は変えていません。変更は次の2点だけです。
- 読み・ローマ字の行の寸法を測る処理を、共通部品 `romajiWrap.ts` に移しました。
- ゲームの一覧に1件追加しました。

- **練習**
  - 問題は `problems.json` の500文から1回5・10・20問（既定10）を出します。同じ練習の中で同じ問題は出さず、最近の問題や、同じ主語・同じ文末・同じカテゴリの文が続かないように選びます。
  - 判定は既存の RomajiMatcher に読みを渡すだけです。お手本は設定のローマ字の方式で表示し、別の打ち方も正解です。
  - 時間制限はありません。スペースでの開始は開始待ちのときだけで、練習中は庭のメニューを出しません。
- **ごほうび**：1問ごとに水1・花びら1。完成した問題の読みのかなの文字数が累計20文字になるごとに水1（端数は持ち越し、完成時に精算）。打鍵数・ミスは使いません。
- **育成**：苗木 → 若木 → つぼみ → 満開。最初の無料の木は水5・10・20、ほかは10・25・50。水やりは在庫と満開までの残りの小さい方までしか使いません。満開の木では「鑑賞する」になります。
- **お店**
  - 8種類の苗は、累計の完成問題数でお店に並びます。飾りは5種類です。
  - 不足のときは不足数を表示します。交換の確認を開くときに ID を1つ作るので、二度押しても交換は1回です。
- **庭**
  - 桜は3本まで植えられ、植える場所が埋まっているときは入れ替えます。
  - 飾りはマス目に置きます（場所を押す・ドラッグ・移動・片付け）。桜の根元とほかの飾りには重ねられません。
  - 3つの庭は累計150・350問で使えるようになります。庭の名前（20文字まで）と庭の画像の保存（背景と置いた物だけの PNG）があります。
- **図鑑・持ちもの**：満開の記録（8種類）、成長と所有数。
- **保存**
  - 記録は ID 付きの出来事の一覧として保存し、そこから状態を計算し直します（`src/core/garden/state.ts`）。そのため再送・再読み込み・別の端末との同期でも二重になりません。
  - 正しくない出来事（残高不足・重なりなど）は反映しないので、残高がマイナスになりません。
  - ゲストは localStorage に、ログイン利用者は新しい表 `garden_events` に保存します。保存・同期の表示は実際に成功したときだけ出します。
- **画像**
  - `scripts/garden_assets.py` で、素材シートを連結成分ごとに段階へ切り出します（隣の木を混ぜず、枝先も切りません）。根元の位置を求めて WebP にし、元の PNG は `assets/garden-source/`（配信対象外）に残しています。
  - references（確認用の画像）は取り込んでいません。
- **DB**：`20261011000000_garden_events.sql`（本人だけが追加・閲覧、変更・削除不可、種類・大きさ・日時の制約）。
- version 1.4.0、CHANGELOG・README・`docs/garden.md`・`docs/setup.md`（手順2の7）・`docs/security.md`・`docs/manual-checks.md`（15章）・`docs/screenshots/v1.4.0/` を更新しました。

## テスト

- typecheck・build：OK
- `npm test`：278件すべて成功（追加分：ごほうびと端数、二重付与の防止、成長の境界、交換、解放、配置と重なり、記録の合成、出題、画像の切り出しと接地、ゲストの保存）
- `npm run test:db`：167件成功（`garden_events` の RLS 16件を追加）
- `validate:questions`・`check:readings`：問題なし
- Playwright 全体：1回目の全体実行で失敗したのは、ゲームの一覧が1件という既存の確認だけでした（3端末分）。2件に直したうえで、関係する spec を再実行してすべて成功しています。
  - 追加した spec は `e2e/garden.spec.ts` と `e2e/garden-cloud.spec.ts`（アカウントの分離・別の端末・再送・表がない場合）です。
  - 画面の確認は 1368×912・1280×720・スマートフォン幅で行いました。

## 実機での確認が必要な点

`docs/manual-checks.md` の15章（Surface のタッチ操作・iPhone/iPad の Safari・画像の保存・本物の Supabase での同期）を参照してください。

body:
## Summary

Two Codex fixes in the daemon, both found during Windows verification runs.

- **A recovered pane no longer blocks the Codex cwd bind** (Fixes #1887). The cwd binder treated an untracked pane as a live Codex pane whenever its persisted `lastDetectedAgent` said `codex`. Recovery, a supervised restart and a promotion carry that field onto a fresh shell where nothing runs, so a recovered pane refused every new Codex in the same folder (`[codex] cwd bind refused … another live Codex pane shares its cwd`) until it was closed. Untracked panes now count only on boot-local evidence, their canonical identity (a fresh exact-routed hook, or this PTY's own screen). The persisted field is untouched; the resume pill and the #1840 heal still use it.
- **An empty Codex 0.158 composer is proven empty again** (Fixes #1890). 0.158 draws `← for agents · ? for shortcuts` under the footer, with an optional `⚠ 1 warning · f2 to view` badge (a narrow pane cuts the hint to `? for shortcut`). `codexComposerEmpty` filtered only 0.157's bare `? for shortcuts`, so `chat/messages` to any 0.158 pane answered `409 input-not-provably-empty`. The hint row is now matched by its known shapes; any other row under the footer still refuses.

## Changes

- `src/daemon/transcript/codexRolloutByCwd.ts`: `codexLiveFor(tracked, liveSlug)`, the pure rule.
- `src/daemon/index.ts`: `paneFacts` feeds it `canonicalIdentityFor(...)` (tracker, hook authority, `bridge.getLastAgent()`) instead of `lastDetectedAgent`.
- `src/daemon/transcript/deliverChatPrompt.ts`: `CODEX_SHORTCUT_HINT`.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/daemon/transcript/__tests__/codexRolloutByCwd.test.ts src/daemon/transcript/__tests__/deliverChatPrompt.test.ts`: 45/45 pass. The two new 0.158 composer tests fail on `main` (checked by swapping in the `main` file), and use rows captured from live native Windows `codex-cli 0.158.0` panes (#1780/#1800 verification runs).
- `npx vitest run src/daemon/transcript`: everything passes except `chatSkills.test.ts` (2, symlink `EPERM` on this box, known environment limit, untouched file).

## Not verified live

No live Codex was run: the owner's Codex workspace is deactivated, and copying credentials into a throwaway home was out of bounds for this run. Both fixes are platform-neutral logic, covered by the unit tests above. Not live-checked: the daemon wiring of `paneFacts` (a recovered pane next to a new Codex launch), and a `chat/messages` send to a live 0.158 pane.

Owner decision needed, no code here: #1891 (the same Codex thread resumed into two panes on Windows).

author: metaphorics
body: ## Summary The Core-differential suite pinned exactly one `bitcoind` digest — the Linux x86_64 artifact — so on macOS every live lane failed with `bitcoind sha256 mismatch`, and macOS couldn't run the reference binary at all. This makes the pin platform-aware: `core-compat.toml` now models a release artifact as `(target, archive, archive_sha256, bitcoind_sha256)`, keeps `x86_64-linux-gnu` as the canonical row (the fixture-capture identity, unchanged), and adds `arm64-apple-darwin` under `[[reference.release.platforms]]`. `reference_set.rs` parses the new schema into `ReleaseIdentity { canonical, platforms }`, exposes `artifact_for(target)` / `current_artifact()` for live-lane selection and `capture_bitcoind_sha256()` for fixture provenance (a Mac run still validates fixtures against the Linux binary), rejects duplicate targets, and fingerprints the whole tuple under the bumped `bitcoin-rs/reference-release/v2` domain — the new digest covers every artifact row, so platform pins can't drift silently. Two macOS transport quirks are fixed rather than tolerated: - `e2e/src/rpc.rs` `exchange()` writes nonblocking now: a blocked `send` may ignore `SO_SNDTIMEO` on macOS (best-effort per its man page), so the total deadline interleaves between calls. Verified: `send()` returned in ~1ms buffered instead of timing out, hiding a 2s overrun the test asserts against. - `scripts/` pick a tomllib-capable `python3` (system python3 is 3.9 on macOS) and replace `sha256sum --check --strict` (unsupported by macOS `/sbin/sha256sum`) with an exact-match gate. `install-bitcoind.sh` now reads the pinned archive + digest from the manifest for the host target instead of hardcoding the Linux tarball. ## Test results (macOS 26.5.2, arm64) - `cargo nextest run --workspace`: **2815 passed, 3 skipped** — was 22 `sha256 mismatch` failures. - Full e2e Core-differential suite green against the pinned darwin `bitcoind` (sync, reorg, restart, mining lanes). - Native feature lanes build: `rocksdb` (brew `libclang`), `fjall,zmq,kernel` (brew `boost`), `fjall,usdt`, and the `rocksdb,fjall,redb,kernel` full-node combo. - Runtime smoke: regtest node serves RPC and `generateblock`/`getblockcount` work on the full-node binary. Deliberately not done: `getmemoryinfo` still reports 0 RSS off-Linux (documented deviation, no mach FFI added), and `hardware_identity()` falls back to `unknown-cpu` — both are evidence-metadata only. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/425a27dc216a428ba7edca734f9e6fac Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/425a27dc216a428ba7edca734f9e6fac?variant=devin Requested by: @metaphorics --- ## Summary by cubic Makes the Core-differential suite run natively on macOS instead of failing every live lane with `bitcoind sha256 mismatch`, because only the Linux x86_64 artifact was pinned. The pin is now platform-aware, and the macOS transport and script portability quirks the lanes trip over are fixed. - `core-compat.toml` models each release artifact as `(target, archive, archive_sha256, bitcoind_sha256)`, keeping `x86_64-linux-gnu` as the canonical fixture-capture row and adding `arm64-apple-darwin`. - The reference-set parser rejects duplicate targets and fingerprints the whole artifact set under `bitcoin-rs/reference-release/v2`, so platform pins can't drift silently. - `resolve_reference_identity.py` is the single owner of host-platform artifact selection, used by `install-bitcoind.sh`, the fixture provisioner, and the installer cache test; it carries a fixed-shape manifest reader when tomllib is absent (Python 3.6–3.10) and, like the parser, fails closed on duplicate targets, duplicate keys, and unreadable escapes. Scripts use exact-match digest gates (falling back to `shasum -a 256`) and bash 3.2-compatible loops; the formal lane's interpreter probe requires tomllib because `check_models.py` imports it unconditionally. - The RPC exchange uses deadline-checked nonblocking writes and reads with EINTR retries, because both `SO_SNDTIMEO` and `SO_RCVTIMEO` are best-effort for blocked syscalls on macOS. - Genesis now applies before the RPC listener binds; a refused or unsettled connect aborts startup instead of serving RPC with no applied tip. The bootstrap is one owner shared by start_node and the sync tick, which logs and retries only a refused connect — a failed settlement closes chain admission and requests shutdown. Fixture provenance still validates against the canonical Linux binary. Written for commit f136005c7cef0acfa28dab860b8a2168fe9990a8. Summary will update on new commits.

body: The coverage e2e shards were spending most of their time on tests over a second. One of those costs was process startup, not the compiler. The four corpus tests took 20–37s each, and the same helper sits under a few hundred other e2e cases. Flags such as `-Xplugin` still spawn the CLI. The e2e suite is one process again. The four coverage shards and the twenty-two harness shards existed to reset a deadline the whole suite had outgrown. author: jonnycodes420
body:
THREAD-3: nothing that needs a human slips. WIRE-1 left two next steps missing and two decisions open.

**1. A donor email that needs a reply.** An email from a donor or funder in a connected mailbox, with no reply after one business day, opens a "Reply to [Name]: [subject]" step on their Thread. If they already have an open step, it opens a task instead. This runs on every mailbox sync, on an hourly tick, and from `POST /mailbox/run-replies`.

Each email is sorted by `mailKind` (shared/mailboxLog.js):
- **Automatic reply:** auto-reply headers, or an out-of-office subject.
- **Receipt:** a receipt, invoice, order or payment subject (never a Re: or Fwd:), or a receipts@, billing@ or payments@ sender.
- **Newsletter:** List-Unsubscribe, List-Id or bulk Precedence headers, or a no-reply or newsletter sender.
- **Personal:** everything else. Only these become steps.

A reply is an outbound email, or a call, meeting or email logged by a person, that was both written after the email and dated on or after its day. Only the last 14 days count.

**2. Event no-shows.** An event's no-shows open one task per event, "Missed you at [event]", from every place a guest is marked as a no-show. Each person with an email gets a "Missed you" draft in Drafts. Nothing is sent.

**3. Delete with an active plan (default, Jonathan to confirm).** Delete and bulk delete are refused while a plan is live: "[Name] has a $X monthly plan. Cancel it first, or archive them instead." Steward never cancels a Stripe plan as a side effect. Archive is new: it takes the person off the Donors list and Groups, and the plan keeps running.

**4. Next charge dates on the Calendar (default, Jonathan to confirm).** One line a day, "12 monthly gifts expected, $640", starting from Stripe's `current_period_end`. The line opens its rows. Failed charges and cards expiring this month show one by one.

**5. Small fixes.**
- The Agent can read monthly plans and documents. They are read only, and the schema guard stays green.
- The seeded plans' blank steps are fixed, and every plan the server sends out fills in any missing step sentence (`describedPlan`).
- Groups "Email this group" was walked and already works: it opens New Campaign with the group as the audience. I checked every other cross-screen link and none drops its target.

**Test** `tests/thread3-human.test.js` (16 checks). It went red with defects planted: with no plan check on delete and no plan normalisation, 5 failed. Adding imported history before the fix, 2 failed (the walk caught that defect). It passes with the fix. Battery: 113 of 113 suites.

**Map** 157 / 58 / 7 → 163 / 55 / 4. Walk: 14 of 14 at 1440 and 390, screenshots in `docs/thread-3/`.

**The seed changed** (the plan step sentences), so the prod demo needs a re-seed (NEEDS-JONATHAN).

## Summary

A Fusion computation copied an older request from its own worker into the current row evidence. The host then rejected the new output because that old request attested different observation inputs. Store inherited immutable references in the required `fields.input_evidence` array and keep the current request/outcome alone in computation row evidence. Judges and reports strictly validate and carry the input lineage; the full raw input remains in the durable model request and report context.

## Product impact

- Workers can analyze their own earlier retained evidence without presenting it as the receipt for the current call.
- Current receipt replay checks remain enforced. Missing `input_evidence` and malformed or extended reference objects are refused; no old-shape fallback is added.

- Added native broker regression checks acceptance of separated lineage and rejection of flattened or replayed old receipts. `ocamlc -stop-after parsing test/test_lane_addon_worker.ml` and `git diff --check` pass. Native execution was not performed.

body:
\`progress_redirect.cy.js\` failed on #677 with \`cy.wait() timed out waiting 5000ms for the 2nd request to the route: status\`.

\`cy.wait('@status')\` resolves when Cypress sends the stubbed reply. The page still has to \`await res.json()\` before it calls \`setTimeout(poll, 3000)\`. When \`cy.tick(3000)\` runs first, there is no timer to fire, the clock stays frozen, and the second poll never happens.

\`progress_patch_failure.cy.js\` already handles this by waiting for \`60%\` to render before ticking. \`setState\` and \`schedule()\` run in the same synchronous block, so once the building state is on screen the next poll is scheduled. This applies the same guard to both tests in the redirect spec.

author: hecisaza
body:
## Summary

- Let a running prompt-cache save finish before the next request cancels it: `scripts/config.sh` sets `TF_GLM_DISK_FENCE_MS` from a new `DISK_FENCE_MS` (default 15000).
- Patch 0142: log the outcome of prompt-cache saves and expose rank 0's counters in `/health` as `disk_cache_rank0`. The write/cancel policy is unchanged.
- Patch 0143: flush the round profiler's output so `TF_GLM_MULTI_PROFILE` reports appear while the server runs.
- Tests: a fixed tie rule for `test_cp_kv_gather_prompt[fp8]`, a byte-exact gather test, and multi-rank results sent over the multiprocessing queue as plain data.

## What this fixes

| Problem | Fix | Improvement (before → after) |
|---|---|---|
| Long cache save cancelled by the next request | `DISK_FENCE_MS=15000` in `config.sh` gives a running save 15 s before cancellation is requested; 0142 logs save outcomes | ~479k save cancelled on all 3 ranks → written on all 3 (5.85 GiB per rank in 3.1 s), fence wait 301 ms |
| Profiler silent until shutdown | 0143 flushes each `RoundProfile` report | on a `CP=0 PARALLEL=2` boot: 0 reports while running → 9 reports live during one request |
| fp8 near-tie test failure | Fixed 8-bf16-step tie rule, plus a byte-exact gather test | `test_cp_kv_gather_prompt[fp8]` failed → passes; gathered planes byte-exact for fp8, bf16 and fp4 |
| Multi-rank test crashes | Ranks send plain lists or `mp_wire` bytes instead of raw tensors | earlier suite with the gather-test changes only: 262 passed + 2 crashes → 264 passed, 0 failed; fp4 gather test failed 2 of 3 runs → passed 3 of 3; final branch, affected files: 43 passed, 0 failed |

## Problem

1. **Long prompt-cache saves are cancelled by the next request.** After a long prefill, the state is written to disk in the background. A ~479k-token state is about 6 GB per Spark and takes about 3.3 s to write. A request that needs the same cache rows fences the writer. With the engine's default grace of 0, the fence asks the running save to stop immediately, and nothing is logged. In testing, a 479,209-token prompt followed by a short request lost its saved state on all three ranks.
2. **The round profiler shows nothing until shutdown.** `RoundProfile` printed without flushing. The container has no TTY, so `TF_GLM_MULTI_PROFILE` reports only appeared when the server stopped. The profiler exists only with `PARALLEL` above 1.
3. **`test_cp_kv_gather_prompt[fp8]` fails on a near tie.** The test compared one bf16 logits row by argmax. The reference's top two values were four bf16 steps apart (2.40625 vs 2.34375). On the gathered path both were 2.375, so argmax picked the other token.
4. **Multi-rank CPU tests crash intermittently.** A rank puts tensors on a queue and exits. The parent then reads them through a file descriptor that the exited process no longer serves, which raises `EOFError` or `FileNotFoundError`.

## Changes

- **`scripts/config.sh`:** `DISK_FENCE_MS` (default 15000) sets `TF_GLM_DISK_FENCE_MS` when `DISK_CACHE=1`.
  - A conflicting request now waits up to that long for a running save.
  - After the grace, the fence asks the save to stop and keeps waiting for the writer. Cancellation is cooperative and checked between pieces, so 15 s is not a hard bound.
  - A save still queued behind the conflicting request is dropped as before. Changing that needs an engine change.
- **`patches/0142-glm-full-pcache-diagnostics.patch`:**
  - Logs a `pcache:` line when a save is queued, written, declined because the writer queue is full, dropped from the queue by a fence, or cancelled. It also logs how long a fence waited.
  - A repeat of a save already queued is only counted (`pending_declines_total`). One already on disk is skipped without a line.
  - Rank 0's counters and the configured grace appear in `/health` as `disk_cache_rank0`.
- **`patches/0143-glm-full-profile-flush.patch`:** `RoundProfile` flushes each report.
- **`tests/cpu/test_cp_kv_gather.py`:**
  - For fp8, the check keeps the 0.12 × scale band. It accepts a different best token only if that token's reference value is within 8 bf16 steps of the maximum. The margin is fixed and doesn't depend on the measured error.
  - A negative test checks that a wrong winner only this rule can catch is rejected, and so is NaN.
  - Ranks send results as plain lists.
- **`tests/cpu/test_cp_kvg_strong.py` (new):** checks the gathered latent and rotary cache planes byte for byte against what each rank wrote, for fp8, bf16 and fp4. It also compares six rows of logits under the same tie rule.
- **`tests/cpu/mp_wire.py` (new):** `pack`/`unpack` send tensors as (dtype, shape, bytes).
  - `test_full_forward.py` uses it for its three multi-rank tests.
  - `test_kvx.py` reuses one of those rank functions and unpacks its results.
- **`tests/cpu/test_mp_wire.py` (new):**
  - A bit-exact round trip, including signed zeros, infinities and NaN payloads in f32 and bf16.
  - Packed results survive the rank exiting first.
  - Raw tensors reproduce the crash.
- **README, CHANGELOG:** the new setting, the save logs and counters, patches 0142 and 0143, and the profiler's `PARALLEL` requirement.

## Testing

CPU tests used the v0.6.0 image with 0142 and 0143 applied by `patch -p0`, as `prepare.sh` does.

| run | result |
|---|---|
| Full CPU suite on this branch, before `test_mp_wire.py` was added | 263 passed, 1 failed, 10 skipped. The failure was `test_kvx.py` not yet unpacking the shared rank function; fixed in this branch. |
| `test_kvx.py`, `test_full_forward.py`, `test_mp_wire.py` after that fix | 43 passed, 0 failed |
| `test_mp_wire.py` with `-rA` | 4 passed, none skipped, so the raw-tensor case reproduced the crash |
| Full suite before this branch, with only the `test_cp_kv_gather.py` and `test_cp_kvg_strong.py` changes | 264 passed, 0 failed; 262 passed with 2 multiprocessing crashes before them. `test_full_forward.py` still had the queue race in that run; it didn't trigger. |

On three DGX Sparks, with the default configuration plus `DISK_FENCE_MS=15000`:

| check | v0.6.0 | with 0142 + 0143 |
|---|---|---|
| ~479k save, short request queued behind it | cancelled on all three ranks (grace 0) | written: 5.85 GiB in 3.1 s per rank; the request waited 301 ms; nothing cancelled |
| ~479k reload after a restart, request total | 4.9 s (479,144 tokens) | 4.8 s (479,157 tokens), answer correct |
| decode, prose, tok/s | 29.6-30.0 | 28.55, 29.78, 29.80 |
| decode, code, tok/s | 41.4-41.6 | 40.76, 41.46, 41.47 |
| `TF_GLM_MULTI_PROFILE` on a `CP=0 PARALLEL=2` boot | reports only at shutdown | 9 reports live during one request |

- **Decode protocol:** one stream, 512 tokens, thinking off, three runs per prompt type, the same protocol as the v0.6.0 numbers.
- **First decode run:** the first run of each kind was the first such request after the boot. Runs 2 and 3 fall within the v0.6.0 range.
- **Decode path:** neither patch touches it.
- **Earlier grace-15 s run:** an earlier run with 0142's logging and a 15 s grace gave the same result. It wrote a 479,214-token state, 5.85 GiB in 3.3 s, and the next request waited 163-180 ms.

## Notes

- **New image:** 0142 and 0143 change the patches hash, so the image needs a rebuild or a new prebuilt tag. `IMAGE_TAG` and `IMAGE_DIGEST` in `config.sh` still point at `v0.6.0-4f3223245926`. As with any patch change, every node's prompt cache starts empty on the first start of the new image.
- **Same queue pattern elsewhere:** `test_kvx.py`'s tensor-parallel test, `test_cp_raw_q.py` and `test_cp_prefill_fast.py` still put raw tensors on a queue from a rank that then exits. They are unchanged here and could adopt `mp_wire` later. The other multi-process tests already send bytes, lists or numpy arrays.
- **CPU tests:** they run on CPU fakes. The byte-exact gather test does not cover the full GPU/NCCL path.

author: mrogan
body:
The first live run of task 16 (work item 1001) fixed a redirect loop on `/departments/:department`: the department's address now redirects to `/products?department=:slug`. The journeys gate then failed the fix with `missing-alt@/departments/:department`, a defect the fix uncovered rather than caused. Two faults in the crawler made it look like a regression:

- It filed a page under the address it asked for, not where it landed after redirects. The images it found were `/products`' own.
- It recorded every check on every route it knew as passed, whether or not a page was opened there. So on `main`, behind the loop, that check counted as a pass.

## What changes

- **Each page is judged at its own address.** An exchange records where it landed (`senses/http.ts`). A link that redirects is not opened in the browser; where it lands is crawled as a link of its own (`crawler/crawl.ts`).
- **Request checks and page checks are judged in different places.**
  - About the request, on the route asked for: `redirect-loop`, `server-error`, `slow-response`, `not-cached` and `leaks-detail`.
  - About the page (`OF_A_PAGE`): `missing-header`, `browser-error`, `missing-alt`, `low-contrast`, `unlabelled-field`, `broken-link` and `broken-image`.
  - Links and images are judged on the page that holds them, as before.
- **A route where no page opened gives trouble, not a pass.** That is a route that loops or answers 4xx/5xx (`crawler/judge.ts`). A route where no page can be has no page checks at all: an asset, a non-HTML answer, or a redirect to a page elsewhere (`crawler/index.ts`).
- **The journeys gate is unchanged.** A check absent on the base that fails on the change is still a regression, so a newly added check cannot pass unexamined.

## Effect on the live senses

Trouble is only logged, never a signal, so triage, the scoreboard and the console never see it. Each looping or 404 route now logs seven "could not tell" warnings per run. A ticket open on a route that becomes a redirect stops being observed there, rather than passing.

## Tests

- **Browser:**
  - A redirect to a page that fails `missing-alt` is filed under the landed route.
  - A loop gives trouble on every page check.
  - The case from the run compares with no regressions: the base with the loop against the change with the redirect. `missing-alt@/products` is unchanged and `redirect-loop` is fixed.
- **Gate:**
  - The same case, and the case where the base could not tell.
  - A check absent on the base that fails twice on the change still fails the gate.

The new browser tests fail on the old crawler. `make check` passes.

## Also

`BACKLOG.md` gains an optional entry, a blocker work item for a defect a fix uncovers. It is worth building only if a change makes reachable a page that `main` cannot reach at all.

## Rollout, for PR #17 in the app

1. The App pins the new `factory-browser` image.
2. The app's `gates.yml` moves to a factory commit at or after that pin.
3. PR #17 is brought up to date with the app's `main`. Re-running the old check would keep the old pin.

author: bryancassell
body:
Closes #245.

## Why
A test release is signed with BlueCard's release key and a debug build with the machine's debug key, but both used `io.github.bryancassell.bluecard`. Android won't update an app from an APK signed with another key. So running the debug app on a phone with a test release meant uninstalling the release and its data, and the same the other way round.

## What changes
- **Debug application ID.** `applicationIdSuffix = ".debug"` makes debug builds `io.github.bryancassell.bluecard.debug`. The namespace and Kotlin packages don't change.
- **Debug launcher name and icon.** `src/debug/res/values` names debug builds "BlueCard Debug", and makes their icon orange (#BF360C) in place of the blue. That covers both the background and the card's lines, which now take the background's color in both builds. Launchers cut the name to "BlueCard De…", so the color is what tells the icons apart. The color also sets the splash screen's icon background. `app_name` is now marked untranslatable, so a future translation can't replace the debug name.
- **Report sharing.** No code change: the manifest's FileProvider authority (`${applicationId}.reports`) and `PdfReportRepository.fileProviderAuthority` both already follow the ID. `PdfReportRepositoryTest` now expects `io.github.bryancassell.bluecard.debug.reports`, since local tests run against the debug build. That also catches the suffix being removed. The made-up share URIs in two screen tests now use the neutral `content://reports/` that the test fake uses, since the screens never read them.
- **`docs/toolchain.md`.**
  - The three backup-check commands now use the debug ID.
  - The four release-build commands keep the release ID. Step 1 of "Checking a release build" no longer says a debug install shares the release's ID.
  - The `installDebug` row gives the debug app's ID and links to `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
  - The device-to-device check names the package to pass to `test_d2d.sh`.
- **`ARCHITECTURE.md`.** Records the decision under Debug builds and in the Decisions table. It also gives the rule for new code: a name that must be unique on the phone, such as a provider authority, is built from the application ID. Its one use of the ID is the package layout, which is the Kotlin package, so it stays.

## Testing
- `./gradlew build` passes.
- `connectedDebugAndroidTest` passes (`PdfDocumentWriterTest`, 2 tests) on a Pixel 10 emulator, API 37.
- `aapt2` on the APKs:
  - debug: `io.github.bryancassell.bluecard.debug`, labeled "BlueCard Debug", authority `io.github.bryancassell.bluecard.debug.reports`
  - release: `io.github.bryancassell.bluecard`, labeled "BlueCard", authority `io.github.bryancassell.bluecard.reports`
- On the emulator, a release APK signed with a throwaway key stood in for a test release:
  - It and the debug APK both installed and reinstalled (`install -r`) without replacing each other.
  - Each kept its own profile and progress.
  - In both builds, Save report wrote the PDF to Downloads, and Share report opened the Sharesheet with the PDF. Print preview showed that build's scout. No FileProvider or permission errors.
- On the emulator, the debug icon's background and card lines measure exactly #BF360C, both in the drawer and on the splash screen. The release icon's measure #003F87, as before.
- I ran the backup check in `docs/toolchain.md`, with its new `.debug` commands, against the debug build:
  - Backup, uninstall, reinstall and restore succeeded.
  - Only the DataStore file and the database files were restored, and the data came back.
  - The release app's data was untouched.

## Notes
- **Phones with an old debug install.** A phone with a debug build from before this change still has it under the old ID. Uninstall it before installing a test release. To keep its data, export it from that app and import it into the new debug build first.
- **Themed icons.** With themed icons on (Android 13+), both apps use the same monochrome icon, so only the name tells them apart.

author: drewbearly
body:
### Description

Use the shared Intel footer across Docusaurus and Sphinx. Docusaurus fetches and renders the shared footer after hydration; Sphinx resolves the include from the deployed site/base path, so local and PR previews do not depend on a production cross-origin fetch.

Configure Intel WAP for the Robotics site (`profile-microsite`, `us-en`, `dev-robotics-intel`, `prod`). Docusaurus sets SPA mode for client-side navigation; Sphinx pages use full-page navigation. The shared bootstrap preserves Google Analytics and queues it and the optional performance script behind Analytics consent. Kapa chat loads through the Functional queue; its fallback button appears only when OneTrust/Optanon preferences can be opened. Generated redirect pages retain their own bootstrap and privacy links, while the shared footer avoids duplicating the Intel corporate footer's links. The storage categories and functional impacts are documented in `docs/common-includes/README.md`.

### Any Newly Introduced Dependencies

No new npm or Python packages.

### How Has This Been Tested?

- Sphinx and Docusaurus production builds passed; generated HTML was checked for the bootstrap across 289 pages.
- JavaScript syntax and focused consent-queue checks passed. Synthetic browser checks confirmed the fallback stays hidden without a preferences opener, appears and opens preferences with a mocked opener, and is replaced by the real Kapa launcher when the Functional callback is invoked.
- Ran the website regression script from `aherrold/website_vulns` against the built site without merging that branch: 21/21 viewport checks passed, along with hydration, route and client-navigation checks. That runner blocks external assets.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Live OneTrust grant/reject/revoke behavior, vendor-managed cookies and tags, WAP section provisioning, and Adobe CJA ingestion have not been verified. The WAP/Adobe team should validate those before release. The WAP script loads before consent to manage preferences; the site-controlled GA, performance and Kapa loaders are consent-queued.

- [x] I agree to use the APACHE-2.0 license for my code changes.
- [x] I have not introduced any 3rd party components incompatible with APACHE-2.0.
- [x] I have not included any company confidential information, trade secret, password or security token.

body:
On 7 Oct JML services asked a customer for her email "and I'll send the quotation over"; she sent it as `Fielding.natalie@` / `Yahoo` / `. co . uk`, and none of the three looked like an address on its own.

**Changes (pre-award only; post-award unchanged)**
- Each new message is also checked joined with the sender's last 3 messages in the thread from the past hour, for email addresses and mobiles.
- New single-message email detection: an @ touching a word, spelled-out addresses (`at yahoo dot co dot uk`, `(at)`), mail provider names (gmail, yahoo, hotmail, icloud, btinternet…; not outlook/live/sky, which are ordinary words), spaced or spelled endings (`. co . uk`, `dot com`), and asking for or offering an email (`your email`, `email me`).
- Refusals keep the existing `email_or_link` / `phone` flags, so standing, recording and the 30-day moderation hold behave as before.

**Replay:** all 130 stored pre-award messages run through the old and new rules: 4 newly refused, all from the JML thread above, so no false positives in that set.

Tests: 3 new cases in messageText.test.ts; full suite passes.

## What and why
Officers can add, edit and remove anyone’s alts, and make an alt their main, on the officer roster. Alt rows sit below their member. Main editing keeps rank controls; alt forms omit them. Confirmations explain what changes, and errors remain visible.

No API, auth, database or deployment changes.

## How to verify
Preview: https://bureaucracy-forever-n4vcghatj-roberts-projects-f78421c0.vercel.app (successful deployment for this PR’s commit; retrieved from GitHub’s deployment record because Vercel has not posted a PR comment). Previews require Vercel login; Discord login does not work on their changing addresses. On staging with an officer login:

author: theatrus
body:
## Summary

A Target Scheduler project became a Planning plan once, at its first listing. Changes made in N.I.N.A. after that never reached the plan, so the plan drifted from its rows, and activating it would have undone those changes. On the reporting server, Elephant Trunk's plan asked for 150 frames per filter where Target Scheduler had been raised to 400.

An imported plan now follows its project until someone changes it in Planning or activates it.

- **Meta schema 26: `draft_import`.** (#753 took schema 25 on main, so this is 26.)
  - It records the source project a plan's drafts came from, and the revisions the import saved: the framing's layout revision and the plan's revision.
  - A listing that makes both drafts records them.
  - The upgrade marks plans an earlier build imported: both drafts at revision 1, saved in the same millisecond, one source project, and no activation. A plan made in Planning saves its framing and plan at different times, so it isn't marked.
  - `retire` deletes the row.
- **Following.**
  - A listing reads a marked plan's project again while its drafts are still the import's and no activation exists.
  - Each draft saves under the revision it had, so a save made in Planning in between wins, and the plan stops following.
  - The plan keeps its objective and contribution ids filter by filter.
  - The framing keeps the survey, view width and shown rigs the person chose. A view change isn't an edit, because following compares the layout revision.
  - A draft that reads the same isn't saved again.
- **Warnings** from a plan read again aren't repeated on every listing.
- **Docs:** `docs/DIRECTOR.md` describes the new rule, and the release notes say what users get.

## Checked on real data

I copied the reporting server's planning store and three of its rig databases (read-only SQLite backups) and opened them with this build.

- The upgrade marked all 75 imported plans.
- The first listing brought 30 plans in line with their projects:
  - the raised frame counts (Elephant Trunk 150 → 400, Sh2 86 100 → 300, Teddy Bear and Snapshot);
  - each template's Moon settings, which the older import left out;
  - the project's priority on every objective, which the older import ranked alphabetically.

author: rishigoswami-code
body:
Stacked on #108 (which is stacked on #107 and #106) — until those merge, this PR's diff also shows their commits. The four commits that belong here start at "Invitations: the candidate can accept or decline".

## Invitations

- **Accept / decline** — a company's invitation asks for an answer before it offers Start. Declining asks once more, takes an optional reason, and closes the invitation; a declined one can't be started. The company sees "Declined" in the pipeline with the reason, and "accepted" with the date.
- **Invitation email** — inviting a candidate mails them a link to their assessments page and says which address to sign in with. The invite form reports what actually happened to the email, and the candidate page shows whether one was sent. The link is not a one-time token: the invitation belongs to whoever signs in with the invited address.

## Notifications

The bell shows an invitation waiting for an answer, a due date within three days or passed, and a report that is ready or failed. Nothing is stored as a notification: each is worked out from the candidate's records when the bell is read, so it disappears once the thing it is about is dealt with. Read and dismissed are kept on the server. In-app only — no email is sent for a deadline or a report.

## Dashboard setup

- **Environment check** — opens the camera and shows the picture, opens the microphone and shows the level it hears, and asks the browser for each thing the workspace uses. A failure says what to do about it. Passing all three ticks the step on the dashboard. What is saved is the browser's own report, not something the server measured.
- **Practice run** — opens the real workspace on a small task with one bug and a test that catches it. There is no session behind it, so nothing is recorded, timed or submitted; only that one was opened is kept. The AI assistant is off in a practice run, and the brief says so.

## Settings

The invitation email needs `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM` and `CANDIDATE_PORTAL_URL` on the company portal. Without them the invitation is still created and the form says no email was sent.

## Migration

`0019_invitations_and_setup.sql` — additive: answer and email columns on `assessments`, environment-check columns on `candidate_users`, and the tables `practice_runs` and `candidate_notification_state`. `assessments.status` and `candidate_applications.stage` gain the value `declined`. Already applied to the shared database.

## Checked

- `node src/lib/notifications/derive.check.ts`, `node src/lib/environment-checks.check.ts`, and `node src/lib/ide/practice-task.check.ts` (the last runs the practice task on real Python: it fails as given and passes once fixed).
- In the browser against the shared database: accepting an invitation, declining one with a reason, the bell's content and read state, the environment check (a refused permission, then a pass), opening a practice run, and the dashboard's setup card and practice counter.

## Not checked

- The company portal's view of a declined or accepted invitation was not opened in a browser. It passes a typecheck, and the rows it reads were confirmed in the database.
- The invitation email was not sent, even to a stand-in server. The message is built by a pure function and sent through the mailer the portal already uses for team invites.
- The environment check ran on stand-in devices, not a real camera or microphone.

author: mrogan
body:
In the first live run of task 16, the journeys gate failed work item 1001's fix on a defect the fix had uncovered rather than caused. The work went back to the coder, which rightly changed nothing, twice. The line counted each as a failed step and held the work item with cause `failures`. That hold's answers are "run the coder again" or "close", and the coder's reason was recorded nowhere Martin could read it.

## What changes

- **The coder's result** (`agents/coder.ts`) can be `{unchanged: why}` (up to 200 characters) as well as `{title, note}`. The prompt says when: in a returned round, if the failure is not the change's doing, or the change already does what was asked; in a first round, if the code already meets every criterion.
  - No patch and no reason is still a failed step.
  - So is `unchanged` with a patch.
- **After a return, "unchanged" is an outcome, not a failure** (`unchangedHold`, `machine.ts`). The work item holds where the work came back from, under that cause: `gates` or `review`. The hold's reason carries the coder's words. Martin's answer means what `ANSWERS` says for that cause.
- **In a first round, it holds with a new cause, `nothing-to-fix`.** Approving closes the work item, as Martin agrees with the coder. Answering sends the spec back to the planner, told the coder's reason and Martin's words. Rejecting closes it.
- **`hold.started` moves to v3**, for the new cause, with a pass-through upcaster as `action.refused` v2 had. The samples and the console's fixture are regenerated, with only their version numbers changed.
- **Approving a `review` hold that followed a return** now clears that return, so the describer runs rather than the coder again.

The console needs no change: its card for a `gates` or `nothing-to-fix` hold shows the evidence and the hold's reason.

## Tests

- **`machine.test.ts`:** each hold, and every answer to it, as event lists.
- **`line.test.ts`:**
  - 1001's case: the gates fail, the coder hands back `unchanged`, and the work item holds as `gates` with the reason and no failure counted. Martin's answer sends the work back with his words, and the next round pushes.
  - A first round that finds nothing holds as `nothing-to-fix`, and the answer re-plans.
  - A contradictory result is counted as a failure.
- The coder's schema and prompt, and `hold.started` v3's upcast and validation.

`make check` passes.

## Not changed

Approving a `gates` hold still sends the work back to the coder, as `ANSWERS.gates` says. After an "unchanged", answering or rejecting are the useful choices. `SPECIFICATION.md` needs no change. Its Build row could mention "or a reason why no change is needed, which holds for a human", if Martin wants it stated.

author: saladday
body: Fixes the `native / platform (windows-amd64)` failure on #515 and #516. R1 made Codex unavailable on Windows, because the model-catalog probe needs Unix process groups, so the Windows onboarding smoke (which installs Codex) never saw its Harness connect. The probe is needed only for `low` and `high`. Protocol `medium` is the default text amount: a model with verbosity support applies the `model_verbosity` override, and Codex ignores it for any other model. So: - the Codex adapter skips the catalog probe for `medium` on every platform, and Codex is available again on Windows, declaring `TextVerbosity` unsupported; - Core requires `text_verbosity` only for an explicit non-`medium` verbosity, instead of whenever the profile supports it; - the self-hosted platform table lists Codex as supported on Windows again (en + zh). Checks: Codex adapter tests, Core `execution`, integration `TestExecutionRejectsRuntimeMissingCapabilityBeforeClaim` (now with an explicit `high` verbosity), darwin and windows daemon builds, `make check-names check-docs check-ci`. --- Need help on this PR? author: leekt
body:
Outcome: a portal signer can prove control of its credential and receive a
short-lived same-origin session cookie bound to that signer.

  POST   /portal/sessions/challenge {signer_id?}                  -> {nonce, expires_at, message?}
  POST   /portal/sessions           {signer_id, nonce, signature} -> {signer_id, expires_at} + Set-Cookie
  DELETE /portal/sessions                                         -> {} + cleared cookie

Owner: `session.rs`. ECDSA signers sign an ERC-4361 message the relay builds
itself (domain = issuer authority, URI = issuer, Chain ID 421614 because
ERC-4361 requires one, the nonce, and the challenge's own issue/expiry
times), recovered over its EIP-191 hash only. WebAuthn and P-256 signers sign
the 32 nonce bytes through the existing grant root verifier (rpId = issuer
host, origin = issuer, UP+UV, webauthn.get, challenge = nonce). Cookie:
`oaath_portal_session=<opaque>; Max-Age=1800; Path=/portal; HttpOnly; Secure;
SameSite=Strict`; only its SHA-256 is stored.

State: challenge issued -> consumed (one sign-in) | expired (5 min);
session active -> expired (30 min) | signed out. A failed proof consumes
nothing; a consumed, expired, or unknown nonce never authorizes. Records
persist in memory and PostgreSQL (oaath_portal_challenge_v1,
oaath_portal_session_v1); schema v10 is recreated, not migrated.

Proof: SIWE success with the exact message and cookie; another key, another
domain, another URI, the raw nonce, replay, unknown and expired nonces
refused; passkey success and wrong challenge/origin/rpId refused; sign-out
and expiry end only that session; a PostgreSQL restart keeps sessions and
refuses consumed nonces.

Limits: nothing requires a session yet; the follow-up PR gates per-signer
portal routes, signs in from the portal, and makes the id_token claim true.

- `releases/latest/download/cbom.cyclonedx.json`, uploaded before the draft flag comes off, so `releases/latest` never lacks it
- `05b-cbom.cyclonedx.json` inside the signed evidence bundle

It lists each algorithm the package offers (ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87, ML-KEM-768, ML-KEM-1024, SLH-DSA-SHA2-192s, HKDF-SHA-512, HMAC-SHA-256, SHA-256), the four the native backend runs only to probe OpenSSL, and the classical ECDSA of the npm registry and Sigstore. Each carries its OID, NIST category, purpose, protocol context, sizes per field in bits, and the file and line where the source uses it.

## Why declared, not scanned

kxco-pq-scan reads the lock file, which cannot show parameter sets, HKDF, HMAC or the key identifier hash. So the inventory is declared in `scripts/build-cbom.mjs` and reconciled against `src/` on every build. `npm test` and the evidence build both fail if the source binds an algorithm the CBOM does not declare, or if a declared use has gone.

That check caught the 1.9.0 change while this was being ported: release signing moved off `mlDsa.sign`, and the build refused until the declaration was updated. ML-DSA-87 is now declared as the default for new keys and as the release signer once `KXCO_RELEASE_SEED_87` is configured (kid `d35341d56b82c4bf`, checked against `release-signing-key-87.pub.hex`). ML-DSA-65 is declared for existing keys and as the release signer until then.

## Documents

- PQCMM Level 4 criterion 1: **Yes, from 1.9.0**. Level 4 as a whole stays not met while zero-legacy capability is undetermined. The declared level stays 3.
- PQCMM.md and CRYPTO-INVENTORY.md said SLH-DSA was offered in ten parameter sets. The API offers one, SLH-DSA-SHA2-192s, and conformance covers all twelve. Both now say so.

## Tests

- `npm test`: 153 of 153 across 11 files (139 on #38 plus 14 new), and 39 of 39 pinned vectors
- The 14 CBOM tests validate against the vendored CycloneDX 1.6 schema and include five negative controls: an undeclared import, a node:crypto call naming its own algorithm, a dropped declaration, a vanished use, and a use mentioned only in a comment
- devDependencies `ajv` 8.20.0 and `ajv-formats` 3.0.1, pinned exactly

author: felipelavorenti
body:
Antes: os itens só tinham JSON. Não havia como baixar, gerar, ler ou mandar arquivos entre os nós, e os nós de arquivo do n8n (Convert to File, Extract from File, Compression, Edit Image, Read/Write Files from Disk, iCalendar) ficavam de fora na importação.

Depois: os itens podem levar arquivos (`binary`, no mesmo formato do n8n). Chegam os seis nós de arquivo do n8n, e o HTTP Request, o Gmail, o HTML e o Crypto passam a trabalhar com arquivos. Na tela, a saída de cada nó mostra os arquivos com os botões Abrir e Baixar.

Como:
- Engine: `binary.ts` com os utilitários; nós novos em `files-convert.ts` (exceljs, csv-parse/csv-stringify, pdfjs-dist, ics) e `files-disk.ts` (fflate, sharp, fast-glob); conversores do importador.
- HTTP Request: corpo multipart e binário, e formato da resposta (automático, JSON, texto, arquivo). No automático, respostas de tipo binário (PDF, imagem, zip, Excel) agora viram arquivo em vez de texto corrompido.
- Gmail: arquivos do item como anexos e anexos baixados como arquivos. A opção de manter o conteúdo em base64 no JSON vem ligada por padrão para não quebrar fluxos salvos; fluxos importados do n8n ficam com ela desligada.
- Servidor: migração `007_arquivos_execucao` (tabela `execution_files`). O conteúdo dos arquivos só é guardado nas execuções manuais e reexecuções (até 64 MB por execução, sem repetir arquivos iguais); nas outras fica só nome, tipo e tamanho. Nova rota `GET /api/executions/{id}/files/{ref}`.
- Read/Write Files from Disk só usa as pastas de `FILES_DIRS`; no docker-compose, `/files` ligada à pasta `./arquivos`.
- Dockerfile instala fontes (DejaVu) para o texto do Edit Image.
- Limites: XLS e ODS não são lidos nem gerados (só XLSX e CSV); Edit Image usa sharp no lugar do GraphicsMagick, com pequenas diferenças descritas na documentação técnica.
- Documentação: manual, documentação técnica e API atualizados (docs/*.md e os documentos do Claude).
