author: architectds
body:
## Title
Issue: none - a follow-up to STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE (978d355, 0.1.40.2).

## Summary
`STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE` (0.1.40.2) hands the decode CPU pool a share of a small chunk's streamed experts. On a PC
that maps its experts (`--mmap-experts`) it took none, because it only takes page-locked experts; it also stopped at
1,024-token chunks and ran on one GPU only. With this change, when it is set:

- it takes any expert the CPU reads from RAM as it is: the arena, the page-locked copy, or the mapped `experts.bin`'s
  pages in the file cache;
- chunks below 3,072 tokens are staged after their routing (only those can hand the CPU a share), instead of streaming
  every expert from 1,024 tokens on; `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE_MAX=1024` keeps the old limit;
- on a layer split every stage has the pool, and one stage at a time takes it for a chunk.

Unset, nothing changes: every new path is behind `cpu_share_on()`.

Measured on Windows 11, Ryzen 9 5900XT, 96 GB DDR4-3200, PCIe 3.0 x8, `--mmap-experts`, q4_0 KV. Fresh prompts read
after an 8K prewarm, medians of 5 interleaved rounds, off / auto, ms:

| machine | 512 tokens | 1,000 tokens | 2,000 tokens | 3,000 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 5070 Ti, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS (huihui-ai's build) | 3,322 / 1,706 (-49%) | 3,990 / 2,357 (-41%) | 5,413 / 3,354 (-38%) | 5,525 / 4,309 (-22%) |
| RTX 3060 + RTX 5070 Ti (layers 0-11 / 12-47), IQ3_S | 3,452 / 2,037 (-41%) | 4,506 / 2,680 (-41%) | 6,376 / 3,869 (-39%) | 6,733 / 5,138 (-24%) |

A coding agent's recorded conversation on the two cards (a 100K-token start, then 8 turns of 1-5K tokens of code, 128
tokens written a turn; both read the same tokens): 137.4 s off, 130.6 s auto (reading 121.1 -> 114.3 s).

## What changed
- `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`
  - `stream_all_min()`: once the share is armed, the share's own limit (`STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE_MAX`, default 3072,
    at least 1024) instead of 1024. `Prefill::arm_cpu_share` sets it before any loan is sized; `init` sets it too.
  - The experts the share may take: page-locked, or not `transient()` with a stable blob. The blob pointers are taken
    while the experts are chosen (on the prefill thread, as before); an expert without one stays on the GPU.
  - A chunk takes the pool only when no other stage of a layer split holds it (`g_cpu_pool_busy`), and gives it back
    at the end of the chunk, after the last layer's CPU thread has been joined.
- `include/strata/prefill/prefill.hpp`: `Prefill::arm_cpu_share`, and `set_cpu_pool`'s comment.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`
  - serve: the limit is armed before the loans are sized, and every stage of a split gets the pool (still not with
    `--batch`);
  - the one-shot generate path: armed before `plan_lend` (one GPU, as before).
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: the CPU share section, with the table above.

## Extra Notes
- **Before this, on the same setup, the share took nothing.** With it on, the one-card short reads took off's times
  (3,319 against 3,322 ms at 512 tokens; 3,000 tokens 5,487 against 5,525).
- **Output with it on changes in the last bits**, as the section already says. On one card, all 9 greedy answers of the
  conversation differ from off, the first differing word coming after 4-41 words (near ties).
- **It has run for a while.** The fork architectds/Strata has had its own CPU share since 0.1.36, on by default in its
  builds and in daily use for coding agents since 2026-10-02 (one RTX 5070 Ti, later with an RTX 3060 beside it). The
  same tests measured it equal to this up to 1,000 tokens, and 3% / 5% faster at 2,000 / 3,000 tokens on one card (on
  the two cards within 1.5%): it quantizes the layer's activations on the GPU and copies a quarter of the bytes down,
  where this copies floats and quantizes on the CPU. That part can follow as its own PR.
- **How much it helps depends on the hardware.** It pays where streaming an expert costs more than computing it on the
  CPU: a narrow or older PCIe link (3.0, x8 or x4, an eGPU, a laptop), a card whose cache holds few of the experts, and
  a CPU with many cores and good RAM bandwidth - the PC above has all three (-41% to -49% at 1,000 tokens and below).
  It helps less with PCIe 5.0 x16 or a card that holds most experts, and a slow CPU or low RAM bandwidth gets a small
  share (`auto` measures both sides). The table in DETAILS.md already has -19% to -35% below 1,000 tokens on three other
  PCs. Not measured here: PCIe 4.0 / 5.0 links, AMD or Intel GPUs, Linux.
- **Tested:** Windows, CUDA 13.0, sm_86 + sm_120 (RTX 3060 + RTX 5070 Ti). Not tested: Linux, HIP, SYCL.

author: ethanreyna
body: ## Summary Rebuilds the poster around the guild's reference posters: a background picture with torn parchment laid over it, instead of one flat sheet. Layout as chosen — **title and subtitle strips at the top left, parchments tiling the width beneath them, footnote strip along the bottom**. - **`@background: `** picks the picture. Backgrounds are uploaded through the existing `/api/upload` → R2 route (same as barrel screenshots) and listed in `db.backgrounds`, so they're kept for the whole guild and the next poster picks one off a thumbnail shelf. The editor's Upload button writes the `@background:` line for you. - **`@panel`** starts another parchment. `Poster` now holds `panels`, each with its own blocks and sections; a template with no `@panel` is one panel, so everything saved before this still parses. - **Torn parchment** is drawn as a seeded wandering outline — seeded so the edge is identical on every redraw rather than dancing on each keystroke — with a warm gradient, a soft drop shadow and a darker rim. - **One renderer.** The HTML sheet is gone; the canvas draws both the preview and the PNG. With the poster being artwork over a photograph there was no honest way to keep an HTML version and a canvas version agreeing, and this way the preview *is* the export. - 1280×720 logical, exported at 2x → **2560×1440**, matching the references. A poster that needs more room grows rather than overflowing, and the background re-fits (cover, cropped not squashed) to the final shape. - URL safety: `db.backgrounds` only accepts our own `/api/img/` paths or plain `http(s)` addresses, so a hand-edited document can't put a `javascript:`/`data:` URL into an ``. ## Verification Parser: the real template gives 1 panel / 4 sections / 31 rows; `@panel` splits into 2; `@background` and quoted cells (`"Sword, broken"`) survive; `@theme` still lands in metadata. Canvas, against a stubbed 2d context: 2560×1664 for the sample, 126 strings, every coordinate finite, nothing past any edge, and identical size with a background attached. Degenerate inputs — empty, title only, three panels, a 180-character item name, rows with no `@columns`, footer only — all return 1280×720 without hanging. **Found and fixed during that:** a single parchment holding a long list rendered as a 1280×1299 ribbon with empty ground either side. Sections now flow into up to three columns inside a wide parchment, bringing the same poster to 1280×832. **Not verified:** how it actually looks. No browser here, so the geometry is checked but not the typography or the torn edges. The reference title uses a runic display face I don't have — this uses a bold serif. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` - [x] `pnpm build` - [x] Parser and canvas geometry verified standalone - [ ] Poster → Upload a screenshot → it appears in the shelf and behind the parchment. - [ ] Load the example → two parchments side by side → Save as PNG → 2560×… image matching the preview. - [ ] Save to the guild, Clear, re-open it, edit, Save changes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: courtneyr-dev
body:
Follow-up to #361. The `build` job now compares the committed `build/` with the fresh `npm run build:prod` output and fails if they differ: any tracked change (`git diff --exit-code --stat -- build/`), or an untracked file under `build/`, which `git diff` doesn't report. On failure it prints `git status --short build/` and the rebuild command.

The step runs after "Upload build artifacts", so a red run still has the fresh `build/` as a downloadable artifact.

## Determinism

I checked CI's own output before relying on it:

- The `build` job in #361's run resolved Node v24.21.0, the version the committed build came from.
- That run's `build` artifact (ubuntu, fresh build of #361 on top of 921dc99) matches `build/` at fcdd2b9 in all 70 files. `blocks.asset.php` has version `c3e0b175ca81654a81b3` on both.
- The push run for f2dcdf9 (#359's npm overrides) produced the same 70 files as fcdd2b9. Against main's committed `build/`, only `blocks.js` and `blocks.asset.php` differ, which is the #346 drift.
- All 70 tracked `build/` files are mode 100644, so a fresh build can't add a mode change that the artifact diff missed.

`node-version: "24"` floats. If a later 24.x ever changes the output, this step is where it shows up.

Locally, the step script passes on a clean tree and fails, listing the file, for a modified, an untracked and a deleted `build/` file.

## CI here

#361 merged before this PR opened, so this run's merge ref is main at 4967431 plus only the `ci.yml` change. On that unchanged tree, `Build` passes, new step included ([run 37665489849](https://github.com/courtneyr-dev/post-kinds-for-indieweb/actions/runs/37665489849)).

Branch protection has `strict: false`, so two PRs that each pass against an older main can still combine into a stale build. The push run on main runs the same step and goes red after that merge.

## Dependabot

`dependabot-auto-merge.yml` turns on auto-merge for patch and minor Dependabot PRs, and those touch only `package-lock.json` (plus `package.json` for grouped updates). A bump that changes the bundle now fails `Build` until someone pushes a rebuild commit to the Dependabot branch. `Build` is a required check, so auto-merge waits and nothing stale lands, but the PR sits red.

`src/` imports nothing outside `@wordpress/*`, and all of those are externals except `@wordpress/icons` (neither `.asset.php` lists `wp-icons`). The bumps that can move the bundle are the weekly `wordpress-packages` group (`@wordpress/icons`, and `@wordpress/scripts` with the webpack/babel/terser chain under it) and lockfile-only bumps inside that chain. The last 15 merged Dependabot PRs were lockfile-only, and #359 is the one I confirmed left the bundle unchanged.

Two ways to handle it. Neither is in this PR:

1. Keep it manual. When a Dependabot PR goes red on `Build`, download its `build` artifact or run `npm ci && npm run build:prod` on the branch, commit `build/` and push. Dependabot stops rebasing a PR once someone else commits to it, and `@dependabot recreate` drops the rebuild commit.
2. Add a workflow that rebuilds and pushes `build/` to Dependabot branches. A push made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` doesn't start new workflow runs, so the required checks would never report on the rebuild commit and auto-merge would stall anyway. It needs a PAT or GitHub App token with contents write, stored as a Dependabot secret.

I'd start with 1 and revisit if the `wordpress-packages` group goes red most Mondays. Your call.

author: mikael-bashir
body:
A silently auto-bound name is either an intentional free type variable or a typo of something already in scope (a declaration's own binder, or a `variable` the author renamed/removed). `autoimplicit` already distinguishes Greek-letter names (the type-variable idiom, `warn`) from everything else (`fail`); this adds a second, deterministic signal: a non-Greek auto-bound name within one or two edits of a unique candidate already in scope at that point is flagged in the detail as a likely typo.

A tie between two equally-close candidates is reported as no match rather than an arbitrary pick — the first version of this picked whichever tied candidate happened to come first in a `set`'s iteration order (nondeterministic across runs), caught by a local unit test before it ever reached a fixture. Five cases, including that exact tie, are now permanent regression tests in `selftest.py`.

Also removed a dead, pre-existing `DECL` regex that an earlier fix on this branch had silently shadowed (Python re-binds the name; only the second definition was ever used).

author: mcereal
body:
The routing draft said nothing about a neighbour table with no room, and the firmware kept whoever it heard first. Running the firmware's core in the simulator with the 32 places the Heltec port had showed what that costs: on the 1000-node region with 200 relays, 64% of pairs held a route at SF7 and 17% at SF8 on 62.5 kHz, against 97% and 92% with 255 places.

## The rule

With no room, an announce from a node not kept is looked at against the neighbours whose links are not up. If its floor is `REPLACE_BAND` (6 dB) or more below the highest floor among them, it takes that neighbour's place. A link that is up is never replaced.

## Measured

Share of ordered pairs holding a route after the warmup, three seeds, firmware core in ternmesh/sim:

| Places | SF7, first heard | SF7, this rule | SF8/62.5, first heard | SF8/62.5, this rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 64% | 88% | 17% | 82% |
| 64 | 93% | 96% | 77% | 91% |
| 255 | 97% | 97% | 92% | 92% |

Variants tried on one seed and rejected are in the rationale: replacing links that are up, and preferring relays.

## Open

- With 32 or 64 places at SF7 some seeds do not settle: six hours on they still send requests and about five times the announces of the seeds that do. Listed under "Not yet measured".
- No test vector: the rule depends on the table's state. The firmware's unit test covers it.

author: iremlopsum
body:
Release 5.2.1: one fix. A `:name` in a path is filled only where it starts a path segment, the same rule the types and the unfilled-param check already used.

## The fix

**The URL builder and the types disagreed about what a `:name` is.** `buildUrl` (`src/utils/path-params.ts`) filled a `:name` anywhere in the path. The `PathParams` type and the check for unfilled params only count one that starts a segment. Two results:

- `path: '/v1/documents:batchGet'` called with `{ batchGet: 'yes' }` sent `/v1/documentsyes`, a URL the type said could not exist.
- `path: '/v2/simple/price?:qs'` typed its params as `{}`. Without `qs`, it sent `?:qs` as text. With `qs`, it encoded the whole value into one query parameter (`price?ids%3Dbitcoin%26…`).

What changes:

1. **The fill is anchored** to the start of a segment: `/(^|\/):name/` with the prefix captured, because lookbehind is banned. `/v1/documents:batchGet` and `/time/12:30` are sent as written.
2. **A mid-segment `:name` that a param of the call names is refused.** This is the one case where the anchor changes behaviour: `new Request` with an explicit type and `/items/v:version` was filled before. Without the refusal, the value would quietly move to the query string or the body. With no param of that name, the colon is plain text and nothing is said.
3. **`?:name`, `&:name` and `=:name` in the path's query string are refused on every call.** `defineRequest` refuses them at compile time too, with `QueryTokenGuard` next to `FragmentGuard`. The message points to the second type argument.

Each refusal is a `'network'` Result with a `TypeError` that says what to change, and nothing is sent.

- **Order:** fragment, then a query-string `:name` (both template mistakes), then mid-segment, then an unusable value, then an unfilled token. A test pins the order.
- **`error.request.url`:** a query-string refusal reports the URL with its path params filled, as a fragment refusal does. `FragmentError` is renamed `TemplateError`; it's internal and not exported.

## Tests

- New tests in `tests/path-params.test.ts`, `tests/unresolved-path.test.ts`, `tests/error-url.test.ts` and `tests/types.test-d.ts`.
- **Revert-verified:** with the fix inert, each behaviour test fails with an AssertionError, and the type tests fail with "Unused '@ts-expect-error'". Each part of the fix was also disabled on its own, and caught.
- **Pinned on purpose** (these pass before and after): a mid-segment colon with no param, `/v1/operations/:name:cancel`, `/search/:q?x=1`, `/events?at=12:30`, and `?next=/:id`.

## Docs

- Defining endpoints › Path params.
- A new Behaviour in detail › "Colons in a path" section, with type-checked blocks, including the compile error.
- The `path` row in Endpoint options.
- Handling errors: a corrected sentence. It claimed every refused call's message ends in "so the call was not sent"; most don't.

## Release notes

- `package.json` and the lockfile are at 5.2.1 (`npm version 5.2.1 --no-git-tag-version`).
- The CHANGELOG has a 5.2.1 entry with the compare-link footer.
- `MIGRATION.md` has `## Upgrading to 5.2.1`: no action needed unless a path has a `:name` that doesn't start a segment.
- `node scripts/release-check.mjs --mode pr --base-version 5.2.0`: "5.2.1 is ready to release once merged".
- **Sizes:** REST only grows from 6667 to 6966 B gzipped (+299 B), against a 7000 B budget. The other bundles grow by about the same amount and stay under their budgets. The README badge and the Exports size table are updated.

## Checks

The full gate passes:
- typecheck and type tests (1156);
- 1174 tests and 48 integration tests;
- `docs:check` and `docs:types`;
- build and size;
- the site build (45 pages) and its 84 tests.

## After merge

1. The release workflow runs the gate, then waits for you to **approve the `npm` environment**.
2. After you approve, it publishes with provenance, verifies a fresh install, tags `v5.2.1`, creates the GitHub Release from this CHANGELOG entry, and redeploys the docs.

Before: on a phone, the Plan screen opened on a flag-coloured banner (Wikipedia's main image for Italy is its flag). Below it came a stack of boxes: About, a cramped link bar with five icons, suggestions, an ask box and checks. Only then did the first day appear, as a heavy panel. The top bar repeated the name with a Sign out link, and the bottom bar used emoji.

After: the trip opens on a real destination photo. A row of date chips stays pinned while you scroll and jumps to any day. There is one "Paste a link, or add a place" field with a + sheet. author: ezyang
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.18.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #200106

## The bug

Materializing a lazily cloned (copy-on-write) tensor copies the shared data.
On CUDA, that copy was a synchronous cudaMemcpy on the legacy default stream:
not ordered with respect to PyTorch's (non-blocking) current stream, and not
recorded at all under CUDA graph capture. It ran once at capture time, so every
replay read a stale snapshot:

```python
static_in = torch.full((N,), float("nan"), device="cuda")
g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with torch.cuda.graph(g):
    y = static_in._lazy_clone()
    y.data_ptr()        # materializes y (as raw Triton launchers do)
    out = y * 2
static_in.copy_(torch.randn(N, device="cuda"))
g.replay()              # out is NaN: the copy into y was never captured
```

This was hit with distributed MoE + CUDA graphs in TorchTitan;
`torch.compile(mode="reduce-overhead")` is affected too.

## The idea

A lazy clone has the semantics of a `clone()` enqueued on the stream that is
current when `_lazy_clone()` is called. Users synchronize as if that clone had
happened then, so materialization, which happens later and possibly on another
stream, must preserve that ordering. Materialization either copies the data (if
other references remain) or steals it (if this is the last reference).

### Copying

`Allocator::copy_data` now enqueues the copy on the current stream
(`cudaMemcpyAsync`), so it is ordered like any other op, and captured under
CUDA graph capture. That fixes the example above: every replay redoes the copy.

A copy is only ordered like the clone() it stands for if it is enqueued on the
stream the lazy clone was made on (for the source of a lazy clone: the stream
its memory was allocated on, which the caching allocator orders reuse by).
Otherwise we raise an error rather than synchronize; there's no recordStream
and no host blocking anywhere:

```python
y = x._lazy_clone()            # on the default stream
with torch.cuda.stream(s):
    y.add_(1)                  # error: the copy on s could read x before it's
                               # ready, and y's new memory would belong to s
```

Each COW DataPtr now has its own `COWReference` context (pointing to the shared
`COWDeleterContext`) that records the stream the lazy clone was made on.

### Stealing

When the last reference steals the data, it writes to it in place, which must
come after copies of it that may still be pending on other streams. Copies can
happen late, after the user's synchronization:

```python
with torch.cuda.stream(s):
    y = x._lazy_clone()                        # semantically: clone on s, now
torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s)     # correct for an eager clone
with torch.cuda.stream(s):
    y.add_(1)                                  # y materializes now: copies x on s
x.add_(1)                                      # x steals the data on the default
                                               # stream: must wait for that copy
```

So each eager copy records an event on its stream (one per stream; later ones
supersede earlier ones), and the stealing stream waits on them on the device.

Stealing has to stay (rather than always copying): it is what turns the last
COW reference back into a normal tensor in place. Otherwise the standard
side-stream-warmup pattern would move the graph's input to a new allocation:

```python
with torch.cuda.stream(s):                     # warmup, as the docs recommend
    model(static_input)                        # lazily clones static_input, and
torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s)     # materializes the clone on s
with torch.cuda.graph(g):
    out = model(static_input)
static_input.copy_(data)    # steals in place (waiting for the warmup copies);
g.replay()                  # copying instead would move static_input, and the
                            # graph would read its freed memory
```

Lazily cloning on a side stream like this is allowed. Until it is materialized,
the clone's uses on that stream count as side-stream uses of the original
allocation, which must be synchronized before it is freed, as usual.

### CUDA graph capture

A captured copy is redone by every replay. That is right for a lazy clone made
during capture, but not for one made before it, which stands for a snapshot.
Stream identity can't tell these apart (it's the same before and during
capture), so each reference also records whether its stream was being
captured, and copying is only allowed if that matches:

```python
with torch.cuda.stream(s):
    y = x._lazy_clone()                  # snapshot of x, before capture
    with torch.cuda.graph(g, stream=s):
        y.add_(1)                        # error: replays would recopy x into y
```

Materializing the source of a lazy clone during capture would also move it to
a new allocation inside of the graph. That's wrong if its memory predates the
capture, e.g. a graph input:

```python
with torch.cuda.graph(g):
    y = static_input._lazy_clone()
    static_input.add_(1)    # error: would move static_input to graph memory;
                            # every replay would then copy the stale original
                            # over the user's new inputs
```

Memory allocated during capture comes from a private pool, for which the new
`Allocator::was_allocated_on_stream` returns unknown; a known allocation stream
means the memory predates the capture.

Captured copies are not waited for when stealing: they only run on replay,
which is ordered by the stream the graph is launched on, and the user already
orders input writes with respect to replays.

## Limitations

- Allocators that can't report allocation streams (cudaMallocAsync, pluggable
  allocators; ROCm's masquerading wrapper doesn't forward the query) skip the
  checks that need them, but still get stream-ordered copies and event waits.
- Captures aren't distinguished from each other: a lazy clone made during one
  capture and materialized during another on the same stream isn't rejected.
  Neither is the source of a lazy clone whose memory came from another graph's
  private pool.
- This only affects explicit `_lazy_clone()` users; nothing else creates COW
  tensors.

See "Streams and CUDA graphs" in c10/core/impl/README-cow.md. Tests in
test/test_cuda.py cover each example above.

Fixes #200155

author: hoffmang9
body: Dependabot cursor review now runs once for a given upgrade. A later rebase, recreate, or rebuild of that same pull request does not start another review after the first one has posted its comment. The skip identity is `git patch-id --stable` of the pull request diff. Commit messages, titles, and bodies are not used. Dependabot's YAML trailer is not used: a refresh can leave that trailer on an older version while the lockfile has already moved. ## Diff source The trusted step calls `pulls.get` with `mediaType: { format: 'diff' }` and pipes that text into `git patch-id --stable`. That response is GitHub's pull request diff, the merge-base-to-head unified diff. A single combined diff produces one patch id. `git log -p` produces one id per commit, so the helper rejects more than one id line and the review runs. This stays off the pull request tree. No pull request objects are fetched into the workspace, and no pull request code runs to compute the id. A diff the API refuses, an empty diff, empty patch-id output, or more than one id line leaves the marker empty and the review runs. `git patch-id` only hashes the diff text; it does not check out the branch. The marker is `` on the first line of a `github-actions[bot]` comment. Older markers do not match, so the next push reviews once and then stamps the new form. ## What stays the same, and what moved The commit gate remains, and it is not redundant. A maintainer rebase or cherry-pick can keep the Dependabot author, a verified signature from the maintainer's own key, and the same diff. The patch id would match, so the review would skip. The gate still requires every commit, via paginated `pulls.listCommits`, to have `author.login === dependabot[bot]`, `committer.login === web-flow`, and `commit.verification.verified === true`. Anything else fails open. `actions/checkout` of the pull request head treats the workspace as a non-git directory and deletes `.trusted-dcr-helper`. The workflow now copies the trusted scripts to `$RUNNER_TEMP/trusted-dcr-helper` before that checkout. Resolve and post `require` those copies. A pull request that ships `.trusted-dcr-helper` is not loaded. `complete` on the combiner output is display-only. The trusted post script reads `cursor_output_malware.json` and `cursor_output_compatibility.json` itself: a successful result object, `is_error` not true, no `error`, and a non-empty analysis string in both files. A pull request copy of the combiner cannot arm the skip. The single job, the per-step `already_reviewed` guards, `always()` on upload, fail open, permissions, the `pull_request` trigger, and `node --test` inside `make test` are unchanged. ## Trade-off `git patch-id --stable` ignores line numbers, so a plain rebase or a recreated commit with a different message keeps the same id. A lockfile context shift, where the base changes lines around the hunk, produces a different id and the review runs again. That is the safe direction: an extra review, not a skipped one. A newer version or an added human commit also changes the id. Residual risk: the two agent output files live in the workspace. The steps between the agent run and the post step execute trusted default-branch scripts, not pull request code. A later step that ran pull request code in that window could replace those files with a fake successful analysis and arm the skip. The combiner's `complete` field cannot. ## Tests - Real git repos: a rebase onto a moved base keeps the id; a rewritten commit message keeps the id; a version bump changes it; an added human commit changes it; a lockfile context shift changes it. - One combined multi-commit diff is one id. A `git log -p` series is rejected. - Empty input, a non-diff, and a diff over the size bound do not build a marker. An API error, an empty diff, and a too-large API response fail open. - A non-`web-flow` committer, an unverified commit, another author, an empty list, and more than 100 commits fail open. A bad committer past the first 30 commits is visible only because `paginate` returns the full list. - Trusted `complete`: missing files, empty files, plain-text `Error: agent exited`, `is_error`, a dumps fallback, one-sided success, and a forged `complete: true` in `cursor_output.json` do not stamp. Both successful analyses do. - The workflow requires resolve and post from `$RUNNER_TEMP`. Deleting the workspace copy still leaves the `$RUNNER_TEMP` scripts loadable. ## Verification - `make test` (Go tests, 84 Python tests, 17 node tests) - Prettier and actionlint on the expanded `dependency-cursor-review.yml` Diff against `main`: 1223 insertions, 87 deletions. Production code is 360 insertions and 86 deletions. CI wiring is 5 insertions. Tests are 858 insertions and 1 deletion.

author: tristanmatthias
body:
G4 (`avra-8sb5.34.53.25`), ladder step 4 of `docs/2026_10_06_FLOW_G4_DESIGN.md`. Python only; no compiler or runtime change.

## What it does
`python3 tools/flow_trace.py <trace> --graph [--at <ms>]` prints who waits on whom at one instant (the trace's end by default):
- every live task and each source of its wait set: a task it joins ("a task nothing runs" for a fiberless one), a descriptor and its direction, a time, a gate — named with the last task whose claim came through it;
- every ring of joins, once, from its smallest task;
- a count line: tasks alive, waiting, ready or running.
The graph is built from a table of waits (`waits_at`), so step 3's live listing prints through the same `graph`.

## Measured

body: ## 改了什么 工具审批还在排队时，网页顶栏用量条旁边常驻短指示（中文「等待审批 n」，英文 `Waiting for approval n`）。转录为空、滚走，或卡片不在视口里，指示仍在顶栏。计数跟着 pending 队列变；通过或拒绝把队列清空后指示消失。 作曲器上方的 approval-card（通过 / 拒绝）保持原样，仍是真正做决定的地方。`toolApproval` 策略、durable / Approvals 契约、TUI 审批界面都没动。桌面壳加载同一套网页宿主，没有单独的原生审批 UI。 页面本来就在审批状态变化时重绘，指示挂在 `buildWebView` 的 `approvalIndicator` 上，所以计数是跟着现有 paint 走的。 ## 怎么核对 1. 把 `toolApproval` 设成会暂停的模式，让一次工具调用停在 pending。 2. 顶栏用量条左侧应出现「等待审批 1」（英文界面是 `Waiting for approval 1`）。多条同时排队时数字跟着变。 3. 清空转录或把作曲器上方的卡片滚出视口，顶栏指示还在。 4. 在卡片上通过或拒绝，直到队列为空，指示消失。卡片本身的通过 / 拒绝按钮还在。 ## 测了 / 没测 测了： - `npm run typecheck --workspace @amazme/web` 通过 - `npm run build --workspace @amazme/web` 通过 - `npm test --workspace @amazme/web`：10 个文件，104 个测试通过 - `view.test.ts`：pending 时指示在，通过一条后计数减一，拒绝最后一条后指示和卡片都没了 - `approval-status.test.ts`（happy-dom）：空转录时顶栏指示可见且不在转录 / 作曲器里；通过后计数更新；拒绝后指示隐藏、卡片消失 没测： - 浏览器或 Electron 窗口里的实机点击 - 真实宿主上的审批门与 `toolApproval` 策略（语义未改，也未重跑 coding-agent 的审批测试） - TUI 审批界面

body:
Closes the two versioning questions Stage 13's close routed to the owner (the owner's word, 2026-10-07, on the recommendation): the pre-release bound is the first production build for a schema flipped `active` before that build as for an `approved` one (the flip changes what a schema claims, not when the wire binds), and a pure relaxation of a bound that every emitted value already satisfies is additive before the build and a widening after it (behind a new minor on a result shape; sent only at a new minor on a params shape).

One docs commit: ADR-0017's second amendment of 2026-10-07 as a triple (Decision sentence, log row, history note) with its digest bullet; LOCAL-IPC.md §Version negotiation carries the rule; the plan's three routed-question sites gain dated parentheses (append-only records). Plus the fold of main after #219.

Class: docs-only
Work commits: 1 (f252aaf3); 2 review fixes (c381f070: a params relaxation after the build is a major, the after-build half in LOCAL-IPC.md; 861ea0d8: two P3 wordings). LOCAL-IPC.md matches the boundary list by path, so under 8 work commits the arm needs the owner's word.


## Also on this branch (2026-10-08, after the fold of origin/main at 4483d93b)

**ADR-0028 A 2026-10-08 — The ancestor walk stops at the trust boundary the binding supplies** (0d84cfd7, 1 work commit). rust-ui-dev's finding: the ancestor rule merged in #224 refuses every Android app-private directory (`/data`, `/data/data` are `0771 system:system`). The walk now runs up to a trust boundary the composition supplies to `profile-config` — `/` from the daemon and `transportctl`, so nothing changes on a Linux host; on Android the app's own data directory as the platform reports it, canonicalised once, the runtime's private directories directly under it at `0700`. Code lands with the Android binding's first package (plan §20). Triple, digest, configuration.md, the threat model's control and residual columns, IDENTITY.md.

**plan §20 — Stage 17's Exit gate and State line** (692faf30, 1 work commit). fabric-coordinator's observation after #227's thread: the Stage 17 section had no gate. Conditions (a)–(i): the two spikes closed PASS with the Keystore round-trip and the recovery path on invalidation; every step with a named test; android-e2e over direct and relayed paths and the three `tests/interoperability` items; ADR-0028's trust boundary and the store on the device; the endpoint overlay's persistence; render parity, the accessibility reach and the PeerId copy; the trust-audit sink under a strict filter; Dependency-Check as a required context; an empty stage-17 ledger and the status moving on the owner's word. Two review rounds; the review is posted on this head.

Count: 3 work commits (ADR-0017, ADR-0028 trust boundary, plan §20 gate) + review fixes; under the floor — the owner's word arms. `Class: docs-only`

body:
## What

- Adds the cookie consent banner and Consent Mode setup (SPEC §10.5). Analytics stays off until the visitor accepts, and Google Tag Manager (T015) has a consent state and event to hook into.

## Changes

- Consent Mode defaults go into `dataLayer` from an inline script at the top of `<head>`, with every type denied. A returning visitor who accepted gets `analytics_storage` granted again. Advertising types are never granted.
- `src/lib/consent.ts` reads and writes the `cbhs_consent` cookie (`analytics` or `rejected`, 6 months, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure`) and provides `hasAnalyticsConsent()`. Every choice dispatches a `cbhs:consent` event for T015. Rejecting deletes `_ga*` cookies on the host and its parent domains.
- The banner renders in the root layout with copy from the `cookie-consent` global. Accept and Reject use the same secondary style. It links to the cookies page using that page's title. It isn't a modal and doesn't trap focus. It sticks to the bottom of the viewport inside the page flow, so it never covers the header Donate button.
- The footer's "Cookie settings" is now a button that reopens the banner and moves focus to it. Focus goes back to the button after the visitor chooses.
- Publishing the cookies page revalidates every page, because the banner link uses its title.
- Unit tests: `tests/int/consent.int.spec.ts`.

## Ticket

- `docs/tickets/T030-cookie-consent.md`, report at `docs/tickets/reports/T030.md`

## Notes

- No migration. The global has no field for the `/cookies` link label, so the link uses the cookies page's title.
- No banner renders until Amagi fills in and publishes the global's `heading`, `acceptLabel` and `rejectLabel`. Only `settingsLabel` is seeded so far. Until then the footer also hides "Cookie settings", and analytics stays off.
- AC4: Lighthouse's only failing audit is the existing header Donate button contrast (white on `--orange`, 2.36:1), which fails the same way with the banner closed. This is a brand colour decision for T024.

## Summary
**Commit 1: the Apps Pro patch, applied as given (`git am`).**
- Adds 5 new apps in `src/apps-private/`, so Apps Pro now has 7.
- Adds the `/apps-pro` sales page.
- Adds the PayPal Orders v2 client (`src/lib/paypal.ts`) and the `/apps/buy` + `/apps/paypal-return` checkout.

**Commit 2: PayPal checkout for every other digital product.** Stripe charges are disabled on the account, so every buy button pointed at a checkout that couldn't take money.
- **`/buy/<product id>`** starts a PayPal order at that product's price. The products are the Weekly Reset Checklist ($15), Follow-Up Email Templates ($19), Client Onboarding Kit ($29), Digital System ($49) and Bundle ($97). While PayPal isn't configured, it falls back to an email order, so no button is dead.
- **`/buy/paypal-return`** captures the order on the server and checks it was completed for the **full price of the product it names**. Only then does it mint a signed `/api/download` token, show a "Download now" button, email the link and record the order.
- **Every buy link now points at `/buy/<id>`:**
  - pages: home, products, store, about, request, agent
  - all 12 blog posts with a buy link
  - the free tools page
  - upsell emails
  - the AI email-draft prompt
- **Checkout copy** on the home, products, store, terms and privacy pages now says PayPal.

## Handoff items that needed no change
- **`/api/download` was already gated.** It never served a file without a valid signed or stored order token (the tests below confirm this).
- **`wrangler.json` no longer has plaintext secrets.** They were removed on Sep 18, but they **remain in public git history**, so they still need rotating (see below).
- **Product files** were removed from the repo in #58.
- **`/tools`** stays public as free samples.

## Testing
Ran `astro build`, `tsc`, then `wrangler dev --local` against a local stand-in for PayPal's API (`PAYPAL_API_BASE`): **42/42 checks passed**.
- **Downloads.** Each of these is refused:
  - no token: 400
  - garbage token: 401
  - token signed with the wrong secret: 401
  - expired token: 401
  - Apps Pro token used on a product: 404

  A valid token gets the file (200, attachment).
- **Checkout.**
  - All 5 `/buy/<id>` routes redirect to PayPal with the right price ($15/$19/$29/$49/$97).
  - A paid order shows the success page, and its download link returns the file (200).
  - These are refused with 402: a declined order, an unknown order, a forged order naming the $97 Bundle but paying $15, and a forged order with an unknown item.
  - A malformed order id gets 400.
- **Apps Pro.**
  - All 7 apps return 402 when locked, including with a product token used as the access cookie.
  - The paid PayPal flow leads to `/apps/unlock`, which sets an HttpOnly cookie, and then all 7 apps return 200.
  - A forged $1 Apps Pro order is refused (402).
- **Free samples.** `/tools/` returns 200.

## Not done / needs the owner
- **Real PayPal sandbox not tested.** No PayPal credentials are available here, so the flow was tested against a local stand-in for PayPal's API. Set `PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID`, `PAYPAL_SECRET` and `PAYPAL_ENV=sandbox` as Worker secrets, then buy once with a sandbox account before going live.
- **Leaked secrets.** Rotate `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (roll it in Stripe) and `DOWNLOAD_TOKEN_SECRET`; both are in public git history. Rotating `DOWNLOAD_TOKEN_SECRET` invalidates existing download and unlock links.
- **Domain registration flow.** `/domains` and `api/domain-interest` still use the Stripe link (`STRIPE_CHECKOUT_URL`). This PR doesn't change them.

author: zennay
body:
## Quality-validation

Adds a repository-wide privilege and supply-chain boundary for GitHub Actions without touching Watch/runtime, gateway/provider behavior, frozen v1.5.2 bytes, or physical acceptance semantics.

### Why
Raise AI already hardens many validation workflows individually, but there was no aggregate fail-closed contract preventing a future workflow with repository secrets, write-token permissions, `pull_request_target`, or floating external action refs from being exposed to untrusted pull-request execution.

### What
- forbid `pull_request_target` across every tracked workflow;
- forbid repository secret references in any workflow triggered by `pull_request`;
- forbid top-level or job-level `write` permissions in any workflow triggered by `pull_request`;
- require every external `uses:` reference in a pull-request workflow to be pinned to a full 40-character commit SHA;
- regression-cover top-level/job-level permission parsing plus valid immutable and invalid floating action fixtures;
- explicitly preserve privileged manual workflows outside the PR boundary.

The new test is auto-discovered by `tools/run_python_contracts.py`, so the existing unfiltered **All Python contracts CI** runs it on every PR without changing an owned workflow surface.

### Coordination
New file only: `tests/test_workflow_privilege_boundary.py`. Current YAML and Markdown owners remain untouched.

### Exact-head validation
Head `9a62facb48d9273ed4f7226c460588d7b774d483`:
- All Python contracts CI `37665613283`: GREEN
- Python surface contract CI `37665613289`: GREEN
- Tracked secret hygiene quality CI `37665613230`: GREEN

### Gate
Guarded squash merge only while this exact head remains current and GitHub reports the PR mergeable.

author: easydeed
body:
Design's package asks for this directly — *"re-measure the row counts in the
browser fit gate for this layout and pin them"* — and the first market kind
shouldn't be built against an unmeasured density. Measured before wiring.

Method: `scripts/measure_market_pagination.py`, reproducing the production path
in Chromium's own paginator with PDFShift's reserved space (0.44in top, 0.89in
bottom, body flowing in 9.67in), 120 listings.

## Design's layout is less dense than ours in both positions

| | Design's spec | ours, no narrative | ours as production renders |
|---|---|---|---|
| `closed` page 1 | **13** | **15** | 11 |
| `closed` continuation | **26** | **29** | 29 |

**The middle column is the comparison.** Design removes the AI narrative from
the table and gallery kinds ("Page-1 capacity is one state per kind"), so their
13 reads against our no-narrative 15, not against the 11 production renders
today. Comparing against the live figure would be comparing two different
documents — the error this whole exchange has been about.

Two fewer rows on page 1, three fewer on continuation. Their rows are taller.

## The page cost, from their own formula

Design gives `P = ceil((N − 13) / 26) + 1`. On the 118-row `closed` report in
their own per-kind table:

| | pages for N=118 |
|---|---|
| Design's spec (13 + 26/page) | **6** |
| ours (15 + 29/page) | **5** |

**One extra page on the highest-volume kind.** Cheap to adjust in a design file,
expensive to discover after eight kinds are wired — so it goes back as a
question rather than being absorbed.

## And the improvement their design brings is real

Page 1 is currently **not a fixed capacity**:

| `closed` page 1 | rows |
|---|---|
| with the narrative | 11 |
| without it | **15** |
| continuation, either way | 29 |

A four-row swing driven by model-generated prose of no fixed length. Removing
the narrative from the table kinds makes page-1 capacity **deterministic**,
which our build cannot be given without the same decision. `market_snapshot` is
the extreme case: with the trend chart, **zero** listings fit on page 1 — and
Design's snapshot carries no listings table at all, which resolves it rather
than working around it. That's the strongest argument in their layout, and worth
saying back to them.

## What was stale, and what was not

`PAGE_1_CAPACITY` in `test_narrative_box.py` is **current** — it matches this
measurement exactly, because it's re-pinned from `--emit-capacity` rather than
retyped, which is what that mode exists for.

The **docstring** of the measurement script was not. It stated "13 rows on page
1 and 25 on page 2" and a one-row narrative effect; the harness now produces 11
then 29 and a four-row effect, because §7.1's running-head change recovered
1.07in of every page and the continuation pages took the gain. The derived value
was maintained and the prose beside it wasn't — D-173's cap table again, in the
file whose own docstring argues for derivation over transcription.

## The gate's first version passed on a false match

`test_the_document_quotes_the_pinned_capacity` checked `str(rows) in text`. The
regression moving `closed.no_narrative` from 15 to 17 **passed**, because the
document contains `D-173` and `"17" in "D-173"`. Substring-is-not-a-construct,
in the gate written to stop a document going stale — third time in this session.

§5 is now a parseable ` ```capacity ` block and the comparison is dict equality
both ways. Six regressions, each seen to fail, including the two the substring
version let through:

| applied | caught |
|---|---|
| a pinned capacity moves (15 → 17) | **yes, now** — passed before |
| a state dropped from the document's block | **yes, now** — passed before |
| the page-cost arithmetic edited | yes |
| the stale docstring figures restored | yes |
| the "middle column" framing removed | yes |
| the no-narrative comparison broken | yes |

Root suite **2,690 passed**, 67 skipped, 18 xfailed.

## UNCERTAIN ABOUT

- **Whether the extra page is intended.** I'm reporting the arithmetic, not
  assuming the answer. If 26 rows is a deliberate air choice, it's theirs to
  confirm; if it fell out of a row height, 29 is available.
- **The continuation figure is ours, not theirs, measured on our current rows.**
  Design's 26 is a claim about *their* row height, which I cannot measure without
  building the layout. The honest comparison after wiring is re-running this
  harness on the new template — which §5 exists to make a diff rather than a
  surprise.
- **Twice now my own regression harness has misreported.** A same-second,
  same-size restore left Python running stale bytecode; a backup taken before an
  edit silently reverted that edit when restored. Both failed safe. Neither
  would have in the other direction, and I don't yet have a guard.
- **No market template has been touched.** This is measurement only. The wiring
  starts from these numbers.

Fixes #61

## What

- **Question design is locked and versioned.** `JEV_QUESTION_VERSION = "relevance-v1"` (`src/config.ts`) names the exact question text and criteria. M6's decision reuse depends on it, and it must be bumped whenever either changes.

author: marcusk639
body:
## The bug

`payment_intent.succeeded` decremented `rentOwed` with `FieldValue.increment(-amountCents)` and no guard. `increment` is atomic against concurrent writers but **not idempotent** — applying it twice for one payment credits the resident twice and the house absorbs the difference. Stripe can deliver the same event more than once, and any retry after a partial failure re-enters this handler.

The `payments` doc write next to it was already safe (`.set(fields, { merge: true })`, keyed on `paymentIntentId`). Only the decrement was exposed.

## The fix

The decrement now runs in a transaction that reads `payments/{paymentIntentId}`, skips if `rentApplied` is set, and otherwise decrements and sets the flag in the same commit. That doc is already written by `recordPaymentDoc` and keyed by PaymentIntent id, so no new collection is needed — and the guard lives in the data rather than in the delivery path, which is what makes it hold across redeliveries *and* retries.

## What I deliberately did NOT change, and why

`checkAndMarkEventProcessed` claims the event **before** the handler runs (`:1114`, `:1334`), and the dispatch `catch` logs then returns `res.status(200)`. So Stripe never retries, and a transiently failed event is dropped permanently — a successful payment whose rent is never credited. That is a real defect and it is still there.

I did not fix it here because the obvious fix is a trap. Returning 5xx so Stripe retries is only safe once every handler is idempotent, and the increment above was the clearest case where it was not. **Enabling retries first would have traded a silent under-credit for a silent double-credit** — arguably the worse direction, since the resident's balance would be wrong in the house's favour and nothing would flag it.

Making this decrement exactly-once is the precondition. Switching to 5xx and releasing the claim still needs a per-handler idempotency audit across the other 13 event types. That is a separate change and a product decision about which failure direction you prefer while the audit is outstanding.

## Test plan

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `regroup/functions` | 56 suites / **872 tests pass** (871 before, plus the new one) |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |

The new test drives two sequenced transactions — event unseen, payment already rent-applied — and asserts no second decrement.

**Verified non-vacuous**, which matters because it is a negative assertion and those pass just as happily when the handler does nothing at all. Removing the guard from the source makes it fail with:

```
Received: 0, [{"rentOwed": {"__increment": -50000}}]
```

Both webhook suites' fake transactions needed `txn.update` and a snapshot `.get()`, since the write moved inside a transaction. They delegate to the same doc-level mocks the existing assertions already use, so those assertions still pin the write itself rather than the mechanism. No test was removed or weakened.

## Deploy note

Needs `regroup/functions` deployed to take effect. Existing `payments` docs have no `rentApplied` flag, so the first redelivery of an old event would still apply a decrement once more — the guard is forward-looking, not retroactive.

author: smilerz
body:
Phase 3 of 3 for seeded random ordering (backend seed #911, search page #913). The home page's Random section reshuffled on every load, and its More link could not open the recipes it had shown.

Each Random section now keeps its own seed in sessionStorage until it expires (30 minutes, minted on first use and replaced once stale), sends it with its recipe request, and passes it in the More link as ordering=random&seed=..., so a refresh keeps the same recipes and the search page opens on the same order. Sections are keyed by their position on the page because the default layout has two Random sections, which would otherwise share a seed and show identical recipes. If storage is blocked the seed is simply not remembered. Recently viewed and the Randomize-toggle sections are unchanged.

  - Storage-backed getOrMintStoredSeed in utils/randomSeed.ts (injected storage, tolerant of blocked storage); new optional seedKey prop on the section component, set by StartPage
  - Tests: the helper (mint, reuse, expire, independent scopes, blocked storage), the section (sends a seed, More carries the same seed, survives remount, per-section seeds, stale seed replaced, Recently viewed unseeded), and StartPage giving each Random section its own key
  - No backend or generated-client change

author: altech0
body:
Fixes the bug that lost five of seven seeding runs earlier.

## What went wrong

Dispatching several combos back to back cancelled all but the last:

```
37376210866  21:29:45  success     <- only this survived
37376201445  21:29:40  cancelled
37376192538  21:29:35  cancelled
37376184525  21:29:30  cancelled
37376167450  21:29:20  cancelled
37376159449  21:29:16  cancelled
```

GitHub keeps only **one pending run** per concurrency group, so each dispatch evicted the one waiting behind it. `cancel-in-progress: false` protects the *running* job, not the queue — which is the part I had wrong when I wrote the workflow.

## The fix

An **"all combos (sequential)"** option that loops inside a single run, so a full sweep is one dispatch rather than eight. A single combo resolves to a one-line list, so the seed step has one code path either way.

Two robustness points while in there:

- **One combo failing no longer abandons the rest.** A later combo may have plenty of room even if this one is saturated or its upload failed. Failures are counted and the step still exits non-zero, so a partial sweep isn't reported green.
- **`timeout-minutes` raised to 355** for the worst case. Note GitHub caps a job at 360, so eight combos at 3000s each *cannot* finish — a full sweep wants a smaller `seconds`, which is what the option is for. Called out in a comment.

5×5 and 6×6 are in the sequential list but still out of the nightly rotation: a deliberate sweep may as well confirm they're still saturated, where a nightly slot would just spend 50 minutes doing so.

Both workflows now document the pending-run behaviour so it isn't rediscovered the same way. `seed-dev-engines.yml` has the identical bug but no sequential option — it's dev-only and its comment says to dispatch one at a time.

## Verification

- Combo resolution, the read loop, the six-day rotation and the unknown-combo error path all exercised in a shell harness.
- Failure tolerance confirmed: a failing middle combo doesn't stop later ones, and the step still exits 1.
- All three `run:` blocks pass `bash -n`; no tabs in either YAML file.

Not run in CI yet. Worth one `all combos (sequential)` dispatch at `seconds: 60` after merge — that also finishes the interrupted sweep, since Tangled 8×8 (4 puzzles) and the Original combos never got their test run.

author: pputra
body:
…rce_arns and filter normalization; structured COH validation errors

Compute Optimizer:
- Add resource_arns to look up recommendations for specific resources via each operation's ARN filter, resolving the region from the ARNs.
- Normalize filter keys, names, and values for every operation against per-operation accepted values (from the botocore model where the filter accepts the whole enum), echo applied_filters, and reject a bare Finding on RDS as ambiguous (derived from the model's filter names).
- Return structured errors for InvalidParameterValueException (with valid_filters when a filter was rejected) and for local checks on max_results and account_ids.
- Add order_by to get_idle_recommendations, defaulting to SavingsValueAfterDiscount descending.
- Surface more recommendation fields and the response-level errors list.

Cost Optimization Hub:
- Give the 12 local validation errors top-level error_type, operation, and service, and use the shared service-name and operation constants in every handle_aws_error call.

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD041 MD043 -->
Fixes

## Summary
                                                                                                                                                
### Changes                                                                                                                                               
**Compute Optimizer (`compute-optimizer` tool)**

- **`resource_arns`**: new optional parameter to look up recommendations for specific resources. It takes a JSON array of ARNs or a single bare ARN, and isent as each operation's ARN filter (`instanceArns`, `autoScalinunctionArns`, `serviceArns`, or `resourceArns` for RDS and idle).The region is taken from the ARNs when `region` is omitted. ARNs spanning multiple regions, or in a different region than `region`, are rejected.         - **Filter normalization for every operation** (previously idle alues`), names (case- and singular/plural-insensitive), and values (case- and underscore-insensitive, so a returned `OVER_PROVISIONED` can be passed back as `Overprovisioned`) are mapped to the spelling the API expects. The accepted values per operation come from the botocore service model where the filter accepts the whole enum. Where the API accepts only part of the enum, they're listed explicitly; I checked those lists against the live API. Tag filters are left as given, and unrecognized names and values pass through unchaso the service stays the authority. The response echoes the sent.
- **Ambiguous filter names:** RDS has no plain `Finding` or `FindingReasonCode` filter, only instance and storage variants. A plain one is rejected locally with the choices listed. The choices are derived from the botocore model's filter names rather than hardcoded.                                            - **Structured errors:** `InvalidParameterValueException` now re `operation`, `service`, `request_id`, and `http_status`, plus`submitted_filters` and `valid_filters` when the service reports a filter problem, since its message names neither the rejected value nor the valid set. New local checks also return a structured `validation_error`:
  - `max_results` above the API limit (1000, or 100 for idle)
  - more than one entry in `account_ids` (the API accepts one)
  - `order_by` on a non-idle operation
- **`order_by` for `get_idle_recommendations`:** `{"dimension": "SavingsValue"|"SavingsValueAfterDiscount", "order": "Asc"|"Desc"}`, matched              case-insensitively. The default is `SavingsValueAfterDiscount` dholds the largest savings.
- **More response fields:** finding reason codes, current performance risk, inferred workload types, migration effort, GPU info, savings after discounts, utilization metrics, lookback period, effective recommendation pp capacity, EBS volume configuration, and RDS cluster and storagedetails. EC2, ASG, EBS, RDS, and ECS responses also carry the API's response-level `errors` list.
- **Tool description:** now lists the accepted filter names and values per operation, and describes `get_rds_recommendations` as covering RDS and Aurora.

**Cost Optimization Hub (`cost-optimization-hub` tool)**

- **Structured local validation errors:** the 12 parameter checke calling the API now carry top-level `service`, `operation`, and`error_type`, matching the shape `handle_aws_error` returns:
  - missing or invalid `group_by`
  - missing `recommendation_id`
  - invalid `order_by`, `granularity`, efficiency-metrics dates, or `ranking_mode`
  - unsupported operation (`error_type: 'invalid_operation'`; the other checks use `validation_error`)

  The legacy `status`/`data`/`message` payload is preserved.
- **Shared constants:** every `handle_aws_error` call uses the shared `COST_OPTIMIZATION_HUB_SERVICE_NAME` (moved to `utilities/constants.py`) and the `OPERATION_*` constants instead of string literals.

Both tools build their errors with the `error_type`/`operation`/`service` keyword arguments that #4716 added to `format_response`.

**Tests:** new coverage for ARN parsing and region resolution, filter normalization per operation, ambiguous names, idle `order_by`, the new local limits, structured `InvalidParameterValueException` errors, response fields, botocore-model consistency of the filter tables, and the COH local-validation errors (12-case parametrized test). New code has 100% line and branch coverage.

### User experience

**Before**

- Looking up one resource meant paging the full recommendation l
- Filter values had to match the API's exact casing. `{"name": "Finding", "values": ["overprovisioned"]}`, or passing back the `OVER_PROVISIONED` the EC2 API returns, failed with a bare `InvalidParameterValueException: Invalid filter value.` that named neither the bad value nor the valid ones.
- On RDS, a natural `Finding` filter failed the same way.
- Idle results came back in no particular order.
- COH validation errors had no `error_type`/`operation`/`service`, so they couldn't be told apart from successful responses.

**After**

- `resource_arns='["arn:aws:ec2:us-east-1:123456789012:instance/i-0abc"]'` returns just that instance, and the region is inferred.
- `overprovisioned` and `OVER_PROVISIONED` are sent as `Overprovisioned`, and `applied_filters` shows what was sent.
- A filter value the API still rejects comes back with `submitted_filters` and `valid_filters`, so the caller can fix the request in one step.
- A plain `Finding` on RDS is rejected locally with `filter_name_choices: ["InstanceFinding", "StorageFinding"]`.
- Idle results are sorted by savings after discounts, highest first.
- COH validation errors, e.g. `{"status": "error", "service": "Cost Optimization Hub", "operation": "list_recommendation_summaries", "error_type": "validation_error", ...}`, can be classified like AWS errors.

## Checklist

If your change doesn't seem to apply, please leave them unchecked.

* [x] I have reviewed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/awslabs/mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
* [x] I have performed a self-review of this change
* [x] Changes have been tested
* [x] Changes are documented

Is this a breaking change? (Y/N) N. All new parameters and response fields are additive, and the legacy error payloads are preserved. Behavior changes to note:

* idle results are now sorted by default;
* `max_results` above the API limit and multiple `account_ids` are rejected locally (the API rejects them as well);
* the Compute Optimizer `InvalidParameterValueException` response now uses the structured error shape (the idle-specific keys are kept).

## Summary

```diff
 verify(name, birthDate, familyNameSpelled)
   candidates = same DOB, surname sounds alike, given initial matches
-  if one candidate matches the text exactly -> verified(that one)

author: andymai
body:
## Summary

Fit tests can now print as an outline-only ring around each cutout. Its inside edge marks where the cutout wall will be, including clearance. The full card can also be printed at 0.2mm, one layer.

Outline height ranges from 0.2mm to 2mm in 0.2mm steps. The default is three layers, 0.6mm, so it can be lifted from the plate in one piece. One layer remains available for checking fit directly on the build plate.

## Why

The requested workflow only needs the cutout’s 2D shape and clearance. Previously, the reporter reduced the 1mm full card to one layer in the slicer, then placed the real tool on it while it remained on the build plate. The new “Outline only” choice supports that check directly.

## Changes

- Added a “What to print” choice with “Full card” and “Outline only”.

- Outline rings are 0.8mm to 2.4mm wide in 0.4mm steps, defaulting to 1.2mm. Width is measured outward from the cutout edge. Overlapping cutouts share one outline, and rings stop at the board edge.

- Entry chamfers, engraved labels, label sockets and text cutouts are omitted. Open-side channels and knife-slot exits are included in bed checks, piece counts and seam placement.

- The outline is traced from the generated bin rather than rebuilt from the cutout list. The bin is sliced just under its fill surface and compared with the same body without cutouts. This gets every cutout kind and option through one path, including groups, arrays, rotation, paths, imported mesh pockets and open sides. The footprint is offset, clipped and extruded in Manifold’s 2D domain.

- STL and 3MF exports are supported. STEP is disabled with an explanation. Oversized outlines export as ZIP pieces, with seams planned around every ring (channel rails included); a seam that cannot move clear is counted as blocked and shows the warning. Pieces containing no ring are skipped.

- Shared path and polygon outline utilities now give planning, builders, seam planning and cost estimates the same corrected opening sizes. The dialog includes an outline-specific cost estimate.

- Full-card thickness now starts at 0.2mm, adjusted for the deepest entry chamfer so its bottom layer remains straight wall. Cards below 1mm omit the underside stamp and its tip.

- Added worker, planning and options modules, with 12 new strings translated across all 15 locales.

## Risk

Scenario tests measure exported ring edges against generated holes and described openings, including arrays, groups, paths, imported meshes and open sides. Shared utility, bin-designer and generation suites pass: 677 files and 8680 tests. Full generator tests pass: 377 files and 3792 tests. Typecheck passes, and a representative top view was checked visually.

No bin geometry changed, so no mesh cache version bump is needed. Total JS (gzip, one locale) reads 2,349,787 B on this branch's base and 2,354,754 B on the branch, so the feature adds 4,967 B, its own code. Main now reads 2,350,355 B, which would put the merge about 300 B over the 2,355,000 B limit, so the limit is raised to 2360 kB. That also covers the open PRs #4525 (about 1.9 kB) and #4527 (about 0.8 kB).

Fixes #4517

author: kaylannesatiro
body:
## Resumo

Implementa a HU-011 no recorte de consulta e visualização do histórico de ciclos, incluindo endpoint autenticado, paginação, resumo estatístico, classificação de confiança, tela, componentes reutilizáveis e integração frontend/backend.

A branch foi sincronizada com `origin/develop`. Foram resolvidos conflitos em `container.js`, `App.js`, `createAppServices.js` e `createAppServices.test.js`, preservando tanto o histórico de ciclos quanto as alterações recentes no fluxo de anticoncepcionais.

## Origem da mudança

- [x] História de Usuário prevista no documento de requisitos
- [ ] Issue relacionada: Closes #
- [x] Correção ou manutenção técnica sem Issue
- [ ] Mudança não prevista no documento de requisitos

### História de Usuário entregue

**HU-011: Visualizar Histórico de Ciclos**

Como pessoa autenticada, deseja visualizar uma lista de seus ciclos passados com suas respectivas durações para acompanhar a regularidade ao longo do tempo.

Critérios contemplados neste PR:

- consulta somente dos ciclos pertencentes à pessoa autenticada;
- ordenação decrescente pela data de início;
- apresentação de início, término ou estado em andamento;
- apresentação da duração da menstruação e duração do ciclo;
- indicação não dependente somente de cor para estimativas incertas;
- resumo com mediana do ciclo, mediana da menstruação, quantidade registrada e nível de confiança;
- carregamento incremental por cursor;
- estado vazio com orientação para acesso ao calendário;
- estados de carregamento, erro inicial e falha em página adicional;
- ações acessíveis de editar e excluir expostas em cada cartão.

Permanecem fora da conclusão integral da HU:

- atalhos definitivos a partir de Home, Calendário e Parâmetros do Ciclo;
- integração real das ações de editar e excluir com as HU-009 e HU-010;
- abertura real do Calendário pelo estado vazio.

Essas ações ainda aparecem como alertas provisórios em `App.js`.

### Contexto adicional

A interface do histórico foi inicialmente construída antes da disponibilidade dos cálculos consolidados de previsão e confiança. A etapa final incorporou somente os utilitários necessários para calcular as métricas no backend, sem importar telas ou fluxos não relacionados da branch de previsão.

Também foi incluída uma correção pontual na exportação do ícone `NotePencilIcon`, necessária para preservar o funcionamento de `ProfileField` após a integração do catálogo compartilhado de ícones.

A branch recebeu posteriormente as alterações atuais de `develop`, incluindo a edição e remoção de anticoncepcionais. Os conflitos foram resolvidos preservando os serviços, rotas, rate limits e testes dos dois fluxos.

## Tipo de mudança

- [x] `feat`: nova funcionalidade
- [x] `fix`: correção de defeito
- [x] `refactor`: alteração interna sem mudança de comportamento
- [x] `test`: criação ou manutenção de testes
- [ ] `docs`: documentação
- [ ] `build` / `ci`: dependências, build ou automação
- [ ] `chore`: manutenção
- [ ] Mudança incompatível (*breaking change*)

## Áreas afetadas

- [x] Frontend (React Native / Expo)
- [x] Backend (Node.js / Express)
- [x] API / contrato HTTP
- [ ] Banco de dados / Prisma / migração
- [x] Autenticação / autorização / consentimento parental
- [ ] E-mail / comunicação externa
- [ ] Armazenamento local / SecureStore
- [x] UI / design system
- [x] Acessibilidade
- [ ] Documentação
- [ ] Dependências / configuração / ambiente

## Contexto e motivação

### Situação anterior e necessidade

#### Ausência de uma consulta consolidada do histórico

O backend não disponibilizava um contrato próprio para recuperar o histórico completo da pessoa autenticada.

Em um cenário com vários ciclos registrados, o frontend não conseguia solicitar uma página ordenada nem obter de forma segura somente os registros vinculados à sessão atual.

Isso impedia a implementação da HU-011 e poderia levar à duplicação de regras de negócio no cliente ou a consultas sem limite.

Para quem usa o aplicativo, a consequência era não possuir uma tela confiável para acompanhar a regularidade dos ciclos.

#### Ausência de resumo estatístico integrado

A duração representativa dos ciclos, a duração da menstruação e o nível de confiança não eram calculados pelo fluxo do histórico.

Por exemplo, uma pessoa com seis ciclos completos não recebia a mediana dos intervalos recentes nem uma classificação consistente de confiança.

Calcular esses valores separadamente em cada tela poderia produzir resultados divergentes e transferiria regras sensíveis para o cliente.

A consequência seria a apresentação de informações inconsistentes sobre o ciclo menstrual.

#### Ausência de carregamento incremental

Não existia paginação específica para históricos extensos.

Carregar todos os ciclos de uma única vez aumentaria tráfego, memória e tempo de renderização. O impacto seria mais perceptível em celulares com poucos recursos ou em contas com muitos registros.

Sem paginação, a tela poderia demorar para abrir, consumir memória excessiva ou travar durante a renderização.

#### Ausência da experiência visual completa

O frontend não possuía tela dedicada, resumo, cartões individuais nem estados consistentes de carregamento, vazio e erro.

Também não existiam componentes compartilhados para ações por ícone e representação padronizada da confiança.

Isso impedia uma leitura clara e acessível do histórico e aumentava a repetição de estilos e comportamentos entre telas.

#### Integrações de navegação ainda parciais

O histórico atualmente é acessado pela aba de ciclos da navegação interna.

Os atalhos previstos em Home, Calendário e Parâmetros do Ciclo ainda não estão presentes neste diff. As ações de editar e excluir são expostas pelos cartões, mas o `App.js` ainda utiliza alertas provisórios.

Isso permite testar a consulta e a apresentação do histórico, porém não conclui os critérios relacionados aos fluxos das HU-009 e HU-010.

### Solução adotada

Foi criado o endpoint autenticado `GET /api/cycles/history`, que valida limite e cursor, consulta somente registros vinculados à identidade da sessão, ordena os ciclos do mais recente para o mais antigo e devolve um contrato paginado.

O backend calcula o resumo usando os registros recentes, mediana para duração do ciclo e da menstruação e classificação de confiança baixa, média ou alta. O frontend valida todo o envelope antes de disponibilizar os dados à interface.

A tela utiliza `FlatList`, páginas de 20 registros, lotes pequenos e janela reduzida. Os ciclos já exibidos são preservados quando uma página adicional falha. Requisições são canceladas durante o desmonte e chamadas concorrentes são bloqueadas.

Os componentes `CycleSummaryCard`, `CycleHistoryCard`, `ConfidenceBadge`, `ConfidenceStatusBar` e `IconButton` concentram apresentação, variantes, estados e acessibilidade.

### Alternativas consideradas

- Carregar o histórico inteiro em uma única requisição: descartado por aumentar tráfego, memória e tempo de renderização.
- Calcular resumo e confiança no frontend: descartado para manter uma única fonte de verdade e reduzir regras sensíveis no cliente.
- Usar média aritmética para todos os históricos: substituído pela mediana dos ciclos recentes para reduzir distorções causadas por valores extremos.
- Importar integralmente a implementação de previsão de outra branch: descartado; foram incorporados somente os utilitários necessários ao histórico.
- Manter o timeout em uma camada adicional de `fetch`: descartado durante o merge porque a versão atual de `develop` centraliza timeout e cancelamento em `apiClient`.

## Escopo

### Incluído

- Endpoint autenticado e paginado para o histórico.
- Validação defensiva de limite e cursor.
- Isolamento dos registros pelo identificador da sessão.
- Ordenação decrescente pela data de início.
- Numeração coerente dos ciclos entre páginas.

# Cambio de plataforma

## Objetivo

La validación programada de `main` falla desde el 2026-10-07 (ejecución de
las 11:50 UTC): `ERROR: the unconditional pinned Traefik warning did not
occur exactly once`. El canal `traefik:v3` avanzó a Traefik v3.7.14
(publicada el 2026-10-06), que incluye «Silence encoded characters warning
when some are disallowed»: el aviso de caracteres codificados solo se
registra si ningún entryPoint deniega alguno
([`cmd/traefik/traefik.go` en v3.7.14](https://github.com/traefik/traefik/blob/v3.7.14/cmd/traefik/traefik.go#L103-L113)).
Los cuatro entryPoints de `stacks/edge/static.yml.j2` los deniegan todos.

`scripts/validate-traefik-config.sh` y `scripts/validate-edge.sh` leen ahora
la versión de la imagen que arrancan (`org.opencontainers.image.version`) y
esperan el aviso una vez hasta v3.7.13 y ninguna desde v3.7.14. Una versión
con otro formato detiene el validador. El resto de comprobaciones (ningún
otro aviso, la deprecación de `underscoreHeadersStrategy` 0 o 4 veces) no
cambia.

Comprobado en el host arrancando la configuración renderizada con las dos
imágenes, con el mismo endurecimiento que el validador:

```text
v3.7.14 encoded=0 deprecation=4 other_warn=0
v3.7.13 encoded=1 deprecation=4 other_warn=0
```

Fuera de alcance: actualizar Traefik en producción. El servicio vivo sigue en
v3.7.13 por digest; `edge` es `autoupdate: false`.

## Riesgo y rollback

Solo cambian dos validadores y sus pruebas; nada se despliega. Revertir el
commit devuelve el fallo de CI.

## Evidencia

- [ ] `./scripts/validate-iac.sh`: lo ejecuta el CI de este PR con
  v3.7.14
- [x] `./scripts/lint.sh`: shellcheck `--severity=style` y markdownlint de

- [x] Se ensayó Ansible con `--check` o se justificó `N/A`: `N/A`, no toca
  Ansible
- [x] Se definieron validación posterior y disparadores de rollback: el CI
  de `main` vuelve a verde
- [x] El backup/restore requerido está probado o el cambio no toca estado

`tests/test_edge_contract.py` (`EdgeTraefikKnownNoticeTests`) prueba las dos
funciones con v3.6.20, v3.7.9, v3.7.13, v3.7.14, v3.7.15, v3.8.0 y v3.10.1, y
que `""`, `3.7.14`, `v2.11.58`, `v3.7`, `latest` y `v3.7.14-rc1` fallan.
