author: atareao
body:
## Qué

Cada turno decide, **antes del bucle ReAct**, qué habilidades necesita y expone al modelo solo las herramientas de esas habilidades. Hoy se envían las **13 definiciones completas** y se **reenvían en cada iteración** (`agent.rs:737`): medido con `token_estimate`, **8.972 bytes / ~4.016 tokens** por petición.

```
mensaje → ¿qué skills?  →  (core ∪ skills activas) ∩ habilitadas  →  LLM
          (Jev, 1 llamada)      + fragmentos de prompt por skill
```

- **Catálogo cerrado de 8 skills** agrupando las 13 tools **con sus prerrequisitos** (`clima` incluye `geocode`; `lugares` incluye `geocode` y `reverse_geocode`), más un **core no enrutable** (`render_widget`, `get_current_time`). Un test de integridad exige **13/13** cubiertas: registrar una tool y olvidarla en el catálogo rompe los tests.
- **`SkillRouter`**: **una decisión por turno**, una pregunta `noul` por skill enrutable **habilitada** (no se pregunta lo que no se puede ofrecer), todas en **una llamada** a la Decisions API de Jev (`typesafe/jev-1.13`, pineado). Una selección vacía es un resultado legítimo: el turno es conversacional y solo se expone el core.
- **Fallo abierto garantizado** (el router **nunca** quita capacidades por un fallo suyo): apagado, sin `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, sin skills enrutables, error HTTP, timeout, respuesta **sin respuestas reconocidas** o umbral no finito → **todas las habilitadas** y prompt intacto. Cada caso tiene test.
- **Fragmentos de prompt por skill** (`SKILL_<ID>_PROMPT`): se inyectan **solo** para las skills activas, se omiten si están vacíos y **no se duplican** si el prompt base ya contiene su encabezado. El prompt de personalidad no se toca.
- **Configuración en `settings` con hot-reload y apagada por defecto**: `ROUTER_ENABLED=false`, `ROUTER_THRESHOLD=0.3`, `ROUTER_MODEL=typesafe/jev-1.13`, `ROUTER_TIMEOUT_MS`, `ROUTER_HISTORY_TURNS`, sembrados por migración idempotente que no sobrescribe valores del usuario.
- **Arnés de evaluación** (`valet-route-eval`): mide la **cobertura** de las herramientas realmente usadas usando `messages.tools_used` como verdad de referencia — **sin etiquetar nada** — más activaciones por skill, p50/p95, tokens y coste. Es el instrumento para fijar el umbral.
- **`GET /api/skills`**: el catálogo servido desde `catalog()`, para que la UI no lo duplique.
- **UI**: control del enrutador en «Herramientas» (interruptor, umbral, modelo, mapa de skills y core) y los fragmentos en «Prompts».

## Lo que **no** hace (deliberado)

- **No es una frontera de seguridad**: filtra lo que se *anuncia*; `registry.execute`, permisos y guardrails no cambian. Está escrito como requisito para que nadie lo confunda.
- **No toca el prompt de personalidad** ni el contrato SSE ni el flujo OIDC. Sin cambios de comportamiento con el router apagado.

## Verificación

`just check-all` → **EXIT=0**. Rust: **752** tests de lib + 13 del bin + integración (26 de migraciones, 12 de `/api/tools`…). Frontend: **306** tests, `tsc` limpio, `lint:ci` (`--max-warnings 0`) en 0.

TDD por grupos (RED verificado por CLI antes de cada GREEN: p. ej. `698 passed; 23 failed` con los 23 nuevos exactos; y en los dos arreglos de la auditoría se pegaron las salidas RED).

## Auditoría y hallazgos aplicados

`rust-reviewer` y `react-reviewer`. Lo relevante corregido:

- **Crítico** (Rust): una respuesta con `answers` vacío o solo ids desconocidos se leía como «selección vacía» → **reducía** el conjunto a solo el core. Ahora es fallo abierto. Con test.
- **Mayor** (Rust): `ROUTER_THRESHOLD="NaN"` pasaba el parseo (`"NaN".parse::<f32>()` tiene éxito) y desactivaba el enrutado en silencio. Ahora exige **finito ∧ [0,1]**; `ROUTER_TIMEOUT_MS=0` → default; `ROUTER_HISTORY_TURNS` acotado.
- **Mayor** (UI): el control mostraba valores **no guardados** al reabrir. Ahora es autocontenido (como `ToolsTab`) y se remonta en cada apertura.
- **Mayor** (UI): guardar el enrutador **descartaba ediciones sin guardar** de otras pestañas (reemplazaba la identidad de `settings`). Ya no toca el estado compartido.
- Menores: fallo abierto registrado con `warn!`, `skill_of_tool` usado por el arnés (informa **qué skill habría cubierto** cada herramienta que faltó), historial del arnés alineado con producción, un `tools_used` corrupto ya **no** cuenta como cubierto (no puede inflar la cobertura), a11y (etiqueta asociada al interruptor, sin `aria-label` redundante), `parseThreshold` alineado con la validación del backend.

## Estado del encendido — **pendiente y a propósito**

El enrutador se entrega **apagado**. La tarea **8.4** ("medición real y umbral fijado con los datos") queda **sin hacer**: el arnés está implementado y verificado en `--dry-run` (**66 turnos emparejados** en la BD de desarrollo), pero **no se ha ejecutado contra el servicio** porque requiere `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. Encender sin esa medición sería justo lo que el change evita.

Para medirlo: `cargo run --bin valet-route-eval -- --limit 200` (coste del orden de céntimos: Jev factura solo entrada a ~$0,042/M y cada turno son ~600 tokens).

## Limitación conocida de test

El `afterOpenChange` del `Modal` de antd **no dispara en jsdom** (rc-motion espera un `transitionend` que jsdom no emite), así que la regresión del reseteo al reabrir se cubre con el comportamiento observable equivalente —remontar el control— en lugar de un test dependiente de ese evento.

author: m-szymon
body:
Both latte workloads read their whole dataset into `ctx.data` during
`prepare`. latte deep-copies `ctx.data` into every worker thread, so
resident memory scaled with both the dataset size and `--threads` —
roughly 1 GB for a 51 MB vector file — which forced `--threads 1`, the
setting where the load is also slowest, since the parse ran serially in
`prepare` before the first insert. Large datasets were limited by the
client rather than by the server under test.

latte 0.50, already required here, provides what this needs: seekable
binary file handles and the `prepare_worker` hook, which exists so an
open file can be created per worker rather than passed through the copy.
`prepare` now indexes the file — the fbin header, or one byte offset per
text line — each worker opens its own handle, and `load` seeks to its row
and reads it. The per-row work moves out of serial `prepare` into the
cycles, which are spread across `--threads`.

Load phase, 50k x 256 vectors (51 MB) and a 107 MB / 200k-document corpus,
against a single-node ScyllaDB:

| | peak RSS `-t1` | wall clock `-t1 / -t4 / -t8` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| vector fbin, before | 1001 MB | 1.90 / 2.82 / 4.40 s |
| vector fbin, after | 20 MB | 0.76 / 0.33 / 0.26 s |
| vector text, before | — | 4.51 / 5.29 / 7.08 s |
| vector text, after | — | 3.54 / 1.19 / 0.80 s |
| fts, before | 926 MB | 2.09 / 2.45 / 3.48 s |
| fts, after | 51 MB | 1.80 / 0.93 / 0.83 s |

Faster at every thread count, including one: preloading never scaled with
`--threads` and got slower past four, because each worker built and held
its own copy.

Scope is the load phase only. `search` still loads its query and
ground-truth files up front — they are small, and file I/O inside the
measured path would add a side latency to reported query latency.
`recall_buckets.rn` is untouched and keeps the eager text loader, since it
reads one bucket at a time.

Behaviour worth knowing when comparing with older runs:

- An fts body containing a tab is now stored whole; it used to be
  truncated at the second tab, so BM25 results for such a corpus will
  differ from older baselines.
- Load-phase latency percentiles now include a synchronous per-cycle read,
  so they measure the client as well as the server. Read them as
  throughput; take latency from `search`, which does no file I/O.
- Malformed datasets fail at `prepare` where the failure would otherwise
  be silent (a line with no separator would quietly shrink the row count),
  and an empty dataset no longer divides by zero once per cycle.

Testing: the latte workloads are not exercised by CI, so this was verified
by hand against a single-node ScyllaDB plus vector-store — the extended
`fbin_dataset_test.rn` loader test, all three vector formats and the fts
corpus loaded end to end, and recall over a 200-vector set with exact
ground truth identical for `text`, `fbin` and `fbin_packed`.

Fixes: VECTOR-1033
Refs: VECTOR-759

author: worksahilca-jpg
body:
## What this changes

For the realtor team trial (founder, 2026-10-07: "Lets do it bro", drawings approved, "yes wait for trail"). His sales team gets 600 ad leads a month. Half never pick up and wait about two months for the next call. Everything is behind one switch on the Team page, **"Your team calls customers"**, which is off by default. With it off, nothing shows and nothing is recorded.

- **Call box** on each customer with a phone number: Call, then **No answer** or **Already spoke**.
  - No answer records the call and plans the next one a day later (it stops after three).
  - On the first one, it writes one fixed text: "Hi Priya, it's Sam from Maple Realty. I just tried to call you. When's a good time to talk?" The text is **held for an OK** and goes as a text. It's an email when no text number is connected.
  - Undo removes the call, the unsent text and the plan.
- **Today → Calls to make**, above the replies: calls that came due, and new customers with a number nobody has called or written to. Each card has No answer · Already spoke · Later (3 hours). A teammate sees their own customers and the unassigned ones.
- **Team → This week** (admins only): one sentence for the team, then each person's calls, who they spoke with, and meetings booked. Only someone who is calling and has no meetings gets the orange dot.
- **Data:**
  - New `CallAttempt` table, with RLS on, included in the export and erased with the business.
  - New fields `Business.teamCalls` and `Lead.nextCallAt`. The migration only adds things.

author: wingedsheep
body:
## Problem
With Geist of Saint Thalia ("Noncreature spells you cast cost {1} less") on the battlefield, casting a prepared creature's prepare-spell copy got no discount.

CR 722.3c: the exiled copy has **only** the prepare spell's characteristics, so it's a noncreature spell. But its cost went through `calculateEffectiveCostWithAlternativeBase`, which
- drops every `YouCast` / reduction modifier, and
- matches modifiers against the whole card's type line (Creature).

Every face cast shared that path, so the same bug hit Adventures / Omens (CR 715.3b), split halves (CR 709.3b) and modal DFC backs (CR 712.11c). The type mix-up also cuts the other way: a "noncreature spells cost {1} more" tax never applied to an Adventure.

## Fix
- `CostCalculator.calculateFaceCastCost` prices a face as a normal cast of that face: the face's characteristics, its own mana cost as the base, every modifier judged against the face. Commander tax is still looked up by the card (new `card` param on `calculateEffectiveCost`).
- Wired into `CastCostTotaller` (face casts + `MODAL_BACK_FACE`), the prepare-copy offer in `CastFromZoneEnumerator`, and the split-half / adventure / modal-back offers in `CastSpellEnumerator`.

## Tests
`GeistOfSaintThaliaScenarioTest`:
- Studious First-Year's Rampant Growth copy is offered at `{G}` and castable with one Forest.
- Minecart Daredevil cast as Ride the Rails is castable with one Mountain.

Not run locally (the fresh worktree build was still compiling) — relying on CI.

## Not in scope
CR 118.9d says cost reductions also apply to alternative costs, but `calculateEffectiveCostWithAlternativeBase` deliberately skips them, so reducers don't touch flashback / escape / warp / dash etc. Separate, wider change; follow-up.

author: charzl
body:
Draft, in the fork only. Prometheus side of #70248, using `prometheus_client` multiprocess mode ("design 1": one backend per exporter, chosen once at start).

### What it does

`metrics.exporter: prometheus` no longer goes through the OpenTelemetry SDK. Counters and histograms are `prometheus_client` metrics. Every process (master, MWorkers, minion job processes) writes into a shared directory; the main process adds the files up at each scrape and serves one `/metrics`.

- One series per metric and label set. No per-process label, nothing to `sum`.
- Values of exited processes stay in the total until the master stops, so counters do not go backwards.
- Observable gauges stay callbacks. They run in the serving process at scrape time (that is where Salt registers them), so they did not need to be rewritten.
- Metric names match the OTel exporter (`salt_jobs_completed_total`, `salt_job_duration_milliseconds_*`).
- The shared directory is a fresh temp dir per start (or `prometheus.multiproc_dir`, wiped at start). No stale files.
- OTLP and console exporters are untouched.

### Not in this PR

- The OTLP `service.instance.id` fix (that is saltstack/salt#70360).
- Windows (the new tests are skipped there; multiprocess mode is not verified on Windows).
- Compacting the files of exited workers. One 64 KiB file per exited worker pid stays until the master stops. They cannot just be deleted (counters would drop, which Prometheus reads as a reset); `prometheus_client` has no compaction for counters and histograms. Documented in `doc/topics/metrics/index.rst` and in the module docstring, with the way to do it if it ever matters.

### Behaviour changes to be aware of

- `get_meter()` returns `None` with this exporter.
- Output differs from the old OpenTelemetry Prometheus exporter: `service_name` / `resource_attributes` are still exposed on `target_info`, but the `otel_scope_*` labels are no longer added to each series. Dashboards that filter on `otel_scope_name` need a change. (Nothing in this repo's monitoring setup uses it; external dashboards are unknown.)
- If `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR` is already set in the environment, Salt logs a warning and uses its own directory.
- After a failed bind, processes forked later do not try again.
- Needs `prometheus_client` (already pulled in by `opentelemetry-exporter-prometheus`, so no requirements change here).

### Testing

Nothing was run locally. First run is this PR's CI:
- `tests/pytests/unit/utils/test_metrics_prometheus.py`
- `tests/pytests/functional/utils/test_metrics_prometheus_multiprocess.py` (3 forked workers + parent, real HTTP scrape)
- existing `test_prometheus_exporter_binds_listener` should still pass unchanged.

Not verified: a real master with real MWorkers and a Prometheus server.

author: meetayyab
body:
Stacked on **#190** (phone uniqueness) — base is `fix/duplicate-phone-signups`, so review only shows this work. Merge #190 first; GitHub will retarget this to `main` automatically.

Closes the two holes flagged in #190.

## 1. The email was never verified

`/api/auth/register` set **`emailVerified: true`** outright and **never sent a verification email**. `issueEmailVerificationOtp` was only ever called on the guest-upgrade path.

Consequences:
- The address was never proven — invented inboxes worked fine.
- Login refuses unverified accounts, but new signups were born verified, so it never bit.
- The daily spin is "verified members only" (`accountCanSpin`) — **that rule was doing nothing**.
- **6,315 of 6,582** non-guest accounts are "verified" without anyone reading an inbox.

Registration now sends the OTP and leaves the account unverified — the same flow a guest upgrade already uses.

## 2. The signup bonus had no check at all

It read `signupBonusEnabled` and paid out. So an address nobody owned still earned money.

**The bonus now moves to `/api/auth/verify-email`**, which already granted it for guest upgrades. It's now paid in exactly one place, only after the address has been read, and only once — `signup_bonus_granted_at` makes a replayed verification a no-op.

**Plus a per-IP cap:** at most **3 bonuses per address per rolling 30 days**. Three rather than one because families and flatmates share a connection. Going over **withholds only the bonus** — the account is still created and still verified. Refusing the account outright would cost more in support than the bonus is worth.

## What the data says

Counting by *registration IP* rather than by name or phone:

| | |
|---|---|
| Distinct IPs this person used | **19** |
| Accounts sharing those IPs | **57** |
| Points held on them | 3,066 |

That's more than the 45 found by phone, and far more than the 16 found by name.

## A correction worth noting

**`users` has no `ip_address` column.** Registration passes `ipAddress` to `createUser` and it is **silently dropped** — nothing by that name exists on the table. (I'd previously said the IP was recorded there; it isn't.)

The real record is the `user_ip_logs` row written on the same request, so the count joins through that. It was indexed only on `user_id`, so `0032` adds an address index. The count runs in **0.8ms** on staging, verified with `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` inside a transaction and rolled back.

## Client change (required, not optional)

`register.tsx` sent an ordinary signup to `/login`, which would now dead-end on *"verify your email first"*. It now follows the same path as a claimed guest, to `/verify-email`. The verification page **already** renders the welcome-bonus popup from that response, so the bonus is announced where it's actually granted.

## Also fixed in passing

The verify path credited bonus **points with no transaction row at all** — no audit trail. Both cash and points now write one, matching what registration used to do.

## Nothing is backfilled

Existing accounts keep their bonus and stay verified. `signup_bonus_granted_at` stays NULL for them, which reads as "never paid" — correct for the count, and harmless for idempotency since they're all already marked verified and can't reach verification again.

## Verification

- 12 new unit tests; full suite **417 passed / 34 files**
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: `server/routes.ts` **423 before, 423 after**; 0 in `shared/schema.ts`, `register.tsx` and both new services
- Migration `0032` applied against staging inside a transaction, index use confirmed by the planner, then rolled back — staging unchanged

author: delaanthonio
body:
## Summary

Forecasts, what-if, the optimiser and reverse stress need approved base, adverse and severely adverse assumptions for each bank. Until now, only our test data had them, so these tools refused to run for every real bank. This PR adds the backend for a governed register: a bank user proposes a dated set of assumptions, a different authorised user approves it, and every forecast records which approved version it used. A newly provisioned bank gets no values; it sees a plain "not computable until approved" state until it approves its own set.

This is PR 1 of 3, backend only. The dashboard workflow (draft, submit, approve, version history and provenance, and the NII tab reading a selected or edited run) and the extended #290 journey follow in the stacked PRs above this one.

## What changed

- **New `app/forecasting/` feature package** (the first in the CODEBASE_CONVENTIONS.md §5 layout): a bank-scoped `ForecastAssumptionVersion` register. Each version is one complete set: 3 scenarios × 7 drivers, with validated ranges.
- **Lifecycle API** under `/banks/{bank_id}/forecast/assumption-versions`: read the register, draft, revise, submit, approve, reject.
  - Drafting and revising need Forecasting edit authority; approving and rejecting need Forecasting approval authority plus the maker-checker condition.
  - The approver cannot be anyone who drafted, revised or submitted the version.
  - A rejection needs a note.
  - Approved and rejected versions are final.
  - Every step writes an audit event.
- **Effective dating by book date.** A run on date D uses the approved version with the latest effective date on or before D; ties go to the later approval. A correction can take effect before an already-approved future-dated version.
- **One open proposal per bank.** A bank can have at most one draft or submitted version awaiting a decision. This is deliberate: it stops two competing pending approvals for the same register.
- **Concurrent requests are serialised.** Edit, submit, approve and reject lock the version until commit, so a concurrent request cannot change a decided version.
- **Approval refreshes the live forecast.** It enqueues the existing live and BI refresh in the same transaction.
- **Forecast, what-if, optimizer and live forecast runs resolve only from an approved version.**
  - Custom overrides cannot bypass a missing approval.
  - Each run records `assumption_provenance` (version, effective date, approver) beside its snapshot, never inside the value-based `input_hash`, so earlier saved runs keep their inputs, hash and results.
  - Forecast, what-if and optimizer reads, and the scenario catalogue, expose that provenance.
- **Provisioning writes no assumption values.** Its new `forecast_assumptions` step names the missing approved set and the four-eyes path.
- **Migration `202610070084`** creates the empty register (with RLS) and the `regulatory_runs.assumption_provenance` column. Legacy `param_stress_shock` forecast rows are no longer read and are left untouched.
- **Generated OpenAPI schema and TypeScript client regenerated.** ARCHITECTURE.md ("Governed forecast assumptions") and the backend README document the rules.

Out of scope, by decision: governed author and approve for the liquidity `combined` and capital `severe` scenarios that reverse stress scales, now tracked in #368. Reverse stress therefore still refuses for a real bank until #368 lands.

Refs #342 (forecast presets governed here; reverse-stress scenarios move to #368), #343 (backend provenance; the dashboard display is in the stacked PR). #344 and #290 are delivered by the stacked dashboard and journey PRs.

## Why

The #290 forecasting journey found that a real bank could never run a forecast: assumptions came only from test fixtures, provisioning created none, and nothing let a bank author or approve them. Stress-testing assumptions must be governed: documented, independently reviewed and approved, and traceable to the results they produce (BCBS, *Stress testing principles*, October 2018, Principles 2 and 8). Maker-checker approval, effective dating and per-run provenance give each projection that audit trail. They also keep saved results reproducible.

## How it was tested

no user-visible change - screenshots not applicable

- **Before the pipeline:**
  - The full hermetic backend suite passed.
  - After rebasing onto #366, the architecture, forecasting, provisioning, seed and impersonation-boundary tests passed (1,980).
  - The Postgres migration and RLS-completeness tests passed.
  - basedpyright reported 0 errors, and the generated client was fresh.
- **In the no-mistakes pipeline:**
  - Review found real gaps and fixed them: revision actors could approve, lifecycle races, approval not refreshing the live forecast, and overrides bypassing approval.
  - Test, docs and lint passed.
  - All 13 live API scenarios below passed against disposable PostgreSQL 17 and MinIO with real JWT and scoped-binding authorisation.
- **CI:** every check is green on `23d13a73`. Storage contract first failed while pulling the MinIO image (registry rate limit), unrelated to this change, and passed on rerun.

### Live validation evidence

author: berendt
body:
Closes #1305

## Summary

The Horizon operator rendered `CACHES["default"]` without a `KEY_PREFIX`, so every dashboard on one Memcached read and wrote the same keys. Horizon keeps its Angular template-cache preload in a Django fragment cache inside a django-compressor block. A release that reads a fragment another release wrote finds no matching key in its own offline manifest, and every page (`/auth/login/` included) raises `OfflineGenerationError`. The dashboard answers HTTP 500 until the foreign entry expires (`NG_TEMPLATE_CACHE_AGE`, 30 days by default). PR #1303's `basic-deployment-2026-2` suite hits this next to the 2025.2 and 2026.1 suites.

This branch renders `KEY_PREFIX` as `horizon-` plus the first 12 hex characters of the SHA-256 of `spec.image.Reference()`. The prefix is scoped per image: two CRs on one image share a warm cache, and an image change starts with a cold one.

## Walkthrough, in commit order

### 1. `1f9b71cf1` feat(horizon): scope the Django cache KEY_PREFIX per image

- `operators/horizon/internal/controller/reconcile_config.go` adds `cacheKeyPrefix` and two constants, `cacheKeyPrefixStem = "horizon-"` and `cacheKeyPrefixHashLen = 12`. `defaultSettings` puts `"KEY_PREFIX": cacheKeyPrefix(horizon)` into `CACHES["default"]`. The renderer sorts dict keys, so the entry lands between `BACKEND` and `LOCATION`. The hash is 12 characters (the ConfigMap suffix uses 8) because a collision between two releases would bring the poisoning back. The function has no error path. A zero `ImageSpec` hashes `":"`.
- The prefix is a pure function of the spec, so the CRD and the ControlPlane projection do not change. Every existing Horizon CR gets a new content-addressed ConfigMap and rolls once when the fixed operator starts.
- `operators/horizon/api/v1alpha1/config_ownership.go` gives the `CACHES` owned key an `Impact` text. An `extraConfig["CACHES"]` override still wins, and the `ExtraConfigHealthy=False` condition (reason `OwnedKeysOverridden`) and the `ExtraConfigOwnedKeyOverride` event now say that the override drops the prefix.
- `reconcile_config_test.go`:
  - `TestReconcileConfig_RendersLocalSettings` asserts the full `CACHES` line.
  - `TestCacheKeyPrefix_DerivesFromImageReference` pins literal prefixes (table below), checks that a second call returns the same string, and checks that all five rows differ.
  - `TestReconcileConfig_SameImageRendersSameConfigMapName`: the same image gives the same ConfigMap name (the second render goes through the `AlreadyExists` path), and a tag change moves the name.
  - `TestReconcileConfig_CachesOverrideDropsKeyPrefixAndIsReported`: a LocMem override renders without `KEY_PREFIX`, and both the condition message and the Warning event name it.
  - `TestRenderLocalSettings_EmptyCacheSpecRendersLocationNoneWithKeyPrefix`: a `CacheSpec` with neither `clusterRef` nor `servers` still renders `"LOCATION": None` beside the prefix.

| Image reference | `KEY_PREFIX` |
| --- | --- |
| `ghcr.io/c5c3/horizon:2025.2` | `horizon-cb859537a8dc` |
| `ghcr.io/c5c3/horizon:2026.1` | `horizon-e3b48cc65c6f` |

| `ghcr.io/c5c3/horizon@sha256:38fee8a6` + 56 zeros | `horizon-2ac8c5c0813f` |
| zero `ImageSpec` (`":"`) | `horizon-e7ac0786668e` |

### 2. `a4f680465` test(e2e): assert the image-scoped KEY_PREFIX in the Horizon suites

Step 4 of `tests/e2e/horizon/basic-deployment` and `tests/e2e/horizon/basic-deployment-2026-1` used to check only that a `<cr>-config-` ConfigMap exists. It now reads the ConfigMap name from the Deployment's `config` volume, because the retention sweep keeps up to three historical ConfigMaps beside the current one. It then greps the suite's own literal: `horizon-cb859537a8dc` for 2025.2 and `horizon-e3b48cc65c6f` for 2026.1. Both suites run on the shared `openstack-memcached` in one leg, so a green leg shows two releases rendering two prefixes on one Memcached.

### 3. `fea27e937` docs(horizon): describe the image-scoped cache KEY_PREFIX

- `docs/reference/horizon/horizon-crd.md`: the `cache` row states the derivation and the tag-versus-digest limit. The `extraConfig` row names `CACHES` as a reported override that drops the prefix.
- `docs/reference/horizon/horizon-reconciler.md`: the Config row mentions the image-scoped `KEY_PREFIX`.
- `docs/reference/horizon/index.md`: a new design-decision bullet, "Cache keys: scoped per image", explains the `OfflineGenerationError` mechanism.
- `.claude/skills/debug-e2e-failure/SKILL.md` and `scripts/collect-e2e-failure.sh` gain a `shared-memcached-500` signature next to `shared-memcached-401`. No suite file contains `OfflineGenerationError`, so the collector pattern cannot match echoed script source.

## Deviations from the issue

- **CRD `cache` row wording.** The page already uses its one allowed antithesis ("rather than", line 62). The row therefore says "The prefix follows the spec and the operator never resolves the running digest: two builds pushed behind one tag share a prefix" in place of the issue's "The prefix follows the spec, not the running digest: …". It states the same tag-versus-digest limit.
- **CRD `extraConfig` row.** It reads "(for example `STATIC_ROOT`, `COMPRESS_OFFLINE`, or `CACHES`, whose override drops the image-scoped `KEY_PREFIX`)". This avoids parentheses nested inside parentheses.
- **Step 4 shell.** Both scripts pin `shell: bash` and start with `set -euo pipefail`. Chainsaw's default `sh` rejects `pipefail`, and without `set -e` the issue's `test -n "$cm"` guard would not stop the script. `grep -F` runs without `-q`, so grep drains kubectl's output and the pipe does not break under `pipefail`.
- **Collector signature row.** `.claude/skills/debug-e2e-failure/scripts/collect-e2e-failure.sh` is outside the issue's Affected Areas, but the skill's Notes require a collector row for every new pattern with a stable log literal. It is one line and can be dropped on its own.
- **Extra unit test.** `TestRenderLocalSettings_EmptyCacheSpecRendersLocationNoneWithKeyPrefix` gives the `cacheLocations` criterion a test of its own.
- **Commit trailers.** Each commit carries `On-behalf-of: @SAP` directly above `Assisted-by` and `Signed-off-by`. That is the repository's trailer convention.

## Open for the author

The self-review left two points for a decision:

1. **Floating tag.** The ControlPlane default projects the tag `cp.Spec.OpenStackRelease` (`operators/c5c3/internal/controller/reconcile_horizon.go:149`), and a tag pin defaults to pull policy `Always`. Two builds pushed behind one tag therefore share a prefix. The docs state this limit. The alternative raised in review hashes the image's `STATIC_ROOT/CACHE/manifest.json` at settings load.
2. **No HTTP 500 to 200 proof on this branch.** The behavioural proof is #1303's `basic-deployment-2026-2` suite once #1303 is rebased onto this fix. `Closes #1305` closes the issue when this PR merges, before that leg has run.

## Noticed but not touched

- `docs/reference/horizon/index.md:73` says "No events, no finalizer in v1", but the operator emits the `ExtraConfigOwnedKeyOverride` Warning event.
- The comment above the `const` block at `reconcile_config.go:27` ("Condition type and reason constants for ConfigReady.") also covers unrelated constants.
- `horizon-crd.md` and `horizon-reconciler.md` are over the style-guide em-dash, filler and slang budgets on main. This branch adds no new device to them.

author: markg981
body:
The endurance tool previously exercised API reads and plan queues only. Add `npm run load:resilience` to build a disposable two-tenant Docker installation and exercise real Chromium agents, BullMQ schedules, screenshot artifacts, worker/Redis restarts and agent reconnection. Reconcile accepted and scheduled IDs against paginated history, replay idempotency keys, verify retained artifact links and SHA-256 hashes, and observe stalled-job redelivery before deciding the verdict.

Controlled worker restarts use SIGTERM and require every run to complete. The separate `--worker-restart crash` diagnostic expects `error/worker_lost` only for the run observed active before SIGKILL, preserving its ID without replay. Reports explicitly distinguish a passed crash diagnostic from successful continuation. Duplicate or malformed partial results, missing artifacts, unexpected failures and deadlines still fail the tool. The existing platform recovery policy is unchanged.

Validation:
- 8 resilience-tool unit tests, 24 existing endurance tests, 35 recovery/state-machine tests and 13 Collaudo tests passed.
- `npm run check`, documentation build and code review passed.
- Real graceful scenario: 14/14 completed runs, 42 downloadable artifacts, no lost or duplicate IDs; worker recovery 34.3 s, Redis recovery 36.4 s.
- Real crash scenario: 13 completed runs and exactly one expected `worker_lost`, 39 downloadable artifacts, no lost or duplicate IDs; crash detection 131.5 s. This does not certify continuation of the interrupted run.
- Both disposable stacks cleaned up. Subsequent validation-only hardening has unit regression tests and offline checks against the retained real-run IDs, artifact hashes/links and deadlines; Docker was not rerun for those assertions alone.

EN/IT documentation and Collaudo OPS-32–OPS-35 are updated; manual cases remain Da eseguire. The new Node.js 22 `resilience-tool` CI job runs the unit checks. CI on the final head is pending, so this PR is draft.

The release image hardening now uses three APT download retries and 30-second HTTP/HTTPS timeouts. Index updates fail on any repository error. This addresses the worker CI failure caused by dropped Ubuntu mirror connections while preserving pinned OpenSSL versions and security gates.

Additional validation: all 40 release tests passed; the full local Dockerfile.worker build passed, including a freshly executed hardening layer that installed the pinned packages.

author: jfb112697
body:
## Summary

Serein's microphone suppression offered RNNoise and WebRTC. This adds **DeepFilterNet** ([Rikorose/DeepFilterNet](https://github.com/Rikorose/DeepFilterNet), DeepFilterNet3) as a third, separate choice under **Voice & Video → Custom → Noise suppression**.

- `NoiseSuppression::DeepFilterNet` runs in the existing worker-owned chain after AEC, in the same slot as RNNoise, before AGC, gain and the sensitivity gate. Calls and the microphone test share it.
- The **Voice Isolation** profile is unchanged (still RNNoise). DeepFilterNet is opt-in through Custom, because it costs more CPU, adds latency and is unverified on live calls.
- Mute, device and security resets restore the model from a pristine copy, so look-ahead and recurrent history holding earlier microphone audio is dropped without reloading.
- Extensions: `suppression` accepts and reports `deepfilternet` (SDK docs updated).
- crates.io `deep_filter` stops at 0.2.5 (2022) with no inference runtime or model. The upstream Rust crate and DFN3 model are vendored in `vendor/deepfilternet` at commit `d375b2d` with **unmodified source** and a trimmed manifest, wired through `[patch.crates-io]` like the other vendored crates. `vendor/deepfilternet/SEREIN-PATCH.md` records every change.
- The reference CLI stage thresholds (−15/35/35 dB) are used instead of the library defaults. With the defaults, an offline check on real speech showed the stateful decoders being skipped mid-speech and output quality falling below the input.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask check` passes on the rebased branch (format, strict Clippy, workspace tests, `--no-default-features` check, policy).
- New test `audio::tests::deepfilternet_removes_noise_and_resets_history`: at least 10 dB noise reduction and bit-identical output after a reset.
- `cargo run -p discord-voice --example echo` now runs its noise/bypass assertions for both RNNoise and DeepFilterNet. The "voiced signal survives" assertion is RNNoise-only: DeepFilterNet silences that stationary synthetic tone as non-speech.
- `debug_processing_check` covers DeepFilterNet inference and history reset.
- Local, uncommitted offline check with upstream's sample speech and noise recordings (Creative Commons, not redistributed here): clean speech passes at 0.0 dB energy change; mixed speech+noise SI-SDR improves from 0/5/10 dB to roughly 10/15/18 dB with one noise recording and 13/16/19 dB with white noise; output delay is 1440 samples (30 ms).
- `cargo xtask package` succeeds for baseline and branch (NSIS unavailable locally, so no installer).

**Not verified:** live Discord calls, a physical microphone, macOS and Linux builds, slower CPUs, perceived quality. No microphone or account was used.

## Before / after

Synthetic `--demo --demo-settings=voice` on Windows, 1120×760, dark. Voice controls are read-only in the offline preview, so the after image uses a new demo-only flag, `--demo-deepfilternet`, that preselects Custom with DeepFilterNet. The baseline has no such preset and shows the unexpanded profile list.

| Before (baseline `c5e50e77`) | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://github.com/jfb112697/Serein/blob/d3a50317553a2ac31449964a432b4b5fa9727dd2/docs/pr-evidence/deepfilternet/before.png?raw=true) | ![after](https://github.com/jfb112697/Serein/blob/d3a50317553a2ac31449964a432b4b5fa9727dd2/docs/pr-evidence/deepfilternet/after.png?raw=true) |

## Performance

Windows 11 Pro, Ryzen 7 7800X3D, 32 GB, rustc 1.98.1; `cargo xtask package` in separate worktrees and target directories.

| Metric / method | Baseline `c5e50e77` | After | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Standard voice-enabled executable | 85,833,728 B | 110,105,088 B | **+24,271,360 B (+28.3%)** |
| Installed `dist` | 90,024,844 B | 114,323,454 B | +24,298,610 B (+27.0%) |
| ZIP of `dist` (Python deflate) | 49,948,608 B | 63,371,697 B | +13,423,089 B (+26.9%) |
| Capture chain per 20 ms frame, RNNoise (median, 3 runs × 529 frames) | 0.184–0.186 ms | unchanged path | — |
| Capture chain per 20 ms frame, DeepFilterNet | n/a | 0.86–0.89 ms median, 0.93–1.32 ms p99 (4.3–4.7% of real time) | new |
| Selecting DeepFilterNet (model load on the audio worker) | n/a | 242–274 ms once | new |
| Added microphone latency | RNNoise 10 ms | DeepFilterNet 30 ms | +20 ms when selected |

Timings are elapsed single-thread component times from an offline harness, not process CPU. Process memory, whole-app CPU and startup are unmeasured. Details are in `docs/performance.md`.

## Risks / blockers

- **Binary size:** +24 MB for every build, selected or not (tract ONNX runtime plus the embedded 8 MB model). Voice has no feature flag here, so this is the main trade-off to decide on.
- **Repository size:** the model adds a 7.98 MB binary to git history.
- **Model load blocks the audio worker** for about a quarter second when DeepFilterNet is selected or a call starts with it selected, which can drop a few frames once. The model type is not `Send`, so it cannot be built on another thread without moving inference there too.
- **Dependencies:** 53 new locked packages. tract is pinned to `=0.21.4` (upstream's locked version; newer 0.21.x do not compile with the unmodified source). `tract-core` has debug assertions disabled in the dev profile because its debug-only graph name check rejects this model. `deny.toml` gains a CC0-1.0 exception for compile-time `tiny-keccak`. `cargo deny`/`cargo audit` are not installed locally, so the license and audit CI jobs are untested.
- **Notices:** DeepFilterNet and tract license texts are retained; texts for the remaining new support crates are not yet, as noted in `PROVENANCE.md`.
- **SDK wiki:** not synced. This PR comes from a fork without wiki access.
- A profile saved with DeepFilterNet will not deserialize in an older build.

author: koala-man-64
body:
Rudy decided on 2026-10-07 that agents never force-push, `--force-with-lease` included. Once a branch is pushed, agents merge the base branch into it instead, so an approved PR always covers exactly what merges. His global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` already says so, but the installed guard (f715939) still allowed `--force-with-lease`, and one such push went through today. This PR makes the guard enforce the rule. It is independent of #277.

## Guard (`pre_tool_use_bash_guard.py`)
- **Denied push options:** `git push` and `git send-pack` with `--force`, `-f` (also bundled, as in `-uf`), any `--force*` option, `+refspec`, `--mirror`, `--prune` or `--all`/`--branches`. Each long option also matches any prefix git accepts, through `long_option()`. `--force*` covers `--force-with-lease`, with or without a ref, and `--force-if-includes`.
- **Denied forcing configuration:**
  - `git -c remote.<r>.push=+…` or `-c remote.<r>.mirror[=true]`;
  - `git config` writing either setting;
  - `git remote add --mirror[=push]`;
  - a forcing setting already configured for the pushed remote, or for any remote on a bare push. The guard reads it with `git config --get-regexp`.
- **Ask:** deleting a remote branch (`--delete`, `-d`, `:ref`) that is neither checked out here nor merged into the base branch. Protected branches stay denied.
- **Allow:** plain pushes of the task branch, `--no-force-with-lease`, deleting the current or a merged branch, `git remote add --mirror=fetch`.
- The deny message tells agents to merge the base branch in, not to use `--force-with-lease`.

## Profile
- `profile/claude/CLAUDE.md`: the git line is synced to Rudy's global wording; the file now matches `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` exactly.
- The `strict-branch-and-merge-discipline` skill and the README describe the new rule.
- `setup-manifest.json` and `settings.template.json` gain `*--force-*` deny twins for Bash and PowerShell, with and without `-C`, as a text-rule backstop. The live `~/.claude/settings.json` is not changed here.
- **Not changed:** the Codex profile still recommends `--force-with-lease`. It belongs to the Codex guard's owner.

## Validation
- `python -m pytest -q` in `profile/claude/hooks`: 278 passed. New coverage is in `NoForcePushTests`, with every force form, aliases, wrappers, config forms, existing config, deletes and the allowed pushes. Three old expectations were reversed: `--force-with-lease` is now denied, and so is `--force-if-includes` combined with it. `--delete` of a branch neither checked out nor merged now asks.
- `agentic-ide-setup/tests`: 17 failures. `origin/main` fails the same 17 in this shell (`%ComSpec%` is not set). They are unrelated to this change.
- Independent security review by Sonnet:
  - Round 1 returned NO-GO on three gaps: option prefixes for `--mirror`, `--all` and `--branches`, a valueless `-c ….mirror`, and push configuration already in place. All three were fixed in 858b8e0.
  - Round 2 returned **GO**.

## Accepted residual risk
- `include.path` config files.
- `--config-env` and `GIT_CONFIG_*`, which ask rather than deny.
- Dynamic arguments and other interpreters.
- A force push after an unresolvable `cd`, which asks.
- Conservative false positives: `-c remote.*.push=+…` on non-push subcommands, case-insensitive remote names, and a bare push when any remote has forcing config.

Not installed into `~/.claude/hooks-release`; merge and install need Rudy's go-ahead.

body:
## Summary
- stop writing the app log to a shared rotating file
- emit JSON logs to stdout for the RPi app services
- ingest backend/huey/bot journal entries in Alloy instead of tailing log.json

## Why
The previous setup used a shared RotatingFileHandler with multiple processes writing to the same file. That caused rollover races and inconsistent file ordering, so Grafana could miss log windows and the backup files did not represent a clean timeline.

## Changes
- update Django logging config so RPi app logs are JSON on stdout
- remove the file-based Alloy tail for /var/log/mainframe/log.json
- route backend/huey/bot logs through journald and parse their JSON payloads

- `wix-redirecciones-import.csv`: las mismas 137 redirecciones en dos columnas para importar en Wix (verificar el formato antes).
- `titulos-y-descripciones.csv`: títulos y descripciones nuevos para 25 páginas (≤60 y 120–160 caracteres). Confirmar con el cliente los datos que no estén en el sitio.

## Hallazgos principales
- 103 de 104 URLs con tráfico de selvamayatours.com dan error 400 (375 clics en 16 meses).
- 91 URLs de jaguarmayatours.com dan 404, sobre todo `/product-page/…` de la tienda anterior de Wix (256 clics y fragmentos de producto).
- 631 de 1.171 clics (54 %) llegan hoy a una página con error.
- jaguarmayatours.com tiene 2,1 veces más clics que selvamayatours.com; los datos no respaldan invertir la dirección de dominio.
- El correo de @selvamayatours.com sigue en el hosting cPanel antiguo (riesgo si se cancela).
- Competencia (datos públicos y Similarweb, solo estimaciones): solo Tikal Go está claramente por delante en tráfico; los otros dos están en la misma banda que Selva Maya. Similarweb sobreestima a Selva Maya ~8 veces frente a Search Console, y el HTML lo advierte.

## Notas
- Auditoría de solo lectura: no se modificó Wix, DNS, correo ni el hosting. Respaldo del hosting hecho fuera del repo.
- Solo agrega la carpeta `auditoria/`; no toca las páginas del sitio.

author: danfiedler-msft
body:
## Summary

This PR pins GitHub Actions to full-length commit SHAs for improved security and reproducibility and adds a 7 day cooldown to Dependabot configuration for GitHub Actions. This work is described in more detail at https://aka.ms/action-pinning.

## Why?

Pinning actions to commit SHAs prevents supply-chain attacks where a tag could be moved to point to malicious code. This is a recommended security best practice per the [GitHub Actions security hardening guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions).

This change mitigates the risk of tag retargeting to malicious code as seen in incidents like the [tj-actions/changed-files action compromise](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/harden-runner-detection-tj-actions-changed-files-action-is-compromised) or [codfish/semantic-release-action compromise](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/supply-chain-compromise-codfish-semantic-release-action) and improves the integrity and reproducibility of the CI/CD pipeline.

## What changed?

**Action pinning:** Third-party action references in `.github/workflows/` that used mutable tag-based references (e.g., `actions/checkout@v4`) have been updated to full-length commit SHAs with a version comment (e.g., `actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`) using the [pinact](https://github.com/suzuki-shunsuke/pinact) tool. References that were already pinned to a SHA, or that used immutable release tags, were left unchanged.

**Dependabot configuration:** `.github/dependabot.yml` has been updated to ensure a `github-actions` package-ecosystem section is present with a `cooldown` configuration (`default-days: 7`). If the file did not exist, it was created. If a `github-actions` section already existed, only the `cooldown` block was added or its `default-days` value was increased to 7 if it was lower. The 7-day cooldown provides a window for the community to detect and report compromised releases before they are automatically proposed as updates, reducing exposure to supply-chain attacks via newly published malicious versions.

## Is this safe to merge?

Yes. The pinned SHAs correspond to the same commits that the existing tags pointed to. No behavioral changes in action execution are introduced. You can verify the pinned SHA value using the GitHub REST API (e.g., the commit hash for `actions/checkout@v7` can be found in the `sha` property in the JSON response for `GET https://api.github.com/repos/actions/checkout/commits/v7`).

## Additional Information

For more information, please see https://aka.ms/action-pinning

author: nathan-swiftee
body:
The 2FA code was asked for at every sign-in, on the same computer, every day.

## What changes
- **Web:** the code step has "Remember this device for 30 days", ticked by default. Ticking it sets an httpOnly cookie (`<session cookie>_trusted`, 30 days). Within that time, a correct password alone signs in.
- **Mobile:** always remembered. `login/2fa` returns `trustedDeviceToken`. The app stores it in SecureStore (`AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY`) and sends it with the next `login`.
- **Schemas:** `loginInput.trustedDeviceToken`, `twoFactorCodeInput.rememberDevice`, `SessionGrant.trustedDeviceToken`.

## What a remembered device still cannot do
- **Skip the password.** It is only consulted after the password checks out.
- **Act as a session or a pending 2FA token.** `verify` refuses any token carrying `trust`, and `verifyPending` refuses anything not marked pending.
- **Vouch for another account.** It is bound to `sub`.
- **Survive a password or 2FA change.** It carries a fingerprint (sha256 of the password hash and the 2FA state) that is compared at every sign-in. Changing either forgets every remembered device at once, with no new table or migration.
- **Outlast 30 days**, or be forged.

It is kept through sign-out, which is the point.

## Checked
- New `check:trusted-device`, added to CI. It drives the real `AuthController` and `AuthService` through all of the above, for browsers and phones. Removing the session refusal makes it fail.
- `check:2fa-gate` still passes.
- API, web and mobile typecheck. Web tests 189, mobile tests 76.

Mobile needs a new build (or OTA) to start remembering phones. The web side is live on deploy.

body:
## Summary

On the **web build**, a failed **Share your work** (the library zip) now says:

> Could not share your work. Use the tC Mobile app to share it.

The native shell (APK / iOS app) keeps "Could not share your work. Try again." Nothing else changes: the failure mark stays, the space refusal (`storage`) keeps its own line, and the share flow, routing and timing are untouched.

This is #1332's copy-only fix for Share Book (#272), applied to the library scope by the same mechanism:

- `strings.shareAllFailedWeb` sits beside `shareAllFailed` in `src/lib/strings.ts`, as `shareBookFailedWeb` sits beside `shareBookFailed`.
- `libraryShareErrorText`'s `failed` arm (`src/components/share-error-copy.ts`) picks it with `isNativeShell()` (`hooks/share-target.ts`, `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()`), the same probe #1332 uses in `shareErrorText`. That covers both places the line appears: the storage banner's Notice and the share overlay's `libraryShareProgressText`, which delegates to it. It is **not** a user-agent read. The #490 guard (`tests/share-progress.test.ts`) is untouched and passes.
- #1332 added no helper, only the inline `isNativeShell()` choice, so this adds no helper either.

## Why

The library zip is sent as `application/zip` (`src/hooks/use-library-share.ts`), the same type as Share Book's. #1332 traced in Chromium source that `canShare()` never checks MIME type, and that Android's allowlist refuses the zip inside `share()` with `NotAllowedError`, which `classifyShareError` maps to `failed`.

**The Android failure for Share your work is an inference.** Nobody has run Share your work in an Android phone's browser (#1333 says the same). The reasoning is the shared zip type and #1332's Chromium trace. On the web build, the app pointer is also accurate for the other causes of `failed` (no Web Share, a transient refusal), so the wording holds even if Android turns out not to refuse it.

| Platform | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web build, Share your work `failed` | "Could not share your work. Try again." | "Could not share your work. Use the tC Mobile app to share it." |
| Native shell, `failed` | "Could not share your work. Try again." | unchanged |
| Either build, `storage` / `nothing` / `encoder` | — | unchanged |

## Issue

Refs #1333. **Not "Closes":** the issue's done-when needs an on-device confirmation, and this lane has not done one.

**On-device check (not done):** on an Android phone, open the per-PR or staging build in Chrome and tap the storage banner's Share your work. Expect the encode, then the new line with the failure mark. In the APK, Share your work should still open the native chooser.

## Risk tier

**T2.** Copy on the share path, chosen by a runtime platform probe. Matches #1332's tier.

## Tests (red first)

- `tests/library-share-copy.test.ts`: new case. In plain Node (the web build), `libraryShareErrorText("failed")` and `libraryShareProgressText(outcome("failed"), "failed")` give `shareAllFailedWeb`, which names the app and does not say "try again". With `Capacitor.isNativePlatform` stubbed to `true`, both give `shareAllFailed`. `storage` keeps `shareAllStorage` in both builds. The existing outcome and code tables now expect the web line for `failed`.
- `tests/storage-banner-o4.test.ts`: the rendered banner Notice for `failed` reads the web line.
- **Red:** with the tests written first, 4 tests failed, first with the string absent, then with the string present but no selection ("expected 'Could not share your work. Try again.' to be 'Could not share your work. Sharing yo…'").
- **Mutation:** with `isNativeShell()` inverted in `libraryShareErrorText`, the same 4 tests fail, including the native half. Restored.
- `npm run verify`: exit 0 (374 files passed, 4 skipped; 5082 tests passed, 25 skipped, 3 todo; build; test:dist 5 files, 56 tests passed).

## Version

No bump. AGENTS.md says a fix PR never touches the version, and #1332 did not bump it.
- Pre-push hook (check:prepush, test, build, test:dist): passed on the push of this head (5082 tests passed, 33 skipped, 3 todo; test:dist 56 passed). Two earlier push attempts failed on timeouts in timing-sensitive suites while container load average was ~35; a different set failed each time, and `tests/share-encode-steps.test.ts` passed 3/3 run alone. That those failures came from the load is an inference.

author: brentrager
body:
## Problem

Putting a widget at the top of the `/apps` dashboard needed a raw API call. `th smoo dashboard layout add` only appends below the grid, and there was no way to move a widget.

The web dashboard is a sortable flow grid (dnd-kit): it renders widgets in **array order** and recomputes x/y itself. So placement means reordering the saved array. Editing x/y alone does nothing, which is how the first manual attempt left the widget at the bottom.

## Change

- `th smoo dashboard layout move <widget> --to top|bottom` moves a widget already on the dashboard.
- `th smoo dashboard layout add <widget> --at top|bottom` places a new one. The default is still `bottom`.
- Both go through one `place()` function.
  - **Top:** first in the array, x 0 / y 0, every other widget shifted down by its height.
  - **Bottom:** last in the array, below everything else.

## Verification

Unit tests: move-to-top order and y-shift, move-to-bottom, and a missing widget fails loudly. The developer machine was out of disk, so CI runs them.

Same operation used live on the Smoo AI dashboard to put `cost_rollup` first.

author: alexcarpenter
body:
## Description

Stacked on #10111.

Turns on the stricter rules Fredrik flagged as errors in the `packages/mosaic` lint block: `no-explicit-any`, the five `no-unsafe-*` rules, `ban-ts-comment`, `no-floating-promises`, `no-misused-promises`, `await-thenable`, `only-throw-error`, `prefer-promise-reject-errors`, `use-unknown-in-catch-callback-variable`, `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` and `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`.

Hits are fixed at the source. No new bulk suppressions; the `create-actor.ts` assertion count drops from 9 to 8.

- `utils/errors.ts`, password errors: read API errors through the typed `ClerkAPIError` interface instead of the class, whose `meta` defaults to `any`. The picture controller uses a new `toGlobalError`.
- `css-vars.ts`: narrow floating-ui's untyped `alignSelectedItem` middleware data from `unknown`.
- `use-mosaic-environment.ts`: a type guard replaces the `@ts-expect-error` on `__internal_environment`.
- `use-reverification-with-state.ts`: the fetcher type is derived from `useReverification`'s parameter instead of restating its `any` constraint.
- `use-in-view.ts`: observer options are read from the latest-params ref, like `onChange` already was, so the ref callback stays stable.
- `create-actor.ts`, `jest-dom.d.ts`: `any` replaced with `unknown`.

Four disables remain, each with a reason:
- `user-button.tsx` (x2): `appearance` from `@clerk/shared` is an unresolved type until a framework augments `ClerkAppearanceRegistry`. It is passed through untouched.
- `machine/types.ts`: `invoke` needs a per-state output type. With `unknown`, typed `onDone` handlers fail to compile (checked with tsc).
- `use-render.tsx`: the `ref` on render props. This was already an intentional `any` with a SAFETY comment; the reason moved into the directive.

`react/jsx-no-leaked-render` is left out. It is not type-aware, and all 10 sites it flagged were false positives, mostly `&&` inside props rather than children.

author: brandondelgadoo
body:
## Lane

B035: Projects registry (`plan/lanes/backend/B035.json`, size S, P2 Workspaces)

## What changed

- **Projects API:** `GET`/`POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/projects`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /v1/projects/{id}`, with ETags, optional `If-Match` (412 when stale), `Idempotency-Key` on create, and CT-PAGE keyset pages bound to the workspace.
- **`repo` safety:** values that look like local paths, URLs with credentials, credential query parameters or token shapes (plus anything the B005 log redactor would hide) are a 422 on `/repo`. The rejected value is never echoed or logged.
- **Storage:** `projects` table (migration `20260102001000_projects.sql`) with a case-insensitive unique name per workspace, and `createProjectStore` in `@centcom/db`. Reads and locks only see live workspaces, and concurrent creates of one name give one project and 409s, never a 500.
- **Purge:** `registerProjectPurgeHook` in `@centcom/worker` deletes a purged workspace's projects before B027's purge, which the foreign key requires.

## Contracts

- Implements: CT-API-WORKSPACES (`listProjects`, `createProject`, `updateProject`, `deleteProject`)
- Consumes: CT-PAGE, CT-IDS, CT-RBAC, CT-ERR
- Contract files changed: **none**

## Built against

The real B021 RBAC, B024 idempotency, B025 pagination and B036 audit plugins, and B027's purge registry, all as on `main` at `768fff0`. In-memory stores for route tests, and Postgres 16 + Redis 7 for the `*.postgres` / repo tests.

## Tests

- [x] unit · [x] contract fixtures (`validate('api/Project' | 'api/ProjectPage')`) · [x] property/fuzz (fast-check over paths, credentialed URLs, token shapes, accepted references) · [x] failure paths
- Commands run (Node 22.23.3, pnpm 12.9.1), after merging main at `063602a` (B019):
  - `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && npx prettier --check .`: all pass
  - `pnpm test` (no DB): **189 files / 3190 tests pass**, 16 skipped (DB-only)
  - `DATABASE_URL=… REDIS_URL=… pnpm test` against `postgres:16` + `redis:7`: **204 files / 3384 tests pass**, 1 file skipped. Main's earlier integration failures were fixed by #36.

| Acceptance criterion | Test |
|---|---|
| POST as member → 201 + ETag; guest/billing → 403; same Idempotency-Key replays with `Idempotency-Replayed: true` | `projects.routes.test.ts`: "answers a member with 201…", "lets owner, admin and member create…", "replays the same Idempotency-Key…"; `projects.postgres.test.ts` |
| `Api` / `api` conflict in one workspace (409); same name in two workspaces is fine | `projects.routes.test.ts`: "keeps names unique per workspace ignoring case…"; `packages/db/test/repos/projects.test.ts` |
| `repo` of `/home/alex/work/repo`, `~/repo`, `C:\Users\a\repo`, `https://user:pw@github.com/a/b.git` or >256 chars → 422; `github.com/acme/app` and `sha256:ab12…` accepted | `projects.validation.test.ts` (table + property tests) |
| DELETE as member → 403, admin → 204; another workspace's project → 404 | `projects.routes.test.ts`: "deleting a project" |
| 120 projects, limit=50 → 3 pages, stable order, `has_more` true,true,false | `projects.pagination.test.ts` |
| After workspace deletion the purge hook removes all its projects (row count 0) | `projects.postgres.test.ts` (rows), `apps/worker/test/projects.purge-hook.test.ts` (hook wiring), `packages/db/test/repos/projects.test.ts` |
| Failure modes: concurrent create → 409 never 500; stale If-Match → 412; workspace deleted mid-request → 404 | `projects.routes.test.ts`, `projects.postgres.test.ts` (10-way race on the real unique index), `packages/db/test/repos/projects.test.ts` |

## Abuse / failure cases considered

- **Replay:** idempotent create (the same key with another body → 409).
- **Races:** `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on insert and unique-violation mapping on rename give a 409 under concurrency. Create share-locks the workspace row so it can't be deleted mid-insert.
- **Existence leaks:** outsiders, deleted workspaces, other workspaces' projects and unknown/malformed ids all get the same 404 body.
- **Size:** name ≤ 60, `repo` ≤ 128 code points after NFC, enforced in the API and by CHECKs in the table.
- **Privacy:** `repo` refuses paths, credentials and tokens. `created_by` is stored, not returned.

## Logging review

- [x] No tokens, keys, ciphertext, bodies, paths, branch names. Logs carry `project_id` / `workspace_id` only. The refused `repo` is checked not to appear in the 422 or in any log line.

## Deviations from the card (please review)

1. **RBAC stand-in (no CT-RBAC row for projects).** `contracts/01-auth-rbac.md` has no projects row, and B021's matrix must not grow without one. So member+ uses `session.create` (owner/admin/member) and admin+ uses `workspace.update` (owner/admin), exported as `PROJECT_ACTIONS`. **Consequence:** `session.create` has no API-key scope, so **API keys get 403** on list/create/update, although `openapi.yaml` allows `apiKeyAuth`. A denied guest/billing attempt is audited as `permission.denied` with `attempted: session.create`. Proper fix: a Contract PR adding a "Manage projects" row (and actions) in both repos.
2. **Audit stand-in (no `project.*` in CT-API-AUDIT).** The stable action list in `02-rest-api.md` has no project actions, and `audit.emit.test.ts` pins the catalogue to it. Changes are audited as `workspace.update` with `target: {type: 'project', id}` and `meta.fields` (`project` for create/delete, else the changed fields). Create and delete therefore look alike in the log. Proper fix: add `project.create|update|delete` in a Contract PR.
3. **Field name `repo`, not `repo_ref`.** The contract (`ProjectCreate`/`Project`) calls it `repo`, and contracts win over cards. The column is still `repo_ref`.
4. **Length limits.** The card says name 1-60 / repo ≤ 256, `02-rest-api.md` says 1-60 / ≤ 128, and `openapi.yaml` says 1-80 / ≤ 200. I used the strictest (60 / 128), which is valid under every source, but a client following `openapi.yaml` could be refused for a 150-char `repo`. The contracts should be reconciled.
5. **Migration name** is `20260102001000_projects.sql` (the repo's timestamp convention, enforced by `conventions.test.ts`) instead of the card's `0035_projects.sql`. Adrian renamed it from `…000900` when B016's device grants took that slot.
6. **`deleteForWorkspace(workspaceId)`** takes no `trx` (the card's signature does), matching B029's invites and the purge registry's hook signature. The hook itself lives in `@centcom/worker` like `registerInvitePurgeHook`, rather than in the API module.
7. **Empty `repo` (`""`)** is refused with 422 `too_short`; the schema has no `minLength`.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Contract PR for items 1, 2 and 4 above. Until then API keys can't manage projects.
- Wiring: whoever assembles the API/worker entry points must register `projectRoutes` and call `registerProjectPurgeHook(hooks, createProjectStore(db))` before `startWorkspacePurgeWorker`. No entry point exists yet.
- The `repo` token list is a deny-list of well-known shapes. It can't catch every possible secret, which is why the contract asks clients to send a hash.
- **Secret scan:** the repo-reference tests' deliberate fake tokens tripped gitleaks. The test now builds them from pieces (no token shape reaches main through the squash), and `.gitleaksignore` accepts the three findings pinned to branch commit `77c1620`. Heads-up, not from this PR: main's own `secrets` run is failing since B019 (#40), because B019 ignored only its branch commit and the squash commit on main carries the same values.

author: wietzesuijker
body:
`cluv sync` set the cluster's uv to the local uv version, so syncing from a machine with an older uv downgraded the cluster's uv. An older uv can't read the cache a newer one wrote. On clusters whose compute nodes have no internet, every job's `uv sync --offline` then fails, including jobs from other projects, since all projects on a cluster share one uv. Example: a sync from a laptop with uv 0.8.11 downgraded Rorqual from 0.12.23, and the next jobs failed to install torch.

- `install_uv` now runs `uv self update` without a version, so uv only moves forward.
- `run_uv_sync` used to skip whenever the commit was unchanged, even if uv had changed. It now also checks the cluster's uv version, so the cache gets refilled.

Side effect: after upgrading cluv, each project re-runs `uv sync` once per cluster.

author: vehkiya
body:
### Context & Objective

Previously, `sshx` only supported a single alias per SSH host connection block. Users could not configure multiple hostnames and IP addresses for the same connection (for example, allowing `ssh hostname1`, `ssh hostname2`, and `ssh <IP>` to work with the same credentials and options).

This change adds comprehensive support for multi-alias host definitions across the CLI, interactive wizards, parser, TUI, and JSON output.

### Key Changes

1. **CLI & Wizard Multi-Alias Support:**
   - Updated `sshx add [target] [alias...]` to accept multiple space-separated aliases.
   - Updated wizard input forms (title, description, and placeholders) to explicitly accept space-separated aliases.
   - When adding a host with an IP address, `sshx` automatically appends the IP address to the alias list if not already present, ensuring direct IP SSH connections use the configured host parameters.
   - Validation now cleanly accepts space-separated alias tokens while validating each alias individually.

2. **Configuration Engine (`internal/sshconfig`):**
   - `HostItem.Entry()` preserves all concrete aliases via `AllAliases`.
   - `UpdateHost` replaces the managed aliases while preserving wildcards (e.g. `*.corp.lan`), unmanaged directives, comments, and file position.
   - `CloneHost` and `HostSection` correctly match blocks against any target alias.
   - Optimized `FindHost`:
     - Added a zero-allocation fast-path for the common single-alias lookup ($O(N \times A)$ single pass).
     - For multi-token queries, builds an $O(T)$ set to enable $O(1)$ membership checking in a single pass over hosts without nested scans ($O(N \times A)$ vs previous $O(T \times N \times A)$).

3. **Interactive TUI & JSON Output:**
   - Host deletion in TUI passes all concrete aliases to ensure complete section removal.
   - Added `aliases` array to `sshx ls --json` when a host has multiple aliases (while maintaining `alias` as the primary alias).

4. **Documentation:**
   - Updated `README.md` features and usage examples to showcase multi-alias and IP association.

### Quality & Verification

- Added comprehensive tests:
  - `TestMultipleAliasesManagement` in `internal/sshconfig/config_test.go` covering `FindHost`, `UpdateHost`, and `CloneHost`.
  - `TestAccessibleAddHostWizardMultipleAliasesWithIP` and `TestAccessibleEditHostWizardMultipleAliases` in `internal/wizard/wizard_test.go`.
  - `TestAddCLIWithMultipleAliases` in `main_test.go`.
- All quality gates pass:
  - `go test -v -race ./...` (zero failures, zero race conditions)
  - `golangci-lint run` (0 issues)
  - `gofmt -s -w .` (clean)
  - `go mod tidy` && `git diff --exit-code go.mod go.sum` (clean)
  - `TestDependenciesPointOneWay` (clean)

body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Pedro Rodrigues** · [Slack thread](https://supabase.slack.com/archives/C051L8U2EJF/p1791383434405579?thread_ts=1791383434.405579&cid=C051L8U2EJF)_

**Before:** About 21% of MCP `create_branch` calls fail, mostly free-plan orgs getting `PaymentRequiredException` ("Branching is supported only on the Pro plan or above"), often after `get_cost` already quoted them a branch price. Nothing in this repo covered branching. platform-lite had no branch routes and a hardcoded free org.

**After:** Three regression evals (tools mode, `interface: mcp`) for the agreed fix ([Slack](https://supabase.slack.com/archives/C051L8U2EJF/p1791383434405579), [AI-1294](https://linear.app/supabase/issue/AI-1294)):

- `deploy-database-002-branch-free-plan`: free org. The agent checks `get_organization`, never calls `get_cost`/`confirm_cost`/`create_branch`, has zero tool errors, and tells the user a paid plan is needed.
- `deploy-database-003-branch-paid-plan-twice`: Pro org. First branch goes `get_cost` → `confirm_cost` → `create_branch`, both branches exist, `get_organization` is called at most once, zero tool errors.
- `deploy-database-004-branch-free-plan-project-scoped`: free org, project-scoped MCP. At most one `create_branch`, no `confirm_cost`, zero tool errors, and the agent explains the plan.

A "tool error" means `isError: true` or a thrown error. The server's planned non-error "requires Pro" response passes.

**These evals are expected to fail until the MCP server change ships and `MCP_SERVER_VERSION` is bumped.**

**How:**
- platform-lite: the org name and plan can be seeded. `GET /v1/organizations` no longer returns the plan (it didn't upstream either). There's a minimal `GET /v1/organizations/{slug}/entitlements` that only covers branching, and `GET/POST /v1/projects/{ref}/branches`, which returns the platform's 402 for free orgs. A branch is a fresh database with the parent's migrations replayed. Projects can also be seeded with migration history.
- Harness: adds `remote/organization.json` and `remote/migrations/` seeds, plus two frontmatter keys for tools evals: `mcpFeatures: [branching]` (opt-in, so other evals' tool surface doesn't change) and `projectScoped: true` (`--project-ref`).
- Fallbacks: the harness is single-turn, so 002 drops the "ok I upgraded, try again" turn and 003 asks for both branches in one prompt. Each eval README explains this.
- Known limit: a local ai-sdk run showed agents stopping to ask the user to OK the branch price before `confirm_cost`. In 003 nobody answers, so that run fails because the harness is single-turn, not because the agent is wrong. A real follow-up turn needs multi-turn support across all agent harnesses, which should be its own PR.

**Tests:** `pnpm typecheck`, platform-lite tests (111 pass, new `branching.test.ts`), core tests, framework tests, the new `test:regression-lib` scorer tests (17), `pnpm eval:dry`, `pnpm format:check`.

**AI disclosure:** Written end to end by Claude Code (AI). Pedro Rodrigues is the accountable owner and should review before merge.

author: petervanholland
body:
When a Postgres publication includes DuckLake's metadata tables and publishes updates and deletes, most commits fail. Even the second `INSERT` fails with a missing replica identity error on `ducklake_table_stats`, and `DROP TABLE` fails on `ducklake_table`.

Postgres requires a replica identity to update or delete rows in these published tables. Only five DuckLake metadata tables have primary keys. The others, including inlined data and deletion tables, have no replica identity by default.

This change gives every metadata table without a primary key `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` on Postgres: all of them when a catalog is created, the inlined data and deletion tables when a commit creates them, and before and after each migration step, since a migration both updates and creates metadata tables. Tables that already have another replica identity, have a primary key, or belong to another role are left alone, and other catalog types are not affected. A catalog created by an older DuckLake that is never migrated still needs one manual `ALTER TABLE ... REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` per metadata table. A new test runs writes, deletes, maintenance and migrations from 0.2, 0.4 and an older 1.1 development catalog under a publication, and checks a schema name with a quote and `$$`. It fails on main at the second insert. The Postgres tests of the affected areas and the full test suite pass, and the micro benchmarks show no regression.

Fixes #1365

body: ## Summary `export_diagnostics` put the live `courier.db` into the support zip with no redaction. Logs and `config.json` were scrubbed; the ledger was not. Task params are stored verbatim in `events.payload` and `tasks.params`, so a token, API key, or password passed as a task param leaked into the bundle. The export rebuilds a new SQLite file and inserts already-redacted cells. Secrets are learned from sensitive JSON keys, from `key=value` / `key: value` text, from Bearer tokens and common token shapes (`sk-`, `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `AIza`, `AKIA`), and from long mixed-case high-entropy strings, then replaced with the existing `redact_secrets` helper. Hex hashes and ids are left in place. The live ledger is not modified. `courier.db.REDACTION.txt` says the database in the bundle is a redacted copy, the live ledger is not modified, and the copy will not verify against the journal hash chain. body:
## Summary

Brings the Node toolchain up to date and cleans up the issues that surfaced along the way. Four commits, each self-contained:

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `08b4500b` Normalize line endings | `git add --renormalize .` only — 1,356 files, **no content changes** (`git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` is empty). Files were committed with CRLF despite `.gitattributes` declaring them text, so every touched file showed as a whole-file diff. |
| `31a1aac3` CI injection fix | `check.yml` / `format.yml` interpolated changed file names into `run:` scripts via `${{ }}`. A PR adding a file named e.g. `sites/x$(curl …\|sh).js` would execute it in CI. Names now pass via `env:` into a bash array. |
| `753bac37` Dependencies | Every dependency to latest (majors: octokit plugins, chalk 6, commander 15, curl-generator 0.6, @types/pako 3). `engines.node` → `>=22.12.0` (required by chalk 6 / commander 15; Docker and CI already use Node 22). Transitive advisories fixed with **scoped `overrides`** instead of `npm audit fix --force`, which would have downgraded jest 30→25, pm2 7→5, serve 14→10. |
| `b1d63266` Types + CI type check | Fixes all 141 `tsc` errors (TS 6 no longer auto-includes `@types/*`; upstream `.d.ts` bugs; a few real ones in `scripts/`), the one lint error, and adds `npm run typecheck` to the check workflow. |

## Results

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `npm audit` | 17 vulnerabilities (14 high) | **0** |
| `tsc --noEmit` | 141 errors | **0** |
| `npm run lint` | 1 error | **0** |
| `npm test` | 950 / 950 | 950 / 950 |

## Notes for reviewers

- **TypeScript stays on 6.x**: `typescript-eslint` only supports `<6.1.0`, so TS 7 would break linting.
- **Overrides** (`package.json`), each scoped to the package that pulls the vulnerable dep in:
  - `serve > compression ^1.8.2`
  - `pm2 > js-yaml ^4.3.2, basic-ftp ^6.2.2, chokidar ^4.0.3`. chokidar 4 drops `braces`, which has no fixed release; pm2's watcher is unused (`watch: false` throughout `pm2.config.js`), and chokidar 4 keeps the same `watch()` API and CommonJS build.
  - `@istanbuljs/load-nyc-config > js-yaml ^4.3.2`. It only calls `load()`; this also removes `argparse@1` and `sprintf-js`.
- **Behavior fix**: typing `epg-parser` showed `workers:load` could store `null` in `Worker.lastUpdated`; it now stores `undefined`.
- **Merging**: other branches based on the CRLF blobs may conflict with the normalization commit. Run `git add --renormalize .` on them first. Pulling from upstream `iptv-org/epg` may reintroduce CRLF blobs until upstream normalizes too.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test`: 950/950 on a fresh checkout of the branch tip
- [x] `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` are clean
- [x] `npm ci --dry-run`: lockfile in sync
- [x] Full suite passes on a fresh checkout of the normalization commit alone
- [x] Hostile file name through the new CI logic does not execute; eslint and `channels:lint` still work on real files
- [x] `channels:lint`, `grab --help`, `validate --help` and PM2 daemon start/stop smoke-tested
- [x] Check workflow passes on this PR (all steps ran, incl. Type check)

author: tschellenbach
body:
## How it works

```
llm request
 ├─ high-quality tier ── claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5 (new), ...
 └─ low-latency tier ─── ..., claude-haiku-5-5 (new, fallback for llm-fast)
        │
        └─> internal/llm/anthropic (existing package, no code change)
```

| Model | Tier | Price in / out per MTok | AA Intelligence Index |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude-sonnet-5-5` | high-quality | $2 / $10 | 47 at `high` |
| `claude-haiku-5-5` | low-latency | $0.10 / $0.50 (prompts up to 100k) | not yet ranked |

## Why

Anthropic shipped Sonnet 5.5 (2026-09-28) and Haiku 5.5 (2026-10-07). Sonnet 5.5 is second on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at half the price of Opus 5.5; Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic's fastest model at a tenth of Haiku 4.5's price. The provider package already exists, so this is config plus the provider's first live suite.

## Changes

- Two `router.yaml` entries, shaped like `claude-opus-5-5`. Haiku's over-100k price ($0.50 / $2.50) cannot be expressed in the price schema, so its entry uses the up-to-100k rate and a comment says so, as Grok 4.7's does.
- `anthropic_integration_test.go` runs `llmsuite` against both models.

## Unverified

- The live suite has not passed. The `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the local secrets is not scoped to a workspace and every request is a 400 asking for `anthropic-workspace-id`; this affects the existing Opus 5.5 entry too.
- Both models think while the provider reports they do not, so the suite's 512-token truncation test may fail once a key works.
- Sonnet's cache-read price is $0.10 per the Haiku 5.5 announcement; Anthropic's pricing tables still say $0.20.

author: alleneubank
body:
## Problem

On aem5 every CLI call warned `1 source parked as unsupported parser diagnostics, not missing`, while `reconciliation.unsupported_summary` was empty.

The source was a Codex rollout that had been parked on a `retained_context` record before REQ-PARSE-032 (#33, v0.36.5) taught the parser that record. The transcript was later deleted. A parked file is only reselected when its bytes or the parser change, so a deleted one stays parked for good. `coverage.unsupported` still counted it, but `unsupported_summary` filters on `NOT missing`, so the warning pointed at an empty summary and its "not missing" claim was false.

## Change

- `coverage.unsupported` now counts only rows that are `NOT missing`, matching `unsupported_summary`, REQ-CLI-023, and `docs/reconciliation-operations.md`. A deleted file is still counted under `coverage.missing`.
- Regression test: a parked Codex row with the diagnostic captured from the affected source (`record: 'retained_context'` at byte 768845) is marked missing. The test asserts coverage reports it as missing, not unsupported. It fails without the fix (`assert 1 == 0`).

## Verification

- `uv run pytest -q` (full suite), `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `ty check` all pass locally.
- Not verified yet: the live daemon on aem5. That needs a promote and restart after release.
